\begin{lemma}[Strings, and the content symmetry]\label{lem:strings}
Fix a positive root $\alpha$ and its triple
$(E,F,H):=(E_\alpha,F_\alpha,H_\alpha)$ on
a table space $M$ (Construction~\ref{con:gentable}'s root
triples), the matrix
units' at the letter pairs. The triple's span is
transpose-closed ($E^{\mathsf T}=F$, $H^{\mathsf T}=H$), so $M$ splits
orthogonally into subspaces invariant for the triple and irreducible for
it (Lemma~\ref{lem:orthsplit}, descending the dimension), each generated
by a triple-top $v$ at its $H$-eigenvalue $h$, at the join
$q+(h+1)=p+1$ over the top's coroot pair $\langle p\!:\!q\rangle$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:tops}(i),(ii) at the
triple), and spanned by
$v,Fv,\dots,F^hv$ with $F^{h+1}v$ the sum's unit: the string's $H$-eigenvalues
descend from the top's $h$ by two per lowering, the depth-$b$ eigenvalue
the pair $\langle h\!:\!2b\rangle$ at positive $b\le h$, each
once, two depths at the join $b+b'=h$ reading member swaps. At
the matrix units the splitting is the residual walk at the ordered
pair's height, the first letter's count against the second's: the
span's contents run at the height descending, a raising moving the
height key up by two, and at a
content a group member off the collected members' span names a
top, the membership test's residual itself
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}), per content the members closing at the
exchange bound, one top per refusal, the walk's count the
group's own (Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}); each deeper member's
self-pairing is the raise coefficients' telescoped multiple of the
top's at the fold's read
$E\,F^{b+1}v=(b{+}1)(h{-}b)\,F^{b}v$. The triple moves contents by $\alpha$ alone,
fixing every reflection-fixed read, so the strings split each joint
grading, and
summing string by string,
\[
\dim M_\mu\;=\;\dim M_{s_\alpha\mu}
\]
at the root reflection $s_\alpha$
(Construction~\ref{con:gentable}; the
transposition of the two letters at the matrix
units): content
multiplicities are invariant under every root reflection and
their compositions. At the matrix units a block's
occupied contents are permutation-closed, sit at or below the top
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}), and so sit at or above its reversal
$w_0\lambda$ in the dominance order, a sorted prefix sum falling as its
tail rises; the reversal is occupied once, at the top's own
multiplicity.
\begin{proof}
The least $m$ at
which $F^mv$ is that unit has
$h+1=m$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:tops}(ii)), so the eigenvalues descend two
per lowering. \emph{The walk.} The named top is perpendicular to the
collected members by the solve's identity and inside the group's
span; the top's raising image sits in the content above's group
span, spanned by the walk's own members there, and perpendicular
to them, so the image's self-pairing reads the sum's unit at the
positive pairing and the image with it. The top's gap is the
pairing's read, the lowered image's self-pairing joining the
second count's multiple of the top's to the first's,
$\langle Fv,Fv\rangle+\nu_j\,\langle v,v\rangle
=\nu_i\,\langle v,v\rangle$, the crossed exchange's read at
the letter pair (Lemma~\ref{lem:tops}(ii)), the positive pairing
forcing the second count at or below the first, the height their
gap; each deeper member's
self-pairing is the telescoped multiple at the fold's read, off the sum's unit through
the height and reading it at the further lowering, the
coefficient's own unit there; and per content the members close at
the exchange bound.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The Casimir reads the shape]\label{lem:casimir}
$C:=\sum_{p,q}E_{pq}E_{qp}$ commutes with every unit, $C\,E_{ab}=E_{ab}\,C$
(Construction~\ref{con:units}). On a
block $W_v$ at top content $\lambda$ of degree $k$ it is therefore one
scalar (Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}(ii)), read at the top:
\[
C\big|_{W_v}\;=\;q(\lambda)+\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle ,
\qquad
q(\lambda):=\sum_i\lambda_i^2,\quad
\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle:=\sum_{p<q}
\langle\lambda_p\!:\!\lambda_q\rangle\,,
\]
the balance-pair fold over the place pairs, a natural at the sorted
rows, collected per row as the balance-pair row weights
$\sum_i\lambda_i\,\langle r+2\!:\!2i\rangle$.
The units instantiate the Casimir field
(Construction~\ref{con:gentable}): the diagonal read
$\sum_pE_{pp}^2$ at the row squares, the pair terms
$E_{pq}E_{qp}+E_{qp}E_{pq}$ at weight one, every length two, and
the top read the display's.
\emph{The trace recursion.} On a table space's block at top
content $\lambda$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}), write
$\mathrm{mult}(\nu)$ for the content summand's dimension and, per
positive root at the root coroot pair
$\nu(\alpha^\vee)=\langle p\!:\!q\rangle$,
$\nu^{(l)}:=\nu+l\,\alpha$ for the moved contents: tracing the
Casimir fold over the $\nu$-summand, the summand's trace the one
value at every orthogonal spanning list
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}'s trace read), the block scalar against
the diagonal and the root terms' string traces
(Lemma~\ref{lem:strings} at the root triples), reads
\begin{multline*}
q(\lambda{+}\rho)\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu)
+\sum_{\alpha}[\,\langle\alpha,\alpha\rangle:2\,]\,
2\sum_{l\ge1}q\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})\\
=
q(\nu{+}\rho)\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu)
+\sum_{\alpha}[\,\langle\alpha,\alpha\rangle:2\,]\,
2\sum_{l\ge1}(p{+}2l)\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})\ .
\end{multline*}
\emph{The telescope.} Per positive root, with
$D_\alpha$ the coroot read per monomial,
$D_\alpha\,x^\nu=\nu(\alpha^\vee)\,x^\nu$, and
\[
G_\alpha:=\Big\langle\sum_\nu\Big(\sum_{l\ge1}(p{+}2l)\,
\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})\Big)x^\nu\,:\,\sum_\nu\Big(\sum_{l\ge1}
q\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})\Big)x^\nu\Big\rangle\ ,
\]
each member finite at the occupied contents, at the move's two sides,
$\alpha=\langle\alpha_+\!:\!\alpha_-\rangle$ per coordinate,
\[
x^{\alpha_+}\,G_\alpha\;=\;x^{\alpha_-}\,
\big(G_\alpha+D_\alpha\,\mathrm{ch}\big)
\qquad\text{at}\quad
\mathrm{ch}:=\sum_\nu\mathrm{mult}(\nu)\,x^\nu\ ,
\]
and the recursion collects to
\[
q(\lambda{+}\rho)\,\mathrm{ch}
\;=\;\mathcal L\,\mathrm{ch}
+\sum_\alpha[\,\langle\alpha,\alpha\rangle:2\,]\,2\,G_\alpha
\qquad\text{at}\quad
\mathcal L\,x^\nu=q(\nu{+}\rho)\,x^\nu\ .
\]
The generator list reads it through the Fierz sum
(Definition~\ref{def:generators}): a matrix acts as
$\sum_{pq}A_{pq}E_{pq}$, so
\[
\Delta\;=\;\sum_aX_a^{\dagger}X_a\ ,
\qquad
d_f\,\Delta+\xi\,\mathcal Z^2\;=\;\xi\,d_f\,C ,
\qquad \mathcal Z:=\sum_pE_{pp} ,
\]
positive semidefinite by its shape, its split the fold of squares, and the block read is the additive bracket
$d_f\,\Delta|_{W_v}+\xi\,k^2=\xi\,d_f\,\big(q(\lambda)+\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle\big)$,
the cleared content read of the weight-lattice Casimir at the form's scale $\xi$.
At the one-box shape $\lambda=(1)$ the cleared bracket reads
$1+r\,(r+2)=d_f\,(1+r)$, the one-value join $r(r+2)+1=d_f^{\,2}$: so
$\hat c_2(f)=[\,r(r+2):2d_f^{\,2}\,]$ against the adjoint's
below. At $\lambda=(2,1^{\,c})$ at $c+2=d_f$ the traceless read is
$2\,d_f$: the adjoint
Casimir is $C_2(\mathrm{adj})=d_f$ at
$\xi=[\,1:2\,]$, the Fierz weight of Definition~\ref{def:generators}.
\begin{proof}
\emph{The commutation.} $C$ is a diagonal
unit at the grading's read, every fold term reading each content
summand to itself with the unit at its scalar there
(Construction~\ref{con:units}), and an ordered letter pair at the
derivation here: per factor
the table's display reads the join at the factor's letters
(Construction~\ref{con:units}),
$E_{qp}E_{ab}+\delta_{bq}E_{ap}=E_{ab}E_{qp}+\delta_{pa}E_{qb}$
and
$E_{pq}E_{ab}+\delta_{bp}E_{aq}=E_{ab}E_{pq}+\delta_{qa}E_{pb}$,
the second read inside the first's middle term chains the two; a
letter off a content's support acts at the sum's unit there, the
Leibniz fold over a vacant place index
(Construction~\ref{con:units}): at the unit's own letter off the
source content's support the identity's two members read that
unit together, and inside the fold the governing letter is the
inner factor's lowered one, each member read at its own side's
content, the source on the one side and the unit's image on the
other, an image-side vacancy sitting at the unit's own lowered
letter alone at its one source count, the term's surviving
members closing at the display's own shorter instance, a factor
written at a content pair off the action's own move reading the
null map, the grading's read (Construction~\ref{con:units}), and
the vacant image letter's own pair closing at the diagonal reads'
square, the one count twice; so the collected reads run at the
letters each side supports, the unit's letter supported in the
source throughout, the chained term's two move orders one content
and the collected summands' contents one spelling at the
round-trip and chain reads through the supported unit letter, the
degenerate letters' members at the sum's unit on both sides; and
the $(p,q)$-fold collects each side's delta families to the one
join
\[
C\,E_{ab}+\sum_pE_{pb}E_{ap}+\sum_qE_{aq}E_{qb}
\;=\;E_{ab}\,C+\sum_qE_{aq}E_{qb}+\sum_pE_{pb}E_{ap}\ ,
\]
the two folds a summand on both members fixing the value
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}): $C\,E_{ab}=E_{ab}\,C$.
\emph{The top read.} At the top $v$,
$E_{pq}E_{qp}v$ at $p<q$ is $[E_{pq},E_{qp}]v
=\langle\lambda_p\!:\!\lambda_q\rangle\,v$, the row pair's value, the
commutator the site
datum at $E_{pp}=E_{qq}+[E_{pq},E_{qp}]$, a vacant row $p$ reading
the term and the pair's value at the sum's unit together, the row
list's descent putting the later row at that unit with it
(Construction~\ref{con:places}),
and at $p>q$ is the sum's unit, the raising's value at the top.
\emph{The trace recursion.} The $\rho$-shift is the form's
bilinearity at the weight collection
$\langle\nu,2\rho\rangle=\sum_\alpha
[\,\langle\alpha,\alpha\rangle:2\,]\,\nu(\alpha^\vee)$, and per
string one identity: an $\alpha$-string through $\nu$ at depth
$j$ from its top reads the trace coefficient
$(j{+}1)\,d+j\,(d{+}1)$ at the tie $d+q=p+j$, its moved reads
collect at $2\sum_{l\le j}(p{+}2l)=2j\,(d{+}1)+2j\,q$, the two
folds one gap identity, and a string above $\nu$ sums its moved
reads to equal members, the depth pairs at the join swapping
members. \emph{The telescope.} At the monomial $x^{\nu+\alpha}$, whose
coroot pair is $\langle p+2\!:\!q\rangle$, $G_\alpha$'s first
member reads $\sum_{l\ge1}(p+2+2l)\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l+1)})$,
the fold at $l$ from two, and $D_\alpha\,\mathrm{ch}$ reads
$(p+2)\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(1)})$, the term at $l=1$, so their join
is $x^{\alpha_+}G_\alpha$'s coefficient there,
$\sum_{l\ge1}(p+2l)\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})$, one further move
dropping one $l$; the second members read $q$ at every term, the
coroot pair's second member fixed by the move; and the recursion's
fold over $\nu$ against $x^\nu$ collects the string sums into
$G_\alpha$'s members, the displayed fold. \emph{The two
reads.} At $\lambda=(1)$, $q=1$,
$\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle=r$, $k=1$; at $\lambda=(2,1^{\,c})$,
$k=d_f$, $q=r+3$, $\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle=2r$, and the cleared
bracket reads $k^2+2d_f\cdot d_f=d_f\,\big(q+\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle\big)$,
both sides $3d_f^{\,2}$.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Duality, and the unit read]\label{lem:dualread}
\emph{(i) The dual.} A unit space $M$ defines its \emph{dual action}
on the underlying paired space, $E^\vee_{ij}$ the balance partner of
$E_{ji}$, the sum's every entry of equal members
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}'s displayed reads), a dual image the
exchanged letters' image scaled by the unit's own partner and a
pairing reading the partner on either side. The
dual obeys the table,
\[
[E^\vee_{ab},E^\vee_{cd}]+\delta_{da}\,E^\vee_{cb}
\;=\;\delta_{bc}\,E^\vee_{ad}\ ,
\]
the exchanged letters' read of Construction~\ref{con:units}'s, and
the transpose identity, $(E^\vee_{ij})^{\mathsf T}=E^\vee_{ji}$. Each
content is the original's balance partner, $\mu+\mu^\vee$ of equal
members coordinatewise, the dual diagonal reading a content summand
at its coordinate's partner. Invariant subspaces agree, so duals of
blocks are irreducible (Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}(i)), and
$(M^\vee)^\vee=M$. The pairing's evaluation
$\mathrm{ev}:M^\vee\otimes M\to\mathbb P$ is equivariant to the unit,
a letter pair's Leibniz image reading
$\langle E^\vee_{ij}f,\,x\rangle+\langle f,\,E_{ij}x\rangle$ at the
sum's unit. Its \emph{Gram-dual coevaluation} at a stated
independent spanning list $y$ is the determinant-scaled identity
datum,
\[
\mathrm{coev}\;:=\;\sum_{j,k}A_{jk}\;y_j\otimes y_k
\ \in\ M^\vee\otimes M\ ,
\]
$A$ the Gram's adjugate against its determinant, the list against
the adjugate reading the determinant's diagonal
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}), the grading splitting the Gram at one
block per occupied content, the cross pairings of equal members, so
the adjugate collects each block's own at the further blocks'
determinants; and the coevaluation is equivariant to the unit as
well, the moved coevaluation pairing every member pair at the
sum's unit. And $\mathrm{inv}(M^\vee\otimes W)\cong\mathrm{Hom}(M,W)$
at the equivariant maps: an \emph{invariant} of the dual tensor is
a family $\sum_if_i\otimes w_i$ at matched contents, the dual
diagonals' unit read, whose every letter pair's Leibniz image, the
dual action at the first factor, pairs every member pair of the
two carriers' stated lists at the sum's unit. The invariant reads
as the equivariant $x\mapsto\sum_i\langle f_i,x\rangle\,w_i$, the
fold the argument's own content group at the matched contents with
every cross-content pairing the sum's unit, the map's data one
matrix per occupied content with the moved reads
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}'s matrix families); and back through the
coevaluation, an equivariant $\varphi$ reads the invariant
$\sum_{j,k}A_{jk}\;y_j\otimes\varphi(y_k)$, the coevaluation's
second slot at the map's value, the family at matched contents
with each value at its member's own content. The round trips read
the determinant's scale: the composite at an equivariant $\varphi$
reads $\det G\cdot\varphi$ and the composite at an invariant reads
its $\det G$-multiple, the determinant off the sum's unit at the

series member reads $\hat c_2$ at or above the least of the end
list's and the dominant roots' reads, the statement's
trichotomies, the member's floor. At a fixed member the descent
runs in the coroot coordinates: a content with a coroot read at
two or beyond moves by that simple root, the off-key Cartan reads
balance partners of naturals (the member's displayed data), their
subtraction raising the off-key coroot reads, so the move keeps
dominance, one root with the class kept and the fall the
identity's, terminating at the member's clearing factor; the
contents at every coroot read at most one are finitely many, and
each reads its Casimir at or above every occupied fundamental's,
\[
C_2(\mu)\;=\;\sum_{i,j}\mu_i\,\mu_j\,\langle\omega_i,\omega_j\rangle
+\sum_i\mu_i\,\langle\omega_i,2\rho\rangle\ ,
\]
every summand at the fundamental form reads' upper sides or equal
members (the adjugate rows' form reads) with
$\langle\omega_i,2\rho\rangle=2\sum_j\langle\omega_i,\omega_j\rangle$
positive at the root fold's all-twos coroot list
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}): the member's floor is the
least fundamental read, one trichotomy fold over the member's
fundamental Casimir list with the displayed minima the
statement's, and at $E_8$ the fold reads the adjoint, the least
nonunit label the highest root at level one. The link count follows, each occupied link
contributing at least $\hat c_2(f)$ to the content.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[The alternant identity]\label{thm:weylchar}
Write $\mathrm{mult}_\lambda(\nu):=\dim(W_\lambda)_\nu$ and
$\mathrm{ch}_\lambda:=\sum_\nu\mathrm{mult}_\lambda(\nu)\,x^\nu$ for a
block's content generating polynomial, $q$
the standard square, and, at a list $\beta$ of naturals, $a_\beta$ the
\emph{alternant pair}, the
swap-graded sum over $S_{d_f}$
(Construction~\ref{con:places}), a balance pair of polynomials
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}):
\[
a_\beta\;:=\;\Big\langle
\sum_{w\ \mathrm{even}}x^{\,w\beta}\;:\;
\sum_{w\ \mathrm{odd}}x^{\,w\beta}
\Big\rangle ,
\]
each monomial on its permutation's side; an odd permutation of the
exponent list exchanges the members and an even one fixes them (the
grading additive, Construction~\ref{con:places}), and a repeated
exponent makes the members equal, the repeat's transposition mapping
either side onto the other, the wedge's repeat read. Then, at the
beta-sets of Construction~\ref{con:places}, $U$ the unit set with
sorted display $u$ and $X_\lambda$ the shape's with sorted display
$\lambda+u$,
\[
a_{u}\ \mathrm{ch}_\lambda\;=\;a_{\lambda+u}\ .
\]
\begin{proof}
\emph{The Casimir trace, string by string.} Trace the Casimir over the
content summand $(W_\lambda)_\nu$, the summand's trace the one
value at every orthogonal spanning list (Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}'s
trace read): the block scalar reads
$\big(q(\lambda)+\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle\big)\,
\mathrm{mult}(\nu)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}), the diagonal part reads
$q(\nu)\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu)$, and each pair $p<q$
traces $E_{pq}E_{qp}+E_{qp}E_{pq}$ over its strings
(Lemma~\ref{lem:strings}): a string through $\nu$ at depth $j$ from its
top, of top eigenvalue $h$, at the depth's raise factor $d$, the pair
$\langle h\!:\!j\rangle$, reads the
$\nu$-line coefficient
$(j{+}1)\,d+j\,(d{+}1)$, reading
Lemma~\ref{lem:tops}(ii)'s fold twice, at the words $F^{\,j+1}$ and
$F^{\,j}$, at the string's tie
$d+\nu_q=\nu_p+j$ the coefficient the identity
\[
(j{+}1)\,d+j\,(d{+}1)+\nu_q\;=\;2j\,(d{+}1)+\nu_p\ ,
\]
every read the balance pairs' own.
The pair's value at a content is the pair
$\langle\mu_p\!:\!\mu_q\rangle$ (Definition~\ref{def:ground});
writing $\nu^{(l)}$ for the pair's $l$-th move of $\nu$, the
occupied content at the joins $\nu^{(l)}_p=\nu_p+l$ and
$\nu^{(l)}_q+l=\nu_q$ with every other coordinate equal
(Construction~\ref{con:units}'s letter-pair moves iterated), the
value at $\nu^{(l)}$ is the pair
$\langle\nu_p{+}2l\!:\!\nu_q\rangle$; the string's values from its
$\nu$-line up to its top sum at the tie,
$2\sum_{l\le j}(\nu_p{+}2l)=2j\,(d{+}1)+2j\,\nu_q$, while a string
above $\nu$ sums its values to equal members: the value at depth $m$ is
the pair
$\langle h\!:\!2m\rangle$, the top's its one-member instance, two
depths at the join $m+m'=h$ reading
member swaps, the summed members equal.
Collecting string by string, the string coefficients' $\nu$-terms
collecting to the two side weights, $\nu_i$ weighted per place by
the gaps at $1+o=i$ and at $i+o'=d_f$, the equal-degree tie
$\sum_i\lambda_i=\sum_i\nu_i$ with the shared reads $q(u)$ and
twice the degree closing both sides, and the block's row read closing
at
$\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle+(d_f{+}1)\sum_i\lambda_i
=2\sum_i\lambda_i\,u_i$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}'s fold), gives
\[
q(\lambda{+}u)\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu)
+2\sum_{p<q}\sum_{l\ge1}\nu_q\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})
\;=\;
q(\nu{+}u)\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu)
+2\sum_{p<q}\sum_{l\ge1}(\nu_p{+}2l)\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})\ ,
\]
the pair sums over the places $p<q$ at their moves; the display
runs at every content list of the block's width, the recursion
family's keys the read's own finite carrier, and a key at the
count's unit reads the display as the moved folds' one value, the
above-string clause's read alone.
\emph{The generating telescope.} With $D_i:=x_i\partial_i$ and the
pairs' reads entering as balance pairs,
\[
G_{pq}\;:=\;\Big\langle
\sum_\nu\Big(\sum_{l\ge1}(\nu_p{+}2l)\,
\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})\Big)x^\nu
\;:\;
\sum_\nu\Big(\sum_{l\ge1}\nu_q\,
\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})\Big)x^\nu
\Big\rangle ,
\]
the outer sum over the natural exponent lists, each member finite (an
entry at $\nu$ reads occupied move targets alone,
the occupied contents finitely many, the multiplicity the occupancy
family's own count at the span's contents
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}'s counts at the read), the recursion's
keys the family joined to every pair move's sources, and a key off
that join reading the count's unit on both sides): a balance pair
of polynomials,
and the inner sums telescope
coefficientwise, one further move dropping one $l$, to
\[
\langle x_p\!:\!x_q\rangle\,G_{pq}
\;=\;x_q\,\langle D_p\,\mathrm{ch}\!:\!D_q\,\mathrm{ch}\rangle ,
\qquad\text{and the recursion reads}\qquad
q(\lambda{+}u)\,\mathrm{ch}
\;=\;\mathcal L\,\mathrm{ch}+2\sum_{p<q}G_{pq} ,
\]
$\mathcal L:=\sum_i(D_i+u_i)^2$ reading $q(\nu{+}u)$ on $x^\nu$.
At a key with $\nu_p=0$ the $x_p$-shift sits off the natural keys
and the identity's line is the string's own palindrome:
$\mathrm{ch}$ symmetric (Lemma~\ref{lem:strings}) pairs the
string's targets, two shifts at the join $l+l'=\nu_q$ reading one
multiplicity, so the moved weights collect to the second
exponent's count,
$\sum_{l\ge1}2l\,\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})
=\nu_q\sum_{l\ge0}\mathrm{mult}(\nu^{(l)})$.
\emph{The assembly.} $a_u=e\,V$ at the full monomial
$e:=\prod_kx_k$ and the pair product
$V:=\prod_{i<j}\langle x_i\!:\!x_j\rangle$
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}): the graded sum is
graded, an odd variable swap exchanging its members
(Construction~\ref{con:places}), so at $x_i=x_j$ its members are
equal, the
swap fixing the evaluation while exchanging the members; the
division at $\langle x_i\!:\!x_j\rangle$, monic in $x_i$
(Definition~\ref{def:poly}), leaves that evaluation as remainder,
members equal, so each factor's division is exact, the factors' in
turn, a product of polynomial pairs of equal members exactly at a
factor with equal members (the leading reads multiply), and $e$'s
cofactor reads monomial by monomial, every arrangement reading every
variable at least once, the factors and the variables pairwise
coprime (each factor monic linear in its higher variable, the
variables prime); the two sides
match at degree, $\sum_ju_j$ against $\binom{d_f}2+d_f$,
and at the leading monomial $x^{u}$, on the even side at
coefficient one: $a_u=e\,V$. So, at the cofactors $Q_{ij}$ at
$\langle x_i\!:\!x_j\rangle\,Q_{ij}=V$, one value each at the
factor of unequal members with the index swap exchanging the members,
the cofactor's coefficients are the monic letter's division descent
(Definition~\ref{def:poly}), $V$'s at the keys moved along the pair,
and $D_ie=e$ with the derivative read
$D_iV=\sum_{j\ne i}x_i\,Q_{ij}$ closing per key: a pair's moved
line through a key reads $V$ at its two arrangements alone, the two
fillings of the line's open values at the exchanged grading; the
monic descent opens at the key itself, one head read per variable
beyond $i$, the swapped cofactors moving the letter strictly; at an
arrangement with exponents $v$ the collected reads close on the
value's places split,
\[
v_i+\#\{\,j>i:\ v_i<v_j\,\}
\;=\;\#\{\,j>i\,\}+\#\{\,j<i:\ v_j<v_i\,\}\ ,
\]
$v_i$ the count of the values below the letter's over the places'
trichotomy; and at every further key the lines' reads close in
pairs: a line matched at both fillings joins its two arrangements'
reads at the exchanged grading within its own fold, and at a
one-sided hit the pair's value in the key occupies a second place,
whose line keeps the hit's upper filling with its further filling
at the receding value below the letter's, one one-sided hit per
partner line, an involution off its own fixed points; the two
hits' reads enter at opposite members, the places' transposition
exchanging the grading at partner places on one side of the
letter and the swapped cofactor's memberwise exchange reading the
join at places the letter splits, so the collected reads join at
equal members. Per pair the operator
identity
$\langle x_pD_p\!:\!x_qD_q\rangle
=x_q\,\langle D_p\!:\!D_q\rangle+\langle x_p\!:\!x_q\rangle\,D_p$
reads
\[
Q_{pq}\,\big\langle x_pD_p\,\mathrm{ch}\!:\!x_qD_q\,\mathrm{ch}\big\rangle
\;=\;V\,G_{pq}+V\,D_p\,\mathrm{ch} ,
\qquad
V\,G_{pq}=Q_{pq}\,x_q\,
\big\langle D_p\,\mathrm{ch}\!:\!D_q\,\mathrm{ch}\big\rangle ,
\]
the second the cleared telescope at the cofactor, and summing pairs,
a pair's two $D_iV$-terms collecting to the first display's
left side,
$\sum_i(D_iV)(D_i\,\mathrm{ch})
=V\sum_{p<q}G_{pq}+V\sum_{p<q}D_p\,\mathrm{ch}$. With the square's
Leibniz rule $D_i^2(fg)=(D_i^2f)g+2(D_if)(D_ig)+f(D_i^2g)$,
$\mathcal L_0:=\sum_iD_i^2$ reading $q$ at every arrangement, one
value $q(u)$, on each monomial of $a_u$, the read
$D_ia_u=a_u+e\,D_iV$, and the collection
$\sum_{p<q}D_p+\sum_iD_i=\sum_iu_iD_i$,
\[
\mathcal L_0\big(a_u\,\mathrm{ch}\big)
=2\,a_u\!\sum_{p<q}\!G_{pq}
+a_u\Big(\mathcal L_0+2\sum_iu_iD_i+q(u)\Big)\mathrm{ch}
=2\,a_u\!\sum_{p<q}\!G_{pq}
+a_u\,\mathcal L\,\mathrm{ch}
=q(\lambda{+}u)\,a_u\,\mathrm{ch}\ ,
\]
the first equality the Leibniz square's collection at those reads,
the second $\mathcal L$'s display, the third the telescoped
recursion.
\emph{The conclusion.} $a_u\,\mathrm{ch}_\lambda$ is graded, an odd
variable swap exchanging its members
($\mathrm{ch}$ symmetric, Lemma~\ref{lem:strings};
Construction~\ref{con:places}), with natural coefficients on each
member, hence a balance-pair combination
$\sum_\mu c_\mu\,a_{\mu+u}$ over dominant $\mu$: a repeated
exponent's read has equal members, the repeat's transposition's,
each strictly
decreasing exponent orbit is one graded sum, and the walk to the
representative is the exchanges' own: a key reading one value at
two places reads the repeat's transposition, a distinct-valued
key's first place pair off the descending order is an ascent
whose exchange lowers the ascending place pairs' count by exactly
one, and Construction~\ref{con:places}'s descent at the reversed
order closes the walk; its coefficient
$c_\mu$ is the pair of the two members' reads at $x^{\mu+u}$.
The support sits at $\mu\preceq\lambda$: $\nu\preceq\lambda$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}) and $wu\preceq u$ add, the permuted
display's prefix read. A leading prefix of $wu$ joins the

triangle $\sum_{i\le k}i$, the top value withdrawn per step at the
length capped by the bound; and the sorted display's prefix is the
triangle's complement at $k\,(d_f{+}1)$, so it clears every
permuted prefix. $c_\lambda=1$: the top content sits on one line
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}) against $wu=u$ alone, every prefix
equal forcing the assignment's prefixes to the triangle and each
entry to the sorted order's own, the identity assignment.
$\mathcal L_0$ reads each graded sum at $q(\mu{+}u)$, so the
display forces the equality
$c_\mu\,q(\lambda{+}u)=c_\mu\,q(\mu{+}u)$, and at dominant
$\mu\preceq\lambda$, $\mu\ne\lambda$,
\[
q(\lambda{+}u)\;=\;q(\mu{+}u)+\sum_{k<d_f}\delta_k\,g_k
\qquad\text{at}\quad
\sum_{i\le k}\mu_i+\delta_k=\sum_{i\le k}\lambda_i,\quad
\lambda_{k+1}{+}\mu_{k+1}{+}g_k=\lambda_k{+}\mu_k{+}2 ,
\]
the prefix gaps $\delta_k$ the dominance order's witnesses with some
$\delta_k$ positive at $\mu\ne\lambda$, every $g_k$ at least two at
sorted shapes: so $c_\mu$'s two members are equal off $\lambda$, such
a summand entering every value read equally on its two sides, and
$a_u\,\mathrm{ch}_\lambda=a_{\lambda+u}$ is the one-value read.

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The member assembly]\label{thm:assembly}
At a member's table with its positive list at the permutation
read (Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), the alternant pair at
$\rho$ assembles as the positive list's product: at the
\emph{side fold} $h$, the halved join
$2h=\sum_\alpha(\alpha_++\alpha_-)$ over the displayed sides,
\[
x^{h}\,a_\rho\;=\;\prod_{\alpha}\,
\big\langle\,x^{\alpha_+}\!:\!x^{\alpha_-}\,\big\rangle\ ,
\]
monomials at the alternant's content keys
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), the positive-parts fold reading
the shift, $\sum_\alpha\alpha_+=\rho+h$. The series' chord-minor
computations are the identity's displayed instances at their
stated shifts, and the fixed members' side folds read $46$, $11$
and $6$ on every key at $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$, with $E_7$'s
$(26,26,26,26,26,26,17,17)$ and $E_6$'s $(16,16,16,16,16,8,8,8)$
at the shared coordinates.
\begin{proof}
\emph{The subset fold.} The product expands over the occupancy
families $S$ at the positive list, reads at most one per member:
the $S$-term takes the second side at $S$'s members and the
first at the rest, its side $S$'s count and its key $h$ against
the join's datum $e_S$ at $e_S+\sum_{\alpha\in S}\alpha=\rho$,
the shift the positive-parts fold, and the product collects
factor by factor, each further factor reading every collected
term twice, the term kept and the term at the key moved by the
factor's root with the side exchanged, the collection a fold over
the running families read per key at the two graded counts, the
read the families' counts' sum at every key: the product is
$x^{h}\,\Phi$
at the graded fold
$\Phi:=\big\langle\sum_{S\ \mathrm{even}}x^{\,e_S}:
\sum_{S\ \mathrm{odd}}x^{\,e_S}\big\rangle$.
\emph{The grading.} Per simple index the pairing $T_i$ joins
$\alpha_i$ to the $s_i$-image of $S$ at $\alpha_i$ off $S$, and
reads the image of $S$'s further members at $\alpha_i$ in $S$:
an involution moving the count by one, with
$s_i\,e_S=e_{T_iS}$ at the letter's read $s_i\rho+\alpha_i=\rho$
and the permutation read, so $\Phi$ is graded, an odd element
exchanging its members.
\emph{The support.} Every image of a key sits at $\rho$ against
a natural fold: at an element $w$, the join
$w\,e_S+\sum_{\alpha\in S}w\alpha=w\rho$ splits at the images, a
member at a positive image contributing it and a member at a
partner image withdrawing its partner from the inversion list,
one member each (the list at the images of the
balance partners), so the $\rho$-fold collects
\[
w\,e_S\;+\sum_{\beta\in N,\ \beta\ \mathrm{kept}}\beta\;
+\sum_{\alpha\in S,\ w\alpha\ \mathrm{positive}}w\alpha\;=\;\rho
\]
at $N$ the element's inversion list, the kept members those off
the withdrawals: a natural fold of positives.
\emph{The pin.} A dominant key at a simple coroot pair the unit
is the letter's own fix, $s_i\mu=\mu$ at one odd letter, so a
graded fold's read there is its own member swap, equal members.
A dominant key at every simple pair beyond the unit is $\nu+\rho$
at dominant $\nu$, and its support read $\nu+\rho\preceq\rho$
solves $\nu$ against the unit fold: pairing the join
$\nu+\sum_ic_i\,\alpha_i$ at the unit fold against $\rho$ reads
$\langle\nu,\rho\rangle+\sum_ic_i\,\langle\alpha_i,\rho\rangle$ at
equal members; $\langle\nu,\rho\rangle$ sits at its upper side or
equal members, twice its read the fold of $\langle\nu,\alpha\rangle$
over the positive list at $2\rho$ the root fold, each member's read
the halved products' fold over its own natural fold,
$2\,\langle\nu,\alpha\rangle=\sum_kc_k\,\nu(\alpha_k^\vee)\,
\langle\alpha_k,\alpha_k\rangle$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}'s read),
every summand the length's natural multiple at a coroot pair on its
upper side or equal members at dominant data, while
every $\langle\alpha_i,\rho\rangle$ sits positive at its fold, so
the join's fold is the unit family and $\nu$ with it: the key is
$\rho$.
\emph{The conclusion.} $\Phi$'s read at a key is its dominant
image's up to the walk's parity, the dominance walk raising at a
lower-side simple pair, the raised key's root-fold dot the key's
own joined to the pair's margin at the letter's positive dot, an
occupied key's dot joining its family's or its witness fold's
positive dots to $\rho$'s own, and the raises closing at the
gap's count; a key off both folds reads each graded fold at equal
members, the two equal-membered reads one value. At the
image $\rho$ the read is one:
$e_S=\rho$ forces $\sum_{S}\alpha$ the unit fold, every member's
root-fold dot positive, so $S$ is the unit family at side even;
the element at each orbit key is one and $\rho$'s images are one
per element (the regular reads,
Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), so on $\rho$'s images $\Phi$
reads the Weyl fold's own members, and at every further dominant
image the pin reads both $\Phi$ and $a_\rho$ at equal members:
$\Phi=a_\rho$, key by key.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The member character identity]\label{thm:memberchar}
At a member's table, on a table space's block at top
content $\lambda$, with $\mathrm{ch}_\lambda$ the content
generating polynomial (Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}'s $\mathrm{ch}$),
\[
a_\rho\ \mathrm{ch}_\lambda\;=\;a_{\lambda+\rho}\ ,
\]
the reads at cleared presentations with stated shifts, every
display one value across the shifts (Definition~\ref{def:ground}'s
homogeneity principle), the $A$-series identity
(Theorem~\ref{thm:weylchar}) the first instantiation.
\begin{proof}
\emph{The eigen-read.} Work at the coordinate dot, the form one
scalar against it (Construction~\ref{con:sertables}'s form
displays), every read one value across the rescaling: the trace
recursion and telescope (Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}) read
$q_0(\lambda{+}\rho)\,\mathrm{ch}=\mathcal L_0^{\,\rho}\,
\mathrm{ch}+\sum_\alpha\tilde w_\alpha\,2\,G_\alpha$ at the dot
weights $\tilde w_\alpha=[\,\mathrm{dot}(\alpha,\alpha):2\,]$,
$\mathcal L_0^{\,\rho}$ reading $q_0(\nu{+}\rho)$ per monomial.
Three reads close the product's recursion. The \emph{cofactors}:
at the assembly identity (Theorem~\ref{thm:assembly}),
$Q_\alpha$ is the cofactor at
$\langle x^{\alpha_+}\!:\!x^{\alpha_-}\rangle\,Q_\alpha=a_\rho$,
and the telescope clears against it,
\[
a_\rho\,G_\alpha\;=\;Q_\alpha\,x^{\alpha_-}\,D_\alpha\,
\mathrm{ch}\ .
\]
The \emph{cross term}: a factor's Euler reads collect at the
part-weighted folds $D_{\alpha_+}$ and $D_{\alpha_-}$, their gap
the dot read, $D_{\alpha_+}=\tilde w_\alpha D_\alpha
+D_{\alpha_-}$ per monomial, so per factor
$\sum_i(D_iF_\alpha)(D_i\mathrm{ch})
=x^{\alpha_+}\,\tilde w_\alpha D_\alpha\mathrm{ch}
+F_\alpha\,D_{\alpha_-}\mathrm{ch}$, the first term clearing
through the telescope at the cofactor,
$Q_\alpha x^{\alpha_+}D_\alpha\mathrm{ch}
=a_\rho\,G_\alpha+a_\rho\,D_\alpha\mathrm{ch}$, and the fold over
the factors collects to
\[
\sum_i\,(D_i\,a_\rho)\,(D_i\,\mathrm{ch})
\;=\;a_\rho\,\Big(\sum_\alpha\tilde w_\alpha\,G_\alpha
+D_P\,\mathrm{ch}\Big)
\qquad\text{at}\quad P:=\sum_\alpha\alpha_+\ ,
\]
the positive-parts fold, $D_\alpha+D_{\alpha_-}
\tilde w_\alpha$-collected to $D_{\alpha_+}$ per factor. The
\emph{fold reads the shift}: $P=\rho+h$ at the side fold
(Theorem~\ref{thm:assembly}), the series' displayed checks per
coordinate its instances at $h=b_1\,\mathbf 1$:
the positive-part counts $g_i+g+2$ at $C_\ell$, $2g_i+2g+2$ at
$B_\ell$ and $2g_i+2g$ at $D_\ell$, over the joins $i+g_i=\ell$
and $g+1=\ell$, against $\rho$'s key reads $g_i+1$, $2g_i+1$ and
$2g_i$ with the shifts $g+1$, $2g+1$ and $2g$.
So, at the shifted Euler reads $\tilde D_i$, the diagonal pairs
$\langle\nu_i\!:\!h_i\rangle$ per monomial at the side fold's
keys, and
$\tilde{\mathcal L}:=\sum_i\tilde D_i^{\,2}$: the cleared
$a_\rho$'s exponents read $w\rho+h$, the dot Weyl invariant,
and the read rides the dominance walk at the graded fold: a
key reading the fold off equal members raises along the walk
to $\rho$, the walk and pin's read
(Theorem~\ref{thm:assembly}), with each letter keeping the
form (Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), so $q_0$ reads one
value at $\rho$ and at every such key,
$\tilde{\mathcal L}\,a_\rho=q_0(\rho)\,a_\rho$ at the graded
counts key by key; and the square's Leibniz rule at the three
reads collects to
\[
\tilde{\mathcal L}\,\big(a_\rho\,\mathrm{ch}\big)
\;=\;q_0(\lambda{+}\rho)\,\big(a_\rho\,\mathrm{ch}\big)\ .
\]
The reads close at the $\rho$-dot's own heights: the
Gram's $\rho$-column reads each entry's double as the length's
multiple of the key's coefficient count over the positive folds
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), every entry at its upper side
or equal members against the unit fold, so a dominant key at every
coordinate beyond the unit sits at or beyond $\rho$'s own dot, the
join at $\lambda+\rho$ capping its fold at the simple dots, the
coefficients' fold against the simples' $\rho$-dots at or below
$\langle\lambda,\rho\rangle$'s read, and a member on a root's
line beyond a key sits within the two dots' gap at the root's
positive dot.
\emph{The conclusion.} $a_\rho\,\mathrm{ch}$ is
reflection-graded, $\mathrm{ch}$ invariant
(Lemma~\ref{lem:strings}) and $a_\rho$ graded, so it is a
balance-pair combination $\sum_\mu c_\mu\,a_{\mu+\rho}$ over
dominant $\mu$ at
the cleared shifts: an exponent key whose dominant image holds a
unit simple pair reads equal members at that letter's own fix,
the series' flips at an equal-membered coordinate and swaps at a
repeated magnitude the displayed witnesses, and every further
orbit reads one strictly dominant-shifted representative, the
dominance walk's image at the regular reads
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}). A shifted alternant is
determined at four reads of a reflection-graded family: each
letter joins a key to its image at the exchanged grading,
every key sits at $\mu+\rho$ against a natural fold of simple
roots, the read at $\mu+\rho$ is one at the even grading
alone, and every key off $\mu+\rho$ at each simple coroot pair
beyond the unit reads its two graded counts at one value (the
regular reads, Construction~\ref{con:sertables}): an occupied
key raises along the walk to its dominant image, the raises
closing at the fold's count and the counts mapped letter by
letter, an image at a unit simple pair reads equal counts at
its fixing letter, and the family reads $a_{\mu+\rho}$'s
graded fold key by key. The support sits at
$\mu\preceq\lambda$ ($\nu\preceq\lambda$ at the block,
Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}, and $w\rho\preceq\rho$ at the
inversion list's fold, Construction~\ref{con:sertables}, add),
and $c_\lambda=1$: a pair joining to $\lambda+\rho$ reads its
two witness folds' $\rho$-dots joined at the sum's unit, every
simple's $\rho$-dot positive at its fold
(Theorem~\ref{thm:assembly}'s pin), so both folds are the unit
family and the pair is the two tops': the Weyl fold's one even
read at $\rho$ against the top content's one line
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}), the count one at the even grading
alone. Each
family is $\tilde{\mathcal L}$-diagonal at $q_0(\mu{+}\rho)$, so the
eigen-read forces $c_\mu\,q_0(\lambda{+}\rho)
=c_\mu\,q_0(\mu{+}\rho)$; at dominant $\mu\preceq\lambda$ off
$\lambda$ the two reads' gap is the dominance fold's,
\[
q_0(\mu{+}\rho)
+\mathrm{dot}\big(\lambda{+}\mu{+}2\rho,\
{\textstyle\sum_i}c_i\,\alpha_i\big)
\;=\;q_0(\lambda{+}\rho)
\qquad\text{at}\quad
\mu+{\textstyle\sum_i}c_i\,\alpha_i=\lambda\ ,
\]
positive at dominant data, the fall identity's own read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}): $c_\mu$'s members are equal off
$\lambda$, and the display is the one-value read.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[The dimension is the Weyl product]\label{cor:weyldim}
$d_\lambda=\mathrm{ch}_\lambda(1,\dots,1)$, and the substitution
$x_j:=t^{\,u_j}$ at the unit set's sorted display maps the
character identity's two graded sums
(Theorem~\ref{thm:weylchar}) to full monomials against pair
products, the assembly's one-variable read, each graded sum
reading its full monomial against its pair product, and the two
full monomials' reads clear by the product's injectivity at the
degree tie:
\[
\mathrm{ch}_\lambda\big(t^{\,d_f},\dots,t\big)\,
\prod_{j<k}\big\langle t^{\,u_j}\!:\!t^{\,u_k}\big\rangle
\;=\;t^{\,|\lambda|}\,\prod_{j<k}\big\langle t^{\,l_j}\!:\!t^{\,l_k}\big\rangle
\qquad(l:=\lambda+u) .
\]
Each factor clears by
$\langle t^{a}\!:\!t^{b}\rangle=t^{b}\,\langle t\!:\!1\rangle
\sum_{c+e+1=g}t^{\,e}$ at $b<a$ and its witness gap $g$ at $b+g=a$,
the geometric word
one term per splitting, the two sides with one
$\langle t\!:\!1\rangle$ factor per pair, which drop at the shared
monic factors' withdrawal, two products of one value at the
division's descent (Definition~\ref{def:poly}), and the polynomial
identity read at $t=1$ gives
\[
d_\lambda\,\prod_{j<k}g_{jk}\;=\;\prod_{j<k}g^{\lambda}_{jk}
\qquad\text{at}\quad
u_k+g_{jk}=u_j,\quad l_k+g^{\lambda}_{jk}=l_j\ ,
\]
the unit set's member gaps against the shape's, every right factor at
least its left partner. At a member the identity
specializes at the principal point, the substitution $x^\nu$ to
$t^{\,\mathrm{dot}(\nu,\rho)}$, and the assembly identity reads at either list
(Theorem~\ref{thm:assembly}; Theorem~\ref{thm:memberchar}): the member dimension is the gap product
\[
d_\lambda\,\prod_{\alpha}g_\alpha
\;=\;\prod_{\alpha}g^{\lambda}_{\alpha}
\qquad\text{at}\quad
\mathrm{dot}(\rho,\alpha)=g_\alpha,\quad
\mathrm{dot}(\lambda{+}\rho,\alpha)=g^{\lambda}_{\alpha}\ ,
\]
the folds over the member's positive list, every right factor at
or beyond its left partner.
\begin{proof}
The pair product
expands over its occupancy families at the place pairs
(Theorem~\ref{thm:assembly}'s subset fold at the powers' gaps),
the full monomial joining one display entry per place, so each
family's key is the fold of the display against its \emph{taken
counts}' successors, per place the count of its pairs taken
there with the joined entry's own one, and its side the family's
own count; at two places of one taken count the family joins its
exchange at its first tied place pair, the pairs enumerated at
the later place with the earlier beneath it, one read of the
family kept by the exchange: each further pair reads to its
partner at the places' transposition, sorted at the trichotomy,
its taken place the letter swap's image with the membership
flipped exactly where the sorting crosses the taken position,
and the shared pair's take flipped, one key at an odd move of
the side, the joined graded reads entering at equal members; a
family at
pairwise distinct taken counts takes every pair at one place
against each further place in turn, so its counts fill the
degrees below the width and the family is an assignment's, its
side the inversion list's parity (Construction~\ref{con:places}):
each graded sum reads its full monomial against its pair product.
At a member the
substitution maps a graded fold to the
exchanged list's,
$\mathrm{dot}(w\beta,\rho)=\mathrm{dot}(\beta,w^{-1}\rho)$ at
the kept form with the reversed word's element at its parity
class (Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), so
$a_{\lambda+\rho}$'s principal read is $a_\rho$'s at the list
$\lambda+\rho$'s own point, the series' role-symmetric signed
and plus minors the displayed instances with the $D_\ell$
doubled alternant's two at both sides clearing by the product's
injectivity, and
each factor clears by the geometric word at its
gap as above.
\end{proof}
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[The product's block counts, by the alternant pairs]
\label{cor:steinberg}
For shapes $a,b,c$,
\[
N^c_{ab}\;+\sum_{\sigma\ \mathrm{odd}}
\mathrm{mult}_a(\nu_\sigma)
\;=\;\sum_{\sigma\ \mathrm{even}}\mathrm{mult}_a(\nu_\sigma)
\qquad\text{at}\quad
\nu_\sigma+\sigma(b+u)=c+u\ ,
\]
$\sigma$ over $S_{d_f}$ at the swap grading
(Construction~\ref{con:places}), $u$ the unit set's sorted display,
$\nu_\sigma$ the tie's lattice
solution and the multiplicity read the contents' occupancy read,
the counts
descending to labels at matched degree (Construction~\ref{con:labels}).
At a member the identity runs at the member alternants: at every
member,
\[
N^c_{ab}\;+\sum_{w\ \mathrm{odd}}\mathrm{mult}_a(\nu_w)
\;=\;\sum_{w\ \mathrm{even}}\mathrm{mult}_a(\nu_w)
\qquad\text{at}\quad
\nu_w+w\,(b+\rho)=c+\rho\ ,
\]
$w$ over the member's Weyl list at the reflection grading
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), the ties' solutions matched
lists.
\begin{proof}
$a_u\,\mathrm{ch}_a\mathrm{ch}_b=\mathrm{ch}_a\,a_{b+u}$ and
$a_u\,\mathrm{ch}_a\mathrm{ch}_b=\sum_{c'}N^{c'}_{ab}\,a_{c'+u}$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:weylchar} twice, the second at the product's
content data, the pair list's count at every content by
Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(iii), read over the exhaustion's
blocks at Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(i),(ii)'s graded display),
and the two reads match at the
one monomial $x^{c+u}$: the product $\mathrm{ch}_a\,a_{b+u}$ reads
it at the displayed ties, one summand per permutation at its side
and its solution, while a graded sum $a_{c'+u}$ reads it at
$\sigma(c'+u)=c+u$ alone, the identity assignment at $c'=c$, two
strictly decreasing displays at distinct entries: the coefficient
pair is the display's.
At a member the
content generating polynomials multiply over a tensor product, the
contents' sums, and the tensor exhausts into blocks at the member
counts (Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(i),(ii) at table spaces), so
the product $a_\rho\,\mathrm{ch}_a\,\mathrm{ch}_b$ reads per key
twice (Theorem~\ref{thm:memberchar} twice): as
$\mathrm{ch}_a\,a_{b+\rho}$, a key's two counts the identity
$a_\rho\,\mathrm{ch}_b=a_{b+\rho}$'s fold over the $a$-family, one
instance at each member's withdrawn key, and as the channels' fold
$\sum_{c'}N^{c'}_{ab}\,a_{c'+\rho}$, each channel's identity at the
key itself. At the key $c+\rho$, dominant at every simple pair
beyond the unit, a further channel's fold is vacant, the orbit's
one dominant image its own shifted top, and $c$'s channels read one
at the even grading alone, the shifted key's top (the regular
reads, Construction~\ref{con:sertables}): the member display.
\end{proof}
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[The member count and involution]\label{lem:memberdata}
At a member's table (Construction~\ref{con:gentable};
Construction~\ref{con:sertables}) the fusion count and the label
involution are constructions of the table's data, one each.

\emph{(i) The multiplicity family is the recursion's one solve.}
A block's \emph{family} reads each occupied content at its
summand's count, and the family closes key by key down the
$\rho$-dots from the top, the recursion's one solution: the top's
summand is one line with the
occupied contents at or below the top
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}), every count is its dominant image's
(Lemma~\ref{lem:strings}), and at a
dominant content below the top the trace recursion's display
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}) reads the count's multiple of the two
Casimir reads' gap against the moved string folds' join. The member's fusion count is the member display's
gap read at the family, the two graded sums over the member's
Weyl list at the first factor's family
(Corollary~\ref{cor:steinberg}); the display folds at the family:
each occupied content's moved key, the target's shifted key
joined to the content's balance partner, raises along the
dominance walk to its dominant image
(Theorem~\ref{thm:memberchar}'s conclusion walk), one letter per
raise with the letter count reading the tie element's parity, the
walk's word that element's reversal at one parity class
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}'s grading and transport), a
walk ending at the shifted second factor naming the tie's one
element at the regular reads (Construction~\ref{con:sertables})
with every further end off the ties, the shifted factor its
orbit's one dominant image, so the count is the family's fold at
the walks' parities, one walk per occupied content; and the
fusion row at two labels
is the dominant targets at occupied counts, the targets at or
below the labels' sum (the factors' contents adding over the
tensor product, Construction~\ref{con:gentable}, each at or below
its own top, Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}).

\emph{(ii) The involution is the shifted walk's read.} The dual
action is the transposes' partner read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(i)'s displays at
Construction~\ref{con:gentable}'s fields, each commutator's
transpose the exchanged pair's with two partners composing to the
original), so a dual block's occupied contents are the block's at
their balance partners. The \emph{reversal} is the element at the
full inversion list, grown one letter at a member off the list
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}'s creation read), its image of
every positive member the member's partner, the list's own read,
and its image of $\rho$ is $\rho$'s partner, the root fold's
image at the partner list; its negated image of a dominant
content is dominant, the coroot pairs read across the partner
list. The dual
block's top is the balance partner of the top's reversal image, maximal
among the dual's occupied contents and off the sum's unit
(Lemma~\ref{lem:tops}(i)). So the \emph{dual label} reads at the
shifted walk: the dual's top joined to $\rho$ is the dominant
image of the top-with-$\rho$'s balance partner, one image at the
regular reads (Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), and the
involution's construction is that walk, uniqueness by
construction.
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i)} The dominance walk raises at a
lower-side simple pair with each raise's $\rho$-dot positive
(Theorem~\ref{thm:memberchar}'s conclusion walk;
Theorem~\ref{thm:assembly}'s pin), so a dominant image's
$\rho$-dot sits at or beyond its orbit's every member's; the
trace recursion's gap is positive at dominant data
(Theorem~\ref{thm:memberchar}; Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}'s fall
identity), each moved count in the string folds' join
read at its dominant image of strictly larger $\rho$-dot: the
product's injectivity reads the count off the higher keys'
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}), the descent closes on the finite
window at the dominant keys' $\rho$-dots capped by the top's own
(Theorem~\ref{thm:memberchar}), and the family is the recursion's
one solution.
\emph{(ii)} The reversal's image of a dominance join is the exchanged
join at the partnered folds, so the image order flips and a
block's occupied contents sit at or above the reversal image of
the top, occupied once at the top's line
(Lemma~\ref{lem:strings}; Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}); the dual
block's top is that image's partner.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One box fuses up the shapes]\label{lem:pieri}
$N^c_{\mu f}=1$ at every dominant $c=\mu+e_i$, the row's members
exactly those targets, $f$ the
one-box shape, its contents the $e_i$ once each. At the
complement's one-column shape $f^*$, the depth at the gap $g$ at
$g+1=d_f$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(ii)'s complement at the
one-box shape), the contents are the full column's withdrawn
letters, one letter withdrawn per content at one count each, and
$N^c_{\mu f^*}=1$ at every dominant $c$ at the
join $c+e_i=\mu+(1^{d_f})$, the row's members exactly those
targets.
\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:steinberg} at $a=f$ reads the ties
$\nu_\sigma+\sigma(\mu+u)=c+u$ at $u$ the unit set's sorted
display, the one-box
contents being the $e_i$ once each, so a contribution needs
$c+u=\sigma(\mu+u)+e_p$ at one place $p$: the display $c+u$ sorts
$\mu+u$ with one value raised by one, a raise at an occupied
successor reading a repeat ($\mu_h=\mu_{h+1}$ at $h+1=i$ puts the
raised value at its neighbor's), which the strictly decreasing
$c+u$ misses at every $\sigma$, and a raise at a vacant successor
keeping its own place ($\sigma=\mathrm{id}$, one count, on the
even side), the target $\mu+e_i$ dominant exactly there. At $f^*$ a
count read transports across the letters' exchanges through the
shared sorted representative, so each withdrawn letter's content
reads the top line's count, one, and a content holding a letter
twice reads its sorted representative's count, vacant at the
dominance cap (Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan};
Lemma~\ref{lem:strings}), and the
tie analysis reads the complement's row: a contribution needs
$c+u+e_p=\sigma(\mu+u)+(1^{d_f})$ at one place $p$, the tie read
at the inverse permutation with the displays transported across
it, a lowering of the sorted display the flipped assignment's
raise (Construction~\ref{con:places}'s inverse permutation): the
display
$c+u$ sorting the raised display $\mu+u+(1^{d_f})$ with one value
lowered by one, a lowering at a vacant gap reading a repeat
($\mu_p=\mu_{p+1}$ puts the lowered value at its follower's),
which the strictly decreasing $c+u$ misses at every $\sigma$, and
a lowering at an occupied gap keeping its own place
($\sigma=\mathrm{id}$, one count, on the even side), the target
dominant exactly there.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The path count's square sum]\label{lem:pathsquare}
The \emph{path count} $f^\lambda$ of a shape
(Construction~\ref{con:places}) is the count of its descents to the
unit shape by one box removed at a time, the recursion
$f^\lambda=\sum_{\mu\to\lambda}f^\mu$ over the shapes with one box
removed, the unit shape's count one; at $k\le d_f$, over the shapes
of $k$ boxes,
\[
\sum_{|\lambda|=k}(f^\lambda)^2\;=\;k!\ .
\]
\begin{proof}
On the free $\mathbb P$-space of the shapes of at most $k$ boxes,
the unit shape among them, let $U$ add a box over the covers and
$D$ remove one, transposes for the shape pairing, so
$f^\lambda=\langle\lambda,U^k\mathbf 1\rangle$, the recursion read
at $D$'s transpose. At a shape of fewer than $d_f$ rows, every
shape below the degree $d_f$ among them, $DU=UD+\mathrm{id}$: two
distinct shapes of one size share a cover exactly where they share
a covered shape (their union and their intersection, one each,
where they differ by one moved box), and one shape's addable
corners exceed its removable ones by one (each is read off the
distinct row lengths, the additions one more at the rows' end). So
$D\,U^{j+1}\mathbf 1=(j+1)\,U^{j}\mathbf 1$ at every $j<d_f$ by
induction, $D\,\mathbf 1$ the sum's unit and $U^{j}\mathbf 1$ at
the degree $j$, and
\[
\sum_{|\lambda|=k}(f^\lambda)^2
=\langle U^k\mathbf 1,U^k\mathbf 1\rangle
=\langle U^{k-1}\mathbf 1,D\,U^k\mathbf 1\rangle
=k\,\langle U^{k-1}\mathbf 1,U^{k-1}\mathbf 1\rangle
=k!\ .
\]
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The mixed power's invariants are the permutation span]
\label{lem:mixedinv}
At $k\le d_f$ the invariants of $V^{\otimes k}\otimes(V^{\otimes k})
^\vee$ are spanned by the $k!$ place permutations, whose Gram is the
cycle count $d_f^{\,\#\mathrm{cycles}(\sigma\tau^{\mathsf T})}$, the
transpose the inverse permutation's matrix
(Construction~\ref{con:places}), the pairing's
index sums closing each cycle to a factor $d_f$.
\begin{proof}
\emph{The block count is the path count.} $M\otimes V$ exhausts as
$\bigoplus_\mu N_\mu(M)\,(W_\mu\otimes V)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}), and $W_\mu\otimes V$ by one boxes
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pieri}), so at every power
$N_\lambda(V^{\otimes k+1})
=\sum_{\mu\to\lambda}N_\mu(V^{\otimes k})$, the
unit power the scalars' line, over the shapes with
one box removed: $N_\lambda(V^{\otimes k})=f^\lambda$, the path count
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pathsquare}), every shape of $k$ boxes at most
$k\le d_f$ rows deep.
\emph{The invariant count.} An invariant of $M\otimes M^\vee$ is
the dual tensor's family at matched contents with every letter
pair's Leibniz image null (Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(i)), its data
one matrix per occupied content with the moved reads
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}'s matrix families), and its form
coordinates the matrices' entries at the contents' monomials; the
families combine at the entries, the action's row fold reading
each entry once (Definition~\ref{def:elim}), so a member's value,
the moved reads and the coordinates are additive and scale-reading
over the members. At an
exhaustion of the power's carrier (Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(i))
every top's value under the family is a top at the top's own
content, a raising image of the value the moved read at the top's
null image; and a family whose every top value is the sum's unit is
null: Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}(ii)'s cleared line reads every value
at the top's value the sum's unit, the blocks span the
carrier, and a null map's matrices are null at the carrier's own
coordinate vectors. So the stacked top values map an independent
list of invariants to an independent list inside the raising
kernels' joined span, a null image's family null with the
coefficients read back at the independence, and the invariants'
count sits at or below the kernels' count
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}'s exchange clause), $N_\lambda$ tops per
content (Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(ii)) at kernel dimension
$N_\lambda$ each (Definition~\ref{def:blockcount}):
\[
\sum_\lambda N_\lambda^{2}
\;=\;\sum_{|\lambda|=k}(f^\lambda)^{2}\;=\;k!
\]
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pathsquare} at the path-count clause above).
\emph{Independence, the span, and the Gram.} A place permutation is
equivariant (the units' Leibniz sum is place-symmetric,
Construction~\ref{con:places}), its family the permutation matrices
per content, and at $k\le d_f$ the $k!$ of them are independent,
reading distinct monomials on $v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_k$ at
distinct indices; an invariant off their span would extend the
independent list one past $k!$, against the count above: the
permutations span. Two permutations' forms pair at the count of the
monomials their two reads agree on, and the reads agree exactly at
a monomial constant along each cycle of $\sigma\tau^{\mathsf T}$,
one free letter per cycle: the Gram is
$d_f^{\,\#\mathrm{cycles}(\sigma\tau^{\mathsf T})}$.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}
