\section{The form, the carrier, and the setting}

\begin{definition}[Labels, the Casimir, and its weight-free read]\label{def:c2hat}
$\mathrm{Lab}$ is the label set of the calculus, one reduced shape per
label (Construction~\ref{con:labels}) and one block at each
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}(iv)); and
$C_2(\lambda)=\langle\lambda,\lambda+2\rho\rangle$ the quadratic Casimir,
the block read of Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir} at the invariant form's scale
(Proposition~\ref{prop:form}), with $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ the induced
weight-lattice form, the reads $q(\lambda)$ and
$\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle$ Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}'s display's. $\theta$ denotes the highest root, and
\begin{gather*}
\hat c_2(\lambda)\;:=\;\big[\,d_f\,Q(\lambda):2d_f^{\,2}\,\big]
\quad\text{at}\quad
k^2+d_f\,Q(\lambda)=d_f\,q(\lambda)+d_f\,\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle\ ,\\
d_f\,Q(\lambda)=\sum_{p<q}\langle\lambda_p\!:\!\lambda_q\rangle^2
+d_f\,\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle\ ,
\end{gather*}
the second display the join's constructed witness: the square
identity
$d_f\,q(\lambda)=k^2+\sum_{p<q}\langle\lambda_p\!:\!\lambda_q\rangle^2$
collects the row pairs' squares against the degree ($k^2$ reading
$q(\lambda)$ with the place pairs' cross products twice, the pairs'
squares the complement), every summand a natural at the sorted rows
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}'s fold), and at every nonunit label two
coordinates differ (equal coordinates are full columns, the unit
label's class), their pair's square positive by its shape; the
dual label reads one value, $\hat c_2(\bar a)=\hat c_2(a)$, the
complement's pair gaps the label's own at reversed places, one
fold of squares, and the complement's row weights the
balance partners there, the full weight list's fold of equal members
(Construction~\ref{con:labels}; Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(ii)); the
definition reads at the nonunit labels, the unit label's line
$\Delta$'s kernel, the kernel point's read; the clearing factor the
fundamental count (Construction~\ref{con:places}),
the cleared traceless bracket at degree $k$ against the adjoint's
$Q(\theta)=2d_f$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}): one quadratic form on the weight lattice read against itself,
the form's components $\langle\lambda,\lambda+2\rho\rangle$ and
$\langle\theta,\theta+2\rho\rangle$ rescaled by the one factor at every
scale of the form, the pair one value across them
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}; Proposition~\ref{prop:form}). The development runs on one
object defined on the label index alone,
$\Delta\chi_\lambda=C_2(\lambda)\,\chi_\lambda$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[One value on the form line]\label{prop:form}
The pairings of the $\theta$-block against its dual are one line, the
\emph{form line}: $\theta$ is self-dual ($\theta^*=\theta$,
Construction~\ref{con:labels}) and an equivariant map between blocks is
the unit of its map space at distinct labels and a scalar at one
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}(ii),(iii)). The \emph{invariant form} is a
point $\xi$ of that line, a scalar pair, and rescaling the point rescales $C_2$
with it while
fixing every character. Hence a pair of two reads, each of degree one in the
form, is one value at every point of the form line. Every energy-type read below ($E$, $\varepsilon_0$,
the coupling weights, the constants $c_i$) accordingly denotes its
read against $C_2(\mathrm{adj})$, and every surviving constant is a count.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Rescaling the form's point rescales $\Delta$'s block read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}), hence
$C_2(\lambda)=\langle\lambda,\lambda+2\rho\rangle$ at every $\lambda$,
and a pair of two such reads is one value at every point, its two
components rescaled by the one factor. A character is a label-index generator,
defined without the form (Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}). $\Delta$, $\mathrm{content}$ and $E$ are each of degree
one in the form and $\chi_\theta$, $V$, $M$ are form-free, so each displayed
pair of two such reads is one value at every form point.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Generators, where a proof reaches for them]\label{def:generators}
$X_a$ are anti-Hermitian, the trace pairing reading
$\mathrm{tr}(X_aX_b)+\xi\,\delta_{ab}$ at the sum's unit and the
Fierz read cleared at the count,
\[
d_f\sum_a(X_a)_{pq}(X_a)_{rs}+\xi\,d_f\,\delta_{ps}\delta_{rq}
\;=\;\xi\,\delta_{pq}\delta_{rs}\,,
\]
at the form's
point $\xi$; the Hermitian companions $T_a$ at $X_a=i\,T_a$ read
$\xi$ throughout; then
$\Delta=\sum_aX_a^{\dagger}X_a$. A generator list is displayed at entries pairs over the
ground at the formal $i$, the remainder lists at $z^2+1$
(Definition~\ref{def:poly}): per place pair $p<q$ the swap
combination, entry one at $(p,q)$ with its balance partner at
$(q,p)$, and the $i$-weighted sum, entry $i$ at both places; per
consecutive place pair the diagonal combination, entry $i$ at the
place's diagonal with $i$'s balance partner at the successor's; each
anti-Hermitian by its shape, the list independent (the
off-diagonal families by their disjoint place pairs and
components, the diagonal telescope by its leading place), its
count at the join $2\tbinom{d_f}2+r+1=d_f^{\,2}$. The sums run
over the list against its
metric dual, $\sum_aX_a(\cdot)X^a(\cdot)$, pair data at the Gram's
adjugate against its determinant;
the orthonormal spelling is that sum's evaluation.

\end{definition}

\begin{construction}[The fusion interface]\label{con:fusion}
The calculus's outputs the chain reads are one interface, its
fields: the \emph{label data}, a set with its equality read,
involution and unit, each label equal to itself at that read; the \emph{count laws}, the fusion counts at commutativity,
associativity and the unit, with the unit read
$N^{\mathbf 1}_{ab}=\delta_{a\bar b}$ and the Cartan strictness
$N^{a+b}_{ab}=1$; the \emph{dimension identity}
$\sum_cN^c_{ab}\,d_c=d_a\,d_b$; the \emph{weight-free Casimir},
positive at every nonunit label, with its floor at the named
least labels, its dominance growth along a row, and the drift
identity; the \emph{self-dual $\theta$}, with the character's
two-sided form cap, its square's channel list at multiplicities,
dimensions and Casimirs, the base $c_1$, and $\theta$'s own
content list; the \emph{class data}, the vertex law's classes
over the root folds with the winding floors per class, the classes
a finite group at the fold's sum with the unit class its unit; the
\emph{magnetic list} $L$, a list of nonunit labels, its \emph{involution
closure} $\bar L$ the label set of its members with their duals,
the \emph{plaquette character} $\chi_L:=\sum_{\lambda\in\bar L}
\chi_\lambda$, the closure's characters' fold, involution-fixed by
the closure, and the list \emph{faithful} where its classes' folds
under the class group's sum reach every class, the adjoint's list
$\{\theta\}$ faithful at the unit class group alone; the
\emph{evaluation}, the unit-coefficient read with orthonormal
characters and the coefficient carrier's evaluation identity and
integration by parts; and
the \emph{presentation}, the evaluation's computation at stated
factor lists. A \emph{series} enters with one further tier: the
declared residue with every field a polynomial-pair read in it at
stated reach clearances, the banded families the fusion-closed
interiors with the $\theta$ content list among their data, and the
generic lift's discipline; a fixed member
enters at the member fields alone, its reads displayed finite
evaluations. The label calculus above instantiates every field,
each instantiating statement the field's own derivation, and a
further member's or series' instantiation is its own construction
of the field data, the chain reading the fields alone: the
classification's members each enter with every field a derived
read at their weight tables, their positive lists, alternants,
assembly, character identity, fusion rows, pairing spans and
defining tables the fields' own instantiations, the count and
involution fields at the member constructions
(Lemma~\ref{lem:memberdata}), the member's \emph{stated list} a
faithful magnetic list, the $A$-series' fundamental $f$, the $B$ series' spinor, the
$C$ series' first fundamental, the $D$ series' spinor at odd rank
and its vector beside the spinor at even rank, $E_6$'s $\omega_1$,
$E_7$'s $\omega_7$, and the member floor label at $G_2$, $F_4$ and
$E_8$, whose class group is the unit's, each list's classes
reaching every class at the member's class group, the classes the
remainder families of Construction~\ref{con:sertables} (two at $B$,
the spinor's odd parity generating; two at $C$, the first
fundamental's odd sum; four at $D$, the spinor of order four at odd
rank and the vector with the spinor the two generators of the
two-by-two group at even rank; three at $E_6$ at $\omega_1$'s
remainder one; two at $E_7$ at $\omega_7$'s occupied remainder), and
every chain derivation reads
the fusion data through the fields, at every member at once.
\end{construction}

\begin{construction}[The lattice interface]\label{con:lattice}
The carrier's region data are one interface, and every derivation
reads the lattice through its fields: a set of \emph{links} and a set
of \emph{vertices}, each link with one tail and one head, the
orientation the labels' duality read; the
\emph{plaquettes}, each boundary a cyclic word of four distinct
oriented links; \emph{simplicity}, two vertices sharing at most one link; the
\emph{even-cycle read}, every cycle's length even, a two-coloring of
the vertices its witness datum; the $d$ \emph{directions}, a
partition of the links with a transverse-cut family per direction,
each cut crossed by its own direction's links alone; the
\emph{boundary read}: a \emph{cycle} at coefficients in a finite
group $A$ (the class group of Construction~\ref{con:fusion}) is a
family over the links with the vertex law, each vertex's outgoing
coefficients' fold equal to its incoming coefficients', a
\emph{boundary fold} the fold of plaquette boundaries at
coefficients, each boundary's links at the coefficient and its
balance partner at the traversal signs, and the read is that every
cycle whose \emph{flux}, its fold over any transverse cut's crossing
links at the crossing signs, reads $A$'s unit at every cut is a
boundary fold, derived at a \emph{tree}: a link subset joining every
two vertices by one path, the count one below the vertices', an
off-tree link's \emph{fundamental cycle} the link closed by its
tree path, a cycle's off-tree coefficients naming its fold of
fundamental cycles with the gap a cycle inside the tree, the unit
family at the tree's one path per vertex pair, so the read is the
fundamental cycles' at the stated fluxes; the
\emph{translation action} on a
torus window, permuting links, vertices and plaquettes and preserving
directions, two shifts composing to the keys' one composite with
the directions' composites one map at either order; and the signed coordinate
permutations $B_d$, permuting the link and plaquette sets with
orientation reversal dualizing labels. The fields read at two
instantiation families. The region fields, the links, the vertices,
the plaquettes, simplicity, and the even-cycle read with its
two-coloring witness, are every carrier window's, the boxes of the
directed family; the direction data
with their transverse cuts read at both families. The translation
action and the signed coordinate permutations are the torus
family's, the windows of the momentum fibering: there a
contractible cycle's wrap count is even, so its length reads even
at the coordinate parity, while a winding cycle reads the side's
parity and is odd at odd side, so a torus is a carrier of the
interface's fields off the even-cycle read; the boundary read holds
at the box and at the torus: at the box the tree is the
\emph{comb}, the last direction's links off the last position
joined to the comb of the further directions at the first position,
one direction at a time, the tree path between two vertices
descending the directions' columns to the first positions in turn
and ascending, the two descents' shared segment withdrawn, and
every fundamental
cycle bounds its \emph{strip}, the plaquettes between the link and
the tree path: at an off-tree link in direction $i$ the strip is
the fold of the plaquettes of the $(i,j)$-planes along the two
descents' columns in the later directions $j$, one column per
direction at the link's transverse coordinates, joined to the
direction-$i$ segment's plaquettes at the first positions, each at
its traversal sign, the fold's boundary the fundamental cycle with
every interior link traversed twice at exchanged signs; so every
cycle is a boundary fold, the fluxes reading the unit outright; at
the torus the comb sits inside one box of the fundamental domain, a
box link's fundamental cycle its strip's boundary fold at the box's
read, a wrap link's fundamental cycle
crossing its direction's cut at the wrap position once and every
further cut at the sum's unit, so a cycle at unit fluxes reads its
wrap coefficients per direction folding to the unit, its wrap part
the fold of the differences of the direction's wrap cycles against
one of them, each difference the boundary fold of the strip between
the two wrap links, a boundary fold as well; the momentum fibering's
stated family is the odd tori at side five or beyond.
A \emph{label-graph isomorphism}
between two supports is a bijection of their links and vertices
preserving incidence, orientation and labels. The
dimension enters through the direction count alone, its reads (the
neighbor count $2d$, the per-link and per-vertex plaquette
counts, the per-direction momentum products, the
charged direction sums) polynomial in it: at the family's boxes at
two directions or beyond a link sits on at most $2(d-1)$
plaquettes, two in each plane through its direction, and a vertex
on at most $2d(d-1)$, four in each plane at the vertex, and at one
direction each sits on at most two, the consecutive squares sharing
one link.
\end{construction}

\begin{definition}[The carrier]\label{def:carrier}
The sector is an
indexed family with multiplicities, built from the fusion
interface's fields alone (Construction~\ref{con:fusion}). A
\emph{configuration} $a$ assigns a nonunit label to each link of its
\emph{support}, finitely many links at a natural count
(Construction~\ref{con:labels}); its \emph{content} is
$\sum_{\ell\in\mathrm{supp}\,a}C_2(a_\ell)$, positive at every
configuration; a vertex of $\mathrm{touched}(a)$, the support's
endpoints, is \emph{occupied} where the incident labels'
product, dualized on incoming links, reads an invariant count of at
least one, and
$a$ is \emph{occupied} where every touched vertex is. A
\emph{region} is a \emph{box}, the vertices at coordinates within
stated bounds in every direction with the links and plaquettes
among them (Construction~\ref{con:lattice}), the square window of
one side its equal-sided instance, the boxes directed
under inclusion, and every finite link set sits inside its
\emph{hull}, the least box holding it, its bounds the set's
coordinate extremes. The window
index is the occupied configurations at the region and the cutoff,
and the window is the unit's line with their fibers:
\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathrm{Idx}(\Lambda,C)=\Big\{a\ \text{occupied}\ \Big|\
\mathrm{supp}\,a\subseteq\Lambda,\
\sum_{\ell\in\mathrm{supp}\,a}C_2(a_\ell)\le C\Big\},\\
\mathrm{Sect}(\Lambda,C)=\mathbb P\,\mathbf 1\ \oplus
\bigoplus_{a\in\mathrm{Idx}(\Lambda,C)}\mathrm{Fib}(a),
\qquad
\mathrm{Fib}(a)=\bigotimes_{v\in\mathrm{touched}(a)}\mathrm{inv}(v,a),
\end{gathered}
\]
with
$\mathrm{inv}(v,a)$ the vertex's intertwiner space, the incident
labels' product's invariants at a stated independent spanning
list, incoming links dualized (Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}'s
collected reads at Definition~\ref{def:blockcount}'s count), and
$\mathrm{vmult}(v,a)$ its count, the vertex intertwiner
multiplicity, a natural at every occupied vertex. The
pairing is definitional as well: $\mathrm{gram}$ is the orthogonal direct sum
of the unit line's pairing at one and the fibers' own pairings,
per configuration the invariant lists' power pairing at the links'
cleared block scale, one factor $[\,1:d_{a_\ell}\,]$ per support
link: positive definiteness is by construction, the power pairing
a coordinate fold at positive scales. The windows are directed under
$(\Lambda,C)\le(\Lambda',C')$, the inclusions
$\mathrm{Sect}(\Lambda,C)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Sect}(\Lambda',C')$ are the
summand injections mapping the unit line and each fiber to
themselves, compatible under
composition, and the carrier is
their colimit
\[
\mathrm{Sect}_\infty\;=\;\varinjlim_{(\Lambda,C)}\ \mathrm{Sect}(\Lambda,C).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[A window is finite-dimensional, and its dimension is a
count]\label{prop:windowfinite}
For a region $\Lambda$ of finitely many links, the labels at
content at or below $C$ are finitely many,
$\mathrm{Idx}(\Lambda,C)$ is finite, each $\mathrm{Fib}(a)$ is
finite-dimensional, the dimension is one at the unit line alone,
and at an occupied index
\[
\dim\mathrm{Sect}(\Lambda,C)\;=\;1+\sum_{a\in\mathrm{Idx}(\Lambda,C)}
\ \prod_{v\in\mathrm{touched}(a)}\mathrm{vmult}(v,a)\ ,
\]
\emph{a count computed from the structure constants $N^c_{ab}$}, the vertex
multiplicity being $m\{a,b,c\}=N^{\bar c}_{ab}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}).
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
For dominant $\lambda$ the read $\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle$ is a fold
of natural products by its shape (Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}'s display), so
$C_2(\lambda)\ge\langle\lambda,\lambda\rangle$ and the labels of content at most
$C$ satisfy $\langle\lambda,\lambda\rangle\le C$: finitely many. At a
reduced shape, at most $r$ rows deep, the fold
$\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle$ reads at or beyond the degree, the last
place's pairs the rows' own reads, so $d_f\,Q(\lambda)$ clears
$d_f\,k$ (Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}) and an enumeration at a stated
cutoff on $d_f\,Q$ closes on the degrees whose $d_f$-multiple sits
at or below the cutoff, at most the cutoff's quotient at the count. A
configuration of $\mathrm{Idx}(\Lambda,C)$ assigns to the links of its
support, within $\Lambda$'s finitely many, labels from that finite
set, so
$\mathrm{Idx}(\Lambda,C)$ is finite; and the enumeration reads the
cutoff per link: a configuration's content is the fold over its
links' reads, each a natural, so a partial assignment's content
sits at or below every completion's and the enumeration refuses a
partial beyond the cutoff with every completion refused beside it,
the pruned walk and the whole product's filter one list; and the
enumeration reads two cutoffs as one list: the nonunit labels at
content at or below a cutoff are those at content at or below a
larger cutoff filtered at the smaller, in the larger enumeration's
order, so the index at the smaller cutoff is the index at the larger
filtered at content at or below the smaller, the product lists'
filter at the pointwise read, and Definition~\ref{def:carrier}'s
inclusion of the window into the larger one reads at the window
list's own positions. Each $\mathrm{vmult}(v,a)$ is a
natural at an occupied configuration
and the product defining $\mathrm{Fib}(a)$ has finitely many factors, so
$\mathrm{Fib}(a)$ is finite-dimensional and the displayed sum is a finite sum of
finite products of structure-constant reads. Both indices are needed: the
content bound alone leaves a loop free to sit at every translate, all at one
content, so the region is what makes the count finite.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Fusion rows lie in content balls]\label{prop:fusionfinite}
Every constituent of $a\otimes b$ has
highest weight below the Cartan product $a+b$ in the dominance order, and
$\hat c_2$ (Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}) is increasing there (at
$\mu\preceq\lambda$ dominant,
$C_2(\mu)+\sum_k\delta_k\,h_k=C_2(\lambda)$ at the dominance order's
prefix gaps $\delta_k$ and the gaps $h_k$ of the sorted list
$\lambda+\mu+2u$ at $u$ the unit set's sorted display
(Construction~\ref{con:places})), so
\[
\hat c_2(c)\ \le\ \hat c_2(a+b)\ =\ \hat c_2(a)+\hat c_2(b)
+\big[\,2d_f\,\langle a,b\rangle:2d_f^{\,2}\,\big]
\qquad\text{for every nonunit member }c\text{ of the row},
\]
the unit member, one exactly at $b=\bar a$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}), the Casimir's kernel point, inside
every content ball outright,
the cross term twice the bilinear read
($C_2(a+b)=C_2(a)+C_2(b)+2\langle a,b\rangle$).
So a fusion row lies in a content ball, and content balls are finite,
the labels at weight-free Casimir at or below a stated pair finitely
many (Proposition~\ref{prop:windowfinite}).
The \emph{attained maximum} $\Phi(C,C')$ at two contents is the
largest content of a product of two configurations at contents at or
below $C$ and $C'$: over two label lists at a shared link count at or
below the two link caps' sum, the caps $L$ at $L\,\hat c_2(f)\le C$
and $L'$ at $L'\,\hat c_2(f)\le C'$ at the member's floor
$\hat c_2(f)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}), each
list's labels in its content's ball with its fold at or below its
content, and over every shared link's fusion target at the two labels,
a label one list leaves vacant kept at the other's and a link vacant
in both lists reading the unit label, the targets'
contents' fold, one trichotomy fold over finitely many reads. This bound and $\Phi$ do different jobs: the bound
makes the row a finite set, while $\Phi$ is the \emph{attained} maximum over it,
and the window index uses $\Phi$, since a bound composed from the two
contents' root sum forces a rounding whose composition depends on the order
taken.
\begin{proof}
A constituent's top content is a content of the product, contents of a
tensor product add over the factors, and a block's contents sit at or
below its top (Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}). In the displayed identity every
summand is two naturals' product, so $C_2$ and $\hat c_2$ rise along
the dominance order. In the display
$d_f\,\langle a,b\rangle$ is the weight lattice's integer read, every term
one form read against itself, the pair at one value across the
form's scales
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}; Proposition~\ref{prop:form}). The
labels at Casimir at or below a stated pair are finitely many
(Proposition~\ref{prop:windowfinite}); a configuration at content
at or below $C$ holds at most $L$ links at $L\,\hat c_2(f)\le C$,
every occupied link's read at or beyond the floor
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}), so a shared link count at or below the
caps' sum holds every pair of configurations with their vacant
links padded, the label lists at each count are finitely many, each
shared link's row finite by the ball, and the fold's values finitely
many, the largest at the trichotomy fold.
\end{proof}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Every element has a least window, read off its index
support]\label{prop:leastwindow}
An
$A\in\mathrm{Sect}_\infty$ is represented by some $x\in\mathrm{Sect}(\Lambda,C)$,
a unit coordinate with its family of fiber components over the
index. The \emph{index support}
$\mathrm{ix}(A)$, the member configurations, is representative-free;
the unit coordinate is at home in every
window, multiplying as the scalar it is, every window its own. An
element whose index support has members reads its window data over
them:
\[
\Lambda_A=\text{the hull of}\ \bigcup_{a\in\mathrm{ix}(A)}\mathrm{supp}\,a ,
\qquad
C_A=\max_{a\in\mathrm{ix}(A)}\mathrm{content}(a)
\]
are one value at every representative (Definition~\ref{def:carrier}'s
hull), and
$\mathrm{supp}(A)=(\Lambda_A,C_A)$ is the least window whose
image contains $A$'s components. Both are \emph{counts off the index}: the links the element
occupies and its members' largest content.
A probe is an element of the
carrier, and its window is this one.
\begin{proof}
The index support is representative-free because the
inclusions are summand injections and map the unit line and each
component to themselves, so two representatives read one member
family and the window data, reads of that family, one value.
\end{proof}
\end{proposition}

\begin{definition}[The product and the involution]\label{def:algebra}
$\mathrm{Sect}_\infty$ is a unital $\ast$-algebra. A factor of the
unit coordinate alone multiplies as its scalar, every window its
own (Proposition~\ref{prop:leastwindow}); at $A$ and $u$ whose
index supports have members, at the least windows
$\mathrm{supp}(A)=(\Lambda_A,C_A)$ and
$\mathrm{supp}(u)=(\Lambda_u,C_u)$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:leastwindow}), the \emph{target window} is
$\mathrm{Sect}_0:=\mathrm{Sect}\big(\Lambda_A\vee\Lambda_u,\
\Phi(C_A,C_u)\big)$ at the boxes' hull, its \emph{window list} the unit line's vector
with the fibers' stated lists, the pairing's Gram of
unequal-membered determinant at the lists' independence
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}; Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}), and the
product $A\cdot u$ is the
target window's element at the reads
\[
\mathrm{gram}\big(A\cdot u,\;v\big)\;=\;\mathrm{Eval}\big(\bar A\,\bar u\,v\big)
\qquad\text{at every window-list member }v ,
\]
the element the reads' solve, the adjugate column against the
Gram's determinant (Definition~\ref{def:elim}), one finite ground
computation per read, the right side the \emph{unit read}: $\mathrm{Eval}$ reads its
argument's unit coordinate in the label index
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}), a finite ground computation at
the product's exhaustion, the unit block's component
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(i)), at a loop window the invariant
count's own read (Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}). Its matrix elements between
summands, $\mathrm{gram}(x,A\cdot y)$ for $x,y$ window-list members,
are the label-index reads
of Proposition~\ref{prop:repring} on the changed edge alone, and the
magnetic form is built from them. The involution is contour reversal, descending from the words' own
involution, $\mathrm{Eval}$ one value under it.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[The product reads the pairing identity, and the algebra laws
are structure-constant identities]\label{prop:algebra}
The product of Definition~\ref{def:algebra} reads the pairing
identity against every element,
$\mathrm{gram}_\infty(A\cdot u,\,v)=\mathrm{Eval}(\bar A\,\bar u\,v)$
at every $v$, at the colimit pairing $\mathrm{gram}_\infty$, two
elements' read at a shared window, one value at every window; it is
the target window's one element at that identity, and every window
at or beyond the target window solves the identity to it; the product of two window elements
sits in a window, the \emph{window bound} stated on the index alone,
\[
A\cdot\mathrm{Sect}(\Lambda,C)\ \subseteq\
\mathrm{Sect}\big(\Lambda_A\vee\Lambda,\ \Phi(C_A,C)\big),
\]
$\Lambda_A\vee\Lambda$ the hull of the two boxes' union and $\Phi$
the attained maximum (Proposition~\ref{prop:fusionfinite}); and in the colimit commutativity, associativity and the unit
are the identities
\[
N^c_{ab}=N^c_{ba},\qquad
\sum_eN^e_{ab}N^d_{ec}=\sum_fN^f_{bc}N^d_{af},\qquad
N^c_{a\mathbf 1}=\delta_{ac} .
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Take $A$ and $u$ whose index supports have members, with
$\mathrm{Sect}_0=\mathrm{Sect}\big(\Lambda_A\vee\Lambda_u,\ \Phi(C_A,C_u)\big)$
the target window of Definition~\ref{def:algebra} at the least
windows (Proposition~\ref{prop:leastwindow}); a factor of the unit
coordinate alone multiplies as its scalar, its identity the
scalar's read. The window bound: at $u\in\mathrm{Sect}(\Lambda,C)$
the least window sits at $\Lambda_u\subseteq\Lambda$ and $C_u\le C$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:leastwindow}), so the target window's box
sits inside $\Lambda_A\vee\Lambda$ and its content
$\Phi(C_A,C_u)$ at or below $\Phi(C_A,C)$, the attained maximum
nondecreasing in each argument, the larger content's lists holding
the smaller's (Proposition~\ref{prop:fusionfinite}); the product,
the target window's element, sits in the displayed window.

\emph{The functional reads equal members off $\mathrm{Sect}_0$.} $\mathrm{Eval}$ reads the unit
coordinate, so
$\mathrm{Eval}(\bar A\bar uv)$ is of equal members unless the labels of $v$ occur among the
constituents of $\bar A$'s against $\bar u$'s, dual labels at one
link set and one content each (Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}). Those constituents sit on the links
of $\Lambda_A\vee\Lambda_u$ and, by Proposition~\ref{prop:fusionfinite}, at
content at most $\Phi(C_A,C_u)$: they are summands of $\mathrm{Sect}_0$. So
$v\mapsto\mathrm{Eval}(\bar A\bar uv)$ is of equal members on every summand beyond $\mathrm{Sect}_0$.

\emph{On $\mathrm{Sect}_0$ the identity is the definition's solved read.} $\mathrm{Sect}_0$ is
finite-dimensional (Proposition~\ref{prop:windowfinite}) and its window list is
independent with its pairing Gram of unequal-membered determinant
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}; Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}), so
the identity's reads against the list solve the one
$x\in \mathrm{Sect}_0$ with
$\mathrm{gram}(x,v)=\mathrm{Eval}(\bar A\bar uv)$ at every $v\in \mathrm{Sect}_0$, the adjugate
column against the determinant
(Lemma~\ref{lem:genericlift}(ii); Definition~\ref{def:elim}); two
stated lists spanning $\mathrm{Sect}_0$ solve one element, each
solution reading the identity against the other's members, the
solutions' gap at equal members against every member with its
self-pairing that unit at the positive pairing, so
a presentation's wiring list reads the determination at its own
Gram. For $v$ in any larger window, $\mathrm{gram}(x,v)$ reads
only $v$'s $\mathrm{Sect}_0$-summands, $\mathrm{gram}$ being the orthogonal direct sum, and
both sides are of equal members off $\mathrm{Sect}_0$ as above. So the product reads the
identity against every $v$; a window at or beyond the target reads
the identity at its own list to one further solved element, each
reading the identity against every $v$, the two agreeing against
every element, one element at the positive pairing on the larger
window; and the product sits in $\mathrm{Sect}_0$ and descends to
the colimit.

\emph{The laws.} $\mathrm{Sect}_\infty$'s elements are character polynomials
and $\mathrm{Eval}$ reads their product's unit coefficient, so the product
just constructed is the character polynomials' own, commutative and
associative with the unit label as its unit. Read in the label index those three statements are
the displayed identities on $N$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}). The pairing and the link Laplacians are
compatible with the summand injections, so they descend to $\mathrm{Sect}_\infty$
and restrict to every window: a pairing of two colimit elements is read at any
common window, one value at every window.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Matrix elements are reads at the support's reach]
\label{lem:stableentries}
Let $x,y$ be elements of a window with joint support
$S:=\Lambda_x\cup\Lambda_y$. Then $\mathrm{gram}(x,y)$ and
$\langle x,Ey\rangle$ read the index data on $S$ alone, and the magnetic
row reads only the plaquettes meeting $S$'s vertex neighborhood: at
$\partial p$ sharing a vertex with $S$, the entry
$\langle x,\chi_L(U_{\partial p})\,y\rangle$ at the plaquette
character (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}) is the changed-edge read
of Definition~\ref{def:algebra} at the labels incident to $p$; at
$\partial p$ off that neighborhood it factorizes,
\[
\langle x,\chi_L(U_{\partial p})\,y\rangle
=\mathrm{Eval}(\bar xy)\cdot\mathrm{Eval}(\chi_L),
\qquad
\mathrm{Eval}(\chi_L)=\sum_{\lambda\in\bar L}\delta_{\lambda\mathbf 1}
\quad(\text{Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}}) ,
\]
the fold of equal members at the list's nonunit members
(Construction~\ref{con:fusion}).
Consequently a label-graph isomorphism of the supports' vertex
neighborhoods transports every pairing, electric and magnetic read across
windows: each entry is one polynomial-pair read in the residue, window-free
once a window's region
contains the neighborhood. The \emph{locality band} is that reach,
the plaquette neighborhood's: a magnetic row's entries off it are
the factorized reads at the unit character, the sum's unit, so
every pencil row reads within one band of its support, at every
window.
\begin{proof}
$\mathrm{gram}$ is the orthogonal sum of the fibers' pairings at matched
configurations and $E$ scales each summand by its content, both index
reads on $S$ (Definitions~\ref{def:carrier},~\ref{def:pencil}); the
product $\bar xy$ is supported on $S$ at bounded content
(Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}). For the factorization: two elements
on disjoint links and vertices have $\mathrm{Fib}$ data at disjoint
vertex sets and label data at disjoint links, so the product's index
summand at $(a,b)$ is the concatenation of the two summands, each
vertex's $\mathrm{vmult}$ reading its own incident labels; a concatenation
occupies a link exactly where a part does, so the
product's unit coordinate is the unit coordinates' product,
and $\mathrm{Eval}(\chi_L)$, a fold of Kronecker deltas at two
labels each at a nonunit member (Construction~\ref{con:fusion}), is
of equal members, the far plaquette's term with it. The near case is Definition~\ref{def:algebra}'s read, a
fusion computation at the labels incident to $p$.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{construction}[The coefficient carrier]\label{con:coeff}
The carrier's vertex-free companion drops the invariance constraint: per
link the \emph{coefficient family}
$\bigoplus_\lambda W_\lambda\otimes W_\lambda^\vee$, one block per label
(Construction~\ref{con:labels}; the blocks and duals of
Lemmas~\ref{lem:blockirr},~\ref{lem:dualread}),
per window the tensor product of its links' families over the window index
of Definition~\ref{def:carrier}, the involution the blocks' dual
exchange with the unit block fixed.
$\mathrm{Eval}$ extends as the per-link unit coefficient: a product of
coefficient elements decomposes by the fusion data, and its unit
coefficient is the invariant line's read on both data, the vector
datum's component at the orthogonal split
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(i); Lemma~\ref{lem:orthsplit}) against the
functional datum's value on the line, the component the projection
fold's read at the line's member (Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}).  Two
one-block elements pair at the \emph{block orthogonality},
\[
d_\lambda\,\mathrm{Eval}\big(\,\overline{u\otimes f}\ (u'\otimes f')\,\big)
\;=\;\langle u,u'\rangle\,\langle f,f'\rangle\ ,
\]
the product a coefficient of the dual block against the block, its
unit channel one line (Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}'s unit read;
Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}(ii),(iii)) at the coevaluation's tensor, and

of coefficient vectors' Gram is positive semidefinite

T^{\dagger}T\;=\;\eta^{2}\,X_a^{\dagger}X_a+G^{2}
+\big\langle\,\eta\,(X_aG)\,\big\rangle^{\!\vee}\ ,

\begin{definition}[The electric and magnetic operators, and the pencil]
\label{def:pencil}
$E$ is the electric operator, diagonal in the label index, scaling
a configuration's summand by its content and reading the unit line
as its kernel, so $E$ is positive semidefinite, every content positive
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier});
$\Delta_\ell$ is its per-link summand, scaling by $C_2(a_\ell)$, so
$E=\sum_\ell\Delta_\ell$; $M$ is the plaquette multiplication
$\sum_p\chi_L(U_{\partial p})$ at the magnetic list's plaquette
character (Construction~\ref{con:fusion}), the fold over the list's
involution closure $\bar L$ of the labels' characters,
involution-fixed, at the member's stated list where a statement
names one and at every magnetic list otherwise, the sum over
the region's plaquettes, $\#p$ their count; $\chi_p$ abbreviates the
plaquette's term $\chi_L(U_{\partial p})$. The \emph{pencil} is the family
of form pairs $(\alpha E:\beta M)$ with $H$ their site datum at the
join
\[
\alpha\,E\;=\;\beta\,M+H\big([\alpha\!:\!\beta]\big) ,\qquad
\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N
\]
over the end-weight pairs of
Proposition~\ref{prop:segment} with the two ends' one-member
instances, an end's pair reading its one member alone, the contact
end's datum the magnetic member's balance partner. On a window
list with positive-definite Gram $G$ (Definition~\ref{def:carrier}),
the symmetric matrices $E$, $M$ and $H$ are
forms; their actions $\mathsf E$, $\mathsf M$ and $K$ are the
Gram solves
\[
G\mathsf E=E,\qquad G\mathsf M=M,\qquad GK=H,
\qquad \alpha\mathsf E=\beta\mathsf M+K.
\]
Each column is the Gram's adjugate applied to the form's column
against $\det G$, the solved witness of Definition~\ref{def:elim}.
The ground level $\varepsilon_0$ is the least located root of the
pencil (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}). Its \emph{level-gap form} is the
site datum $S$ at $\varepsilon_0G+S=H$, positive semidefinite;
its \emph{level-gap action} is $D$ at the Gram solve $GD=S$.
Thus $K=\varepsilon_0 I+D$. A window ground $\psi$ reads
$H\psi=\varepsilon_0G\psi$, $K\psi=\varepsilon_0\psi$ and
$D\psi=S\psi=0$, the last glyph the sum's unit; every read at a
window ground quantifies over the grounds.
On these coordinates the pairing is $\langle x,y\rangle_G:=x^{\mathsf T}Gy$.
A map $A$ from a list of Gram $G$ to a list of Gram $G'$ has its
pairing adjoint at the solve $GA^\dagger=A^{\mathsf T}G'$.
Its squared-action form is $A^{\mathsf T}G'A$.
In particular,
\begin{gather*}
D^{\mathsf T}G=S,\qquad
SD=D^{\mathsf T}GD,\\
\mu_1(v)=v^{\mathsf T}Sv=\langle v,Dv\rangle_G,\qquad
\mu_2(v)=v^{\mathsf T}SDv=\langle Dv,Dv\rangle_G.
\end{gather*}
The first identity is the transpose of $GD=S$ at $S$ symmetric;
the further identities are its products. A form's restriction to
columns $L$ is $L^{\mathsf T}FL$, with the pairing restricted to
$L^{\mathsf T}GL$. At a unit Gram the form and its action read
one matrix. The state reads actions, $\omega(A)=\langle\psi,A\psi\rangle_G$;
an observable's form $F$ reads $\psi^{\mathsf T}F\psi$.
At a positive pair $h$ and an orthogonal two-block list,
$G=G_1\oplus G_2$, write
$D_{ij}$ for the action blocks. Block multiplication of
$SD=D^{\mathsf T}GD$ gives the whole detector's second block,
\[
(SD-hS)_{22}
=D_{12}^{\mathsf T}G_1D_{12}
+D_{22}^{\mathsf T}G_2D_{22}-hG_2D_{22}.
\]
The first summand is the positive Gram of the action's image
in the first block, and $S_{22}=G_2D_{22}$ is the restricted
first-moment form.
At two nested cutoffs in one region, write $J$ for the
smaller list's inclusion and $J_\perp$ for its orthogonal
complement, with $G=J^{\mathsf T}G'J$ and
$G_\perp=J_\perp^{\mathsf T}G'J_\perp$.
Let $e',D',S'$ be the larger window's data and $e,D,S$
the smaller's, with the gap $\delta\ge0$ at $e'+\delta=e$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). Then
\[
J^\dagger D'J=D+\delta I,\qquad
B:=J_\perp^\dagger D'J,
\]
and inserting the two orthogonal projections into the square gives
\[
J^{\mathsf T}(S'D'-hS')J
=SD-hS+2\delta S+\delta(\delta-h)G+B^{\mathsf T}G_\perp B.
\]
The exterior image's Gram and the ground's shift enter the
whole-square compression at these displayed terms.
The \emph{ground-relative level read} at an offset $a$ is
\[
\operatorname{rev}(S:aG)
\;=\;\operatorname{rev}\big(H:(\varepsilon_0+a)G\big).
\]
The site datum $R$ at $S=aG+R$ reads
$H=(\varepsilon_0+a)G+R$ at the ground's join, so the two
counts read one matrix and one split. At positive offsets
$\ell<h$, with $\ell+w=h$, the two absolute lines are
$\varepsilon_0+\ell$ and $\varepsilon_0+h$, and their gap is
$w$ at the displayed sum's associativity and injectivity.
The ground is the window's least located root, with its
designation read at that window and coupling; the offsets are
the fixed data in a statement over windows. The unit vector's
electric form reads the sum's unit and its magnetic form reads
$\mathrm{Eval}(\chi_L)$ per plaquette, the fold of the nonunit
labels' unit coefficients (Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}), so
the unit vector's pencil form reads the sum's unit and the least
root sits at or below it (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}).
The gap chain reads a
coupling in its \emph{root coordinate}: the weights
$[\,q^2:p^2\,]$ at the pair $\tau=[\,p:q\,]$, $q\,\tau=p$ the
cross-multiplied tie, a cell's reads taken at pair $\tau$, the
pair-$\tau$ rays the coordinate's own points; toward the contact end the dual coordinate weights the couplings
$[\,\sigma:1\,]$ at pair $\sigma$. The \emph{word sector} is
$\mathrm{Sect}_\infty\,\psi$, the image of multiplication by $\psi$
(Definition~\ref{def:algebra}).
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[The base is a closed segment]\label{prop:segment}
A coupling is an \emph{end-weight pair} $[\alpha\!:\!\beta]$ at
$\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N$, taken up to rescaling: $\alpha$ weights
the free end's electric member $E$ and $\beta$ the contact end's
magnetic member $M$,
the coupling pencil the pair $(\alpha E:\beta M)$'s site datum at
the displayed join. The base
$\mathcal C$ is the couplings with the two \emph{ends}, the
one-member weightings: the \emph{free end}, the electric member
alone, $H=E$ there, and the \emph{contact end}, the magnetic
alone, $H$ the member's balance partner. Every coupling pair is interior,
both weights present by the shape of its data, and the base is the
closed segment, the free and the contact end its two endpoints. A spectral quantity of the
pencil homogeneous of degree one scales by one factor along a ray,
so the pair of two such reads is one value on the ray, the
homogeneity principle's read (Definition~\ref{def:ground}), and
descends to $\mathcal C$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The pair's site datum is additive over its members and degree-one
in each weight by the join's shape, so
rescaling the weights by a natural $u$ rescales the pencil by $u$,
and scaling an operator by $u$ scales its spectrum by $u$: a
degree-one spectral quantity acquires that one factor, so both
components of a pair of two such reads acquire it and the pair
reads one value across the ray, the homogeneity principle's
read, every rescaling a ground rescaling and so
order-preserving by the type. The weight data up to that rescaling
are the two-member rays and the two one-member classes: the
segment's interior and its two ends.
\end{proof}

\section{The statement}

Write $r$ for the member's derived residue, the pairing's own fold
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}; Proposition~\ref{prop:anchor}),
the $A$-series' declared scalar its instance with the successor
name the fundamental count $d_f=r+1$
(Construction~\ref{con:places}), $\mathcal C$ for the
closed segment of Proposition~\ref{prop:segment}, $E_0$ for the free-end
level (Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}), and $\mathcal K$ for the invariant
(Definition~\ref{def:K}).

\begin{proposition}[The free end's level is the floor loop]\label{prop:E0}
At the free end the \emph{floor loop}, a member floor label $f_0$,
a nonunit label of the least weight-free Casimir
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}, $f$ at the $A$-series), around one
plaquette's boundary, is an eigenvector of the pencil at the least
occupied content, the \emph{free-end level}
\[
E_0\;:=\;4\,\hat c_2(f_0)\ ,
\]
$[\,2r(r+2):d_f^{\,2}\,]$ at the $A$-series, at every member and on
either carrier, positive by its shape.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
At the free end the pencil is its electric member $E$ alone
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}; Proposition~\ref{prop:segment}), and
$E$ is diagonal in the label index, scaling the summand at $a$ by
$\mathrm{content}(a)=\sum_\ell C_2(a_\ell)$ (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}). In
that index the floor loop is the configuration assigning $f_0$ to
each link of $\partial p$ at the traversal's orientation, occupied
at every corner, one outgoing $f_0$ against one incoming at
$\mathrm{vmult}=N^{\mathbf 1}_{f_0\bar f_0}=1$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}; Definition~\ref{def:carrier},
incoming links dualized), so it is an eigenvector of $E$ with
eigenvalue its content, the fold over $\partial p$'s four links
(Construction~\ref{con:lattice}), $4\,C_2(f_0)$, read against
$C_2(\mathrm{adj})$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:form}) the display. It
is the least occupied content: at an occupied configuration every
touched vertex reads an invariant count of at least one
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}); at a vertex meeting exactly one
support link an invariant line would be an equivariant line between
the unit block and a nonunit one, and an equivariant line forces one
label (Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}; Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}(iii)),
against the support's nonunit datum, so the support's links meet
each of their vertices at least twice; a finite graph of minimum
degree two holds a cycle (a forest has a leaf), every cycle is even
and at least four, the graph simple (the even-cycle and simplicity
reads of Construction~\ref{con:lattice}); and each occupied link
reads content at or beyond the member floor
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}): every occupied content sits at or beyond
four times the floor, the floor loop's own. On the coefficient
carrier the floor loop is the $f_0$-blocks' coefficient at the
boundary's four links, each link's $\Delta_\ell$ scaling its block
at $C_2(f_0)$ (a matrix coefficient of $\lambda$ differentiates
to one, Construction~\ref{con:coeff}) with every further link's
summand at the sum's unit, so the eigen-read is the four-link fold
there as well, one value on either carrier.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The free end reads the invariant at one]
\label{lem:freeend}
At the free end the window cut of Definition~\ref{def:K} is a diagonal read, and
\[
\mathcal K\;=\;1
\qquad\text{at the free end},
\]
at every member, with one admitted by every finite-window cut
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}; Definition~\ref{def:K}), the level the
free-end level $E_0$ itself (Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}).
\begin{proof}
At the free end the pencil is its electric member $E$ alone,
diagonal in the label index with the
contents as eigenvalues (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}). Every
configuration's content is positive
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}), so the ground is the unit's line,
$\psi$ the algebra's unit
(Definition~\ref{def:algebra}) and $E$'s kernel point
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), the floor of equal members there and the
level-gap form reading $S=E$ and its action $D=\mathsf E$, and
the word sector is the window itself.
The cut's pair $(SD:E_0\kappa S)$ is block diagonal, the
unit summand its kernel's and each configuration's block its
Gram at the multiple $c\,\langle c:E_0\kappa\rangle$,
$c$ the configuration's content: the cut
at $\kappa$ holds exactly where every occupied configuration's
content is at least $E_0\kappa$. Every occupied content sits at or
beyond $E_0$, the floor loop's content, and the floor loop attains it
(Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}), so the cut holds at every $\kappa$ at
or below one. In a region containing the floor plaquette,
every cutoff at or beyond $E_0$ holds its loop and refuses a
floor beyond one, the floor loop's entry
$E_0\,\langle E_0:E_0\kappa\rangle$ on its lower side there: the
contents are window-free data, so the read is one diagonal
computation at every window. Every window cut admits one,
and a window holding the floor loop refuses every pair beyond
one. Their meet therefore has edge one and admits it
(Definition~\ref{def:K}).
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[The invariant]\label{def:K}
$\mathcal K$ is the pencil's level read against the free-end level $E_0$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}, given by its window cuts: at a coupling $v$, a
window $\Lambda$ and a pair $\kappa=[\,p:q\,]$,
\[
\mathcal K_\Lambda(v)\ \ge\ \kappa
\qquad\textbf{is}\qquad
\big(q\,SD\big)_\Lambda
:\big(E_0\,p\,S\big)_\Lambda
\ \text{ positive semidefinite},
\]
the pair clearing its pencil to integer coefficients, a
positive rescaling fixing the count (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}),
with $S$ the level-gap form and $D$ its action from the Gram solve
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), read on the word sector
(Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}), and $(\cdot)_\Lambda$ the compression to the
window's word sector, taken of the detector form whole: the count reads the square's compression, a compression keeping the
positive-semidefinite read (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). The display
quantifies over the window grounds (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}),
the ground freedom's quotient read: at a ground the compression is
the detector pair's pullback along word images spanning the
sector, a spanning list by elimination (Definition~\ref{def:elim}),
a combination reading its image vector's pair and a kernel
combination reading the sum's unit, so the pulled-back pair is
positive semidefinite exactly with the pair on the word sector,
its entries quadratic in the ground's coordinates over the located
stage (Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}, the kernel's spanning list
Lemma~\ref{lem:split}'s), one reversal count per ground, exact by
$\mathrm{LDL}^{\mathsf T}$ there (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia};
Corollary~\ref{cor:momentdivisor}), settled by integers; a ground
line reads one count, the pullback quadratic's scale the
homogeneity principle's read (Definition~\ref{def:ground};
Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}); a kernel of one line reads its quotient
at a point, and a deeper kernel indexes the display over its
ground space, the window pair's read covering every member at
once; and the window pair, the detector form whole, reads every
ground at once, a compression keeping the read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), the spectral read fixed at
Theorem~\ref{thm:levelequiv}. Each window cut is available at every point of the
\emph{closed} segment: a window compression is finite-dimensional
(Proposition~\ref{prop:windowfinite}), so a least eigenvalue and an
exact reversal count exist at either end and at every coupling ray, an
end's pencil its one member's own
(Proposition~\ref{prop:segment}). For a fixed region $\Lambda$, write
$\mathcal K_{\Lambda,C}(v)$ for this finite cut at total cutoff
$C$. The cut of $\mathcal K(v)$ is the meet over every region
and every cutoff of Definition~\ref{def:carrier}:
\[
\mathcal K(v)\ge\kappa
\qquad\text{is}\qquad
\mathcal K_{\Lambda,C}(v)\ge\kappa
\quad\text{at every region }\Lambda\text{ and every cutoff }C.
\]
Every finite read uses that window's ground and whole detector.
The \emph{regional cut} $\mathcal K^{\mathrm{reg}}_\Lambda(v)$
reads at every positive strict subfloor: its membership at
$\kappa$ requires, for every positive pair $\kappa'<\kappa$,
a constructed cutoff key $C_0(\Lambda,v,\kappa')$ and the
finite-window read
\[
\mathcal K_{\Lambda,C}(v)\ge\kappa'
\qquad\text{at every }C\ge C_0(\Lambda,v,\kappa').
\]
The key and the splits at a stated cutoff are certificate
data; the assertion at every further cutoff is the theorem
at that cutoff, each test the finite read above. A floor
holding at every cutoff from one constructed key gives its
regional membership by the downward read. Every member of
$\mathcal K(v)$ belongs to every regional cut: the finite
reads at every cutoff give every strict subfloor's reads
from the cutoff key one.
Each cut is downward closed, the window read weakening as
its positive level falls and the regional read using the
strict subfloors' keys. A member pair is the positivity
read, every pair positive by its shape. A value of a cut
is its located edge where one is named. Each finite-window
upper cap caps the global edge, the meet's members admitted
by that window. A regional upper
cap is a cap at every cutoff beyond a constructed key.
It caps the global edge through the finite-window cap at
the key itself.

\emph{Two scalings, and which one each clause reads.} Moving along a ray,
$[\alpha\!:\!\beta]\mapsto[\,t\alpha\!:\!t\beta\,]$, is the freedom the
pair reads through, one value on the ray
(Proposition~\ref{prop:segment}); rescaling the family, $E\mapsto uE$ and
$M\mapsto uM$, is a second freedom, and a level of the pencil is degree one in
each. $\mathcal K(v)$ takes $E_0$ at
the free end against the level at $v$, so it is free of the second and
degree one in the first: its \emph{side} is a property of the ray, and
its value at a window reads at the coupling's stated pair.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
Let the member run over the classification's stated domain, each
member once: the $A$-series at the declared residue $r\ge1$
(Construction~\ref{con:places}), and $B_\ell$ at $\ell\ge2$,
$C_\ell$ at $\ell\ge3$, $D_\ell$ at $\ell\ge4$ and the five fixed
members at their weight tables
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), the index floors reading each
member once with the low-index coincidences the classification's
own identifications; let the magnetic list be the member's stated
list, faithful (Construction~\ref{con:fusion}); let $r$ be the
member's derived residue, $d\in\mathbb N$ the direction count
(Construction~\ref{con:lattice}), and $[\,\alpha:\beta\,]$ the
coupling's end-weight pair at $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N$, interior
by the shape of its data
(Proposition~\ref{prop:segment}). Then:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,itemsep=2pt]
\item a pair is a member of the cut of
      $\mathcal K\big([\,\alpha:\beta\,]\big)$, positive by its
      shape; and
\item at every window and every coupling of the closed segment
      whose cut names an edge, the edge is the compressed pair's
      least root, a located root of the window pencil's symbol
      (Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(i); Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}),
      attained at a word image
      with the two moments at equality and the first positive
      (Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(i),(ii)); and
\item every continuum datum, a finite list of supports, separations
      and Euclidean pairs at pair coordinates against the corner
      scale, reads at the chain's height: at every scale the height
      is located between the ray's cut member of clause (i) and its
      caps, every probe's two moments' read at any window and the
      two-member cap line at a simple ground, the spacing that
      height's read under the
      unit map, and at two directions or beyond the spacing falls
      under every floor beyond the floor's key
      (Theorem~\ref{thm:continuum}(iii)); and each
      cell's window cut's edge, where one is
      named, is the compressed pair's least root read at a word
      image at the corner scale
      (Theorem~\ref{thm:continuum}; Lemma~\ref{lem:corner};
      Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerfloor}; Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerkey};
      Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerpivot}; Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(i),(ii)).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Clause (i) is Theorem~\ref{thm:gappos} at the cells' closed union,
the root coordinate's located segment from the free end to the
validity top: the cells' reads at the root coordinate's rays, the
counting sandwich of its clause (v) at every further end-weight
ray of the union, the cutoffs reaching the cut within
Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}'s priced modulus at the unit electric
representative. Clause (ii) is Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}: the
window cuts' edges located roots of their symbols read at word
images (Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}). Clause (iii) is
Theorem~\ref{thm:continuum}: the located brackets, the scale
closure, and the chain's height located at every scale between
the cut's member and its caps with its fall beyond the floor's
key at two directions or beyond (Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerfloor};
Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerkey}), the cells' edges read at word images
(Lemma~\ref{lem:corner}).
\end{proof}

Clause (i) is a count of $\mathcal K$'s cut (Definition~\ref{def:K})
and clause (ii) a located root at a word image; each is weight-free,
one value at every form point (Proposition~\ref{prop:form}), the
cut's level read against the free-end level. Clause (iii)'s located
values are the family's continuum reads, the spacing among
its outputs (Theorem~\ref{thm:continuum}); and the
state's space is the word sector's own
(Lemma~\ref{lem:statespace}). Remark~\ref{rem:dictionary}
records the correspondence between these objects and their usual names.

\begin{theorem}[The vacuum sector's cut at every magnetic list]\label{thm:sector}
Let the member, the residue and the direction count run as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, and let the magnetic list be any
involution-closed list of nonunit labels
(Construction~\ref{con:fusion}), the pencil at its plaquette
character (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}); let the \emph{vacuum
sector} be the unit label's fusion closure at every window
(Construction~\ref{con:depthchain}) and the sector's cut
Definition~\ref{def:K}'s read at the detector pair compressed to
the sector's word images, the sector's own ground its kernel point
(Lemma~\ref{lem:sectorspan}). Then at every interior end-weight
ray a pair is a member of the sector's cut, positive by its shape,
the cell list's reads at the sector's depth chain
(Theorem~\ref{thm:gappos}(vi)); at a faithful list the sector's cut
is the unit charge's part of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}(i), the
sectors the charges (Construction~\ref{con:depthchain}); and at
the adjoint list $\{\theta\}$ the sector is the adjoint walk
(Construction~\ref{con:xfusion}), whose one-plaquette sector
compresses to the tower at every residue and is the tower itself
at the residue one (Proposition~\ref{prop:row}), its data the walk's
own reads, the tower matrix (Proposition~\ref{prop:row}), the channel
divisor (Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}; Definition~\ref{def:channelreads})
and the walk residue (Theorem~\ref{thm:walkresidue};
Definition~\ref{def:excess}), the pair $(3,H_r)$ their assembly
(Definition~\ref{def:contactpair}; Theorem~\ref{thm:closing}), the
scalar certificate the block certificate's instance
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerblock}; Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerpivot}), and its scheme bridge the count
$2d_f$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:bridge}; Remark~\ref{rem:certtarget}).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The cell list runs on the vacuum sector's depth chain at every
magnetic list: the caps and the deficit reads at the closure
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fpcap}; Lemma~\ref{lem:loopcap}), the truncation
(Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}; Lemma~\ref{lem:dualtrunc}), the
grading and the decimation on the sector's chain
(Lemma~\ref{lem:grading}; Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}), the
dual chain's cells (Lemma~\ref{lem:contactcell}) and the corner
certificate at the list's constants (Lemma~\ref{lem:corner};
Construction~\ref{con:sectorcert}(iii); Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerblock};
Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerpivot}) read the
sector's pencil alone, the
faithfulness read entering the sectors' identification with the
charges alone (Construction~\ref{con:depthchain}); so
Theorem~\ref{thm:gappos}'s cells cover the interior on the sector
and its clause (vi) reads the sector's cut at every ray. The
adjoint list's instance is Construction~\ref{con:xfusion}'s chain,
its one-plaquette residue-one sector the tower labels alone, every
label of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ a Cartan power of the adjoint at even
degree, so the walk's reads are the sector's own there.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The strong-coupling cut]\label{cor:strongcoupling}
Let the member, the residue, the direction count and the magnetic
list run as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. The free cell's certificate
reads two located outputs per member and direction count
(Lemma~\ref{lem:freecell}): its \emph{floor} $\kappa_1$, the
certificate's located datum, the pair at $E_0\kappa_1$ within the
flat window's width less the brackets' width and the band block's
cap, read outright at the free end
(Theorem~\ref{thm:gappos}(iv); Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend}), and its
\emph{extent} $\tau_1=[\,n_1\!:\!d_1\,]$ at that pair, each positive
by its shape. Then at every ray $[\,1:\tau^2\,]$ at $\tau\le\tau_1$
the cut of $\mathcal K([\,1:\tau^2\,])$ holds $\kappa_1$ as a
member, the window cuts' meet over every region and every
cutoff (Definition~\ref{def:K}). Every such window cut
holds $\kappa_1$, and the ground multiplicity is one
on the segment from the free end (Theorem~\ref{thm:SO}). At every further
end-weight pair $[\,\alpha:\beta\,]$ at
$\beta\,d_1^{\,2}\le n_1^{\,2}\,\alpha$ the cut at that
representative holds $\alpha\,[\,\kappa_1:2\,]$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:gappos}(v)); and at every window and every such
coupling the finite-window cut's edge, where one is named, is the compressed
pair's least root attained at a word image with the two moments at
equality and the first positive (Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(i),(ii)).
The free end reads the invariant at one (Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend}),
and the extent's positivity is the free end's interiority read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:freecell}).
\begin{proof}
The free-cell certificate's two counts read at its fixed offsets
at every region and every cutoff (Lemma~\ref{lem:freecell}).
Its counts are the original pencil's total counts through
the pivot witnesses (Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(i)), with
the separated product at its actual cutoff selection
(Lemma~\ref{lem:relfiber}(iv)). At the upper offset $h$,
$\ell+E_0\kappa_1\le h$; count monotonicity gives one at
$e+\ell+E_0\kappa_1$, with $e$ that window's ground.
Monotonicity and the ground below $e+E_0\kappa_1$ give
the count one at that line, hence the window cut and
simple ground (Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}). Taking every
window gives the meet's membership (Definition~\ref{def:K}).
At a further pair ray, fix one
region and write $P$ for its plaquette count, $W:=P\,d_L$ for its
magnetic form cap, and $\gamma:=E_0\kappa_1=[\,g:h\,]$.
The natural
\[
q:=\alpha+4P\,d_L(2n_1+d_1)h+1
\]
sits beyond $\alpha$ and beyond
$[\,4W(2n_1+d_1)h:d_1g\,]$, the latter comparison at
$d_1g\ge1$. Let $p$ be the least natural from one at
$\beta q^2\le\alpha(p+1)^2$, the stepping read with witness
$\beta q^2$ (Definition~\ref{def:ground}). Its predecessor
refuses, with the start's strict read at $q>\alpha$, so
\[
\alpha p^2<\beta q^2\le\alpha(p+1)^2,
\qquad pd_1<n_1q.
\]
The second comparison follows by joining the first to
$\beta d_1^2\le n_1^2\alpha$. Thus the pair $t:=[\,p:q\,]$
sits inside the free cell. At $b:=[\,\beta:\alpha\,]$ the weight
gap $\delta$ at $t^2+\delta=b$ satisfies
\[
\delta\le[\,2p+1:q^2\,]\le[\,2n_1+d_1:d_1q\,],
\qquad 4W\delta<\gamma.
\]
Fix any cutoff of the stated region.
The two window pencils' difference is capped two-sidedly at
$\rho:=W\delta$ against $G$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}), so
the count sandwich (Theorem~\ref{thm:gappos}(v)) puts every
ordered root within $\rho$ of its root at $t$.
At a window of order at least two, its first two roots therefore
read a gap at or beyond $\langle\gamma:2\rho\rangle$, beyond
$[\,\gamma:2\,]$; the ground at $t$ is simple by the
free cell's count one. At order one the level gap is the sum's unit and
the detector read holds outright. Scaling the pencil by $\alpha$
gives the cut member $\alpha[\,\kappa_1:2\,]$ at
$[\,\alpha:\beta\,]$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}). The natural $q$
reads the stated region's $P$, while this cut member depends on
the member, direction count and end weights alone, so the read
holds at every region and every cutoff and belongs
to the window cuts' meet. The finite-window edge is
Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}'s at the window pencil's symbol
(Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(i)).
\end{proof}
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[Correspondence with the usual formulation]\label{rem:dictionary}
The objects above are recorded here under their standard names, so
that Theorem~\ref{thm:main}'s lattice statements and the spacetime
construction of Pending~\ref{pen:covariance} have their conventional
readings.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,itemsep=3pt]

\item \emph{The theory.} $H(1,b)=E+bM$ is the lattice gauge Hamiltonian, $E$ its
electric term, a sum of link Casimirs, and $M$ its magnetic term, a sum of
plaquette characters at the magnetic list (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}),
the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian of the Wilson action at a faithful
character: at the $A$-series the list is the fundamental with its dual and
the plaquette character is $\chi_f+\chi_{\bar f}=2\,\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{tr}\,U$,
the standard action's own term, and at every member the list's classes
reaching every class is the character's faithfulness, the classes the
center's characters (Construction~\ref{con:fusion}). Its space is the carrier
$\mathrm{Sect}_\infty$, a colimit of windows each finite-dimensional
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}, Proposition~\ref{prop:windowfinite}); its
observables are the $\ast$-algebra of Definition~\ref{def:algebra}, whose
products obey a window bound stated on the index alone
(Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}) and whose local algebras have $\mathfrak A$
as their limit (Definition~\ref{def:qla}). That bound and that limit are
locality, and both are read off the index. $H$ is a symmetric rational matrix
on every window, so each level read there is linear algebra
(Theorem~\ref{thm:pairpencil}). Classically the carrier's elements are
the gauge-invariant polynomial functions of the link holonomies,
$\mathrm{Eval}$ is the Haar integral of the compact group, and the pairing
is its $L^2$ one: the compact group, its invariant mean, and its coordinate
ring are one classical reading of the fusion data, which the calculus above
computes exactly. The label calculus's classical identities are
listed under their usual names: the blocks are the irreducible representations at highest
weights, the orthogonal complement of Lemma~\ref{lem:orthsplit} is what
Weyl's integration buys as complete reducibility, the scalar endomorphisms
of Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr} are Schur's lemma, the alternant identity of
Theorem~\ref{thm:weylchar} is the Weyl character formula, the
alternant pair $a_\beta$ reading as the determinant
$\det\big(x_i^{\beta_j}\big)=\sum_w\mathrm{sgn}(w)\,x^{w\beta}$, the
pair's value its members' difference and the swap grading the sign of
the permutation, the full-column line of
Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(ii) the determinant representation, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:weyldim} its dimension formula,
Lemma~\ref{lem:pieri} the Pieri rule at one box,
Lemma~\ref{lem:pathsquare}'s path count $f^\lambda$ the standard
tableau count at the shape (the raised glyph the classical one,
the unraised $f$ the fundamental label's),
Corollary~\ref{cor:steinberg} the alternating fusion count
(Brauer, Klimyk), and Lemma~\ref{lem:mixedinv} the Schur--Weyl
invariant span. That reading
extends to the local objects: the characters are the blocks' traces on
holonomies, the product reading
$\mathrm{tr}(A\otimes B)=\mathrm{tr}\,A\cdot\mathrm{tr}\,B$ with
$d_a=\chi_a(1)$; the adjoint character runs pointwise over $[-1,n^2-1]$
and the fundamental trace's modulus over $[0,n]$, the tops at $U=1$, the
form caps of Lemmas~\ref{lem:fpcap} and~\ref{lem:loopcap} read
pointwise; the form line of Proposition~\ref{prop:form} is the invariant
symmetric bilinear forms on $\mathfrak{su}(n)$; the two-plaquette fiber
of Construction~\ref{con:fiber} is $L^2(G\times G)^G$, the functions of
the two plaquette holonomies invariant under simultaneous conjugation,
the theta graph's gauge reduction; and $\mathfrak A$
(Definition~\ref{def:qla}) is the quasi-local $C^*$-algebra, the norm
closure of the inductive limit of the local algebras.

\item \emph{The vacuum.} $\psi$ is a window ground and $\varepsilon_0$ its
eigenvalue, so $(H-\varepsilon_0)\psi=0$ and $H-\varepsilon_0\succeq0$ on
$\psi^\perp$ by construction (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}); on a window the
ground multiplicity is a count, a divisor read
(Theorem~\ref{thm:SO}), and the vacuum's correlation reads sit in
named window brackets, Euclidean pairs included
(Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}). A reader who doubts uniqueness in the limit
keeps every read: the cut is stated on counting functions, every
comparison a count of the pencil itself rather than a read at a chosen
state (Definition~\ref{def:K}; Theorem~\ref{thm:flatstep}), so
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} holds at every ground.

\item \emph{The lattice.} The carrier is stated over the interface of
Construction~\ref{con:lattice}, so the
derivations run on its fields alone. The reading here takes $\mathbb Z^d$, whose
plaquettes are its unit squares, at $d\ge2$, and the plaquette chain at $d=1$,
consecutive squares sharing one link. On either, a plaquette's boundary
is four links, the count Proposition~\ref{prop:E0} reads, and a
link sits in the plaquettes of its direction's pairs, the per-link
plaquette count the gap $g$ at $g+2=2d$ here, the per-vertex
count $d\,g$, a straight cell's stencil $[\,g^{2}:2\,]$, and each
at most two on the chain. $d$ counts the
space directions and time is the pencil's own, so $d=3$ is the case of
$\mathbb R^4$.

\item \emph{The lattice symmetries.} $E$ and $M$ run over all links and all
plaquettes at coefficient one, so $H$ commutes with every symmetry of
$\mathbb Z^d$ permuting those two sets: the translations, and the
hyperoctahedral group $B_d$ of signed coordinate permutations
(Theorem~\ref{thm:restoration}), whose permutation factor is the coordinate
exchanges and whose sign flips are the reflections. $B_d$ is what
Theorem~\ref{thm:restoration} is stated over, the translations entering
separately at the fibering (Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}).
Theorem~\ref{thm:restoration} reads the invariant polynomial spaces
at each argument count: their degree-$2$ spans coincide, and the
degree-$4$ space holds an additional invariant beyond the isotropic
span. The theorem's isotropic
span reads classically as the $O(d)$-invariant ring, the first
fundamental theorem for $O(d)$ the classical side's own
identification. The transformation comparisons for the continuum
correlations are Pending~\ref{pen:covariance}'s data.

\item \emph{The coupling.} The pencil's parameter is the coupling. The
free end's pencil is the electric term alone and the contact end's
the magnetic alone
(Proposition~\ref{prop:segment}), so the two ends are the strong- and
weak-coupling limits; the free cell's cut at the strong end
(Corollary~\ref{cor:strongcoupling}) reads as a floor of the
Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian's gap at every window at magnetic
weight at or below the extent's square, $\beta\,d_1^{\,2}\le
n_1^{\,2}\,\alpha$, the classical strong-coupling regime read at the
chain's outputs.

\item \emph{The continuum's points.} Clause~(i) is stated over
every interior end-weight ray, the root coordinate's rays the
cells' working points (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}). A reader's
continuum point (a Cauchy
or Dedekind real, a nested-bracket datum) reads the cut in through
its own rational comparisons: the counting sandwich of
Theorem~\ref{thm:gappos}(v) transports the rational reads to every
located coupling at its stated modulus, so ``at every interior
coupling'' holds at whatever continuum the reader brings, each point
reading itself in through the rationals beside it. The chain's own

further point's read.

\item \emph{The scalar pairs.} The translation of the colon
notation is a bijection and reads one way only: a scalar pair
$[a\!:\!b]$ (Definition~\ref{def:ground}) is the positive
rational $a/b$, two pairs at the cross-multiplication
identity being one rational, so the stage glyph $\mathbb P$ reads
as the positive rationals, with $\mathbb Q$, the field, this
remark's own; under that map the displayed sum,
product and order of Definition~\ref{def:ground} are the field's
own on the positive rationals, the signed readings and the zero
this remark's own, a pair of equal members reading zero and an absent
summand a zero term, and
$H_k=\sum_{j\le k}[1\!:\!j]$ is the classical harmonic number
$\sum_{j\le k}1/j$. A coupling's end-weight pair $[\alpha\!:\!\beta]$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:segment}) is the point $[\alpha:-\beta]$ of the

coordinates, the minus this remark's own; the scalar instance is the

$\langle u\!:\!v\rangle$ (Definition~\ref{def:ground}) is the
difference $u-v$, the subtraction this remark's own: its side is the
value's sign, equal members the value zero, and a bracket of
balance-pair endpoints is the signed interval its endpoints name.

\item \emph{The names.} The document's terms of art read against
their standard names, each at its defining site. The reversal
count $\operatorname{rev}(A\!:\!B)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}) is
the negative index of inertia of the difference $A-B$, the
subtraction this remark's own, and its two-splits-one-count
clause is Sylvester's law of inertia. The division descent
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}) is the Euclidean algorithm, its
greatest common divisor taken monic over the pair carrier and, at
the integer representatives, primitive at the stated positive top
with the clearing multipliers the remark's own rescaling; the
cleared division at a stated top is the classical
pseudo-division. The
remainder lists at a monic $S$ (Definition~\ref{def:poly}) are the
quotient ring $K[x]/(S)$ read as data. The cofactor $c$ at
$Y\,c=X$ (Definition~\ref{def:ground}) is the exact quotient $X/Y$,
computer algebra's own cofactor, and
the gap $g$ at $q+g=p$ the difference $p-q$, the remark's own
operations (the classical matrix cofactors enter as the
adjugate's entries, under that name). The deck relation $z^2+1=wz$
(Definition~\ref{def:deck}; Theorem~\ref{thm:chordmap};
Lemma~\ref{lem:deckfactor}) is the
double cover $w=z+1/z$, the Joukowski map, its deck involution
the cover's deck transformation $z\mapsto1/z$, and the chord
$t=\zeta+\zeta^{-1}=2\cos k$ at the classical momentum $k$ is the
Chebyshev variable of the momentum fiber
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}). The decimation
(Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}) is the classical block decimation,
each step a Schur complement onto the head. A located
element (Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}) is located in Bishop's
constructive sense, the bracket its datum. The $d_f$-ality
(Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}) is the classical $N$-ality at
$N=n$, the box count's class at full columns. The beta-set
(Construction~\ref{con:places}) is the partition's classical
beta-set at the positive shift, $x_i=\lambda_i+(d_f-i)+1$ against
the classical $\lambda_i+d_f-i$. A content (Construction~\ref{con:places}) is the
classical weight of the grading, `weight' in the chain the end and
form data's word; a configuration's content
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}) is its total Casimir, the electric
term's total. The calculus at the symbolic residue is the
unitary group $\mathrm{U}(n)$'s, the determinant relations
per-residue data, the presentation kernel's
(Remark~\ref{rem:kernel}).

\item \emph{The members.} The classification's members read as
the simply connected compact simple groups at $r+1=h^\vee$, the
derived residue
the dual Coxeter number's read, the residue folds of
Construction~\ref{con:sertables} its per-member evaluations; the
title reads here. The $A$-series is $\mathrm{SU}(n)$ at
$n:=r+1=d_f$, whose fundamental representation has dimension $n$
and whose Lie rank is $n-1$, the declared names reading the
matrix size as the fundamental count $d_f$ and the Lie rank as
