weight tables read $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$ and $D_\ell$ as
$\mathrm{Spin}(2\ell{+}1)$, $\mathrm{Sp}(\ell)$ and
$\mathrm{Spin}(2\ell)$, and the five fixed members the
exceptional groups. Theorem~\ref{thm:main}'s prefix instantiates
the classical statement at every simply connected compact simple
group and every
$d\ge1$, each group once: the index floors read each low-index
coincidence at one member, $\mathrm{Spin}(3)$ and
$\mathrm{Sp}(1)$ at $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$ at
$\mathrm{Spin}(5)$, and $\mathrm{Spin}(6)$ at $\mathrm{SU}(4)$,
with
$\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ off the simple list, the identifications the
classification's own.

\item \emph{The weak-coupling comparison, and the root coordinate.}
Classically the weak-coupling theory is read against lattice Maxwell
theory per Lie-algebra direction: the link field is $\log U_\ell$, the
magnetic energy is the abelianized flux squared, and the comparison
diagonalizes in Fourier with dispersion
$\varepsilon(k)^2=2|b|\,\hat h(k)$ at the graph Laplacian $\hat h$ of
$\mathbb Z^d$, massless at $k\to0$. That is the classical identity of the
gap chain's objects: the root coordinate $\tau$ ($b=-\tau^2$, the
remark's reading of Definition~\ref{def:pencil}'s weights) is the harmonic frequency scale, and the
soft momenta the flat step reads cell by cell
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}; Theorem~\ref{thm:flatstep}) are the sector
the massless comparison leaves ungapped: the lift above the comparison is
what the counts read, the corner scale its ruler
(Lemma~\ref{lem:corner}).

\item \emph{The gap.} $E_0$ is the free end's level, the energy of the
lightest one-plaquette excitation there, the floor label's loop, an
eigenvector of the pencil (Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}), and $\mathcal K$ is
the uniform lower cut for excitation gaps at every region and
every cutoff, above each window's own ground, read against that level
(Definition~\ref{def:K}), one at the free end (Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend}).
Since $E_0>0$, clause~(i) is the lattice Hamiltonian gap: on the word sector
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}) the spectrum starts \emph{strictly} above the
vacuum. The window's energy positivity, $H-\varepsilon_0
\succeq0$, is item~2's and holds by construction; clause~(i) is the strict
statement above it. Clause~(ii) locates the level: at every window
the cut's edge is a root of the window's symbol met at a word image
(Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}; Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(i),(ii)), the
lightest excitation a state the local observables create from the
vacuum. A reader who wants an edge as an energy restores the
two scales at which the cut reads one value: it is
$E_0\,\kappa\,C_2(\mathrm{adj})$ at the edge's pair $\kappa$, with
$E_0$ moving with the family's scale and $C_2(\mathrm{adj})$ with
the invariant form (Proposition~\ref{prop:form}), as the level does
with each, which is what makes the product an energy.

\item \emph{The continuum reading.} The usual formulation reads the
contact end's approach through the continuum construction: the spacing $a$
sets the units, the electric weight is $g^2/2a$ and the magnetic
$1/(ag^2)$ at the usual coefficients, and the construction holds the
physical gap $\Delta$ fixed while $a\to0$ along a coupling
trajectory $g\to0$, so its premise is that the gap in lattice units,
$a\Delta$, falls under every floor toward the contact end, the diverging correlation
length. The corner scale maps that premise onto the chain's data
exactly: the two weights' product is $1/2a^2$ at every $g$, one value
across the couplings, so the corner height of
Lemma~\ref{lem:corner} reads classically as $\sqrt2\,a\Delta$ at
every coupling of the approach. The premise therefore reads: the
gap falls below every corner-scale floor toward the contact end, the
corner cell's outputs under every floor. The chain's height at
every scale is a located bracket, its floor the ray's own cut
member and its caps the window's cap line at the tail read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerkey}) and the cutoff-tail probe
caps (Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(iv)); so the premise reads
on the chain at its windows and fibers as the height's fall under
every floor along the scale, the tail read at two directions or
beyond with one direction the floor (Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerkey}), and
the formulation's spacing reads through that datum. The spacetime
action on the correlation family is the construction of
Pending~\ref{pen:covariance}.

\item \emph{The unit map.} The classical construction chooses a
trajectory $g(a)$ by hand; here the spacing is a read: at a
physical gap $\Delta$ the unit is $a=h/(\sqrt2\,\Delta)$ at the
chain's height $h$ at the scale, the located bracket of
clause~(iii), one equation per scale, so
the physical gap reads $\Delta$ at every scale of the trajectory
and the trajectory's spacings are the heights' reads.

\item \emph{The reconstruction data.} The spectral reconstruction
of Theorem~\ref{thm:reconstruct} reads the finite-window Euclidean
families as folds over located energy roots at the probes' spectral
weights. The state pairing is the word sector's own
(Lemma~\ref{lem:statespace}), positive at
Definition~\ref{def:carrier}'s pairing. The lattice correlators'
brackets, clustering comparisons and Euclidean pairs are
Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}'s displays, with
$e^{-u(H-\varepsilon_0)}$ this remark's reading of the Euclidean
bracket families; their moment identities are
Lemma~\ref{lem:momentfold}'s, and the spacing reads the height
(Theorem~\ref{thm:continuum}(iii)). A Wightman reconstruction
requires spacetime covariance, the spectral condition, locality,
the distributional growth conditions and the vacuum properties
on one continuum family. Its covariance and the identification
with the lattice family are Pending~\ref{pen:covariance}'s
construction.

\item \emph{The spectral condition.} $\mathrm{spec}(H)\subset
\{\varepsilon_0\}\cup[\varepsilon_0+E_0\kappa,\infty)$ is the window cut
(Definition~\ref{def:K}; Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}), its edge met at a
word image window by window with the weight at the level where the
inclusion is read (Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}). The lattice momentum
decomposition is the fibering (Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}), and the
roots' spatial momentum reading is isotropic at degree two
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cone}). The relativistic spectral condition is
support of the joint energy--momentum spectrum in the forward
light cone, with the mass gap read there. It requires the
spacetime translation action and its Lorentz transport on the
continuum carrier, Pending~\ref{pen:covariance}'s construction.
The physical energy scale reads through the unit map at the
chain's height, between the ray's cut member and its caps
(Theorem~\ref{thm:main}; Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerfloor};
Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerkey}; Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(iv)).

\item \emph{Locality, and the net.} The regions' lattice algebras
obey the window bounds (Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra};
Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries}; Definition~\ref{def:qla}), and
equal-time products commute (Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}). The
propagation bracket (Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(vi)) prices the
commutator beyond its stated reach at the remainder's width; the
clustering brackets are Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(iv)'s. A
relativistic net requires an algebra at each spacetime region,
transported by the spacetime action, with commutation at spacelike
separation. The support transport is
Pending~\ref{pen:covariance}'s construction; the spacelike
commutation read requires the propagation widths to close at those
supports under the unit map.

\item \emph{Invariance.} Spacetime covariance is the construction
of Pending~\ref{pen:covariance}. Its classical reading is a
strongly continuous unitary representation $U$ of
$\mathbb R^{d+1}\rtimes\mathrm{SO}^{+}(d,1)$ on the continuum
state space, at the identities
\[
U(g)\Omega=\Omega,\qquad
U(g)\mathfrak A(O)U(g)^{*}=\mathfrak A(gO)
\]
for each group element $g$ and bounded open spacetime region $O$.
The pairing identities at the transported words give the

\item \emph{Nontriviality.} The theory is interacting at every

floor separates the state from every generalized free field's.

\item \emph{The conventional target.} The Yang--Mills problem asks,

\section{Fusion data}

\begin{proposition}[A fusion computation is a representation
computation]\label{prop:repring}
The fusion data are counts of the calculus: $N^c_{ab}$ is the number of
$c$-blocks in a product of blocks and $d_a$ the block dimension
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}, on labels by Construction~\ref{con:labels}),
$m\{a,b,c\}$ the invariant count of the triple product, the labels
the label set's (Construction~\ref{con:labels}). Each is read in the label index: $\chi_a$ is the index's generator at
$a$, the product of two expanding over the tensor product's blocks,
\[
\chi_a\chi_b=\sum_cN^c_{ab}\,\chi_c ,
\]
the coefficients the block counts (Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(iii), on
labels by Construction~\ref{con:labels}); the dimension $d_a$ is the
block's count (Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}(iv)); and the unit label
$\mathbf 1$ has $\chi_{\mathbf 1}=1$, the constants' line's.

Four reads follow, and they are what the label index runs on. Write
$\mathrm{Hom}(x,y)$ for the linear maps from $x$ to $y$; then
$\mathrm{Hom}(x,y)\cong x^{*}\otimes y$, the intertwiners are its invariants,
and the unit label's multiplicity in any $x$ is its invariant count.
First,
\[
N^{\mathbf 1}_{ab}=\delta_{a\bar b} ,
\]
the unit read of Construction~\ref{con:labels}. Second, the characters are orthonormal for the evaluation, the
unit-label coefficient read
$\mathrm{Eval}(\chi_c)=\delta_{c\mathbf 1}$, the block's invariant
count, so
\[
\mathrm{Eval}\big(\chi_a\overline{\chi_b}\big)
=\sum_cN^c_{a\bar b}\,\mathrm{Eval}(\chi_c)
=N^{\mathbf 1}_{a\bar b}=\delta_{ab} ,
\]
and a product expanded in the label index therefore has unique coefficients.
Third, $m\{a,b,c\}=N^{\bar c}_{ab}$, with the rotation
$N^{\bar c}_{ab}=N^{\bar a}_{bc}$: the rotation and the factors'
exchange, the transposition, generate the symmetry
of $m$ in its three arguments, and that is the symmetry of $N$ at
self-dual labels. Fourth, the involution's index
read: the dual label's matrix is the transpose,
$N^c_{\bar a\,b}=N^b_{ac}$.
\begin{proof}
The first read: the count of the
unit label in the product at $a$ and $b$ is the full-column-power count
of Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(iii), one exactly at the dual label. The
second display reads the product's display at the unit-label
coefficient with the first read at the dual label. The third: $m\{a,b,c\}=\sum_dN^d_{ab}N^{\mathbf 1}_{dc}$ with
the first read keeps the sum at the dual label's summand alone,
$N^{\bar c}_{ab}$; the display reads at either pairing of the
associativity at the unit target
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(iii)),
$\sum_eN^e_{ab}N^{\mathbf 1}_{ec}=\sum_fN^f_{bc}N^{\mathbf 1}_{af}$,
the first read keeping each sum at the dual label's summand alone,
so $N^{\bar c}_{ab}=N^{\bar a}_{bc}$. The fourth: the triple count reads one value at
every argument dualized, duals of blocks being blocks with the
unit's count kept (Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(i)), and the third
read's symmetry closes the exchange.
\end{proof}
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[The adjoint character]\label{lem:adjchar}
Write $f$ for the fundamental label, the one-box shape's, whose block
is $V$ itself at the declared count $d_f$
(Construction~\ref{con:places}), and $\bar f$ for its
dual, at the residue at or beyond one. Then
\[
f\otimes\bar f\;=\;\theta\oplus\mathbf 1 ,
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
\chi_\theta(U)+1\;=\;|\mathrm{tr}\,U|^2 ,
\]
and the adjoint's
contents are the \emph{letter-pair moves}, one place raised
and one lowered, each ordered pair of distinct places once, with the
unit-monomial content at
multiplicity $r$, the
product's unit-monomial count splitting as the unit line's one with
the adjoint's, $r+1=d_f$.
\begin{proof}
$\bar f$ is the class of the complement $f^*$
(Construction~\ref{con:labels}), the one-column shape at the
complement gap, $r$ rows of one box (Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(ii)),
and $\bar f\otimes f$
exhausts by the one-box row (Lemma~\ref{lem:pieri}): the dominant
one-box additions of $(1^{r})$ are $(2,1^{r-1})$, the label
$\theta$ (Construction~\ref{con:labels}), and the full column
$(1^{d_f})$, the unit label's, one block each with every further
label vacant, and the factors exchange
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(iii)): $f\otimes\bar f=\theta\oplus
\mathbf 1$. The product's contents are the factors' contents'
sums (Construction~\ref{con:places}): the one-box block reads each
letter once and $\bar f$'s block each withdrawn letter once
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pieri}'s complement read), so the product reads
the unit-monomial content at $d_f$, one per letter, and each
letter-pair move once, a letter against a withdrawn one. The
content refinement of Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(ii) reads the
product's occupancies as the two blocks' at their counts, and the
full-column line is occupied at the unit-monomial content alone
(Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(ii)): $\theta$'s occupancies are the
product's with the line's withdrawn, each move once and the
unit-monomial content at $d_f-1=r$. Hence
$\chi_f\chi_{\bar f}=\chi_\theta+1$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}), and
$\chi_f(U)=\mathrm{tr}\,U$ reads the display.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\section{The requirement, in two moments}

\begin{theorem}[The divisor-separation detector]\label{thm:detector}
The level-$\gamma$ \emph{requirement} is the probe family
$\mu_2(A)\ge\gamma\,\mu_1(A)$ at the two moments
$\mu_j(A):=\langle v_A,\,D^{\,j}v_A\rangle_G$
at $v_A:=\Pi A\psi$, the word image projected to the window
(Theorem~\ref{thm:momentform}'s reads), and its \emph{detector pair} at a
spectral point $\lambda$ is $(\lambda^2\!:\!\gamma\lambda)$, the
moments' spectral read: a probe's two moments read the weight fold
over the located spectrum (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), so the
requirement's read at a probe is the fold of the detector pairs' at
the probe's weights. The pair's members are equal exactly at the
kernel point and at the edge $\lambda=\gamma$, the two neutral
points, its site datum the factor read
$\lambda\,\langle\lambda\!:\!\gamma\rangle$, and off them its side
is $\lambda$'s against $\gamma$ at positive $\lambda$: weight below
$\gamma$ drives failure, weight beyond passes, weight at the edge
is neutral, and the vacuum direction, the kernel point, is neutral
as well, the vacuum's saturation untouched.
\begin{proof}
The split's congruence diagonalizes the gram and the level gap at
once at the located roots $\lambda_j$ with the gram's diagonal
entries $g_j$ on their upper sides (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), so at
the probe's vector at coordinates $y_j$ there the moments read
$\mu_1(A)=\sum_jw_j\lambda_j$ and $\mu_2(A)=\sum_jw_j\lambda_j^{2}$
at the weights $w_j=g_jy_j^{2}$, and the requirement's pair
$\langle\mu_2(A)\!:\!\gamma\,\mu_1(A)\rangle$ is the fold
$\sum_jw_j\,\lambda_j\,\langle\lambda_j\!:\!\gamma\rangle$, the
detector pairs' at the weights. The pair
$(\lambda^{2}\!:\!\gamma\lambda)$'s site datum is the product
$\lambda\,\langle\lambda\!:\!\gamma\rangle$, the distributed read
$\lambda\,\langle\lambda\!:\!\gamma\rangle=\langle\lambda^{2}\!:\!\gamma\lambda\rangle$
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}), of equal members exactly where a
factor is, $\lambda$ at the kernel point or
$\langle\lambda\!:\!\gamma\rangle$ at the edge, the product's
injectivity at an occupied factor; off them the factor $\lambda$
is positive and the side is $\langle\lambda\!:\!\gamma\rangle$'s,
$\lambda$'s against $\gamma$.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The level condition over probes is the spectral condition]
\label{thm:levelequiv}
On the word sector's window projection, the level-$\gamma$ requirement (one condition per
probe) is \emph{equivalent} to the form comparison
\[
SD\ \succeq\ \gamma\,S
\quad\text{on the word sector}
\qquad(\text{the kernel point with every further level at or beyond
}\gamma).
\]
\begin{proof}
($\Leftarrow$) With the spectrum at the kernel point and at or beyond
$\gamma$, every detector pair reads its upper side or equal members
(Theorem~\ref{thm:detector}), and every probe's weight fold with
it; read at the pair's certificate, the positive-semidefinite
split prices every sector vector's form through the congruence at
its witness, the blocks' fold of squares
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), and the site datum's decomposition
reads the priced form as the two moments' comparison, the
requirement's own display. ($\Rightarrow$) On a window the reversal count settles it: at
$\operatorname{rev}(SD\!:\!\gamma S)\ge1$ a
lower-side
pivot sits among the elimination datum's $\mathrm{LDL}^{\mathsf T}$ pivots, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct}(2) reads off the elimination a pair-entried $v$
with $\gamma v^{\mathsf T}Sv>v^{\mathsf T}SDv$,
the reversal's own read. The witness is a
vector of that projection, hence $\Pi A\psi$ at some word $A$
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), and that word's probe fails the
requirement outright, the witness's two reads its two moments
(Theorem~\ref{thm:momentform}).
\end{proof}

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The two-moment form]\label{thm:momentform}
At a window ground and a multiplication probe $A$, write
$v_A=A_\Pi\psi$ for the projection of its word image to the
window and $J_A$ for the window commutator's vector
(Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}). The actions and pairing are the Gram solves of
Definition~\ref{def:pencil}. The moments and their operator read are
\begin{gather*}
\mu_1(A)=\langle v_A,J_A\rangle_{G_\Pi}
=\omega\big(A_\Pi^\dagger[K_\Pi,A_\Pi]\big),\\
\mu_2(A)=\langle J_A,J_A\rangle_{G_\Pi}=\omega\big(Q_2(A)\big),
\qquad Q_2(A):=[K_\Pi,A_\Pi]^\dagger[K_\Pi,A_\Pi].
\end{gather*}
In coordinates, at $C_A:=[K_\Pi,A_\Pi]$, the two forms read
$\mu_1(A)=v_A^{\mathsf T}S_\Pi v_A$ and
$\mu_2(A)=\psi^{\mathsf T}C_A^{\mathsf T}G_\Pi C_A\psi$;
the action $Q_2(A)$ has form $G_\Pi Q_2(A)=C_A^{\mathsf T}G_\Pi C_A$.

Their entries are finite pairing reads of
$J_A=\alpha\Pi[\mathsf E,A]\Pi\psi+\beta\mathcal B_A\psi$,
the boundary maps Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}'s. At
$\alpha=1$ and $\beta\mathcal B_A\psi$ the sum's unit, the
moments read the electric commutator $\Pi[\mathsf E,A]\Pi$ at the
projected probe. On the full product carrier, at the residual
$r$ the sum's unit and $\alpha=1$, the full product's vector is
$(K-\varepsilon_0)A\psi=[\mathsf E,A]\psi$ and its two pairing reads are
$\omega(A^\dagger[\mathsf E,A])$ and
$\omega([\mathsf E,A]^\dagger[\mathsf E,A])$.
The family $\mu_2(A)\ge\gamma\mu_1(A)$ is the
positive-semidefinite read of the detector pair
$(S_\Pi D_\Pi:\gamma S_\Pi)$ compressed whole to
these projected word images. Both moments depend on the probe
through $v_A$ alone; the map $A\mapsto\Pi A\psi$ is linear
and its image is the word sector's window projection
(Lemma~\ref{lem:sectorspan}). The full word images have their
pairing in their product windows (Definition~\ref{def:algebra}).

\emph{The gradient read.} At an involution-fixed multiplication
probe $f$, define the coefficient element and the boundary map
\begin{gather*}
D_f:=\sum_a(X_af)^2
=f\,(\mathsf E f)+\big\langle[\,1:2\,]\mathsf E(f^2)\big\rangle^{\vee},\\
W_f:=\Pi'[\mathsf E,f]\Pi=\mathsf E_{\Pi'}V_f-V_f\mathsf E_\Pi.
\end{gather*}
The generators are Definition~\ref{def:generators}'s, and the
first moment reads
\begin{multline*}
\mu_1(f)=\alpha\,\omega(D_f)
+\Big\langle[\,\alpha:2\,]\,
\omega(V_f^\dagger W_f+W_f^\dagger V_f)\Big\rangle^{\vee}\\
+[\,\beta:2\,]\,\omega\big([f_\Pi,\mathcal B_f]\big).
\end{multline*}
The two boundary terms read their displayed pairings, and at
$V_f\psi$ and $\beta\mathcal B_f\psi$ the sum's unit this is
$\mu_1(f)=\alpha\,\omega(D_f)$.
At a character $\chi_c(W)$ on a loop of $L$ distinct
links the electric member reads the loop's own content,
$\mathsf E\,\chi_c(W)=L\,C_2(c)\,\chi_c(W)$, each link's Casimir at the
block's coefficient (Construction~\ref{con:coeff};
Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}), and the square fuses over the
channel list, so the gradient square is the \emph{channel fold}
\[
\sum_a\big(X_a\chi_c(W)\big)^2
\;=\;L\sum_eN^e_{cc}\,
\big\langle\,C_2(c)\,:\,[\,1:2\,]\,C_2(e)\,\big\rangle\,\chi_e(W)\,,
\]
a character polynomial of the loop's holonomy; at the adjoint
character its read at the unit holonomy is the sum's unit,
$\sum_em_ed_e\,\hat c_2(e)=2\,d_\theta^{\,2}$ against
$d_\theta^{\,2}\,\hat c_2(\theta)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}'s
second closure; Theorem~\ref{thm:drift}), and at a difference of
two translates of one loop at disjoint links the gradient squares
add, a generator at one loop's link reading the other's character
at the sum's unit.
\begin{proof}
The ground equation gives $J_A=D_\Pi v_A$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}), so the two moments are the displayed
pairing and square. Linearity of multiplication and projection
makes every combination of projected word images a projected
word image; the detector's form on that combination is the
moments' comparison, the two quadratic reads at that vector.
For the gradient read, the derivation's Leibniz rule and
$\mathsf E=\sum_aX_a^\dagger X_a$ give
$[f,[\mathsf E,f]]=2D_f$ and $\mathsf E(f^2)=2f(\mathsf E f)-2D_f$
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}). The projected double commutator
reads
\[
[f_\Pi,\Pi[\mathsf E,f]\Pi]
=2\Pi D_f\Pi-V_f^\dagger W_f-W_f^\dagger V_f,
\]
by inserting $\Pi+\Pi'=1$ in both products; $[\mathsf E,f]$ has its
adjoint at its balance partner, so $\Pi[\mathsf E,f]\Pi'=-W_f^\dagger$.
The first commutator is
$[K_\Pi,f_\Pi]=\alpha\Pi[\mathsf E,f]\Pi+\beta\mathcal B_f$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}). Its double commutator at the ground
has expectation $2\mu_1(f)$, the two terms with $K_\Pi$ at
an outer slot reading $\varepsilon_0\omega(f_\Pi^2)$ each.
Combining these displays gives the stated gradient read.
At $V_f\psi$ the sum's unit the paired electric boundary terms
read it; at $\beta\mathcal B_f\psi$ the sum's unit the
magnetic term reads it as well, $\mathcal B_f$ having its
adjoint at its balance partner.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Two moments against a divisor]
\label{cor:momentdivisor}
Combining Theorem~\ref{thm:momentform} with Theorem~\ref{thm:levelequiv}, on a
window:
\[
\big(\forall A:\ \mu_2(A)\ \ge\ \gamma\,\mu_1(A)\big)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\big(SD\big)_\Lambda:\big(\gamma\,S\big)_\Lambda
\ \text{ positive semidefinite},
\]
the compression to the window's word sector taken of the detector form
whole, since $\mu_2(A)=v_A^{\mathsf T}SDv_A$ and
$\mu_1(A)=v_A^{\mathsf T}Sv_A$ at $v_A=\Pi A\psi$,
the projected word image of Theorem~\ref{thm:momentform}
(Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}): one reversal count on a form pair over
the located stage, exact by $\mathrm{LDL}^{\mathsf T}$ there
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}), whose read is
the kernel point with every further level at or beyond $\gamma$.
\begin{proof}
Right to left by Theorem~\ref{thm:detector}'s side reads, the
split's transport pricing every sector vector at the site datum's
decomposition (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}); left to right by the count's own
witness, which Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct}(2) reads off the elimination.
\end{proof}
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[The sector's span read]\label{lem:sectorspan}
Multiplication by a window ground is adjoint to its involution image's: at
carrier elements $w$, $x$ and a window ground $\psi$
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}; the involution
Definition~\ref{def:algebra}'s),
\[
\langle w,\ x\cdot\psi\rangle\;=\;\langle w\cdot\bar\psi,\ x\rangle\ ,
\]
and
a ground's involution image is a ground. The \emph{span read} at a window and a ground is the
product matrix's rank at the window's dimension: the matrix
$\mathrm{Eval}(\bar v\,w\,\bar\psi)$ at $w$ over the window list
and $v$ over the product window's
(Proposition~\ref{prop:leastwindow}), every entry a ground
computation, the rank the elimination's read
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}), one decidable read per window and
ground. The span read holds at every window and every ground.
The word sector's window projection fills the window, and the
compression to that projection is the window pair whole. At a window
list $(w_i)$ the probes $w_i\bar\psi$ give a spanning list of
projected word images; their coefficient products and Gram solves
read in their finite product windows
(Definition~\ref{def:algebra}; Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}).
\begin{proof}
Both sides of the display are the read $\mathrm{Eval}(\bar w\,\psi\,x)$, the products'
one value under commutativity with the involution invariance
(Definition~\ref{def:algebra}; Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}). The
involution keeps the pairing
($\mathrm{Eval}$ one value under the involution,
Definition~\ref{def:algebra}) and the pencil, $E$ at the dual
label's Casimir (Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}) and $M$ at the
plaquette character, its own involution image at the closure
(Construction~\ref{con:fusion}; Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), so it
keeps the level gap's kernel: a ground's image is a ground.

Multiplication by a coefficient element off the sum's unit is
injective. The computation uses the coefficient carrier's positive
pairing and derivations (Construction~\ref{con:coeff}), with $0$
the sum's unit in the displays. First, $h^2=0$ forces $h=0$:
at $z=\bar h h$ the involution and the product give $\bar z=z$
and $z^2=\bar h^{\,2}h^2=0$, so
$\langle z,z\rangle=\mathrm{Eval}(z^2)=0$ forces $z=0$,
and $\langle h,h\rangle=\mathrm{Eval}(z)=0$ forces $h=0$.
At $fg=0$ a link generator's Leibniz identity reads
\[
f(X_ag)+(X_af)g=0,\qquad
f^2(X_ag)=0,\qquad (fX_ag)^2=0.
\]
The square read therefore gives $f(X_ag)=0$. Iteration gives
$f(X_bX_ag)=0$ and then $f(\mathsf E g)=0$, since the electric
action is the generator pairs' fold, the pairing adjoints the
generators' balance partners at the metric dual
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}; Definition~\ref{def:generators};
Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}). Sums and scalar products keep this
identity, so $fP(\mathsf E)g=0$ at every polynomial $P$.

Apply this read to $\bar g g$, whose product with $f$ is the
sum's unit. Its occupied positive electric contents form a finite
list $\mathcal E$, the finite product window's index reads
(Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}; Construction~\ref{con:coeff});
every content off the unit coefficient is positive, the links'
Casimirs positive at their nonunit labels
(Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}; Construction~\ref{con:fusion}).
The polynomial and its scalar read are
\[
P(t):=\prod_{c\in\mathcal E}\langle c:t\rangle,
\qquad d:=\prod_{c\in\mathcal E}c,
\qquad
P(\mathsf E)(\bar g g)=d\,\mathrm{Eval}(\bar g g)\,\mathbf1.
\]
At a vacant list both products read one. At an occupied content
the corresponding factor reads the sum's unit, and at the unit
coefficient every factor reads its content, which gives the
display. Thus $d\,\mathrm{Eval}(\bar g g)\,f=0$; at $g$ off the
sum's unit the scalar is positive by the pairing, and scalar
product injectivity gives $f=0$ componentwise
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}). Every product and generator image
in this computation has a finite coefficient window. The argument
also reads over the ground's located stage: the coefficient Grams'
positive splits persist there (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia};
Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}).

The window list's products $z_i:=w_i\bar\psi$ are consequently
independent: a combination at the sum's unit reads
$(\sum_i a_iw_i)\bar\psi=0$, hence $\sum_i a_iw_i=0$ at
$\bar\psi$ off the sum's unit, and every coefficient is the
sum's unit at the window list's independence. Their Gram is
positive definite, with its adjugate solve
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}; Definition~\ref{def:elim}). Given a
window vector $y$, solve
\[
\sum_j\langle z_i,z_j\rangle b_j=\langle w_i,y\rangle
\quad\text{at every }i,\qquad A:=\sum_j b_jz_j.
\]
The opening identity gives
$\langle w_i,\Pi A\psi\rangle=\langle z_i,A\rangle
=\langle w_i,y\rangle$, so $\Pi A\psi=y$ by the window's
positive pairing. The products' independent columns give the
product matrix's rank at the window dimension, the span read;
the probes $z_i$ give the displayed spanning list.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A window spectral read is the cut at that window]
\label{lem:speccut}
At a window and a pair $\kappa$, the spectral read
\[
\mathrm{spec}(H)\ \subset\ \{\varepsilon_0\}\cup
[\varepsilon_0+E_0\kappa,\ \infty)
\]
is the window cut $\mathcal K_\Lambda$ of Definition~\ref{def:K} at
$\kappa$, at every window ground at once: at the read the pair
$(SD:E_0\kappa\,S)$ is positive semidefinite on
the window, and a compression keeps that read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}): every word-sector compression reads it,
the cut's own object, the detector form compressed whole. At every
ground the projection fills the window (Lemma~\ref{lem:sectorspan}),
so the identification holds both ways, the window cut's edge the
spectral edge there. The reading back rides the gap's own
floor: the levels'
positivity, $S$'s positive-semidefinite certificate
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), is the datum locating every root's
side, the side's one source. At the ground multiplicity
$g:=\dim\ker S$, the equivalent count read is
\[
\operatorname{rev}\big(H:(\varepsilon_0+E_0\kappa)G\big)=g.
\]
At every positive pair $h$, the joined count identity is
\[
g+\operatorname{rev}(SD:hS)
=\operatorname{rev}\big(H:(\varepsilon_0+h)G\big).
\]
\begin{proof}
The split of Lemma~\ref{lem:split}
maps the level-gap form $S$ ($\varepsilon_0G+S=H$,
Definition~\ref{def:pencil}) to a diagonal at the kernel point's read
and at reads at or beyond $E_0\kappa$, the detector pair at
each reads its upper side or equal members
(Theorem~\ref{thm:detector}, the two neutral points the ground's and
the edge's), so the pair
$(SD:E_0\kappa\,S)$ is positive semidefinite on
the window and every compression reads it. At every ground the
projection fills the window (Lemma~\ref{lem:sectorspan}), so the
compressed pair is the window pair whole. The reading back: the detector pair's side is $\lambda$'s against $\gamma$
at positive $\lambda$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:detector}), and the
certificate puts every root at the kernel point or on its upper
side, so a root reading the pair's upper side sits at or beyond
the edge. The count at $\varepsilon_0+E_0\kappa$ is the kernel
dimension joined to the count of occupied gaps strictly below
$E_0\kappa$, by the split's diagonal read; thus it equals $g$
exactly at the spectral read. The detector count reads the positive
gaps strictly below $h$: its diagonal at a gap $\lambda$ is the
positive Gram weight against $\lambda\langle\lambda:h\rangle$,
on its lower side exactly at $0<\lambda<h$. The ground and the
gap $h$ read equal members. Adding the ground's $g$ positions
gives the shifted count, including its read at the gap $h$.
At a level on its lower side the pair's read holds outright,
the square sitting on its upper side from either side of its
entry: the floor's certificate is the side's one source.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[The window commutator and its boundary reads]
\label{thm:coeffone}
Let $\Pi$ be a window's orthogonal projection and $\Pi'$ its
complement in a window holding the input and the product images
in the displays below (Definition~\ref{def:carrier};
Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}). A multiplication word $A$ reads
as $A_\Pi:=\Pi A\Pi$ on the input window; its full product is
read in its target window. Write $K_\Pi:=\Pi K\Pi$ for the compressed action at
$\alpha\mathsf E=\beta\mathsf M+K$, and let $\psi$ be a ground of $K_\Pi$ at
$\varepsilon_0$, with $D_\Pi$ its level-gap action.
At its image-list columns $L$, the forms are
$G_\Pi=L^{\mathsf T}GL$ and $H_\Pi=L^{\mathsf T}HL$.
They satisfy $G_\Pi K_\Pi=H_\Pi$ and
$G_\Pi D_\Pi=S_\Pi$ at $H_\Pi=\varepsilon_0G_\Pi+S_\Pi$;
all actions and pairing adjoints are the Gram solves of
Definition~\ref{def:pencil}. The dagger is the adjoint in the
stated pairing (Construction~\ref{con:coeff}). The boundary maps
and their paired read are
\[
U:=\Pi'\mathsf M\Pi,\qquad V_A:=\Pi'A\Pi,\qquad
\mathcal B_A:=U^\dagger V_A-V_{A^\dagger}^{\dagger}U.
\]
Then
\begin{gather*}
[K_\Pi,A_\Pi]=\alpha\Pi[\mathsf E,A]\Pi+\beta\mathcal B_A,\\
J_A:=D_\Pi A_\Pi\psi
=[K_\Pi,A_\Pi]\psi
=\alpha\Pi[\mathsf E,A]\Pi\psi+\beta\mathcal B_A\psi.
\end{gather*}
The vector identity at its additive join is
$K_\Pi A_\Pi\psi=A_\Pi K_\Pi\psi+D_\Pi A_\Pi\psi$.
At $\alpha=1$ and $\beta\mathcal B_A\psi$ the sum's unit, the
line reads $J_A=\Pi[\mathsf E,A]\Pi\psi$. Each boundary product reads
one pairing, $\langle x,U^\dagger V_Ay\rangle=\langle Ux,V_Ay\rangle$,
so its entries read on the independent collection of the boundary
images at their Gram (Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}).
The full product's line reads the ground's residual $r$:
\[
K\psi=\varepsilon_0\psi+r,\qquad r=(\beta U\psi)^{\vee},
\qquad
(K-\varepsilon_0)A\psi=\alpha[\mathsf E,A]\psi+Ar,
\]
the superscript the balance partner. At $r$ the sum's unit and
$\alpha=1$ this reads $(K-\varepsilon_0)A\psi=[\mathsf E,A]\psi$.
The boundary maps' electric and product recurrences are
\begin{gather*}
V_{[\mathsf E,A]}=\mathsf E_{\Pi'}V_A-V_A\mathsf E_\Pi,
\qquad \mathsf E_{\Pi'}:=\Pi'\mathsf E\Pi',\quad \mathsf E_\Pi:=\Pi\mathsf E\Pi,\\
(AB)_\Pi=A_\Pi B_\Pi+\Pi A\Pi'V_B,
\qquad V_{AB}=V_AB_\Pi+\Pi'A\Pi'V_B.
\end{gather*}
At input and output contents $c,c'$, the electric recurrence
multiplies the boundary entry by $\langle c':c\rangle$.

\emph{The disjoint-support cutoff read.} Let $A,B$ be
multiplications on disjoint link sets $R,T$ of one region,
and let $P_{a,c,q}$ select the configurations at partial
electric contents $a$ on $R$, $c$ on $T$ and $q$ on the
further links (Definition~\ref{def:carrier}). All selections
and products read in a finite target holding both product
orders (Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}). At input and output
blocks with
\[
q+a+c\le C,\qquad q+a'+c'\le C,
\]
let $u,v$ be the counts of the respective comparisons
\[
q+a'+c\le C,\qquad q+a+c'\le C,
\]
each one where its comparison holds and the sum's unit
otherwise. Then
\[
P_{a',c',q}[B_\Pi,A_\Pi]P_{a,c,q}
=\langle u:v\rangle\,P_{a',c',q}BA P_{a,c,q}.
\]
At $a\le a',c\le c'$ or $a'\le a,c'\le c$, one has
$u=v=1$, and this holds at $a=a'$ or $c=c'$ as well.
At $a<a',c'<c$ one has $v=1$, and at $a'<a,c<c'$
one has $u=1$. At these two move pairs, put
\[
L:=\max\{a+c,a'+c'\},\qquad
U:=\max\{a'+c,a+c'\}.
\]
Then $L<U$, with gap the lesser of the two moved
contents' positive gaps. The multiplier $\langle u:v\rangle$
is occupied exactly on the cutoff interval
\[
q+L\le C<q+U,
\]
at the balance partner of one for $a<a',c'<c$ and
at one for $a'<a,c<c'$. For $B=\mathsf M_p$ at a plaquette
disjoint from $R$, its boundary summand is
\[
\mathcal B_A^{(p)}
=\Pi B\Pi'A\Pi-\Pi A\Pi'B\Pi
=[B_\Pi,A_\Pi]^\vee,
\]
so its block reads the pair $\langle v:u\rangle$ at
the displayed product block. These are map identities
at the window's actual pairing and restrict to its
invariant subspace (Construction~\ref{con:coeff}).

At a total-content projection $\Pi$ in one fixed region, let
$(A_i)$ be a finite family of maps raising content by positive
data $e_i$: an input of content $c$ has its image at content
$c+e_i$. With $a_i:=\Pi A_i\Pi$ and $V_i:=\Pi'A_i\Pi$,
their adjoint-creation commutators read
\[
[a_i^\dagger,a_j]+V_i^\dagger V_j
=\Pi[A_i^\dagger,A_j]\Pi.
\]
The matrix of boundary blocks $(V_i^\dagger V_j)_{ij}$ is
positive semidefinite in the direct-sum pairing: at vectors
$(x_i)$ in the input window its form is
\[
\sum_{i,j}\langle V_i x_i,V_j x_j\rangle
=\Big\langle\sum_iV_i x_i,\sum_jV_j x_j\Big\rangle.
\]
Every image and composition reads in a finite content window of
that region holding the indicated images.

\emph{The plaquette split.} For a plaquette $p$, let $P_p$ be
the index projection onto configurations at the unit label on
every link of $\partial p$, and let $Q_p$ be its complementary
projection. Write $\mathsf M_p$ for multiplication by $\chi_p$,
and, at the magnetic list's closure, set
\[
C_{p,\lambda}:=M_{\chi_\lambda(U_{\partial p})}P_p,
\qquad
\mathsf R:=\sum_p Q_p\mathsf M_pQ_p.
\]
Then
\begin{gather*}
\mathsf M=\mathsf R+
\sum_p\sum_{\lambda\in\bar L}(C_{p,\lambda}+C_{p,\lambda}^\dagger),
\qquad
[\mathsf E,C_{p,\lambda}]=4\hat c_2(\lambda)C_{p,\lambda},\\
C_{p,\lambda}^\dagger C_{p,\mu}=\delta_{\lambda\mu}P_p.
\end{gather*}
The creation maps commute: disjoint plaquette boundaries give
commuting factors and projections, and intersecting boundaries
give a product at the sum's unit in either order. Their
total-content compressions commute as well. At the member's
per-link floor $f_*:=\hat c_2(f_0)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}) and the per-link plaquette count
$\nu=2$ at $d=1$, $\nu=2g$ at $g+1=d$ for $d\ge2$
(Construction~\ref{con:lattice}), the remainder reads
\[
f_*\,\big|\langle x,\mathsf R x\rangle_G\big|
\le\nu d_L\,\langle x,\mathsf E x\rangle_G.
\]
This read holds at every region and every total-content cutoff,
with $\Pi\mathsf R\Pi$ and $\mathsf E_\Pi$ at the cutoff;
the magnitude is Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s read.
Index the plaquette creators by $i=(p,\lambda)$ and write
$e_i=4\hat c_2(\lambda)$, $a_i=\Pi C_i\Pi$,
$V_i=\Pi'C_i\Pi$ and $\mathsf R_\Pi=\Pi\mathsf R\Pi$.
Their excitation commutator is the additive identity
\[
[K_\Pi,a_j]+\beta[\mathsf R_\Pi,a_j]
+\beta\sum_i\Pi[C_i^\dagger,C_j]\Pi
=\alpha e_j a_j+\beta\sum_i V_i^\dagger V_j.
\]
The full commutator $[C_i^\dagger,C_j]$ reads the sum's unit
at disjoint plaquette boundaries and acts on their boundary
union otherwise.

\emph{The summed creation commutator.} Write $m:=\#\bar L$,
$A_p:=\sum_{\lambda\in\bar L}C_{p,\lambda}$,
$\mathsf A:=\sum_p A_p$, $J_p:=A_pA_p^\dagger$, and let
$N$ be the plaquette count. Write $p\sim q$ at distinct
plaquettes whose boundaries share a link, and let $b_p$ count
such $q$ at $p$. The neighbor cap $\eta$ is two on the square
chain and $4k$ on a box, with $k$ the positive predecessor
of $\nu$ (Definition~\ref{def:ground}); then $b_p\le\eta$.
At
\[
T_{pq}:=[A_p^\dagger,A_q],\qquad
\mathsf L:=NmI-[\mathsf A^\dagger,\mathsf A],
\]
the action $\mathsf L$ is self-adjoint in the pairing and reads
\[
\mathsf L=\sum_p(mQ_p+J_p)
-\sum_{p<q,\ p\sim q}(T_{pq}+T_{pq}^\dagger).
\]
Each of $mQ_p-J_p$ and
$m(Q_p+Q_q)\mathbin{\pm}(T_{pq}+T_{pq}^\dagger)$
is positive semidefinite in the stated pairing. The identities
\begin{align*}
\mathsf L+m\sum_p b_pQ_p
&=\sum_p(mQ_p+J_p)
+\sum_{p<q,\ p\sim q}
\big(m(Q_p+Q_q)-T_{pq}-T_{pq}^\dagger\big),\\
m\sum_p(2+b_p)Q_p-\mathsf L
&=\sum_p(mQ_p-J_p)
+\sum_{p<q,\ p\sim q}
\big(m(Q_p+Q_q)+T_{pq}+T_{pq}^\dagger\big)
\end{align*}
are positive folds. At every total-content cutoff, with
$a:=\Pi\mathsf A\Pi$, $V:=\Pi'\mathsf A\Pi$ and
$\mathsf L_\Pi:=\Pi\mathsf L\Pi$, they give
\begin{gather*}
[a^\dagger,a]+V^\dagger V+\mathsf L_\Pi=NmI_\Pi,\\
f_*\mathsf L_\Pi+m\nu\eta\mathsf E_\Pi\succeq0,
\qquad
m\nu(\eta+2)\mathsf E_\Pi-f_*\mathsf L_\Pi\succeq0.
\end{gather*}

\emph{The remainder at the cutoff boundary.} Let
$U_R:=\Pi'\mathsf R\Pi$, $a_*:=\nu d_L$, and let $Z$ be the
electric solve on the complementary index,
\[
\mathsf E_{\Pi'}Z=U_R.
\]
Every complementary configuration has positive content, so
the solve reads its column at each content $c$ at the pair
$[\,1:c\,]$. Then
\[
f_*^2 U_R^\dagger Z\preceq a_*^2\mathsf E_\Pi,
\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}
a_*^2\mathsf E_\Pi&f_*U_R^\dagger V\\
f_*V^\dagger U_R&V^\dagger\mathsf E_{\Pi'}V
\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
\]
the block read in the direct-sum pairing. Here $U=U_R+V$,
the full magnetic boundary map above. With
$a_e:=\sum_i e_i a_i$, the summed excitation identity is
\[
[K_\Pi,a]+\beta NmI_\Pi+\beta\Pi[\mathsf R,\mathsf A]\Pi
=\alpha a_e+\beta\mathsf L_\Pi+\beta U^\dagger V.
\]
The full commutator $[\mathsf R,\mathsf A]$ is the fold of
$[Q_p\mathsf M_pQ_p,A_q]$ over $p=q$ and $p\sim q$.

\emph{The creator's input cutoff.} At an output cutoff $C$
and a creator $i=(p,\lambda)$ with $e_i\le C$, let
$\Pi_i^-$ project onto the input contents $c$ at
$c+e_i\le C$. This is the window at the gap between
$e_i$ and $C$ where $e_i<C$, and the unit line where
$e_i=C$. Write
\[
\mathcal C_i:=C_i\Pi_i^-,\qquad
K_i^-:=\Pi_i^-K\Pi_i^-.
\]
Then $\Pi C_i=C_i\Pi_i^-$, and the rectangular action reads
\[
K_\Pi\mathcal C_i-\mathcal C_iK_i^-
=\alpha e_i\mathcal C_i-\beta\Pi[\mathsf M,C_i]\Pi_i^-.
\]
At the two windows' ground levels $e:=\varepsilon_0$ and
$e_i^-$, let $\delta_i$ be the gap at $e+\delta_i=e_i^-$,
the vacant read at equality. It sits on its upper side or
at equal members, and the two level-gap actions satisfy
\[
D_\Pi\mathcal C_i-\mathcal C_iD_i^-
=(\alpha e_i+\delta_i)\mathcal C_i
-\beta\Pi[\mathsf M,C_i]\Pi_i^-.
\]
The full magnetic commutator reads at the local fold
\[
[\mathsf M,C_i]
=\sum_{q:\ \partial q\cap\partial p\ne\varnothing}
[\mathsf M_q,C_i].
\]
At $C<e_i$ the output $\Pi C_i$ reads the sum's unit.
\begin{proof}
The two multiplication orders agree before projection
(Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}). Inserting $\Pi+\Pi'=1$ between
their factors gives
\[
\mathsf M_\Pi A_\Pi+\Pi\mathsf M\Pi'A\Pi
=A_\Pi \mathsf M_\Pi+\Pi A\Pi'\mathsf M\Pi.
\]
The two boundary terms are $U^\dagger V_A$ and
$V_{A^\dagger}^{\dagger}U$, since $\mathsf M$ is self-adjoint.
The electric member preserves the cutoff, so
$\Pi\mathsf E\Pi'=\Pi'\mathsf E\Pi$ reads the sum's unit and
$[\mathsf E_\Pi,A_\Pi]=\Pi[\mathsf E,A]\Pi$. The weighted difference of the
two commutators is the first display. Applying it to the ground
uses $K_\Pi\psi=\varepsilon_0\psi$ and gives $J_A$.
The complementary part of $K\psi$ is $(\beta U\psi)^{\vee}$,
the electric image inside the window. The full multiplication
commutator is $[K,A]=\alpha[\mathsf E,A]$, so applying it to $\psi$
gives the residual display. Inserting $\Pi+\Pi'$ into $AB$
gives both product recurrences; the electric recurrence follows
from $\mathsf E$ preserving both projections, its action at each content
the content's scalar (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}). Every product
is evaluated at its finite target window, with a larger window
holding the required images reading its entries at their summand
injections (Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}).

For the disjoint-support read, the three partial-content
selections commute, each a selection of the configuration
index. Multiplication by $A$ fixes the labels on $T$ and
on the further links, and multiplication by $B$ fixes
those on $R$ and on the further links
(Definition~\ref{def:algebra}; Construction~\ref{con:coeff}).
Thus an input at $(a,c,q)$ reaching $(a',c',q)$ in the
order $BA$ has intermediate content $(a',c,q)$, and
the order $AB$ has intermediate content $(a,c',q)$.
Inserting the total-content projection between the two
factors multiplies the first block by $u$ and the second
by $v$. The full products agree
(Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}), giving the displayed
balance pair. Distinct further-link contents give blocks
at the sum's unit in both orders.

For two increasing moves, each intermediate total is at
or below the output total. For two decreasing moves,
each is at or below the input total. At one unchanged
partial content the intermediate totals are the input
and output totals. Both comparisons therefore hold in
these cases. At $a<a',c'<c$ the second intermediate
total is at or below the input total, giving $v=1$;
at $a'<a,c<c'$ the first is, giving $u=1$.
In the first case write $a+x=a'$ and $c'+y=c$
at positive gaps $x,y$. The larger intermediate content
is $U=a'+c$. Its gaps above the input and output
contents are $x$ and $y$, respectively, so its gap
above their larger member $L$ is $\min\{x,y\}$.
The smaller intermediate content is at or below the
input, so the two cutoff counts differ exactly where
the larger intermediate content is beyond the cutoff,
while the input and output are admitted:
$q+L\le C<q+U$. The second case exchanges the two
intermediate contents, with the two counts exchanged
and the gap again the lesser moved gap. At the right
endpoint both counts read one; at the left the input
and output are admitted and the larger intermediate
content is beyond the cutoff.
Finally, inserting $\Pi+\Pi'=I$ into $BA=AB$ gives
\[
[B_\Pi,A_\Pi]+\Pi B\Pi'A\Pi-\Pi A\Pi'B\Pi=0.
\]
This is the boundary summand's stated read at the
plaquette, its Hamiltonian weight the factor $\beta$
in $[K_\Pi,A_\Pi]$.

At the raising family, $\Pi A_i\Pi'=0$, since $C<c$ gives
$C<c+e_i$ at the cutoff $C$; the adjoint
read is $\Pi'A_i^\dagger\Pi=0$. The two products therefore read
\[
\Pi A_i^\dagger A_j\Pi=a_i^\dagger a_j+V_i^\dagger V_j,
\qquad \Pi A_jA_i^\dagger\Pi=a_ja_i^\dagger.
\]
Their difference is the displayed commutator identity. The
boundary form collects by the pairing's additivity to the
self-pairing of the images' sum, on its upper side or at equal
members; its split reads the upper side throughout
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}; Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).

At $P_p$, multiplication by a closure character puts its
nonunit label on all four boundary links. Thus
$P_p\mathsf M_pP_p=0$. Inserting $P_p+Q_p=1$ on both sides
of $\mathsf M_p$ gives its three displayed terms, with
$\mathsf M_pP_p=\sum_\lambda C_{p,\lambda}$ and
$P_p\mathsf M_p=\sum_\lambda C_{p,\lambda}^\dagger$ at the
closure's involution (Construction~\ref{con:fusion};
Definition~\ref{def:pencil}). The created boundary's content is
$4\hat c_2(\lambda)$, joined to the input's content at its
further links, so its commutator with the electric action is the
displayed multiple (Definition~\ref{def:carrier};
Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}). The inputs at $P_p$ are independent
of the boundary links' coefficient variables, so their product
pairings factor over those links; character orthogonality gives
$\langle C_{p,\lambda}x,C_{p,\mu}y\rangle
=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\langle P_px,P_py\rangle$
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}; Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}).
This is the adjoint product read. At disjoint boundaries the
character multiplications and index projections commute. At a
shared link, the first creation puts a nonunit label there,
which the second creation's $P_p$ reads at the sum's unit.
The compressed product is the full product's compression,
$\Pi C_i\Pi C_j\Pi=\Pi C_iC_j\Pi$, since
$\Pi C_i\Pi'=0$ at the positive content shift, so the
commutation holds at the cutoff.

The plaquette form cap gives
$|\langle Q_px,\mathsf M_pQ_px\rangle_G|
\le d_L\langle Q_px,Q_px\rangle_G$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:loopcap}). The projections $Q_p$ are diagonal
on the configuration index. Their sum reads at a configuration
the count of plaquettes whose boundaries meet its support,
at or below $\nu$ times its occupied link count: each such
plaquette contains an occupied link, and each occupied link
belongs to at most $\nu$ plaquettes. The content is at or
beyond $f_*$ times that link count
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}), so
\[
f_*\sum_p\langle Q_px,Q_px\rangle_G
\le\nu\langle x,\mathsf E x\rangle_G.
\]
The plaquette caps sum to the remainder's read by the magnitude
triangle read (Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}). The projections
$P_p,Q_p$ commute with the total-content projection, all three
diagonal on the index, so the displayed comparisons restrict to
every cutoff by compression (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).
Substitute the plaquette split into
$K_\Pi=\alpha\mathsf E_\Pi-\beta\mathsf M_\Pi$.
The compressed creators commute, their electric commutator is
the content shift, and their adjoint commutator is the full
commutator less $V_i^\dagger V_j$, giving the excitation
display. At disjoint boundaries the adjoint's multiplication
and projection commute with the creator's, each reading the
other boundary's labels unchanged; at intersecting boundaries
both compositions act on the union's links alone.

The character orthogonality gives $A_p^\dagger A_p=mP_p$.
Its image sits in $Q_p$, each closure label nonunit on every
boundary link, so $0\preceq J_p\preceq mQ_p$:
at occupied $m$, the map $[\,1:m\,]J_p$ is the orthogonal
projector onto that image, its square its own at
$A_pP_p=A_p$ and $A_p^\dagger A_p=mP_p$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). At a vacant closure the creation
and remainder maps read the sum's unit, and the displayed
comparisons read equal members.

Fix $p\sim q$. A shared link gives
$P_pA_q=P_qA_p=A_p^\dagger P_q=A_q^\dagger P_p=0$.
Put $X:=A_p^\dagger A_q$ and $Y:=A_qA_p^\dagger$.
Their support reads are
\[
X=P_pXP_q,\qquad Y=Q_pYQ_q.
\]
The input parts and output parts are orthogonal. Each map's
squared action is capped at $m^2$ on its input part, the
two factors each capped at $m$ in squared action by the
adjoint product read. Thus for $T:=X-Y=T_{pq}$,
$T^\dagger T\preceq m^2I$, the two output squares adding.
Also
\[
TP_p=0,\qquad P_qT=0,\qquad T=Q_qTQ_p.
\]
For the first read, $YP_p=0$ by $A_p^\dagger P_p=0$.
In $XP_p$, a boundary link of $p$ outside $q$ starts at
the unit label and keeps it under $A_q$; multiplication
in $A_p^\dagger$ puts a nonunit label there, whose $P_p$
projection is the sum's unit. Such a link exists for
distinct square plaquettes of the chain or box
(Construction~\ref{con:lattice}). For the second read,
$P_qY=0$ and a boundary link of $q$ outside $p$ keeps
its created nonunit label under $A_p^\dagger$, giving
$P_qX=0$. It follows that
$m^2Q_p-T^\dagger T\succeq0$. At either side $s=1$ or
its balance partner, the identity
\[
m\big(m(Q_p+Q_q)+s(T+T^\dagger)\big)
=(mQ_q+sT)^\dagger(mQ_q+sT)
+m^2Q_p-T^\dagger T
\]
is a positive fold, giving the two stated comparisons at
occupied $m$ by positive rescaling
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).

The diagonal terms of $[\mathsf A^\dagger,\mathsf A]$
are $mP_p-J_p$ and the disjoint-boundary terms read the
sum's unit. The intersecting pair's two terms are
$T_{pq}+T_{pq}^\dagger$, so the displayed expression for
$\mathsf L$ follows at $P_p+Q_p=I$. Regrouping the
neighbor counts gives the two positive folds. A square's
four links each meet at most $\nu-1$ further plaquettes;
on the square chain only the preceding and following squares
meet it, so $b_p\le\eta$. With
$f_*\sum_pQ_p\preceq\nu\mathsf E$, the earlier support
count, the folds give the two electric comparisons.
Compression keeps their positive reads
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). Summing the raising-family
commutator identity over both indices gives its stated
instance at $a$, $V$ and $\mathsf L_\Pi$.

For the remainder solve, read in one finite target window
holding the input and its $\mathsf R$-image
(Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}). The remainder and its
adjoint read the unit line at the sum's unit, since each
term has $Q_p$ at both ends. On the occupied index let
$\mathsf E_o$ be the electric action and $\mathsf R_o$
the target's remainder compression. The electric action is
positive definite there (Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}), and
$a_*\mathsf E_o\mathbin{\pm}f_*\mathsf R_o\succeq0$
by the remainder comparison. The block
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
a_*\mathsf E_o&f_*\mathsf R_o\\
f_*\mathsf R_o&a_*\mathsf E_o
\end{pmatrix}
\]
therefore reads positive at the sum and difference of its
two input vectors. At the positive electric pivot its
deflation, rescaled by $a_*$, gives
\[
a_*^2\mathsf E_o-f_*^2\mathsf R_o W\succeq0,
\qquad \mathsf E_oW=\mathsf R_o,
\]
the solve of Definition~\ref{def:elim} at each positive
content. The middle electric solve preserves the cutoff
and its complement. Its pairing at the remainder image
splits into the two positive parts, so restricting to the
complementary part gives the displayed comparison at
$U_R$ and $Z$, with the unit input's read the sum's unit.
The block in the statement is the $\mathsf E_{\Pi'}$-Gram
of the two maps $(f_*Z,V)$ joined to its upper diagonal
defect $a_*^2\mathsf E_\Pi-f_*^2U_R^\dagger Z$:
the solve reads $Z^\dagger\mathsf E_{\Pi'}Z=U_R^\dagger Z$
and $Z^\dagger\mathsf E_{\Pi'}V=U_R^\dagger V$.
Both terms are positive semidefinite
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).

Every creation raises content, so
$\Pi'\mathsf A^\dagger\Pi=\Pi\mathsf A\Pi'=0$.
The plaquette split gives $U=U_R+V$, and inserting
$\Pi+\Pi'=I$ in the remainder's commutator gives
\[
[\mathsf R_\Pi,a]+U_R^\dagger V
=\Pi[\mathsf R,\mathsf A]\Pi.
\]
Substitute this identity and
$\Pi[\mathsf A^\dagger,\mathsf A]\Pi=NmI_\Pi-\mathsf L_\Pi$
in the sum of the excitation identities. The two boundary
terms join to $(U_R+V)^\dagger V=U^\dagger V$,
giving the stated identity. The factors of
$Q_p\mathsf M_pQ_p$ and $A_q$ act on disjoint link
variables where $p$ and $q$ have disjoint boundaries,
so their commutator reads the sum's unit there.

For the input-cutoff read, a creator's image at input
content $c$ has content $c+e_i$. The output projection
therefore gives $\Pi C_i=C_i\Pi_i^-$, including the unit
input at $C=e_i$, with every image beyond $C$ at $C<e_i$.
The input projection is a subprojection of the output's.
Inserting these identities gives
\[
K_\Pi\mathcal C_i-\mathcal C_iK_i^-
=\Pi K C_i\Pi_i^--\Pi C_iK\Pi_i^-
=\Pi[K,C_i]\Pi_i^-.
\]
The electric commutator is $e_iC_i$, giving the stated
identity at the pencil's weights. Compression raises the
least root (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}; Lemma~\ref{lem:split}),
so $e_i^-\ge e$ and its gap $\delta_i$ has the stated side.
Substitute $K_\Pi=eI+D_\Pi$ and
$K_i^-=e_i^-I+D_i^-$ to obtain the level-gap identity.
A plaquette multiplication on links disjoint from
$\partial p$ commutes with both the character factor of
$C_i$ and its projection $P_p$, giving the displayed local
fold. Every composition reads in its finite target window
(Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}).
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[The state space]\label{lem:statespace}
The word sector is the state's own space: at a window ground
$\psi$ and carrier elements $A$, $B$,
\[
\omega(\bar A\,B)\;=\;\langle A\psi,\,B\psi\rangle\ ,
\]
the pairing on the word sector the state's, and the sector is
$\mathrm{Sect}_\infty\,\psi$, its own image
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), cyclic by construction.
\begin{proof}
Both sides are the read $\mathrm{Eval}(\bar A\,B\,\bar\psi\,\psi)$,
the left at the pairing identity and the right at the
involution's product read, the products' one value under
commutativity joining the two
(Definition~\ref{def:algebra}; Proposition~\ref{prop:algebra}).
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The level is attained at a word image]\label{lem:attained}
At a window, a window ground $\psi$ (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}) and the located edge $\gamma$ of
the level condition over the word sector
(Theorem~\ref{thm:levelequiv}; the window cut's own read at
$\gamma=E_0\kappa$, Definition~\ref{def:K}): \emph{(i)} the edge is
the compressed pair's least root; \emph{(ii)} a word image reads the
two moments at equality there, the first positive; \emph{(iii)} at
the window's spectral read at the edge the state's weight sits at
the level, a divisor point.

\emph{(i) The edge is the compressed pair's least root.} The compression
is finite-dimensional with pair entries
(Proposition~\ref{prop:windowfinite}; Theorem~\ref{thm:pairpencil}),
and $(S)_\Lambda$, the compression of the level gap, is
positive semidefinite, a compression keeping the read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), with the ground inside its kernel block;
off the kernel block, on the split's upper-side columns, $(S)_\Lambda$
is positive definite (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), and the level
condition's members are the levels at or below the least root of
the pair $\big((SD)_\Lambda:\gamma\,(S)_\Lambda\big)$
there, the located edge that root, the window cut's own edge at
$\gamma=E_0\kappa$.

\emph{(ii) Its kernel point is a word image, and the two moments read
equal members there.} At the edge the site datum $Z$ at the join
$\gamma\,(S)_\Lambda=(SD)_\Lambda+Z$ has a kernel
point $y$ off the sum's unit
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}'s kernel block at a located root), a vector
of the word sector's window projection and hence $\Pi A\psi$
at a word $A$, whose moments read that projection, and
\[
\mu_2(A)\;=\;\gamma\,\mu_1(A)\ ,
\qquad\mu_1(A)\ \text{positive},
\]
the moments read at coefficient one on the multiplication probes'
vectors (Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone};
Corollary~\ref{cor:momentdivisor}). The level-$\gamma$ requirement
therefore holds at equality at that one word, the detector pair's
edge its neutral point (Theorem~\ref{thm:detector}), and the floor
over the probes (Theorem~\ref{thm:momentform}) is met at a probe of
its own. The edge sits off equal members with it.

\emph{(iii) At the window's spectral read the weight sits at the level, a
divisor point.} Where the window reads
$\mathrm{spec}(H)\subset\{\varepsilon_0\}\cup
[\varepsilon_0+\gamma,\infty)$, the jump comparisons' own object
(Theorem~\ref{thm:flatstep}) and the cut's identification at every
ground (Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut};
Lemma~\ref{lem:sectorspan}), the two moments are the weight folds
over the located spectrum (Theorem~\ref{thm:detector}), the split's
congruence diagonalizing the gram and the pencil at once
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), the level gap acting at the gaps
$\lambda_j$ there and its square at their squares, the weights
$w_j$ the coordinates' squares against the gram's upper-side
diagonal entries, and
\[
\mu_1(A)=\sum_jw_j\,\lambda_j\ ,\qquad
\mu_2(A)=\sum_jw_j\,\lambda_j^{\,2}\ ,\qquad
\big\langle\,\mu_2(A)\!:\!\gamma\,\mu_1(A)\,\big\rangle
\;=\;\sum_j w_j\,\lambda_j\,
\big\langle\,\lambda_j\!:\!\gamma\,\big\rangle\ ;
\]
at every occupied weight
$\lambda_j$ is the kernel point's read or the level $\gamma$
exactly, and $\mu_1(A)$ positive puts an occupied weight at
$\gamma$. The level is then a located root of the window pencil, a
point of its divisor at that root's multiplicity
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}; Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(i)), the word
image's weight there positive, and its state is the word sector's
own, the state's space (Lemma~\ref{lem:statespace}).

\emph{(iv) The probe cap.} At a probe $A$ whose two moments read the
pair $(\mu_2(A)\!:\!\gamma\,\mu_1(A))$ on its lower side, a located
root of the compressed pair sits off the kernel point below
$\gamma$; the
edge, the least such root ((i)), sits at or below
$\mu_2(A)$ against $\mu_1(A)$ at every probe with positive first
moment, one pair comparison per probe. At its read against
$E_0$ this caps the global edge, the meet at or below the window cut
(Definition~\ref{def:K}). At a fixed region,
a pair $u$ and a constructed cutoff key, a probe family
with positive first moments and
$\mu_2(A_C)\le E_0u\,\mu_1(A_C)$ at every further cutoff
gives a regional upper cap $u$, hence a cap on the global
edge (Definition~\ref{def:K}). Each moment is read at
that cutoff's actual ground.
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i)} $\psi$ is the unit's own word image and $D\psi$ the sum's
unit (Definition~\ref{def:algebra}; Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), so
the ground sits inside the kernel block. A
kernel point $y$ of $(S)_\Lambda$ reads its self-pairing at
equal members, so $Sy$ and its Gram solve $Dy$ read the sum's unit: $S$ is
positive semidefinite (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}) and its split
reads the pairing as the fold over the blocks
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), a fold of equal members putting the
coordinates off the kernel block at the sum's unit, so $y$ sits in
that block's span and its image with it. Then
$(SD)_\Lambda$ reads its row at $y$ at the sum's unit as
well, the pencil symmetric with
$x^{\mathsf T}SDy=\langle Dx,Dy\rangle_G$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:pairpencil}): both compressions sit on the
split's own columns off the kernel block, the upper-side columns,
where $(S)_\Lambda$ is positive
definite. There Lemma~\ref{lem:split}
splits the pair
$\big((SD)_\Lambda:\gamma\,(S)_\Lambda\big)$ over
located roots, $\mathrm{count}(a)$ the roots below $a$: at $\gamma$
at or below the least root the roots sit at or beyond the level and
the pair is positive semidefinite, the congruence's diagonal
$\langle x\!:\!\varepsilon_j\rangle\,g_j$ reading its upper side or
equal members there, the least root's own read the sharpened one
(Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct}(1)),
while beyond that root the count is at least one and
Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct}(2) reads the count's own witness off
the elimination. So the level condition's
members are the levels at or below the least root and the located
edge is that root.
\emph{(ii)} The kernel point is a vector of the word sector's
window projection, the image of $A\mapsto\Pi A\psi$, a linear map
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}; Theorem~\ref{thm:momentform}); $y$
sits on the split's upper-side columns, where the compressed level gap is
positive definite, so its first moment is positive, and the kernel
read gives the second at the level's multiple. At equal members
the second moment reads them, its display
$\langle Dy,Dy\rangle_G$ putting $Dy$ at the
sum's unit at the positive pairing
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}) and the first moment at equal members
with it, against its positivity: the edge sits off equal members.
\emph{(iii)} Every $\lambda_j$ is the kernel point's read or sits at or beyond
$\gamma$, so every summand of the fold reads its upper side or equal
members, while the display above reads its left side at equal
members: gaps add over a fold, and a natural fold reads the sum's
unit exactly where every summand does
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}), so at every occupied weight
$\lambda_j$ is the kernel point's read or the level $\gamma$
exactly.
\emph{(iv)} The level condition fails at $\gamma$ at that one probe,
so the operator inequality fails on the sector
(Theorem~\ref{thm:levelequiv}) and the split's congruence reads
a root of the level gap's own pencil off the kernel point below
the level (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}; Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}).
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{The window ground}

\begin{theorem}[The window multiplicity is a count, and the count is a
divisor read]\label{thm:SO}
On a window the ground multiplicity $\dim\ker S$ is one
integer, a count at a designation's data; it is the ground
root's multiplicity, one integer per cell of the crossing divisor,
reading $1$ at the free end and over its attached cell, and
moving across a located boundary only at a ground collision, the
boundary's own two-sided read
(Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(ii),(iii)). At a root-coordinate
segment from the free end on which the window cut admits one
fixed pair $\kappa$, the ground multiplicity is one throughout
(Definition~\ref{def:K}; Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}). Where the window read is $1$, a
symmetry of the window, an orthogonal map commuting with the pencil,
maps the ground line to itself at a graded read, $g\psi=\psi$ at
even and $g\psi+\psi$ the sum's unit at odd, the reads of $\omega$
blind to the grading.
\begin{proof}
\emph{The multiplicity is a count.}
A window compression is finite-dimensional with pair entries
(Proposition~\ref{prop:windowfinite}), and
$\mathrm{count}(a)=\operatorname{rev}(H\!:\!aG)$ counts its eigenvalues with
multiplicity below $a$, exact over the pairs by $\mathrm{LDL}^{\mathsf T}$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct}; the multiplicity read is
Lemma~\ref{lem:split}). Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep} gives a pair
$\delta$ below the separation of the pencil pair's site-datum
determinant's distinct located roots (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}'s $\chi$),
and a designation at that width (Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct})
reads levels $l<h$ at a gap at most $\delta$,
the pencil pair at $l$ positive semidefinite and
$\mathrm{count}(h)\ge1$. The bracket is narrower than the separation, so it
admits the ground root alone and
\[
\dim\ker S\;=\;\mathrm{count}(h) ,
\]
one count at the designation's data.

\emph{The count is a divisor read.} The multiplicity is the ground
root's order in the pencil determinant, the split's diagonal read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), and
Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(ii),(iii) lock it: one integer per cell of
the crossing divisor, read $1$ from the free end's level bracket over
the attached cell (every configuration's content is positive, the
unit's line the ground, Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend}), and one two-sided bracket read at
each located boundary.

\emph{The interval read.} Fix a pair $t=[\,a:b\,]$ in the
segment and write $\gamma:=E_0\kappa=[\,g:h\,]$ and
$W:=\#p\,d_L$ for the window's magnetic form cap
(Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}). The natural
$J:=1+8W a^2h$ satisfies $8Wt^2<J\gamma$, the comparison
cleared at $b^2g\ge1$. Subdivide from the free end to $t$ at
$t_j=[\,ja:Jb\,]$ for $1\le j\le J$, with $t_0$ the free
end. Consecutive pencils differ by a form capped two-sidedly at
\[
\rho_j:=W\langle t_{j+1}^2:t_j^2\rangle
\le[\,2Wt^2:J\,]<[\,\gamma:4\,]
\qquad (j<J).
\]
Their least roots $e_j,e_{j+1}$ satisfy
$e_j\le e_{j+1}+\rho_j$ and $e_{j+1}\le e_j+\rho_j$,
the form comparisons read at the least roots
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}; Lemma~\ref{lem:split}). The count
sandwich from those comparisons is
\[
\operatorname{count}_{j}(x-\rho_j)
\le\operatorname{count}_{j+1}(x)
\le\operatorname{count}_{j}(x+\rho_j).
\]
At $x=e_j+[\,\gamma:2\,]$, both outer levels sit strictly
between $e_j$ and $e_j+\gamma$, while $x$ sits strictly between
$e_{j+1}$ and $e_{j+1}+\gamma$. The cut's spectral read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}) makes the outer counts the ground
multiplicity at $j$ and the middle count the ground multiplicity
at $j+1$, so they agree. The free-end multiplicity is one and
induction over the $J$ steps gives that value at $t$. The
subdivision reads the window's cap; the returned count is one
at every window holding the interval read.

\emph{The character.} At a window read of $1$, a symmetry $g$ has
$Kg=gK$ at $GK=H$ (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), so it preserves the ground eigenspace, which is the line; an
orthogonal map on a line is a scalar $c$ at $c^2=1$
($g^{\dagger}g=1$), so $c=1$ or $c+1$ reads equal members; and
$\omega(g^{\dagger}Ag)=\langle g\psi,\,A\,g\psi\rangle_G
=c^2\,\omega(A)=\omega(A)$: the state reads its ground twice, an even
count, blind to the grading.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{The integer constants}

With every pair at one value across the form's scales
(Proposition~\ref{prop:form}), every
constant below is literally an integer or a fusion pair: $4$ (links
per plaquette, the module energy); $2d$ (the neighbor count,
Construction~\ref{con:lattice}'s direction read); the winding floor $\hat c_2(\omega_{c_i})$ per cell and charged
direction, the charged margin's growth (Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}); and the cells'
entries and levels, located roots and jump distances of the decimation's own
divisors, outputs rather than constants. The residue enters through
one pair, $\hat c_2(f)=[\,r(r+2):2d_f^{\,2}\,]$, the minimal content,
its two reads the floor's product (Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}) and the
clearing's count (Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}) at the one-value
identity $r(r+2)+1=d_f^{\,2}$, the $A$-series' read with the
member floors the end lists' (Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}); the
adjoint read against it is the
invariant $[\,2d_f^{\,2}:r(r+2)\,]$, and every further residue read of
the chain is a coordinate read of the cell calculus

\section{The permutation presentation}

\begin{construction}[States]\label{con:states}
Fix a factor list $F=(v_1,\dots,v_m)$, each \emph{factor} a
variable $v_i$ with its \emph{dagger read}, undaggered or daggered,
a variable a link's matrix at the coefficient carrier
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}). To a permutation
$\pi\in S_m$ associate
\[
\Phi_\pi\;=\;\prod_{\text{cycles } (i_1\,i_2\cdots i_k)\ \text{of}\ \pi}
\tr\!\big(M_{i_1}M_{i_2}\cdots M_{i_k}\big),
\]
$M_i$ reading $v_i$ at an undaggered factor and $v_i^{\dagger}$ at a
daggered.
States are the $\Phi_\pi$'s combinations at polynomial-pair
coefficients in the residue (Lemma~\ref{lem:genericlift}). The
states' product is the sites' concatenation: two generators
multiply at the joined factor list, the second wiring's places
shifted by the first list's count, the joined wiring the two
blocks, and the coefficients multiply, the trace polynomials' own
product; the two block orders read one word multiset, the blocks'
exchange a letter-preserving relabeling of the joined list with
the joined wiring composed at it, the product's identities one
value at either order (Remark~\ref{rem:kernel}). Equivalently
$\pi(i)=j$ records that the row index of factor $i$ is contracted
against the column index of factor $j$. The \emph{evaluation
contraction} withdraws an undaggered factor and a daggered factor
of one link wired at the product, the one's row against the other's
column, splicing the wiring across the pair, the evaluation
identity's read at the wiring (Construction~\ref{con:coeff}), the
word index's relation (Remark~\ref{rem:kernel}). This is the trace-polynomial
reduction of the walled Brauer category: the Schur--Weyl dual
presentation, in which the group enters only as the loop value $d_f$
of the calculus.
\end{construction}

\begin{remark}[The word index, and the presentation kernel]
\label{rem:kernel}
The states are indexed gauge-free by the multisets of oriented cyclic
words in the letters, a variable with its dagger read: $\Phi_\pi$
reads only its cycles' words, each
up to rotation, so the positions of repeated factors are a gauge mode of
the $(\pi,\text{positions})$ spelling, and a state's word coefficient is
the class sum of its $\pi$-coefficients, one finite projection at every
residue. Identities of character polynomials close on the word index outright,
coefficient comparisons per word multiset before any pairing, holding at
every residue; the Gram below enters only at the state reads. The word
index's one further datum is the
\emph{kernel}: the map from word monomials to functions has one, the
evaluation identity
$\sum_jU_{ij}\bar U_{kj}=\delta_{ik}$ (Construction~\ref{con:coeff})
imposing polynomial-pair relations among the $\Phi_\pi$ within a factor
list. All function-level linear algebra is
therefore performed through the pairing's Gram (\S\ref{sec:wg}); the null
space of that Gram is the presentation kernel, computed once per
factor list. Determinant ($\varepsilon$-tensor)
relations are invisible at the symbolic residue; this is precisely the statement that the calculus computes the
generic theory, and it is why $r=1$ is its own window read while $r\ge2$ reads
generically.
\end{remark}

\section{The pairing in the permutation presentation}\label{sec:wg}

\begin{lemma}[The generic lift]\label{lem:genericlift}
A \emph{polynomial pair} in the residue is a pair of ground
polynomials named as Definition~\ref{def:ground}'s constructed
pairs are, read at every natural argument through the members' Horner
reads and across representatives by the cross-multiplied identities;
every entry below is one such pair.
\emph{(i)} A polynomial pair whose reads at
infinitely many naturals are of equal members reads equal members at
every argument.
\emph{(ii)} A matrix of polynomial pairs whose evaluation at infinitely many
residues is the Gram of an independent list has its determinant pair
off equal members at each such residue and as a polynomial pair, and
every unit read is solved by the adjugate column against the
determinant (Definition~\ref{def:elim}'s minors), the identity
$\mathsf M\,\mathrm{adj}(\mathsf M)=\det(\mathsf M)\,1$ the
solved witness's whole verification.
\emph{(iii)} A polynomial pair keeps one side beyond its members'
largest located root, the leading-coefficient read at
Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s leading-term bound: the settled side,
one decidable read per pair.
\emph{(iv)} A claim whose per-residue reads are the sides and
equal-member reads of finitely many polynomial pairs in the residue
therefore holds at
every residue beyond their computed radii once its symbolic reads
hold, and the finitely many residues at or below the radii are each
their own window read.
\emph{(v) The rank read.} An \emph{exponential-polynomial pair} in a
natural $\ell$ is a finite fold $\sum_{k\le K}p_k(\ell)\,2^{k\ell}$ at
polynomial pairs $p_k$, read at every natural, two such folds' sums
and products folds again at the keys' sums; at $p_K$ off equal
members it keeps one side beyond a \emph{computed natural}, the top
polynomial's settled side: at $B$ the radius of $p_K$ and $c$ its
\emph{leading margin} at the radius, the leading term's magnitude
there against the further terms' magnitudes' fold
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s leading-term bound), $F$ the tail
coefficients' magnitudes' fold over the keys below $K$ and $m$ the
tail's largest degree, the computed natural is the least natural at
or beyond $B$ and $4m^{2}$ holding the comparison
$c\,2^{\ell}>F\,\ell^{m}$, its witness the larger of $4(m+1)^{2}$,
$B$ and the natural at or beyond $[\,F:c\,]$, the division's quotient
at its successor (Definition~\ref{def:ground}), and beyond it
the tail's magnitude sits below the top's, the settled side, one
decidable read per pair; and (iv) holds at exponential-polynomial
pairs, the polynomial instance's derivation at the rank read, the
naturals at or below the computed one each their own read.
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i)} The pair's cross datum against the pair of equal
members, its first member against its second, is one ground
polynomial reading equal members at every stated natural, so its
located roots are infinitely many where its coefficients are off
the sum's unit; the roots sit inside
Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s bound, finitely many, so every
coefficient reads the sum's unit and the pair reads equal members
at every argument. \emph{(ii)} At each such residue the
determinant is the Gram's, off equal members at the independence
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}), so the determinant pair's members
differ at infinitely many naturals and (i) lifts the read to the
pair: a pair of equal members as a polynomial reads them at every
argument. \emph{(iii)} The leading term dominates at every point of
margin at or beyond the radius (Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}), so
beyond the largest located root each member keeps its leading
coefficient's side and the pair its leading coefficients'.
\emph{(iv)} Each pair keeps its settled side beyond its radius by
(iii), and a finite family's radii have a largest; the residues at
or below it are finitely many, each an evaluation of the pairs.
\emph{(v)} At a natural $\ell$ at or beyond the radius $B$ the top's
magnitude sits at or beyond its leading margin: at the degree $d$
of $p_K$ the leading term against the further terms is $\ell^{d}$
times the margin read at the powers $\ell^{i-d}$, each at or below
$B^{i-d}$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s magnitude carrier), so the
magnitude of $p_K(\ell)$ sits at or beyond $c\,[\,\ell:B\,]^{d}$, at
or beyond $c$. Clearing $2^{K\ell}$ the fold reads
$p_K(\ell)$ joined to the tail
$\sum_{k<K}p_k(\ell)\,[\,1:2^{(K-k)\ell}\,]$, each summand's
magnitude at or below its coefficients' fold at $\ell^{m}$ against
$2^{\ell}$, so the tail's magnitude sits at or below
$[\,F\,\ell^{m}:2^{\ell}\,]$, below $c$ at the comparison. The
witness: $2^{\ell}$ clears
every power $\ell^{m}$ from the natural $4m^{2}$ on, the seed
$2^{4m^{2}}$ at or beyond $(4m^{2})^{m}$ at the exponents'
comparison $4m^{2}\ge2m+2m^{2}$ with $m\le2^{m}$, and the step
$2\,\ell^{m}\ge(\ell+1)^{m}$ at $\ell\ge2m$, the binomial identity per
key collecting to $(\ell+1)^{m}\le\ell^{m}+m\,(\ell+1)^{m-1}$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s binomial identity) with
$(\ell+1)$ at or beyond $2m$; at the degree $m+1$ this reads
$2^{\ell}\ge\ell\,\ell^{m}$ from $4(m+1)^{2}$ on, and at $\ell$ beyond

against $F\,\ell^{m}$ does, the start $4m^{2}$ at or beyond $2m$, and
the least natural is the stepping read at the witness
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}).
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}
