\section{Resolvent, module deflation, and the presentation kernel}

\begin{construction}[The Feshbach resolvent at polynomial pairs]\label{con:res}
Given a state $y$ on factor list $F$:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,itemsep=1pt]
\item \emph{The deflated side}: for each module presentation
$m$ in $F$ (built as $\chi_{\mathrm{adj}}(W)$ times paired
$[1\!:\!d_f]$-contractions of the other factors), the deflation
$y'$ at the join
$\langle m,m\rangle\,y'+\langle m,y\rangle\,m
=\langle m,m\rangle\,y$, its $m$-pairing reading equal members, the
fold over the presentations in list order, each join at the prior
deflation.
\item \emph{The support}: the union of the $\pi$-support of $y'$ and
of the presentation kernel (Remark~\ref{rem:kernel}), closed
under the $E$-insertions (Proposition~\ref{prop:lap};
Proposition~\ref{prop:link}), the closure after the
union (the insertions map the joined support into it).
\item \emph{The solve}: $S\,x+k=y'$ at a presentation-kernel
member $k$, the member's read the symbolic tag's with a window at
or below the clearance radius reading its own kernel's members
(Proposition~\ref{prop:wg}; Remark~\ref{rem:kernel}), and $S$ the
site datum at the module level, the section's pair
$(E\!:\!4d_f)$'s, one exact
adjugate solve over the polynomial pairs, null-space augmented
with the member the augmentation's read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:genericlift}(ii)), then
\item \emph{The solution's deflation}: the solution's component off
the module space, the join of step 1:
$E$ is diagonal in $\hat c_2$, so at the generic residue every non-module gap
reads unequal members as a polynomial pair and the pair
$(E\!:\!4d_f)$'s site datum has the module space as its kernel. The
result is the Feshbach $Q$-resolvent applied to $y$.
\end{enumerate}
The solve's error is the sum's unit \emph{as a function}: the residual
$w$'s self-pairing reads equal members as a polynomial pair.
\end{construction}

\section{The adjoint walk}

The adjoint's fusion closure of the unit label on a loop window is
one chain of the calculus, the \emph{adjoint walk}, the pencil
$E$ against $M_X:=\sum_i\chi_X(U_i)$ at $\chi_X=\chi_{\mathrm{adj}}$
on the loop labels; its data, its tower and its channel divisor are
the statements of this section and the next, a chain of single-label
shells at unit bonds, the scalar instance of the depth chain's
certificate (Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerblock}; Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerpivot}). The theory's magnetic
member is the magnetic list's plaquette character
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), and the walk enters the derivations
at that instance alone.

\begin{remark}[The adjoint walk's reads]
\label{rem:certtarget}
$\chi_X$ keeps every link's label class, the adjoint at the unit
class (Construction~\ref{con:labels}), so the adjoint's fusion
closure of a configuration keeps every link's class; the walk's
two data are Construction~\ref{con:xfusion}'s, its block reads and
structural identities the displays of Theorem~\ref{thm:xdata},
Theorem~\ref{thm:network} and Theorem~\ref{thm:drift}, and the
scheme bridge of Theorem~\ref{thm:bridge} rescales its coupling
coordinate at $2d_f$.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[The adjoint square's channels]\label{lem:channels}
The blocks of $\theta\otimes\theta$ are, at every residue, the labels
\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathbf 1,\qquad \theta,\qquad 2\theta=(4,2^{\,a}),\\
2\omega_1{+}\omega_2^*=(3,1^{\,b}),\qquad
\omega_2{+}2\omega_1^*=(3,3,2^{\,b}),\qquad
\omega_2{+}\omega_2^*=(2,2,1^{\,e}),
\end{gathered}
\]
named by their weights over the fundamentals and the complements,
$\omega_j$ and $\omega_i^*$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor};
Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(ii)), at the run counts $a$, $b$, $e$ at
$a+2=d_f$, $b+3=d_f$ and $e+4=d_f$, at multiplicities
$1,\,c_1,\,1,\,1,\,1,\,1$,
with $c_1=2$ at $r\ge2$ and $1$ at $r=1$; the outer pair are duals,
the complement arithmetic of Construction~\ref{con:labels} the
manifest swap of the names at $\omega_j^{\ast}=\omega_{j'}$, every
index pair joining to $r+1$, and the other rows are
self-dual. The list runs at every residue with each row entering
at its count $m\,d$: the closed forms read the drops themselves,
the dual
pair's $d$ with the factor $g$ at $g+1=r$, the residue's gap from one,
and the last
row's the root $r=2$, while at $r=1$ the row list is the
alternant read's, the run $4,\dots,d_f{+}1$ of $y$ occupied
exactly at $r\ge2$.
The unit channel enters at count one on the unit line, the
Casimir's kernel point, and the nonunit channels close in
the residue:
\[
\begin{array}{lccc}
\text{label} & m & d & \hat c_2\\
\hline
\theta & c_1 & r\,(r+2) & 1\\
2\theta & 1 & [\,(r+1)^2r\,(r+4):4\,] & [\,2r+4:r+1\,]\\
2\omega_1{+}\omega_2^*,\ \omega_2{+}2\omega_1^* & 1 &
[\,g\,r\,(r+2)(r+3):4\,]_{\,g+1=r} & 2\\
\omega_2{+}\omega_2^* & 1 & [\,(r+1)^2(r+2)\,w:4\,]_{\,w+2=r} & [\,2r:r+1\,]
\end{array}
\]
with the two closure identities
\[
\sum_Rm_Rd_R=r^2(r+2)^2,
\qquad
\sum_Rm_Rd_R\,\hat c_2(R)=2\,r^2(r+2)^2 ,
\]
the displayed reads of the proof, the sums over all blocks with the
unit channel's count one among them and its Casimir term's members
equal. The module's distances close in the residue as well:
against $\hat c_2(\theta)=1$, the gaps of the Casimir column read
$1$ at the unit channel and at the dual pair,
$[\,g:r+1\,]$ at $\omega_2{+}\omega_2^*$ over its gap witness
$g+1=r$, and $[\,r+3:r+1\,]$ at
$2\theta$, at the cross-multiplied witnesses $2r=(r+1)+g$ and
$2r+4=(r+1)+(r+3)$: each gap is positive at its row's residues,
one symbolic read at every one of them.
\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:steinberg} at $a=b=\theta$: a permutation contributes
where the tie $\nu_\sigma+\sigma(\theta+u)=c+u$ meets a
shifted content of $\theta$, $u$ the unit set's sorted display,
$(1^{d_f})$ at multiplicity $r$ or its letter-pair moves at one each
(Lemma~\ref{lem:adjchar}), so, writing $y:=\theta+u+(1^{d_f})$, of value
multiset $\{2,4,5,\dots,d_f{+}1,\,d_f{+}3\}$, a label contributes only where
the strictly decreasing $c+u$ rearranges $y$ or $y$ with one entry
raised and one lowered by $1$, the result's entries distinct. Equality is
$c=\theta$ at matched degree, the count $2$ at $2+g=r$ against the
run's adjacent value pairs, $g$ their count: the identity's
read $r$ at the unit-monomial content on the even side against one odd
transposition per adjacent
value pair, the pairs sitting in the run $4,\dots,d_f{+}1$. The modifications
with distinct entries are exactly five: $2\to3$ with $d_f{+}3\to d_f{+}2$
(the unit label at matched degree); $2\to1$ with $d_f{+}3\to d_f{+}4$
($2\theta$); $4\to3$ with $d_f{+}3\to d_f{+}4$ ($2\omega_1{+}\omega_2^*$);
$2\to1$ with
$d_f{+}1\to d_f{+}2$ ($\omega_2{+}2\omega_1^*$); $4\to3$ with $d_f{+}1\to d_f{+}2$
($\omega_2{+}\omega_2^*$); every other
raise or lowering collides with an occupied value, the adjacent swaps
returning the equality case. Each modification preserves the decreasing
order, so the aligning permutation is the identity and each count is
one, on the even side. At $r=2$ the run $4,\dots,d_f{+}1$ is the single value $4$, so
$\omega_2{+}\omega_2^*$'s two
modified entries coincide: the row enters at $r\ge3$; the dual
pair's modifications each move one value of the run $4,\dots,d_f{+}1$,
occupied at $r\ge2$ alone, so the pair enters at $r\ge2$,
$\omega_2{+}\omega_2^*$ at $r\ge3$ as above, while equality reads
$r=1$.

\emph{The dimensions} are Corollary~\ref{cor:weyldim}'s telescopes. At
$2\theta=(4,2^{\,a})$ the factors from either end read one pair
$[\,g+2:g\,]$ over the gaps $1\le g<r$ and telescope to
$[\,(r+1)r:2\,]$ each, the
pair $(1,d_f)$ reads $[\,r+4:r\,]$, and the middle pairs read $1$:
the cofactor at $4\,d_{2\theta}=(r+1)^2r\,(r+4)$. At
$2\omega_1{+}\omega_{r-1}
=(3,1^{\,b})$, at the gap $g$ at $g+1=r$, the five
collected reads are $[\,rg:2\,]$, $[\,r+2:g\,]$, $[\,r+3:r\,]$,
$g$ and $[\,r:2\,]$:
the cofactor at $4\,d=g\,r\,(r+2)(r+3)$, the pair's second count
equal, the dual's
contents the balance partners
(Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}). At $\omega_2{+}\omega_{r-1}
=(2,2,1^{\,e})$, at the gap $w$ at $w+2=r$, the six collected
reads are $[\,w+1:2\,]$, $[\,(r+1)(r+2):r\,(w+1)\,]$, $w$,
$[\,r\,(r+1):w\,(w+1)\,]$, $w$ and $[\,w+1:2\,]$: the
cofactor at $4\,d=(r+1)^2(r+2)\,w$.

\emph{The Casimirs} are Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}'s bracket at the
reduced shapes: $\hat c_2(2\theta)=[\,2r+4:r+1\,]$, the $m=2$ read of the
tower law (Proposition~\ref{prop:anchor}); at $2\omega_1{+}\omega_{r-1}$,
$k=d_f$, $q=r+7$, and the top row's weight $3\,\langle r+2\!:\!2\rangle$
with the run's collecting reads
$\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle=\langle 4r\!:\!2\rangle$, so the cleared
join $d_f+Q+2=(r+7)+4r$ reads
$Q=4\,d_f$: $\hat c_2=2$ at both members of the dual
pair; at $\omega_2{+}\omega_{r-1}$,
$k=d_f$, $q=r+5$, and the top rows' weights
$2\,\langle r+2\!:\!2\rangle+2\,\langle r+2\!:\!4\rangle$ with the
run's summing to equal members read
$\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle=\langle 4r\!:\!4\rangle$, so the cleared
join $d_f+Q+4=(r+5)+4r$ reads $Q=4r$:
$\hat c_2(\omega_2{+}\omega_{r-1})=[\,2r:r+1\,]$.

\emph{The closure identities.} At $r\ge2$, with $v:=r\,(r+2)$ and
$x:=d_f^{\,2}$ at the join $v+1=x$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:adjchar}): the
self-dual outer rows' counts $\Sigma_o$ and the dual pair's
$\Sigma_d$ read the cross-added identities $2\Sigma_o+3x=x^2$ and
$2\Sigma_d+5x=x^2+4$, so, with the unit's one and the $\theta$ row's
$2\,v$,
\[
\sum_Rm_Rd_R+2x\;=\;x^2+1 ;
\]
and the self-dual outer rows' weighted reads collect at their common
factor to $x\,v$, the weights' tie $(r+4)+g=2\,d_f$ at the gap $g$ at
$g+2=r$ closing
it, with
the dual pair's weighted read twice its count, so
\[
\sum_Rm_Rd_R\,\hat c_2(R)+4x\;=\;2x^2+2 ,
\]
the displayed sums $v^2$ and $2v^2$, the statement's two
closes.
At $r=1$ the surviving rows read $1+3+5=9=r^2(r+2)^2$ and
$3\cdot1+5\cdot3=18=2\,r^2(r+2)^2$ directly.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The window data are residue-stable on banded families]
\label{lem:rankstable}
A \emph{banded family} is a pair of weight words at the
fundamentals' two ends: the \emph{top word} $P$, a finite occupancy
family at $\omega_1,\omega_2,\dots$ indexed from the first
fundamental, and the \emph{bottom word} $Q$, one at the complement
fundamentals $\omega_1^*,\omega_2^*,\dots$ indexed from the last
(Lemma~\ref{lem:dualread}(ii): $\omega_i^*$'s column at the gap
$\ell$ at $i+\ell=d_f$), with
\emph{reaches} $a$ and $b$, the words' last keys; the member at the
residue $r$ is
\[
\lambda\;=\;\sum_{j\le a}P_j\,\omega_j\;+\;\sum_{i\le b}Q_i\,\omega_i^*\ ,
\]
one label per cleared residue, the \emph{reach clearance} the
residue at or beyond $a+b+2$, at least two keys off the words
between the reaches, and the member's rows are the weight family's tail sums,
$\lambda_i=\sum_{j\ge i}c_j$ at the coordinates $c$, each row one
fold over the member keys at or beyond it.
The vacuum is the unit pair, a member at every residue outright,
the magnetic list's members are one box on one word each ($P$ at
$\omega_1$ the fundamental, $Q$ at $\omega_1^*$ its dual,
Construction~\ref{con:fusion}), $\theta$ is one box on each word,
and the families are the vacuum's fusion closure's labels: the
fusion-closed interior at
any cutoff and depth is one word-pair list at every cleared
residue.

\emph{(i) The Casimir and the dimension are single polynomial-pair
reads.} The
words read the rows: the \emph{height} $m$, the bottom word's
coordinate total, is the row across the run between the reaches, a
top row adds its tail sum, $\lambda_i=m+p_i$ at
$p_i=\sum_{j\ge i}P_j$ for $i\le a$, and the rows below the run
are the bottom word's prefix sums, $\sigma_t=\sum_{i\le t}Q_i$
the row at the join $\ell+t=d_f$, the \emph{run count} $u$ at
$a+b+u=r+1$. $\hat c_2(\lambda)$ is one polynomial pair in the residue per family
(Lemma~\ref{lem:genericlift}), its
second member a product of integer shifts of the residue and its
powers. The dimension is one
read as well, $d_\lambda$ one polynomial
pair in the residue per family:
in Corollary~\ref{cor:weyldim}'s product the run--run factors are
$1$, a word-against-run factor telescopes over the position gaps
$g$, at the joins $i+h=a$ and $i+b+g_2=d_f$, to the binomial pair
\[
\prod_{h<g\le g_2}\big[\,p_i+g\,:\,g\,\big]
\;=\;\Big[\,\tbinom{p_i+g_2}{p_i}\,:\,\tbinom{p_i+h}{p_i}\,\Big]\ ,
\]
a factor within one word is
residue-free, and a cross factor, the top row $i$ against the bottom row
$\sigma_t$, is the pair $[\,p_i+\tau_{t+1}+g\,:\,g\,]$ at the
position gap's join $i+t+g=d_f$ and the bottom tail sum
$\tau_t=\sum_{i\ge t}Q_i$, one factor per key pair with
both members linear in the residue.

\emph{(ii) The fusion rows are word reads, one row at every
residue.} The list's rows are the one-box rows
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pieri}): the fundamental's row at a word pair
$\lambda$ reads one at every dominant $\lambda+e_i$, a box added at
a top row $i\le a+1$ (the top word moved, $P_i$ raised with
$P_{i-1}$ lowered at $e_i=\omega_i-\omega_{i-1}$, the reach grown
by at most one) or at a bottom row (the bottom word moved so, at
the complement keys); and the dual's row reads one at every dominant
$\lambda+(1^{d_f})-e_i$, a box withdrawn so; every target a word
pair at each reach grown by at most one, every count one, the
diagonal the sum's unit at every family, and the row a word read,
one row at every
residue clearing the family's reach. The adjoint's rows run on
$x:=\lambda+u$, the beta-set's sorted display, on
Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}'s alignment: the $\theta$-contents are the
letter-pair moves at multiplicity one and the unit-monomial content
at $r$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:adjchar}), the diagonal
$N^\lambda_{\theta\lambda}=\#\,\mathrm{supp}\,P+\#\,\mathrm{supp}\,Q$,
the member-key count, residue-free, and the off-diagonal targets
within one key of the words at count one each, the identity
alignment's tie. A
depth-$D$ fusion closure
of the vacuum therefore has as members word pairs at reaches summing
to at most $D$, one box per step,
and its whole data list, the labels, multiplicities, Casimirs, dimensions
and the network weights $w_k=[\,m_kd_k:r^2(r+2)^2\,]$, is one list of polynomial-pair reads at every
residue clearing the reach sum by two, each family with its
reach clearance there, the recoupling
entries included through
Proposition~\ref{prop:wg}'s generic computation, one polynomial pair
per entry agreeing with the per-residue read at every residue beyond the factor
count.

\emph{(iii) The residue is a cell coordinate.} At fixed content cutoff,
region and fiber, the window pencil's entries are the reads of (i)--(ii),
so they are one list of polynomial-pair data in $(t,\tau)$ and the
residue at every residue
clearing the reach sum by two; the
cutoff comparisons $\hat c_2\le\Lambda_C$ selecting the interior are
eventual-sign reads (Lemma~\ref{lem:genericlift}(iii)); and
clearing the second members is a positive rescaling fixing every
count (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). The fiber pencils' entries
then sit in $\mathbb P[t,\tau,r]$ and every count of the gap chain is
Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}'s cell function with $r$ a coordinate: a
divisor's roots in $r$ are located outright
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}, the leading-term bound the coarser
certificate), and each root reads against the compared families'
reach clearances: a comparison's residues are those clearing its
families' reaches, so at every root below them
the divisor keeps its leading side at every one of its residues
and one symbolic count is every residue's at the
cleared families; a family below its clearance reads its finitely
many residues' data directly, the calculus's displays at the
residue's label, one evaluation each; and
Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}'s $r=1,2$
degenerations are each their own window read.
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i)} $q(\lambda)$ splits into the
top rows' squares, the run term $u\,m^2$ at the run count, and the
bottom rows' squares, each row a word read;
$\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle=\sum_i\lambda_i\,\langle
r+2\!:\!2i\rangle$, the row weights balance pairs, splits into
word reads and the run's arithmetic sum; and the degree is
$k=\sum_j j\,P_j+\sum_i \ell_i\,Q_i$ at the complement columns
$\ell_i$, $i+\ell_i=d_f$, linear in the residue, so
the degree's square against the count, $[\,k^2:d_f\,]$, is one pair
term: hence $\hat c_2(\lambda)$ is one polynomial pair in the
residue per family. In the gap product the telescoped
word-against-run factor is the top row's case at its tail sum
$p_i$, with the bottom's its reflection, the run against
$\sigma_t$ at the row gap $\tau_{t+1}$, the bottom tail sum at the
join $\sigma_t+\tau_{t+1}=m$, a pair of two integer binomials
polynomial in the residue each; a factor within one word reads its
rows' and its positions' gaps at the word's own data; and the
cross factors are linear pairs: $d_\lambda$ is one polynomial pair
in the residue per family.
\emph{(ii)} Interior run rows $i-1$, $i$ read $\lambda_{i-1}=\lambda_i=m$,
so $\lambda+e_i$ reads $\lambda_i$ above $\lambda_{i-1}$, off the
sorted read: a box is dominant at the words' ends alone, the
targets the word pairs displayed; and a box added or
withdrawn moves the label, so the diagonal reads the sum's unit.
\emph{(iii)} The second members, integer shifts of the residue and
its powers, keep one side at every residue clearing the reach sum
by two, so clearing them is a positive rescaling fixing every
count (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The series' window data are rank-stable]
\label{lem:serstable}
At a $B$, $C$ or $D$ member (Construction~\ref{con:sertables}) the
magnetic list is the spinor at $B_\ell$, the first fundamental at
$C_\ell$, and the spinor at odd rank with the vector beside it at
even rank at $D_\ell$ (Construction~\ref{con:fusion}), every member
\emph{minuscule}: its contents one orbit of the Weyl list at
multiplicity one, the signed keys at $C_\ell$ and $D_\ell$'s vector
and the half-one lists at the spinors (the defining and spinor
tables, Construction~\ref{con:memtable}), every content's coroot
pair at every positive root at magnitude at most one. A
\emph{leading family} is a finite weight word $W_1\ge\cdots\ge W_a$
at positive reads on the leading keys, its member at the rank
$\ell$ the word's own occupancy family over those keys, and its
\emph{reach clearance} the rank at or beyond $a+2$; a \emph{spinor
family} at $B_\ell$ and $D_\ell$ is a leading word joined to a
spinor, the coordinates the word's raised by one half on the
leading keys and one half on the \emph{run}, the keys past the
reach, the run count $u$ at $a+u=\ell$, at $D_\ell$ the last key's
read one half or its balance partner, the two spinors' families.

\emph{(i) The Casimir is a single polynomial-pair read in the rank;
the dimension is one at a leading family and an
exponential-polynomial pair at a spinor family.} $\hat c_2$ is one
polynomial pair per family, the spinor's
$[\,\ell\,(2\ell+1):8\,(r+1)\,]$ at $B_\ell$ the instance
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}), and a spinor family's read sits at or
beyond the spinor's, the fall identity's read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}). The dimension is the member gap product
(Corollary~\ref{cor:weyldim}), at a leading family a product of
finitely many binomial, rank-free and linear pairs in the rank, and
at a spinor family the pure spinor's own dimension at the rank $u$
times a polynomial pair,
\[
d_\lambda\;=\;2^{u}\,R_\lambda(\ell)\quad\text{at }B_\ell,
\qquad
d_\lambda\;=\;2^{u-1}\,R_\lambda(\ell)\quad\text{at }D_\ell,
\qquad u+a=\ell,
\]
$R_\lambda$ a polynomial pair in the rank, the family's dimension
an exponential-polynomial pair (Lemma~\ref{lem:genericlift}(v)).

\emph{(ii) The rows are the minuscule rows, one row at every rank.}
At a list member $\lambda_0$ and a dominant $\lambda$,
\[
N^{\lambda+\nu}_{\lambda_0\lambda}\;=\;1
\]
at every content $\nu$ of $\lambda_0$ with $\lambda+\nu$ dominant,
and every further target reads the sum's unit. The targets read
the families: at a leading family the vector's contents $\pm e_i$
move one coordinate by one, the targets leading families at the
reach grown by at most one; a spinor's contents move every
coordinate by one half, the targets from a leading family spinor
families at the word's keys moved by a half each and from a spinor
family leading families with a run of ones, the coordinates
$(W_i+[\,1:2\,]\pm[\,1:2\,])$ on the word's keys and one or the
sum's unit on the run, sorted, a leading family at the reach grown
by the ones' count $k$, its Casimir at or beyond $[\,k:4\,]$ in the
weight-free read, so at a stated content bound the targets within
it sit at reaches grown by at most four times the bound. The
diagonal reads the sum's unit at every family, a minuscule member
without the unit content. So the fusion closure from the unit label
is one family list at every rank beyond the reach clearances, its
members at a stated depth the words of at most that many moves.

\emph{(iii) The rank is a cell coordinate.} At fixed content cutoff,
region and fiber, a series member's pencil entries are the reads of
(i) and (ii) with the recoupling entries Proposition~\ref{prop:wg}'s
at the member's tables, one list of exponential-polynomial pairs in
the rank at every rank clearing the reach sums by two, the
dimensions and the spinor table's loops entering at powers of two
(Lemma~\ref{lem:serpairing}; Construction~\ref{con:memtable}), a
leading family's data polynomial pairs outright. The head at a
content bound $\Lambda_h$, the classes at every band component's
content below it, holds, beyond the \emph{head rank} $\ell_h$,
leading families of bounded reach alone: the head rank is
$2\Lambda_h$, and beyond it the head's classes are leading families
at the unit class, and at $D_\ell$ at the vector class beside it, at
reaches below $a+4\Lambda_h$, the bound's read, the head's count
one value at every further rank. The head's magnetic entries are
the vector's rows at $C_\ell$ and at $D_\ell$'s even rank,
polynomial pairs, and the sum's unit at the spinors' terms, whose
targets sit in the tail; the decimated head gains the tail's Schur
reads at the first tail shell, the spinor families joined to the
head at one plaquette term, their contents polynomial pairs, their
vertex counts one (the minuscule rows) and their entries
exponential-polynomial pairs at (i)'s dimensions and the
recouplings' Grams. The tail's dominance comparison, each tail
class's content against its row's magnetic magnitude fold, runs at
the \emph{scaled magnetic weight} $\tilde\beta:=\beta\,d_L$, the
closure's dimension fold absorbed into the ray's coordinate, the
map $[\,\alpha:\beta\,]\mapsto[\,\alpha:\tilde\beta\,]$ a bijection
of the rays at every member, and the comparison at the $\alpha{=}1$
representative holds at every tail class from the rank
$16\,d\,\tilde\beta$ on at the per-link plaquette count $2g$
(Construction~\ref{con:lattice}), the head rank joined. So the
cutoff comparisons are eventual-sign reads, the divisors' rank
roots read against the clearances with the rank read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:genericlift}(v)) at the exponential-polynomial
entries, one symbolic count at every cleared rank beyond the head
rank and the comparison's computed natural, with the ranks at or
below read directly, each a finite member
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}): Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}'s
three reads at the series' own coordinates, the $A$-series' the
first instance, its list's data polynomial pairs outright.
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i)} $q(\lambda)$ is the word's square fold, at a spinor
family the raised word's joined to the run's quarters, $u$ at
$[\,1:4\,]$; $\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle=\sum_iW_i\,(2\rho)_i$
folds the word against the displayed root-fold key reads, each
linear in the rank, at a spinor family the raised word's joined to
the run's half fold $[\,1:2\,]\sum_{i>a}(2\rho)_i$, the arithmetic
sum a quadratic pair in the rank; so $\hat c_2$ is one polynomial
pair per family. In the member gap product at a leading family the
tail factors read one, the word-against-tail factors telescope
over the position gaps to binomial pairs in the rank, the
word-against-word difference factors are rank-free, and the word
sum, short and long factors are single linear pairs in the rank,
finitely many. At a spinor family the word-against-word factors
are rank-free; a word-against-run difference factor telescopes
over the run to a binomial pair in the rank, and a
word-against-run sum factor, $(W_i+1+\rho_i+\rho_j)$ against
$(\rho_i+\rho_j)$ over the run keys $j$, telescopes at the
successor steps to a product of $W_i+1$ linear pairs in the rank,
the run's sums consecutive naturals; and the run-against-run
factors read the pure spinor's own dimension at the rank $u$: the
run's shifted reads $\rho_i+\rho_j$ and the run's raised reads at
two run keys are the rank-$u$ member's own at the keys shifted by
$a$ (the root-fold key reads $2\ell-2i+1$ at $B_\ell$ and
$2\ell-2i$ at $D_\ell$, the shift withdrawing at the difference),
the difference factors one and the sum factors with the short
factors the spinor's gap product at the rank $u$, $2^{u}$ at $B_u$
and $2^{u-1}$ at $D_u$ (Construction~\ref{con:memtable}'s spinor
table at $2^{u}$ keys, the two parity summands at $D_u$), the
further factors' product the polynomial pair $R_\lambda$.

\emph{(ii)} The alignment's member ties
$\nu_w+w(\lambda+\rho)=c+\rho$ over the member's Weyl list
(Corollary~\ref{cor:steinberg}) run at the contents $\nu_w$ of
$\lambda_0$, every content at multiplicity one; at a tie the key
$\lambda+\rho+\nu_w$ reads its coroot pairs at or beyond the sum's
unit at every positive root, $\lambda+\rho$'s at or beyond one and
the content's at magnitude at most one, and $w$ maps it to the
strictly dominant $c+\rho$, so its every coroot pair sits beyond
the sum's unit (a key at a unit pair is fixed by that root's
reflection, its image off the strictly dominant reads,
Construction~\ref{con:sertables}'s regular reads), the key is
strictly dominant, its image is itself at the regular reads and $w$
is the identity: one tie per target at the even side, the count one
at $c=\lambda+\nu$ dominant and the sum's unit at every further
$c$. A leading family at the reach grown by a run of ones of count
$k$ reads its Casimir at or beyond $\omega_{a+k}$'s (the fall
identity, Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}), $k\,(2\ell-k+1)$ at $B_\ell$
against $C_2(\theta)=2\,(2\ell-1)$ and $k\,(2\ell-k)$ at $D_\ell$
against $2\,(2\ell-2)$, each at or beyond $[\,k:4\,]$ in the
weight-free read at $k$ at or below $\ell$.

\emph{(iii)} A spinor-class link's label reads $\hat c_2$ at or
beyond the spinor's, $[\,\ell\,(2\ell+1):8\,(r+1)\,]$ at or beyond
$[\,\ell:8\,]$ at $B_\ell$ and $[\,\ell\,(2\ell-1):8\,(r+1)\,]$ at
or beyond $[\,\ell:8\,]$ at $D_\ell$, a spinor-class configuration
of the vacuum sector holds a cycle of such links, four or beyond,
so its content clears $\Lambda_h$ at $\ell$ beyond $2\Lambda_h$,
and a leading family with a run of ones of count $k$ reads its
Casimir at or beyond $[\,k:4\,]$ ((ii)), so at content below
$\Lambda_h$ the reach sits below $a+4\Lambda_h$: the head rank is
$2\Lambda_h$. At the scaled weight the stencil caps read
$\tilde\beta$ times the term count (Lemma~\ref{lem:loopcap} at the
closure's dimension fold), and a tail class's content per
spinor-class link clears $[\,\ell:8\,]$, so the comparison at the
$\alpha{=}1$ representative holds at every tail class from the rank
$16\,d\,\tilde\beta$ on at the per-link plaquette count $2g$
(Construction~\ref{con:lattice}).
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The member pairing span]\label{lem:serpairing}
At a $B$, $C$ or $D$ member with its defining table
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), the invariants of the
defining power $V^{\otimes 2k}$ at the rank at or beyond $k$,
the $D$ series at or beyond $k{+}1$ (the doubled-rank
alternating invariant sits off the span at the tie
$2\ell=2k$), are
the \emph{pair-partition span}: one vector per pair partition of
the $2k$ places, the partition's fold of the form's dual pairs,
at the count $(2k{-}1)!!$.
\begin{proof}
\emph{The invariant read.} An invariant of the power is a vector
at the unit content with every raising image the sum's unit: a
unit-content top's block is the unit label's line, and a top at a
further content sits at its own label (Lemma~\ref{lem:tops};
Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}), so the invariants are the
unit-content summand's raising kernel, the two reads'
conjunction.
\emph{The defining rows.} $V$'s contents are the signed keys
with the unit content at $B_\ell$, and its fusion rows at a
block are one box up or one box down at the cleared ranks: the
alignment's form read (Proposition~\ref{prop:row}'s alignment form
read, Corollary~\ref{cor:steinberg}'s member ties) reads the $B_\ell$ stay term
against its correction, the unit content's one against the last
letter's read at $(\lambda+\rho)(e_i^\vee)=2\lambda_i+2g+1$ over
the join $i+g=\ell$, one exactly at the last key off the
support: equal members at every label whose support clears the
last key, and the moved ties at the box targets alone; at
$C_\ell$ and $D_\ell$ the signed keys sit off the root list and
the unit content off the table, the rows the box moves
outright.
\emph{The count.} Iterating the rows, the unit-label count of
$V^{\otimes 2k}$ is the closed path fold
$\langle\mathbf 1,(U{+}D)^{2k}\,\mathbf 1\rangle$ over the
shapes at most $k$ rows deep (the clearance; a $B_\ell$ stay
reads at a full-depth shape, its boxes the step count's read,
and the return closes beyond the walk's $2k$ steps, so the
closed folds read the box moves alone), with
$DU=UD+\mathrm{id}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:pathsquare}'s displayed
argument at the member's shapes) and the commutator telescope
$X^{m-1}U=U\,X^{m-1}+(m{-}1)\,X^{m-2}$ at $X:=U{+}D$, so the
fold obeys $m_m=(m{-}1)\,m_{m-2}$ from $m_0=1$: the double
factorial, the matchings' count, and the unit-label count is
the invariant count (Definition~\ref{def:blockcount};
Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount} at table spaces).
\emph{Independence, and the Gram.} A pair partition's vector
reads a monomial the further partitions miss at the rank
clearing $k$, one key pair per part at distinct keys, so the
$(2k{-}1)!!$ vectors are independent and span. The Gram is the
loops' fold: two partitions' union closes into loops, each loop
contracting the form's dual pairs around its cycle; at $B_\ell$
and $D_\ell$ a loop reads the dimension, $r+3$; at $C_\ell$ a
loop reads the doubled rank at its \emph{crossing parity}, the
loop's pair count at either side with its against-order
crossings along one
traversal, the antisymmetric form's memberwise swap per
crossing: the entry is the loops' product, $(2r)$ per loop with
the parities' fold its side, one displayed traversal read per
entry.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{construction}[The adjoint walk's data]\label{con:xfusion}
$\chi_X=\chi_{\mathrm{adj}}$ at
$\chi_X+1=\chi_f\chi_{\bar f}=|\mathrm{tr}\,U|^2$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:adjchar}), so the
adjoint walk's calculus is tensoring by the adjoint, and its data are exactly
two: the fusion matrix $N_{\mathrm{adj}}$ and the weight-free Casimir
$\hat c_2$. The product expands as $\chi_{\mathrm{adj}}\chi_\lambda=
\sum_\mu N^\mu_{\mathrm{adj},\lambda}\chi_\mu$ with unique coefficients, and
the characters are orthonormal for $\mathrm{Eval}$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}), so $M_X$ acts on the label index by
$N_{\mathrm{adj}}$ itself, symmetric because $m\{a,b,c\}=N^{\bar c}_{ab}$ is
symmetric and the adjoint is self-dual,
and $E$ is diagonal there with entries $4\hat c_2(\lambda)$. Every
anchor of the walk is a read of that pair:
$c_1=\langle\mathrm{adj}|\chi_X|\mathrm{adj}\rangle$ is the multiplicity of the
adjoint in $\mathrm{adj}\otimes\mathrm{adj}$, the $m{=}1$
alternant read of Proposition~\ref{prop:row}, $2$ at $r\ge2$ and
$1$ at $r=1$, and the member-key count of $\theta$'s word pair,
one box on each word, at the residues clearing the pair's reach
(Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(ii));
$\langle q,M_X\,\mathrm{vac}\rangle$ is the multiplicity of the vacuum, $1$; and
the adjoint loop's content is $4$ against the free-end level
$E_0=4\,\hat c_2(f_0)$ at the floor label (Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}).

The channel list is Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}'s, one word-pair
list at every residue with each channel entering at its count
(Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}), the two root-drops and the $r=1$ row list
that lemma's own reads, so
every quantity
below is a sum over the channels at their counts.

\end{construction}

\begin{theorem}[The adjoint walk's block data]\label{thm:xdata}
With $q_i=\chi_X(U_i)$ at the adjoint loop's content $4$:
$\langle q_1,Mq_1\rangle$ has the integer coefficients
$\langle q_1,M\,\mathrm{vac}\rangle=1$ and
$c_1=\langle q_1,Xq_1\rangle$, the fusion multiplicity of
Construction~\ref{con:xfusion} ($2$ at $r\ge2$, $1$ at $r=1$); the vacuum $Q$-dressing reads equal
members as a polynomial pair, $M\,\mathrm{vac}$ lying in the module space $Q$ projects off
(Construction~\ref{con:twoplaq}); the module is isolated, the channel
distances the Casimir gaps of Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}'s list.
Structural identities on the constituent data:
$\sum_R m_R\dim_R=r^2(r+2)^2$
and $\sum_R m_R\dim_R\hat c_2(R)=2\,r^2(r+2)^2$, cleared polynomial
identities in the residue.
\begin{proof}
The two coefficients are the walk's anchors, the vacuum's
multiplicity one and the adjoint's own multiplicity $c_1$
(Construction~\ref{con:xfusion}). $M\,\mathrm{vac}$'s component
at a plaquette is the module state itself, the adjoint character
at that plaquette (Construction~\ref{con:twoplaq}'s magnetic
multiplication at the vacuum), so Construction~\ref{con:res}'s
first step, the deflation at the module presentation, withdraws it
whole and the residual's self-pairing reads equal members as a
polynomial pair. The channel distances are positive at their rows'
residues (Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}), the module isolated. The
first identity is the block count of the square
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(ii) over Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}'s
list), the second the
channel table's displayed second closure (Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}),
the uniform drift of Theorem~\ref{thm:drift} at $R=\mathrm{adj}$, where
$d_{\mathrm{adj}}=r\,(r+2)$ and $\hat c_2(\mathrm{adj})=1$ make
$d_Rd_{\mathrm{adj}}(\hat c_2(R)+1)$ read $2\,r^2(r+2)^2$.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\section{The charged anchor}

\begin{proposition}[Charged anchor for the $X$-chain]\label{prop:anchor}
Define charge as Cartan-weight density along the highest root
$\theta$.
The charged tower is the $m\theta$-string, the Cartan powers of
$\theta$ (Construction~\ref{con:labels}), and the residue is the
pairing's own read at the highest root: the row-weight fold reads
$\langle\theta,2\rho\rangle=2\,r$ against the pair-square fold at
$2\,d_f$, the declared scalar's own value, and the tower reads
\[
\hat c_2(m\theta)=\big[\,m\,(m+r):r+1\,\big]
\qquad\text{at the derived residue}\quad r ,
\]
an $l(l+1)$ in shape; at $r=1$ it is $[\,m^2+m:2\,]$, the
integer-spin tower's weight-free read. At a member's weight table
the residue is Construction~\ref{con:sertables}'s one fold,
$\langle\theta,2\rho\rangle=2\,r$ at the form's read
$\langle\theta,\theta\rangle=2$, and the tower reads the member's
form at its two degrees, the form additive in each argument
(Construction~\ref{con:gentable}),
$C_2(m\theta)=m^2\,\langle\theta,\theta\rangle
+m\,\langle\theta,2\rho\rangle=2\,m\,(m+r)$ against
$C_2(\theta)=2\,(r+1)$: the display at the member's derived
residue. The
linear coefficient $r$ is fusion strictness: the abelian tower reads
$C_2=m^2$ and this one $m\,(m+r)$.
\begin{proof}
The join's constructed witness (Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}) reads
a label at two folds,
$d_f\,Q(\lambda)=\sum_{p<q}\langle\lambda_p\!:\!\lambda_q\rangle^2
+d_f\,\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle$, each homogeneous in the rows,
degree two and degree one
($\langle mu\!:\!mv\rangle=m\,\langle u\!:\!v\rangle$,
Definition~\ref{def:ground}'s displayed reads); the tower label's
rows are $m$ times $\theta$'s, $m\theta=(2m,\,m^{\,c})$ at
$c+2=d_f$, so the tower reads off $\theta$'s two folds,
\[
d_f\,Q(m\theta)\;=\;m^{2}\sum_{p<q}
\langle\theta_p\!:\!\theta_q\rangle^{2}
+m\,d_f\,\langle\theta,2\rho\rangle\ .
\]
At the reduced shape $\theta=(2,1^{\,c})$ the square identity
$d_f\,q(\theta)=k^{2}+\sum_{p<q}\langle\theta_p\!:\!\theta_q
\rangle^{2}$ (Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}) at $q(\theta)=r+3$ and
$k=d_f$ reads the pair squares at $2\,d_f$; and the row weights
$\langle r+2\!:\!2i\rangle$ sum to equal members over the run
$2\le i\le r$, so $\langle\theta,2\rho\rangle=2\,r$, the top row's
read, the pairing's read the residue doubled. So
$Q(m\theta)=2m^2+2mr$, and
against $Q(\theta)=2d_f$, the display's own $m=1$ read,
$\hat c_2(m\theta)=[\,m\,(m+r):r+1\,]$; at $r=1$ the value is
$[\,m^2+m:2\,]$.
\end{proof}

\end{proposition}

\section{The $X$-tower matrix and the walk}

\begin{proposition}[The $X$-tower matrix]\label{prop:row}
On the orthonormal character index the multiplication by $\chi_\theta$
is the symmetric matrix of fusion counts $N^\mu_{\theta\lambda}$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}), and
its compression to the tower labels $m\theta$ is the \emph{tower
matrix} $J$, fusion counts alone. Every neighbor entry is one,
\[
N^{m\theta}_{\theta,(m+1)\theta}
=m\{\theta,(m{+}1)\theta,m\theta\}
=N^{(m+1)\theta}_{\theta,m\theta}
=1 ,
\]
upward the Cartan equality, $\theta+m\theta=(m{+}1)\theta$ as
reduced shapes (Construction~\ref{con:labels}), downward the
$m$-symmetry at the self-dual tower labels
(Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}; $(m\theta)^*=m\theta$ by the complement
arithmetic of Construction~\ref{con:labels}); and the diagonal is the
tower's own fusion multiplicity
$N^{m\theta}_{\theta,m\theta}$, one alternant read at
every $m$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:steinberg} at $a=\theta$, $b=c=m\theta$):
the vector $x:=m\theta+u$, at $u$ the unit set's sorted display, has
coordinates $2m+r+1$; the middle members $m+i$ at
$2\le i\le r$, the \emph{run}; and $1$, pairwise distinct, and at $m\ge1$
\[
N^{m\theta}_{\theta,m\theta}+g\;=\;r\quad(r\ge2,\ \ g\ \text{the
run's unit-gap count at}\ g+2=r),
\qquad
N^{m\theta}_{\theta,m\theta}\;=\;r\;=\;1\quad(r=1),
\]
the count $2$, one value at every $m\ge1$, and at the vacuum
the count $N^{\mathbf 1}_{\theta\,\mathbf 1}$ the
Kronecker delta at two labels (Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}): the
vacuum defect. So $J$ is the free Jacobi matrix with a single boundary
defect, neighbor entries one, the diagonal $c_1$ at every $m\ge1$ and
the vacuum's the Kronecker delta at two labels: integer data, $c_1$ the
one parameter, the shape's reads the fusion interface's own, the
Cartan strictness and the unit read at the self-dual $\theta$
(Construction~\ref{con:fusion}).
At a member's table the diagonal is the alignment's form read
(Corollary~\ref{cor:steinberg}'s member ties at $a=\theta$,
$b=c=m\theta$), the member's $\theta$ content list the root list
with its balance partners at one each and the unit content at
the coordinate count, the interface field's instantiation
(Construction~\ref{con:fusion}), derived on a block at top
$\theta$. The dimension is the content list's own fold,
twice the positive count with the coordinate count,
\[
d_\theta=\big[\,(r+2)(r+3):2\,\big]\ \text{at}\ B_\ell\
\text{and}\ D_\ell,\quad r\,(2r+1)\ \text{at}\ C_\ell,\quad
r\,(r+2)\ \text{at the $A$-series},
\]
and $14$, $52$, $78$, $133$, $248$ at the fixed members, the
member gap product's evaluation at $\theta$ its cross-check
(Corollary~\ref{cor:weyldim}). The diagonal
joins the count $z$ of the simples at $\theta$'s equal-membered
coroot pairs to the
coordinate count, $N^{m\theta}_{\theta,m\theta}+z=\ell$ at
every $m\ge1$: the value is $\theta$'s occupied coroot support,
one at every member off the $A$-series, the displayed tables'
single keys, and the $A$-series' the run's read above, two at
$r\ge2$ and one at $r=1$; the
vacuum's ties read every simple at the pair one, the count the
Kronecker delta at two labels, the defect's read at every
member.
With strictly positive off-tower weight: the $X$-tower leaks, and the
family operator is the tower-compressed Jacobi pencil plus off-tower
coupling, the dimension weights riding the off-tower channels alone.
\begin{proof}
\emph{The diagonal at the letters.} A permutation
contributes only where $\sigma x=x$, the adjoint's unit-monomial content, or
where the tie $\nu+\sigma x=x$ holds at a root $\nu$, the adjoint's
occupied contents (Lemma~\ref{lem:adjchar}). At $\sigma=\mathrm{id}$ the
read is $r$, the adjoint's multiplicity at the unit-monomial
content, on the even side; a root tie
forces $\sigma$ to fix every coordinate off some $\{i,j\}$ (the
coordinates
are distinct), so $\sigma=(i\,j)$ at the two coordinates' gap one, an
odd transposition at the root's multiplicity one. At
$m\ge1$ the unit gaps sit in the run alone, $x_{k+1}+1=x_k$ at
$2\le k<r$, a run occupied at $r\ge2$, the two boundary
gaps reading $m+1\ge2$, the displayed count; at the vacuum the boundary
gaps close to $1$ and the two further odd transpositions even the
two sides' counts.
\emph{The content list.} A content's dominant image is a dominant root or the
unit (the descent, Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}, with the content

(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}), the short dominant root's read is

one display per two-length class,
\[
(2\ell{-}2)\,m=2\,(\ell{-}1)\ \text{at}\ B_\ell,\quad
2\,m=2\ \text{at}\ C_\ell,\quad
6\,m=6\ \text{at}\ F_4,\quad
4\,m=4\ \text{at}\ G_2,
\]
each right side the fold of the form reads at the contents above
the short dominant root, and the unit content's read is the
recursion's unit fold, $m\,(r+1)$ the halved lengths' fold over
the root list, at the member join
$\sum_{\alpha}\langle\alpha,\alpha\rangle=\ell\,(r+1)$ over the
positive list, one displayed fold per member ($2\ell^2{-}\ell$
at $B_\ell$, $\ell^2{+}\ell$ at $C_\ell$, $2\ell^2{-}2\ell$ at
$D_\ell$, and $8$, $36$, $72$, $126$, $240$ at the fixed
members' length folds): the unit content at the coordinate
count.
\emph{The diagonal at a member.} A tie
$\nu_w+w\kappa=\kappa$ at $\kappa:=m\theta+\rho$ keeps the
form's square, so $2\,\langle\kappa,\nu_w\rangle$ reads
$q_0(\nu_w)$. At $\nu_w$ the unit content the element is
the identity, $\kappa$ dominant at every simple pair beyond the
unit with its images one per element (the regular reads,
Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), the read the coordinate count
on the even side. At $\nu_w$ a root read, a partner's case reads
the doubled pairing on its lower side against the square, so
$\nu_w$ is a positive $\beta$ at
$\kappa(\beta^\vee)=1$, the element the root's reflection alone,
$w\kappa=s_\beta\kappa$ at the regular reads, odd at the

image; and
$\kappa(\beta^\vee)=m\,\theta(\beta^\vee)+\rho(\beta^\vee)$
reads one exactly at $\theta$'s coroot pair of equal members
with $\beta$ simple, the root fold's pair two at the simples and
beyond two at every further positive member (the fixed members'

joins the count $z$ to the coordinate count.
\end{proof}
\end{proposition}

\section{The tower channel: chord map and divisor}\label{sec:channel}

\begin{theorem}[The chord map and the channel's base]\label{thm:chordmap}
Pass to the dual of the walk: the spectral side, in the deck
coordinate $z$, at the walk's level the balance pair
$y=\langle y_+\!:\!y_-\rangle$, its members cross-added onto the two
sides (Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct}'s levels), the \emph{deck
relation}
\[
z^2+y_+\,z+1\;=\;\big(c_1+y_-\big)\,z ,
\]
one display at every representative (a summand on both members
fixing the value, Definition~\ref{def:ground}),
degree two in $z$ with the \emph{deck involution} $\iota$ exchanging
its two roots, their product the constant coefficient one and
the level read jointly by both, Definition~\ref{def:deck}'s
relation at the chord $w$ joining the level's members,
$w+y_+=c_1+y_-$. The relation's
two roots are equal exactly at the \emph{crossings}, $\iota$'s fixed
points, a double root squaring to the constant coefficient one at
the display
\[
(c_1+y_-)^2+y_+^{\,2}\;=\;2\,y_+\,(c_1+y_-)+4\ ,
\]
the double root's read cross-added onto the two sides, one display
at every representative (Definition~\ref{def:ground}); the chord
is a member of the carrier at the lower crossing alone, and the
display holds
exactly at the
two crossing joins $y_++2=c_1+y_-$ and $y_+=c_1+y_-+2$; the \emph{band}
is the segment between the two crossing levels;
and the defect's root is $z_*$ at $c_1z_*=1$, where the relation
reads the bound-state level at the join $c_1y_++1=c_1y_-$.

\emph{The chord and the defect read distinct integers.} The
relation's two roots are the half-line walk's neighbors, the
coordination count that
fixes the band's width $4$, the level read jointly by the two
roots. The base of the
channel's value
is $c_1$ at $c_1z_*=1$, the mass point's own witness. The two integers
agree exactly at base two, the member-key count's two-key read
(Proposition~\ref{prop:row}), and separate at base one, where the
chord has two terms.
\begin{proof}
At the chord $w$ the relation is $z^{2}+1=w\,z$
(Definition~\ref{def:deck}), so its two roots are a root pair at
product one, exchanged by $\iota$, and they are equal exactly where
the relation has a double root $z$ at $2z=w$ and $z^{2}=1$, the
chord's square $4$: the display is $w^{2}=4$ cross-added at
$w+y_+=c_1+y_-$, and $w^{2}=4$ holds exactly at $w=2$, the lower
crossing $y_++2=c_1+y_-$, and at $w$ the balance partner of $2$,
the upper crossing $y_+=c_1+y_-+2$, the chord a carrier member at
the lower alone. At $z_*$ with $c_1z_*=1$ the relation reads
$z_*^{2}+y_+z_*+1=1+y_-z_*$ at $c_1z_*=1$, the constant
withdrawn at the sum's injectivity and the factor $z_*$ at the
product's, $z_*+y_+=y_-$, and the
$c_1$-multiple is the bound-state join $c_1y_++1=c_1y_-$. The
band's width is the chords' gap between the crossings, $2$ against
its balance partner, $4$; and the two integers, the coordination
count two and the base $c_1$, agree exactly at $c_1=2$, where the
mass point's chord $c_1w=1+c_1^{\,2}$ reads $[\,5:2\,]$ and the
walk's diagonal the member-key count two (Proposition~\ref{prop:row}),
and separate at $c_1=1$, where the chord at the mass point reads
$w=2$, the relation's two terms $1+1$, and the mass point sits at
the lower crossing.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The channel divisor]\label{thm:channeldiv}
The walk's boundary entry $G_0$ in the deck coordinate is the
renewal witness $G_0=z+c_1zG_0$'s series, its divisor the witness's
own at the mass point $z_*$ at $c_1z_*=1$, and the
channel's coordinate is the order pair, the determination: the mass
point a simple pole, order $1$, the $\iota$-symmetrized weight at
order $2$, both orders independent of the base and summing to $3$;
the base $c_1$ is the orders' read, the single-key member's display
at base one, the mass point at the crossing.

\emph{The divisor.} The walk's resolvent reads in the deck
coordinate, the level the balance pair
$y=\langle y_+\!:\!y_-\rangle$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:chordmap}. The
defect-free tail's boundary entry $m^{(L)}$ at the
tail's $L$-site cut $J_L$ is a solved witness of
Lemma~\ref{lem:genericlift}(ii)'s shape, the boundary entry of the
adjugate column against the determinant at the pair
$(J_L+y_-\!:\!y_+)$'s site datum (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia};
Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct}'s levels, the datum at
$J_L+y_-=y_++S_L$), and the boundary entry
solves the pivot identity,
\[
m^{(L+1)}\,\big(c_1+y_-\big)\;=\;1+m^{(L+1)}\big(y_++m^{(L)}\big) ,
\qquad
m^{(1)}\,\big(c_1+y_-\big)\;=\;1+m^{(1)}\,y_+ ,
\]
the one-site read its seed. The truncations generate one series
$m_1$, whose fixed-point identity is the deck
relation in the boundary entry,
$m_1^2+y_+\,m_1+1=\big(c_1+y_-\big)\,m_1$: its
two roots are the root pair, at product one, and the member at the
$z$-multiple series is the coordinate itself, the errors $e_L$ at
$m^{(L)}=z+e_L$ obey
$e_{L+1}=z^2e_L+z\,e_L\,e_{L+1}$, so $m^{(L)}$ agrees with $z$
beyond $z$-order $2L$, and $m_1(z)=z$. The defect site then reads one
further pivot, its
diagonal the vacuum's (Proposition~\ref{prop:row}), and the boundary
read solves it at the renewal witness
\[
G_0\;=\;z+c_1\,z\,G_0 ,
\]
the recursion's own series $\sum_kc_1^{\,k}z^{\,k+1}$
(Definition~\ref{def:poly}), coefficients naturals: its divisor is
the witness's own, the least occupied degree one and the
\emph{mass point} $z_{*}$ at $c_1z_*=1$, the clearing factor
$\langle1\!:\!c_1z\rangle$'s root. The deck
involution exchanges $z_*$ with its $\iota$-image $c_1$, the orbit's product
one: $z_*$ is the orbit's interior member, $z_*^2\le1$ one pair
comparison. The mass point's margin is the crossing read: the
relation at the mass point reads the symbol
$c_1\,w=1+c_1^{\,2}$, its crossing pair
$\langle w^2\!:\!4\rangle=[\,\langle
c_1^{\,2}\!:\!1\rangle^2:c_1^{\,2}\,]$, equal members exactly at
$c_1=1$, and the margin $\langle1\!:\!z_*^2\rangle$ is the mass
weight's own pair, its square the crossing pair's
$z_*^2$-multiple (Lemma~\ref{lem:deckfactor}): $[\,9:4\,]$ at
base two, the member-key count's two-key read
(Proposition~\ref{prop:row}).
Every channel datum is a read of it: the bound-state level
at the join $c_1y_++1=c_1y_-$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:chordmap}); the
mass weight, the pair $[\,\langle c_1^2:1\rangle:c_1^2\,]$ at the
complement $[\,1:c_1^2\,]$, the two summing to one; and the crossing
levels at their joins (Theorem~\ref{thm:chordmap}), with $c_1$
Proposition~\ref{prop:row}'s. The lower crossing's level reads equal
members exactly at
$c_1=2$, the infrared contact forced by the integer counting the cubic
couplings, and at $c_1=1$ the mass point sits at the crossing, $z_*=1$, the
divisor count unchanged there, as below.

\emph{What the channel contributes, and at which base.} The divisor's
data are \emph{two integer orders} and one base. The mass point is a simple
pole of $G_0$, order $1$. The weight reads the clearing factor
$\iota$-symmetrized, the $\iota$-image's cleared read and the symmetrized
pair
\[
z\cdot\big(\langle1\!:\!c_1z\rangle\circ\iota\big)
\;=\;\langle z\!:\!c_1\rangle ,
\qquad
\big[\,\langle1\!:\!c_1z\rangle\,\langle z\!:\!c_1\rangle:z\,\big] ,
\]
whose two $\iota$-image factors each read the base
once, $\langle1\!:\!c_1z\rangle$ at its leading coefficient and
$\langle z\!:\!c_1\rangle$ at its root
$c_1$, so the weight's read at the base is order $2$. Both orders are
independent of $c_1$, and the base collects at the orders' sum,
\[
c_1^{\,1}\cdot c_1^{\,2}\;=\;c_1^{\,3} .
\]
So the channel's coordinate is the integer $3=1+2$ and its base is $c_1$:
the two orders are what the theory determines, the base what they are read
at. The read is one divisor count at every position of the
$\iota$-image root, and $c_1=1$ places that root at the crossing,
the one count throughout.
\begin{proof}
The boundary
couples to the tail by the single entry one, and the unit-triangular
congruence of Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia} splits the pair
$(J_{L+1}+y_-\!:\!y_+)$'s datum as
the boundary pivot against $(J_L+y_-\!:\!y_+)$'s, the pivot the
boundary diagonal $c_1+y_-$ against $y_+$ joined to the coupling's
square, one, times $m^{(L)}$, its unit witness the boundary entry,
the seed the one-site diagonal, so the boundary entry
solves the displayed pivot identity.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The channel reads]\label{def:channelreads}
At a base $c_1$ the channel's derived objects
(Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}) are ground reads
(Definition~\ref{def:poly}): the boundary entry $G_0$
at its renewal witness $G_0=z+c_1zG_0$, as the witness's two
coefficient lists; the mass point $z_*$ at $c_1z_*=1$;
the \emph{pole order} of $G_0$ at $z_*$, the gap of the clearing
factor's root multiplicity there against the series member's; the
$\iota$-symmetrized
weight's factor list
$\big(\langle1\!:\!c_1z\rangle,\ \langle z\!:\!c_1\rangle\big)$
over the second
member $z$,
each factor reading the base at degree one; and the \emph{order
count}, the pole order added to the factor list's count.
\end{definition}

\section{The cell certificate}

\begin{theorem}[Gap positivity on the interior, assembled]\label{thm:gappos}
At every interior end-weight ray of $\mathcal C$ the cut of
$\mathcal K\big([\,\alpha:\beta\,]\big)$ holds a member pair,
positive by its shape: the interior is a union of
located cells, the root coordinate's rays $q\,\tau=p$ read their
cells directly, the counting sandwich of (v) hands every further ray
its cut at the sandwich's stated width, and on each cell the cut is
finitely many counts at a positive level of the cell's own.

\emph{(i) The count has an object.} On a window the compression is
finite-dimensional (Proposition~\ref{prop:windowfinite}), so ``the number of
eigenvalues below a line'' denotes something and
$\mathrm{count}(a)=\operatorname{rev}(H\!:\!aG)$ is an exact reversal count.

\emph{(ii) The interior is covered by located cells.} At any interior
coupling and window, Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}'s modulus puts the
cut's verification on a finite compression at a computable cutoff, at
every coupling, and the decimation presents that compression's counts
per cell of the named divisor list (Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation};
Lemma~\ref{lem:relfiber}; Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}): the cells over
the coupling, the momenta and the residue
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}; Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(iii);
Lemma~\ref{lem:serstable}(iii)), read at
each dimension through stencil caps and momentum sums polynomial in it,
cover the interior, the \emph{free cell} at the free end
(Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend}; Lemma~\ref{lem:freecell}), the \emph{emitted
cells} of the decimation's divisor list between, and the \emph{contact cell}
at the other end (Lemma~\ref{lem:contactcell}; the approach the
corner cell's, Lemma~\ref{lem:corner}), every boundary a
located root.

\emph{(iii) Per cell the cut is a flat step, and the cutoff is priced.}
On each cell the flat step verifies the cut at a level $\kappa$,
finitely many anchored jump comparisons, each two counts at located
pairs (Theorem~\ref{thm:flatstep}), and
Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation} prices the cutoff at the $\alpha{=}1$
representative: at an admissible cutoff's order
$E_{\mathrm{low}}<\Lambda_C$ with its witness gap $\varsigma$ at
$E_{\mathrm{low}}+\varsigma=\Lambda_C$,
\[
E_0\,\varsigma\,\mathcal K_{\Lambda,\Lambda_C}
\;\le\;E_0\,\varsigma\,\mathcal K^{\mathrm{reg}}_\Lambda(v)+\beta^2\#p^2\,d_L^{\,2} ,
\]
at the theorem's admitted cutoffs and simple grounds: given a pair $\vartheta$, taking
$\vartheta\,\varsigma>\beta^2\#p^2\,d_L^{\,2}$ transports the
window reads to the regional cut with a modulus rather than along a
subsequence, at a rate the closure's dimension fold and the
region's plaquette count fix (Lemma~\ref{lem:fpcap}).
At a certified cutoff $C$, the upper count at
$e_C+\ell+E_0\kappa$ equal to one and the comparison
\[
\ell C>\ell W+\ell E_0\kappa+W^2,
\qquad W=\beta\#p\,d_L,
\]
give the cut at $\kappa$ and ground multiplicity one at
every larger cutoff, the cutoff-tail certificate with
$h=E_0\kappa$ and $\eta=\ell$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}). This record gives the
regional membership (Definition~\ref{def:K}).

\emph{(iv) The level is positive per cell, and the whole read closes
on finitely many cells.} The cell's level is a divisor read: on a
cell the original pencil's first two jumps stay separated, the
ground jump at the sum's unit in the level gap
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), read $1$ from the free end's
side (Theorem~\ref{thm:SO}; Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(i)).
At every region and every cutoff the count is the original pencil's total count
through its pivot witnesses, with the separated product read at
the total-content selection (Lemma~\ref{lem:relfiber}(iv)); the
counting functions are flat across
$(\varepsilon_0+\ell,\ \varepsilon_0+\ell+E_0\kappa)$ at the
window's ground $\varepsilon_0$, the fixed pair
$(\ell,\ell+E_0\kappa)$ the cell's offsets, the two counts read
through the ground-relative level identity
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), each count a cell function read
once (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}; Theorem~\ref{thm:flatstep}), and a
pair $\kappa$ named by the fixed offsets' positive gap is a located datum of
the cell, a content cell's the
$H([\,1:\tau^2\,])$ level distance, the free and contact cells
reading theirs outright (Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend};
Lemma~\ref{lem:contactcell}; the contact
approach at the corner scale's heights, Lemma~\ref{lem:corner}) and each
interior boundary one located two-sided read of the divisor, and
\[
\mathcal K(v)\;\ge\;\kappa
\]
on the whole cell, the level at or beyond $E_0\kappa$ above the
ground (Definition~\ref{def:K}), located point by located point, each
cell read at one pair (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}). The level lines,
the fixed offsets joined to each window's designated ground, sit off the
divisor at a cell's boundaries at the margin, their distance from
the first two jumps there, each line's counting function one
cell function on a located segment through the boundary
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}), two consecutive cells' segments
overlap, and the cells' closed union is the segments' union, every
root-coordinate point inside one segment. Each cell's count reads
at the cell's own clearance: a cell's head is one family list at
every rank clearing its reach sum by two and its head bound's rank
(Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(ii),(iii);
Lemma~\ref{lem:serstable}(ii),(iii)), its cutoff a read of the ray at
the scaled magnetic weight (Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation} at the
closure's dimension fold; Lemma~\ref{lem:serstable}(iii)), so on the
cell one symbolic verification is every cleared rank's, the rank
divisors at their leading sides at every one of their ranks off the
classifications' displayed merged roots, those ranks reading their
tied pairs at the multiplicity (the classifications of
Lemma~\ref{lem:chaininstances} and Lemma~\ref{lem:serdivisors} at
the member's stated list; the settled sides,
Lemma~\ref{lem:genericlift}(iv),(v)), the ranks below the clearance
read the cell directly, each a finite member
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}), and a further list's cells read
at the member outright, its member data finite
(Construction~\ref{con:fusion}); a ray's cell at a member is the
member's own, its cutoff read at the ray's scaled weight, so the
member's cell list is its rays' cutoffs', finite at every member with
every ray read at one cell; and the
channel-degeneration residues are each their own read. The
quantifier over the dimension closes at the derivations: the fibering,
the decimation, the charged grading and the flat step are derived at every
$d$, with the stencil caps and the momentum sums polynomial in it, and
the head's jump reads are counts at every window there
(Theorem~\ref{thm:SO};
Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(i)), so each cell's $\kappa$ is a positive
located datum at every dimension, the divisor's own read; a
dimension's cell list is one
instance of those derivations, as is a channel-degeneration
residue's, residues one and two at their own channel data
(Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}).

\emph{(v) The reads close across each cell, at the sandwich's
width.} The cut's
comparisons are counting-function reads, and counts obey a coupling
sandwich: at couplings $v,v'$ of a cell whose pencils' site datum
$S$ at $H(v)=H(v')+S$ is
capped two-sidedly at $\rho\,G$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}) on the
stated list, against $G$'s stored factorization, every count obeys
\[
\mathrm{count}_v\langle a\!:\!\rho\rangle\ \le\ \mathrm{count}_{v'}(a)\ \le\
\mathrm{count}_v(a+\rho)
\]
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}, counts monotone under $\preceq$), so every
jump bracket travels between the two couplings at width $\rho$.
At every interior end-weight pair the cut of
$\mathcal K\big([\,\alpha:\beta\,]\big)$ holds a positive member,
the ray's own cell's floor: the root coordinate's rays read their
cells directly at the cells' located floors, the corner rays at
the decimated head's located gap at the ray
(Lemma~\ref{lem:corner}; Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerfloor}), one positive
pair per ray, and every
further pair ray is a located coupling between them whose margin
absorbs the sandwich's width. At the window pencil the two
couplings' site datum is the magnetic weights' gap against the
magnetic member, capped two-sidedly at that gap's multiple of the
magnetic member's own cap $W$, Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}'s cap at
the unit magnetic weight, so a further pair ray
$[\,\alpha:\beta\,]$ reads its window at a root-coordinate ray
$[\,q^{2}:p^{2}\,]$ with $p^{2}\alpha<\beta q^{2}\le(p+1)^{2}\alpha$,
$p$ the least natural at the squared comparison, and $q$ beyond
$\alpha$ and at or beyond $4W(2\tau^{\ast}+1)$ at a natural
$\tau^{\ast}$ at or beyond the segments' union's top, the cell's
levels cleared to naturals with $W$ the cap at that clearing, the
cell's level gap a natural at or beyond one there, and at a pair
$\kappa$ whose double sits
at or below the neighbor's cell's level gap against $E_0$, the
cell holding the root-coordinate ray $[\,q^{2}:p^{2}\,]$, the ray's cut
holds $\alpha\kappa$ at its representative $[\,\alpha:\beta\,]$,
one positive pair per ray.

\emph{(vi) The sector's read at every list.} Clauses (i)--(v) read
the vacuum sector's depth chain (Construction~\ref{con:depthchain})
at every magnetic list, the faithfulness of the member's stated list
entering the charged sectors alone (Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell};
Theorem~\ref{thm:flatstep}), so on the vacuum sector the cut of
Definition~\ref{def:K} compressed to the sector holds a positive
member at every interior ray at every list, and at a faithful list
the sectors are the charges and the window's cut is the sectors'

counts at a block diagonal).
\begin{proof}
\emph{(iv)} Root collisions sit on the crossing divisor alone
(Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(ii)), so on a cell the original pencil's
first two jumps stay separated. At each window the ground-relative
level identity (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}) reads the fixed
offsets at the absolute lines joined to that window's ground,
their gap the offsets' own. The level lines sit off the

(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}). At each window the two total
counts of Theorem~\ref{thm:flatstep} give its cut by
Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}. The reads at every region and
every cutoff give the meet's membership (Definition~\ref{def:K}).

\emph{(v)} The cap: the decimated entries' derivative coefficient
folds price the site datum entrywise over the pair distance, two
points' values differing by at most the distance against the fold
at the bound (Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}'s priced side read at

The least natural $p$ steps up at the square's order, its witness

and $p$ at or below $q\,\tau^{\ast}$ at the ray inside the segments'

below a quarter of the cell's level gap and the transported window

magnetic cap independently of the content cutoff. The
neighbor ray's certificate reads at each cutoff, and
the displayed sandwich gives that window's transported cut.
Their meet gives the transported membership
(Definition~\ref{def:K}).
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[The rank divisors]
\label{lem:chaininstances}
The rank divisors of the chain's

(Construction~\ref{con:places}): per band family the

and the stencil cap $3\,d_L=6\,n$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:fpcap}). The
depth-two instance closes on $29$ records, the gaps each a product

\]
the seven families at the second fusion depth, the fundamental with

(Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}); the binding comparisons, twenty-one;

against the kernel point at $n=2$ (the gap $2\,(n+1)\,g$ at the

\begin{lemma}[The series' rank divisors]

three further links' floor, one display per member. The unit sector's members are the loops at every label, a loop's
flux the unit at every cut (Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}(i)), so its
depth-two closure is the labels within two list fusions of the
unit label whatever their class, and a charged sector's members
are the string's labels at the sector's class. At $C_\ell$ the

$\omega_1$, its square's two members $2\omega_1=\theta$ and

(Construction~\ref{con:memtable}'s spinor table at the wedge's

(Lemma~\ref{lem:serstable}(ii)), the table's $\omega_k$ row read at
the listed keys; a spinor sector's, based at the spinor, the spinor
families at one run of ones added, $e_1+\cdots+e_j$ at $j$ at or
below the head bound's read, joined at even rank by the vector's
square against the spinor, $2\omega_1+s$; and the
vector sector's at $D_\ell$ the vector against the unit sector's
depth-two members at the vector's class, $\omega_{2j+1}$ and
$\omega_1+\omega_{2j}$ at $j$ at or below the head bound's read
(the vector's row at $\omega_{2j}$, Lemma~\ref{lem:serstable}(ii)),
joined at even rank by the vector's cube's members $3\omega_1$ and
$\omega_1+\omega_2$. The unit tables, the gaps against the unit label's kernel point at
their doubled reads, the spinor rows pairs at four:
\[
\begin{array}{llll}
\text{family} & 2\,\mathrm{gap} & \text{witness} & \text{clearance}\\
\hline
C_\ell:\quad\omega_1 & 2r+1 & & 3\\
\omega_2 & 4\,r & & 4\\
2\omega_1=\theta & 4\,(r+1) & & 3\\[2pt]
B_\ell:\quad\omega_k & 2k\,(r+3-k) & & k+2\\
\text{the spinor} & [\,(r+2)(r+3):4\,] & &\\[2pt]
D_\ell:\quad\omega_k & 2k\,(r+3-k) & & k+2\\
\text{a spinor} & [\,(r+2)(r+3):4\,] & &\\
2\omega_1\ \text{(even rank)} & 4\,(r+3) & & 3\\
\omega_1+s\ \text{(even rank)} & [\,(r+3)(r+10):4\,] & & 3
\end{array}
\]
the leading fundamentals' rows one display at every $k$ and the
spinor's row read at both spinors, a dual pair at odd rank and the
two self-dual spinors at even rank, one gap at every rank. The
charged tables, the gaps against the base's Casimir, the spinor
list one table for $B_\ell$ and $D_\ell$ with a word of odd box
count at $D_\ell$ read at the flipped base, the class kept:
\[
\begin{array}{llll}
\text{spinor word} & \mathrm{gap} & & \text{clearance}\\
\hline
e_1+\cdots+e_j & j\,(r+4-j) & & j+2\\
2e_1\ (D_\ell,\ \text{even rank}) & 2r+8 & & 3
\end{array}
\qquad
\begin{array}{llll}
C_\ell,\ \omega_1 & \mathrm{gap} & \text{wit.} & \text{cl.}\\
\hline
(1,1,1) & 2\,g & g{+}1{=}r & 5\\
(2,1) & 2r+1 & & 4\\
(3) & 2\,(r+2) & & 3
\end{array}
\]
\[
\begin{array}{llll}
D_\ell,\ \text{vector} & \mathrm{gap} & & \text{cl.}\\
\hline
(1^{2j+1}) & 2j\,(r+1-2j) & & 2j+3\\
(2,1^{2j-1}) & 2j\,(r+3-2j)+2 & & 2j+2\\
(3)\ \text{(even rank)} & 2\,(r+5) & & 3
\end{array}
\]
the spinor words' row and the vector sector's rows one display at
every $j$.

\emph{The records.} Per sector, the family gaps and the

$\langle\mathrm{gap}_i\!:\!\mathrm{gap}_j\rangle$ over the sector's
family pairs; and per member the stencil cap $3\,d_L$ at the

$C_\ell$, $3\cdot2^{\ell}$ at $B_\ell$, $3\cdot2^{\ell}$ at odd-rank

even, an
exponential-polynomial pair in the rank
(Lemma~\ref{lem:genericlift}(v)); the record count per head bound is

\emph{The classification} is the equal-members reads of the
displayed divisors in the rank domains, the domains the residue

charged gaps as well ($2r-2$ below $2r+1$ below $2r+4$); at $B_\ell$
and $D_\ell$ two leading fundamentals' gaps $2k\,(r+3-k)$ and
$2k'\,(r+3-k')$ at $k<k'$ differ by the doubled product
$(k'-k)\,(r+3-k-k')$, positive at every rank clearing both
families, $k+k'$ at or below $2\ell-3$ against $r+3$ at or beyond
$2\ell$; the spinor's gap against a leading fundamental's,
$[\,(r+2)(r+3):4\,]$ against $2k\,(r+3-k)$, reads its upper side
beyond the residue $8k$ (the difference
$(r+3)\,(r+2-8k)+8k^{2}$) and its equality at the roots of
$(r+2)(r+3)=8k\,(r+3-k)$, at most two per $k$, each a merged level
read at its rank with the counts at the multiplicity
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}'s boundary clause), the root at $k=1$
the residue five, $D_4$'s vector against its spinors; at $D_\ell$'s
even rank the square's gap $4\,(r+3)$ against $\omega_k$'s ties
exactly at $(k-2)\,(r+3)=k^{2}$, $k-2$ a divisor of four, every
solve below the clearance or at an even residue, and against the
spinor's at the residue fourteen, even; the two spinors read one
gap at every rank, a merged level with the counts at the
multiplicity, and the spinor family $\omega_1+s$ at even rank reads
its gap beyond the spinors' at every rank, off the square's at the
residue six, even, and against $\omega_k$'s on its upper side beyond
the residue $8k$ (the difference $(r+3)\,(r+10-8k)+8k^{2}$, rootless
at $k=1$) and at the roots of $(r+3)(r+10)=8k\,(r+3-k)$ below it, at
most two per $k$, each a merged level read at its rank; two spinor words' gaps
$j\,(r+4-j)$ and $j'\,(r+4-j')$ at $j<j'$ differ by
$(j'-j)\,(r+4-j-j')$, positive at every rank clearing both,
$j+j'$ at or below $2\ell-3$ against $r+4$ at or beyond $2\ell+1$,
and the square's word at even rank ties a spinor word exactly at
$r\,(j-2)=j^{2}-4j+8$, $j-2$ a divisor of four, every solve even or
below the word's clearance;
and the vector sector's rows at $D_\ell$ keep one side at every
cleared rank: $(1^{2j+1})$ against $(2,1^{2j-1})$ at the gap $4j+2$,
two rows of one shape at the fundamentals' read above, a cross tie
$(1^{2j+1})$ against $(2,1^{2j'-1})$ at $j$ off $j'$ reading its
residue at the join $r\,(j-j')=2j^{2}-j-2j'^{2}+3j'+1$, the gap
$j-j'$ a divisor of $2j'+1$ with an odd quotient and the residue
$2\,(j-j')-1+4j'$ joined to it, even, off the odd domain, and the
cube's rows at even rank tying $(1^{2j+1})$ at
$r\,(j-1)=2j^{2}-j+5$ and $(2,1^{2j-1})$ at $r\,(j-1)=2j^{2}-3j+4$,
$j-1$ a divisor of six or of three, every solve even or at odd
rank. So every displayed divisor keeps its leading side at every
further cleared rank, one symbolic read every such rank's, a
comparison's ranks those clearing its families' reaches; and a
family below its clearance reads its finitely many ranks' data
directly, the calculus's displays at the rank's label
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}; Corollary~\ref{cor:weyldim};
Corollary~\ref{cor:steinberg}), one evaluation each.
\begin{proof}
\emph{The spinor pair.} The exchange of the last two simple
letters reads the last coordinate to its balance partner, fixing
the form and the root fold (the last key's read equal members) and
exchanging the two spinor classes, each sector's base with its
closure, so the spinor pair's records are one displayed list.
\emph{The families.} The gap is three folds over the word's
occupied keys: the square fold and the doubled base fold are
rank-free, the word's own form square and its doubled dot against
the base's list, and the root fold's read is the word's fold
against the displayed key reads, linear in the rank. \emph{The unit
tables.} The leading fundamentals' rows read the gap
$2\,C_2(\omega_k)$ at the displayed key reads ($k\,(2\ell-k+1)$ at
$B_\ell$ and $k\,(2\ell-k)$ at $D_\ell$, the residues $r+2=2\ell$
and $r+3=2\ell$), the spinor's the doubled display of
Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor} at the rank's residue,
$2\,C_2(s)=[\,\ell\,(2\ell+1):2\,]$ at $B_\ell$, the square's
$2\,C_2(2\omega_1)=8\,\ell$ and the spinor family's
$2\,C_2(\omega_1+s)=[\,\ell\,(2\ell+7):2\,]$ at $D_\ell$. \emph{The
charged tables.} The rows of $e_1$, $e_1{+}e_2$, $e_1{+}e_2{+}e_3$
and $e_1{+}\cdots{+}e_4$ read $r+3$, $2\,(r+2)$, $3\,(r+1)$ and
$4\,r$, the square's word at $4+2+2\,(2\ell-2)$ over the three
folds, and the vector sector's rows read at the form's reads
$C_2(\omega_k)=k\,(2\ell-k)$ and
$C_2(\omega_1+\omega_k)=2\ell\,(k+1)-k^{2}+1$ against
$C_2(\omega_1)=2\ell-1$ at $2\ell=r+3$, the rows of $(1,1,1)$ and
$(2,1)$ reading $2\,(r-1)$ and $2\,(r+2)$.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}
