\section{The count certificates}

The statements below are the cell calculus's arithmetic, made finite
and constructible: the counts, the located roots, and the window reads
the decimation and the flat step take.

\begin{lemma}[The reversal count]\label{lem:inertia}
Over a located stage (Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}), where every entry's
members' equality and side are stage reads, the \emph{reversal count} of a
form pair, written $\operatorname{rev}(A\!:\!B)$ at symmetric $A$,
$B$ of order $N$, is the side count of the pair: the dimension of
a maximal list on whose span $B$ exceeds $A$ at every combination off
the sum's unit, the two lists of the proof its witnesses. The count is
read off a \emph{pivot split} of the
pair's elimination datum $S$, the site structure at
$A=B+S$ read entrywise (Definition~\ref{def:elim}): a \emph{unit
congruence}, $T$ at its witness $T'$ at $TT'=1$ and $T'T=1$, the
two reads the statement's data,
$T^{\mathsf T}ST=D$ with $D$ block diagonal in nonsingular blocks of
orders $1$ and $2$ and one \emph{kernel block}, its columns' $T$-image
spanning the datum's kernel; a nonsingular block reads its
\emph{sides}, one per unit: an order-$1$ block its entry's side, and
a symmetric $2\times2$ block two side reads off its data (the
determinant on its lower side reads one unit per side, the
\emph{mixed} block; on its upper side the identity
$S_{11}S_{22}=\det+S_{12}^{2}$ puts the
diagonal product on its upper side, both entries of unequal members at
one shared side, which both units read), so a split reads a
lower-side count,
the order-$1$ blocks' sides with the $2\times2$ reads. Every
symmetric $S$ has a split, closed in at most $N$ pivot steps, and
every two splits read one lower-side count:
$\operatorname{rev}(A\!:\!B)$ is that shared count, the split's
pivot ordering certificate data, and $\operatorname{rev}S$
abbreviates the count at $S$ its own elimination datum. A split
enters cleared: over pair data the congruence reads at an integer
$T$, square at the datum's order, its determinant of unequal
members with the adjugate against the determinant the witness's
solve (Definition~\ref{def:elim}), and the block diagonal absorbs
the columns' rescaling at every side fixed, the cleared read the
unit congruence's by the homogeneity principle
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}), one count at either spelling. The split
reads the \emph{rank}
with it, the kernel block's complement, one count at every split and
blind to unit congruence with the reversal count: a split
$(T,D)$ of $S$ is the split $(T,\check D)$ of the memberwise swap
$\check S$ (each entry's member swap) at the block
sides exchanged, so the rank is the two counts' sum,
$\operatorname{rev}(S)+\operatorname{rev}(\check S)$. A datum is
\emph{positive semidefinite} where a split's nonsingular blocks read
the upper side throughout, the split the statement's witness, and
\emph{positive definite} where those blocks' orders sum to the
datum's; a form pair $(A\!:\!B)$ is positive semidefinite where
its elimination datum is, the glyphs $B\preceq A$
and $A\succeq B$ denote that read, and $S\succ0$ denotes $S$
positive definite; a datum $S$ is \emph{capped
two-sidedly} at $C$ where $S\preceq C$ holds and the sum $C+S$ is
positive semidefinite, two splits as the statement's witnesses.
Consequently:
$\operatorname{rev}(T^{\mathsf T}ST)=\operatorname{rev}(S)$
at $T$ with its witness;
$\operatorname{rev}(qS)=\operatorname{rev}(S)$ at a pair $q$ above
the sum's unit, a
split $(T,D)$ of $S$ being the split $(T,qD)$ of $qS$ with every
block's sides and determinant side fixed; a symmetric $\mathrm{LDL}^{\mathsf T}$ reads
$\operatorname{rev}$ as its count of lower-side pivots, and when
the leading principal minors read unequal members the pivots are
their successive cofactors ($m_j\,d_{j+1}=m_{j+1}$), so $\operatorname{rev}$ is the minor
sequence's own orientation-reversal count, the reversals along
$1,m_1,\dots,m_N$ (Jacobi's rule), the name's read;
$S\preceq S'$ gives
$\operatorname{rev}(S)\ge\operatorname{rev}(S')$; a
compression's counts are at most the full form's; inertia adds at a
nonsingular principal pivot,
\[
\operatorname{rev}(S)=\operatorname{rev}(P)
+\operatorname{rev}(S_P)
\quad\text{at}\quad
S=\Big[\begin{smallmatrix}P&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&Q\end{smallmatrix}\Big],
\qquad
B^{\mathsf T}C_P+S_P=Q\ \ \text{at the solve}\ \ P\,C_P=B ,
\]
$S_P$ the pivot's \emph{deflation}, its witness $C_P$ the
adjugate column against the determinant, the deflation symmetric at
a symmetric datum, the coupling's transpose against the witness the
witness's pairing against the pivot,
$B^{\mathsf T}C_P=C_P^{\mathsf T}PC_P$ at the solve's transpose, its
every multiple symmetric with it, a pivot at stated places
entering at the leading position by the congruence at the places'
permutation matrix, its transpose the witness
(Construction~\ref{con:places}'s transpose identity at the matrix
carrier) with the count the congruence read's own, and the determinant
splits with the inertia at the cleared scale: each trailing row
enters at the pivot's determinant against the leading rows'
combination at the solve's witness column, one scale per trailing
row, the minor's scale and combination reads
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}) reading the scale's power at the
deflation's order against the reduced list's determinant, the
coupling's exchange withdrawn at the solve so the reduced list is
block triangular with its trailing block the deflation at one
further scale per row, and a block-triangular list's determinant is
its diagonal blocks' product, every assignment crossing into the
vacant slab reading an entry at the sum's unit:
$\det P\cdot\det\big((\det P)^2S_P\big)=(\det P)^{2o}\det S$
at $o$ the deflation's order, $\det S=\det P\cdot\det S_P$ its
read at the off-unit scale's injectivity;
two square lists' \emph{product}, its entries the first's rows
against the second's columns at the coordinate fold, reads its
determinant at the factors' own, one joined list's two reads: at
the join of the identity's memberwise swap beside the second list
over the first list beside a vacant block, the trailing slab
clears against the leading rows at the first list's own
coefficients, one combination per row with the further summands
repeated-row reads of equal members
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}), onto the vacant slab beside the two
lists' product, and the cleared join's determinant is the
block-triangular read at the swapped identity against the
product's; the slabs' exchange, one transposition per row pair
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}), reads the joined list block
triangular at the factors instead, and the exchange count joins the swapped
identity's diagonal to an even family
(Construction~\ref{con:places}): the signs withdraw and the
product's determinant is the determinants' product;
inertia adds at a block diagonal outright,
\[
\operatorname{rev}(P\oplus Q)\;=\;
\operatorname{rev}(P)+\operatorname{rev}(Q) ,
\]
the addition's instance at a coupling of equal members: the two
splits concatenate to a split of the block diagonal, the
congruences joined at that off-block with the block lists appended,
the kernel columns collected to the tail and the kernel orders
added;
and a symmetric matrix of unequal-membered determinant has a
nonsingular principal submatrix of order at most two.
\begin{proof}
\emph{Existence.} At a nonsingular principal block $P$ of order $1$
or $2$, the unit-triangular congruence at upper block $\check C_P$,
the witness's memberwise swap ($P\,C_P=B$),
maps $S$ to $P\oplus S_P$, and the recursion descends to the
deflation. With every principal minor of orders $1$ and $2$
of equal members, the diagonal reads equal members entrywise, each
order-two minor then reads $S_{ij}^{2}$, and $S_{ij}$ with it, of
equal members: a symmetric
block either has such a pivot or is the kernel block, so the
leftmost admissible pivot closes a split in at most $N$ steps, the
per-step congruences composing to $T$; in particular a symmetric
matrix of unequal-membered determinant has a nonsingular principal
submatrix of order at most $2$.

\emph{The mixed blocks' two witnesses.} At
$P=\big[\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{smallmatrix}\big]$ with the
determinant $\langle ac\!:\!b^2\rangle$ on its lower side, a
lower-side vector is read off the entries:
$e_1$ at $a$ on its lower side; $(b,\,\check a)$ at $a$ on its upper
side, $\check a$ the member swap,
reading $a\,\langle ac\!:\!b^2\rangle$ on the lower; and at $a$ of
equal members, where $b$'s members differ, the vector
$(w,\,b+b)$ at $w$ the balance partner of $c+1$, its read the
balance partner of $(b+b)^2$, the cross terms collecting at the
constant's swap, on the lower side at $b$'s occupied square. An upper-side
vector of $P$ is a lower-side vector of the memberwise swap
$\check P$, the recipe read there.

\emph{The two lists of a split, and the exchange read.} From a split
$(T,D)$ at lower-side count $\nu$, the \emph{lower list} takes, per
lower-side unit, the $T$-image of one block-supported vector: each
lower-side order-$1$ column, both columns of each $2\times2$ at the
shared lower side, and each mixed block's lower-side vector. The list's
$\nu$ members are independent, the strict read's own consequence
(the forcing clause's read below), and $S$ reads the lower side at every
combination off the sum's unit:
distinct blocks' pairings read equal members through $D$, so a combination reads a
per-block sum, every term on its lower side or of equal members and
the terms at coefficients of unequal members on the lower side. The \emph{complement list} takes the
upper-side order-$1$ columns, both columns of each $2\times2$ at the
shared upper side, each mixed block's upper-side vector, and the kernel
block's columns: its member count $\mu$ at $\nu+\mu=N$, the block
orders' total, independent, with every $S$-read of a combination
on its upper side or of
equal members. For two
splits at counts $\nu_1$, $\nu_2$, join the first's lower list to
the second's complement list: the joint rank is one computation, and
a rank defect exhibits a dependency whose read is one stage element
with $x^{\mathsf T}Sx$ on its lower side and off it at once (a
dependency whose lower-list part is the sum's unit sits inside the
independent complement list), against a stage read's one side
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}): the joint list is independent,
$\nu_1+\mu_2\le N$ at $\nu_2+\mu_2=N$, and the exchange symmetrized reads
$\nu_1=\nu_2$. The joint-rank read at an arbitrary first list is the
\emph{forcing clause}: a list of $k$ vectors with every
$S$-read of a combination off the sum's unit on the lower side,
joined to any split's complement list,
forces $\operatorname{rev}(S)\ge k$, the strict read forcing the
list's independence outright: a combination reading the sum's unit
at coefficients off the unit family reads its own lower side
besides, against the trichotomy. The \emph{dual clause} runs at
the complement side with the independence its own stated clause,
an at-or-above read admitting a dependency at the sum's unit: an
independent list of $k$ vectors with every $S$-read of a
combination at its upper side or equal members, joined to any
split's lower list, forces $k+\operatorname{rev}(S)\le N$.

\emph{The consequences.} A split of $T^{\mathsf T}ST$ at $U$ is a
split of $S$ at $TU$: the count is invariant. Splits of $P$ and of
$S_P$ concatenate through the displayed congruence to a split of
$S$: inertia adds, and the two forcing clauses price the identity
besides: the pivot's and the deflation's lower lists, padded and
lifted through the solve with every cross pairing the witness's
own unit read, force one side, and the complement lists at the
dual clause the other. At a coupling of equal members the lift is
a padding besides, and the pricing runs without the solve: the two
lower lists, each padded into its own half of the join, read the
block diagonal at the two forms' sum with the cross pairings at
the sum's unit, and the complement lists at the dual clause read
the other side. An $\mathrm{LDL}^{\mathsf T}$ is a split at
order-$1$ blocks, the congruence by the unit-triangular witness $T$
at $L^{\mathsf T}T=1$, one back-substitution, onto the pivot
diagonal, whose $k$-th leading minor is the product of the first $k$
pivots. At $S\preceq S'$ the datum $R$ at $S'=S+R$ is positive
semidefinite, so $x^{\mathsf T}Sx+x^{\mathsf T}Rx=x^{\mathsf T}S'x$ at every
$x$ through the
congruence with the $R$-read on its upper side or of equal members;
on $S'$'s lower list the $S$-read sits below the $S'$-read, on the
lower side with it, and the
forcing clause reads
$\operatorname{rev}(S)\ge\operatorname{rev}(S')$. For a
compression $P^{\mathsf T}SP$, the compression's lower list
maps through $P$ to an independent list with every $S$-read of a
combination off the sum's unit on the lower side (a
combination with $Pc$ the sum's unit at $c$ off it reads
$c^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}SPc$ on its lower side and of equal members
at once, against the trichotomy), and the forcing clause closes it.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[The designation, and the witness]
\label{thm:certconstruct}
Let $H,G$ have entries of a located stage
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}) with $G$ positive definite, and let $\mathrm{count}(a):=
\operatorname{rev}(H\!:\!aG)$; at a balance-pair level
$\langle x\!:\!y\rangle$ (Definition~\ref{def:ground}) the count is
\[
\mathrm{count}\langle x\!:\!y\rangle\;:=\;
\operatorname{rev}\big(H+y\,G\;:\;x\,G\big)\,,
\]
the level's second member cross-added onto the pencil's own side, so
a root on its lower side reads its bracket as one on its upper does; each
count exact by symmetric $\mathrm{LDL}^{\mathsf T}$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,itemsep=1pt]
\item \emph{(The designation.)} A \emph{designation} of a jump of
the counting function is the data $(l,h,w)$ at $l+w=h$ with the two
counts read at a gap, $\mathrm{count}(l)+g=\mathrm{count}(h)$ at
$g\ge1$, the width $w$ at most the $\delta$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}: the bracket admits one distinct root
alone, at multiplicity
$g$, and the reads are its whole verification. At the least root the
lower read sharpens to the pair at $l$ positive semidefinite, one
split and one count. Designations exist at every stated width, the
refinement closing in the least $k$ at
$w_0\le2^k\delta$ from the starting gap $w_0$ at $l_0+w_0=h_0$,
each step one count. The refinement runs at any
stage read whose trichotomy exchanges sides along a segment, a
polynomial's side read at Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s separation
among them, the equality outcome naming a root outright with the
recentering emitting its bracket. An emitted designation enters as
certificate data, its reads re-read at every verification.
\item \emph{(The witness $u$.)} For \emph{any} form pair $(A\!:\!B)$ of pair
entries with $\operatorname{rev}(A\!:\!B)\ge1$, the symmetric $\mathrm{LDL}^{\mathsf T}$
of its elimination datum has a lower-side pivot, and the corresponding column of the accumulated
pair-entried transform is a vector $u$ with
$u^{\mathsf T}Bu>u^{\mathsf T}Au$, the reversal's read
off the elimination. At $(H\!:\!aG)$ that is the certificate's witness whenever
$\mathrm{count}(a)\ge1$.
\end{enumerate}
\begin{proof}
The bracket is narrower than the separation, and two distinct roots
inside it sit closer than $\delta$, refused by
Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}: it admits one distinct root alone, and
the counts' gap $g$ is that root's multiplicity, the count identity's
read (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}). The existence: the
radius of Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep} reads two starting levels, the
lower below every root at the split and the upper beyond every root
at the full count; from two levels at counts at a gap, the mean's
count sits at a gap against one end's, the half at that gap the next
bracket, the width halving, so the refinement closes in the least $k$ at
$w_0\le2^k\delta$; and at the least-root instance a mean at the
lower end's count either is positive semidefinite, moving the lower
level, or is singular there, the mean naming the root and one
recentering at
$2w'\le\delta$ emitting the designation. The witness: at
$\operatorname{rev}(A\!:\!B)\ge1$ the split reads a lower-side unit
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), $u$ its column of the congruence, and the
congruence's read $u^{\mathsf T}Su$ at the elimination datum $S$ at
$A=B+S$ is that unit's entry on its lower side, so
$u^{\mathsf T}Au$ sits below $u^{\mathsf T}Bu$.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[The count is a cell function]\label{lem:cellcount}
Let $(H(x),G(x))$ be a symmetric pencil whose entries are polynomial in

principal minor of order at most two whose determinant keeps its

(Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}) at a bound containing the subinterval, at
order two its leading entry so as well where the determinant sits
on its upper side, and
beneath it the cleared deflation's own cover, the deflation cleared
once at the designated minor's magnitude, the minor's multiple of the
deflation at a pivot whose determinant keeps its upper side and its
memberwise swap at a pivot keeping its lower side or at the mixed
block, and at a pivot whose coupling to the trailing places reads the
sum's unit the trailing block's own cover in the deflation's place,
the cover at the vacant order holding outright, the determinant's
root-freeness the cover's read; the locus's points are located
over $D$'s squarefree part, the division descent's iterated
divisions with the B\'ezout witnesses the certificate data
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s descent at
Lemma~\ref{lem:stagesplit}'s squarefree read), a bracket's root
count the segment count at the cleared variable
(Lemma~\ref{lem:hermitesign} at Lemma~\ref{lem:deckfactor}'s
clearing); hence the count is one integer on each
piecewise-linearly connected cell of $X$ off that locus; at a box
of $X$ of two variables, one bracket per variable, the cover is the
box cut at stated points, one variable per cut, each point strictly
inside its variable's bracket, into pieces, boxes, a cut's two boxes
meeting along it, each piece with its designated
minor keeping its side over the piece at the box's priced side read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}), at order two its leading entry so as well
where the determinant sits on its upper side, and beneath it the
once-cleared deflation's own box cover over the piece, the deflation
or its memberwise swap at the designated minor's side, so the count

root is at least $a$, the point's read entering as its own split

Write $S(t)$ for the pair's site datum at $H=aG+S$ along the

\begin{lemma}[The located stage]\label{lem:stage}
\emph{The arithmetic.} A \emph{located root} of a polynomial over a
\emph{located stage} ($\mathbb P$, or a field built here, every element
with its bracket) is a root
$\varepsilon$ of its squarefree part $S$ (the division
descent, Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}),
with an isolating bracket of balance-pair endpoints
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}) off $S$'s roots, narrower
than half the separation of Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}, whose
derivation is stage arithmetic outright, division reads,
coefficient folds and bracket comparisons. The stage $K(\varepsilon)$ is $K[x]$
read at $\varepsilon$: at $p\in K[x]$ with $g$ the greatest common
divisor of $(p,S)$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s descent), the value
$p(\varepsilon)$ reads equal members exactly where $g$ exchanges sides on the bracket; at $p(\varepsilon)$
of unequal members
the root sits on the cofactor $S_1$ at $g\,S_1=S$, coprime to $p$, and the B\'ezout read $u\,p+v\,S_1=1$ reads at the root
to the \emph{unit witness}, $p(\varepsilon)\,u(\varepsilon)=1$.
Sums and products
are remainder reads, the division at $S$, a value's unit is
the B\'ezout read's witness,
and a value's side at the root is a count read
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}), the bracket the certificate naming
which root, every entry an elimination read of the stage below, so
the adjunction stays grounded and the recursion ends at the ground
pairs' own comparisons. At $p(\varepsilon)$ of unequal members the
unit witness floors the value: at $U_1$ the coefficient
fold of $u$ over the bracket (Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s
magnitudes), the
witness identity read cross-multiplied floors the margin of
$p(\varepsilon)$ at $\mathrm{margin}\cdot U_1\ge1$; and the
\emph{priced side read}: at bracket endpoints inside a stated
bound's segment, the bound entering at a second datum beyond the
sum's unit, the radius segment among them at the leading
coefficient's margin, two bracket
points' values of $p$ differ by at most the bracket's width against
the derivative's coefficient fold at the bound
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s magnitudes, the binomial identity
per occupied key), so an endpoint value of $p$ clearing that price
keeps its side at every bracket point, the root's among them: the
cleared comparison is the side read's certificate, the endpoint
value's side the comparison's own read at the width price at or
beyond the sum's unit, $p$'s image width over the bracket priced
by the fold. The read runs on a \emph{box} besides: a polynomial
in two variables over the stage, the inner variable's polynomials
the outer variable's coefficients (Definition~\ref{def:poly}'s
polynomials as the entry carrier), at one bracket per variable
inside its own bound, keeps its side at every point of the box
where two priced reads hold, the inner variable's read above at
the corner's outer point, the coefficients read there, and the
outer variable's read at every inner point at once: the outer
derivative's coefficient fold at the outer bound, each coefficient
read at its own fold at the inner bound, against the outer width

derivative's fold at the two bounds, so at every inner point the
outer read's endpoint value sits within the inner price of the

iterates; a finite root list enters as a \emph{tower}, one
extension per root, each extension's polynomial over the stage the
earlier extensions built, the extension order certificate data: a
stored tower names its
order, and every read runs through the arithmetic above.
\begin{proof}
$g$ is a factor of the squarefree $S$, so its one possible root on
the bracket is simple,
and it is $\varepsilon$, the bracket isolating: $p(\varepsilon)$
reads equal members exactly where $g$ exchanges sides there. At
$p(\varepsilon)$ of unequal members the cofactor $S_1$ is coprime to
$p$ since $S$ is
squarefree, so the B\'ezout read exists and reads the unit witness

have their bracket (the isolating data, their image widths priced
above) and its division reads, coefficient folds, endpoint

are the

\begin{lemma}[The pencil's split]\label{lem:split}
For symmetric $H$ and $G\succ0$ of order $N$ over a
stage, with $Z(x)$ the level pair's site datum at $x\,G=H+Z(x)$ and
$\chi(x):=\det Z(x)$,
\[
\chi(x)\;=\;\det G\ \prod_{j=1}^N\langle x\!:\!\varepsilon_j\rangle,
\qquad
\mathrm{count}(a)\;=\;\#\{\,j:\varepsilon_j<a\,\}
\ \text{ at $a$ off the roots},
\]
the factors Definition~\ref{def:poly}'s linear factors at the
$\varepsilon_j$, located roots, and a unit congruence $S_\chi$ over the
stage they generate maps the pencil to diagonal form,
\[
S_\chi^{\mathsf T}\,Z(x)\,S_\chi\;=\;
\mathrm{diag}\big(\langle x\!:\!\varepsilon_j\rangle\,g_j\big),
\qquad g_j\ \text{on their upper sides}.
\]
\begin{proof}
Over the pairs the counting function climbs to $N$ from the
positive-semidefinite read between the radius reads of
Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}, and its jumps sit at the located roots
of $\chi$, each with its isolating bracket at the separation
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}; Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}). At a located root $\varepsilon$, the
kernel of $Z(\varepsilon)$ over $K(\varepsilon)$ has a spanning list by
elimination (Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}), of some dimension $m\ge1$, $G$-orthogonalized within,
and its $G$-complement $W$ another; at $z$ in the kernel and $w\in W$,
$z^{\mathsf T}Z(x)\,w=\langle x\!:\!\varepsilon\rangle\,z^{\mathsf T}Gw$,
of equal members at the complement's defining read, so the
congruence by the two lists is block diagonal, the kernel block
$\langle x\!:\!\varepsilon\rangle\,G_0$ at the kernel's Gram $G_0\succ0$ diagonal, and
\[
\chi(x)\;=\;c\,\langle x\!:\!\varepsilon\rangle^m\,\chi_W(x),\qquad
c\ \text{on its upper side},
\]
$\chi_W$ the deflated pencil's. $\chi_W(\varepsilon)$ is of unequal
members: a kernel vector
of the deflated pencil at $\varepsilon$ has its pairings against $W$ and
against the kernel both of equal members, so it is a kernel vector of the full
pencil lying inside $W$, and the kernel meets $W$ at the sum's unit alone.
Induction on $W$ splits $\chi$ over located roots, each
deflation's root adjoined over the stage the earlier roots built
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}), and concatenates the per-step lists to
$S_\chi$, block diagonal for $G$ and for $H$ at once by
the pairings above; the count identity is then the congruence read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}): at $a$ off the roots, the pair
$(H\!:\!aG)$'s elimination datum is the displayed datum's
balance partner, so
$\operatorname{rev}(H\!:\!aG)=\operatorname{rev}\,
\mathrm{diag}\big(\langle\varepsilon_j\!:\!a\rangle\,g_j\big)=\#\{j:\varepsilon_j<a\}$.
The completed congruence returns the factorization read: the
congruence identity's determinant collects the product read at the
exchanged lists (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia};
Definition~\ref{def:elim}) to $\det S_\chi^{\,2}\,\chi(x)$ against
the diagonal blocks' product
$\prod_j\langle x\!:\!\varepsilon_j\rangle\,g_j$; the identity's
linear coefficient, $S_\chi^{\mathsf T}GS_\chi$ at the diagonal of
the scales, collects its own determinants to
$\det S_\chi^{\,2}\,\det G$ against $\prod_jg_j$, and at a located
root's pair data the cleared factor enters at the scale, the
diagonal's entry $g_j\,(d_jx-n_j)$ at the root
$[\,n_j\!:\!d_j\,]$ with the linear coefficients collecting to
$\prod_jd_j\,g_j$ and the clearing $\prod_jd_j$ riding onto the
factorization's first member, one value at every representative
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}); and the shared
factor $\det S_\chi^{\,2}$, off equal members at the unit
congruence, withdraws at the products' one value key by key
(Definition~\ref{def:poly}): the displayed factorization is the
congruence certificate's own read.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Slab pivots: the factorization, the counts, and the Green
products]\label{lem:greenprod}
Let $S$ be symmetric over a located stage with a slab split $1..L$,
entries at the diagonal and neighboring slab pairs alone,
$A_i:=S[i,i]$, $B_i:=S[i,i+1]$, and the two
pivot recursions at solved witnesses, each solve the adjugate column
against the determinant,
\begin{gather*}
X_L=A_L,\quad X_i+B_i\,R_{i+1}=A_i\ \ \text{at}\ \
X_{i+1}R_{i+1}=B_i^{\mathsf T};\\
Y_1=A_1,\quad Y_{i+1}+B_i^{\mathsf T}\,C_i=A_{i+1}\ \ \text{at}\ \
Y_iC_i=B_i ,
\end{gather*}
at pivots of unequal-membered determinant (a singular slab pivot
re-orders within its slab by
Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}'s principal pivots of order at most two, the count
unchanged). Then:
\emph{(i)} the Schur complement of the tail $[i{+}1,L]$ onto $[1,i]$
maps $A_i$ to $X_i$ and fixes every other block: eliminating slab $L$
touches $A_{L-1}$ alone, the entries at $i<L-1$ against $L$ off the
band, and downward induction
extends it, so one recursion datum holds the whole tail, and every
pivot is symmetric: the seed is a diagonal block of the symmetric
datum, and at a symmetric $X_{i+1}$ the witness identity transposed
reads $B_i=R_{i+1}^{\mathsf T}X_{i+1}$, so the withdrawn term
$B_iR_{i+1}=R_{i+1}^{\mathsf T}X_{i+1}R_{i+1}$ is symmetric with $X_i$,
the induction downward from the seed; and the head pivots are
symmetric at their own induction: the seed $Y_1$ is a diagonal block
of the symmetric datum, and at a symmetric $Y_i$ the witness identity
transposed reads $B_i^{\mathsf T}=C_i^{\mathsf T}Y_i$, so the
withdrawn term $B_i^{\mathsf T}C_i=C_i^{\mathsf T}Y_iC_i$ is
symmetric with $Y_{i+1}$, the induction upward from its seed;
\emph{(ii)} $\operatorname{rev}(S)=\sum_i\operatorname{rev}(X_i)$
and $\det S=\prod_i\det X_i$, each elimination a unit-triangular
congruence (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia});
\emph{(iii)} with $Z_j$ the join's datum at $Z_j+A_j=X_j+Y_j$, read
off the two recursions, the solution of $S\,u=v$ at $v$ supported in
slab $j$ reads blockwise, at $i\le j$,
\[
Z_j\,u_j=v_j,
\qquad
u_i=T_i\,T_{i+1}\cdots T_h\,u_j\quad\text{at}\quad h+1=j\ ,
\]
at the \emph{transfer factors} $T_k$, each the memberwise swap of
the witness $C_k$, so $Y_k\,T_k+B_k$ is the sum's unit:
every Green block is a product of transfer factors and one corner
solve;
\emph{(iv)} at scalar slabs the datum assembled from the slab data
is square at the diagonal's count, at a bond list one shorter, and
its form at a walked vector reads the display's two folds, the
diagonal entries at the squares with the bonds at the doubled
consecutive products.
\begin{proof}
(i) and (ii) are the displayed inductions and congruences. (iii): solve
$Su=v$ at $v$ supported in slab $j$. The rows above $j$ read
$X_{i+1}u_{i+1}+B_i^{\mathsf T}u_i$ at the sum's unit, the tail closing from $L$
downward as in (i); the rows below read
$Y_i\,u_i+B_i\,u_{i+1}$ at the sum's unit at every $i$ below $j$,
the induction from $1$ on the $Y$
recursion; and
substituting both into row $j$ leaves $Z_j\,u_j=v_j$. The display
telescopes the descent, and at $L=2$ it is the two-slab solve outright.
(iv): the leading slab's row read splits the head row's fold and the
block rows' folds into the slab's own entries and the tail chain's
fold, the leading square with the doubled consecutive product the
slab's own read, and the descent closes on the slab count, the shape
read the descent's own length read.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\;+\;\delta\,1
\]
at the tail witnesses' transfer factors $\check R_{i+1}$ and

\begin{theorem}[The window is a root separation, and is explicit]
\label{thm:windowsep}
For a polynomial $P$ over $\mathbb P$ (Definition~\ref{def:poly}), or
over a located stage, every step below one of its operations, a
division, a coefficient fold or a bracket comparison: the stage's
distinct roots have a computed pair separation floor and a computed radius,
by ground arithmetic alone.

\emph{The magnitude carrier.} The \emph{magnitude} of a
balance pair is its members' larger against smaller, the sorted pair
$|\langle u\!:\!v\rangle|:=
\langle\,\max\{u,v\}\!:\!\min\{u,v\}\,\rangle$ at the trichotomy
read, one value at every pair (a summand on both members fixing
it), its value at unequal members the margin, the exceeding
member's gap (Definition~\ref{def:ground}). A sum's magnitude
sits at or below the magnitudes' sum, and a product's magnitude is
the magnitudes' product, a memberwise swap of either datum swapping
the product's members and fixing every magnitude. So a polynomial's evaluations
at points of magnitude at or below a bound are capped by the
\emph{coefficient fold}, the coefficients' magnitudes folded
against the bound's powers, one read over the occupancy family.

\emph{The squarefree part, and the radius.} The \emph{division
descent}, iterated divisions of Definition~\ref{def:poly},
computes the \emph{greatest common divisor} $c(P,P')$: the
descent's last occupied remainder, monic at the rescaling by its
leading coefficient (each coefficient the cofactor at the leading
one), a factor of $P$ and of $P'$ and greatest as named.  At the integer representatives the
rescaling enters as data: the divisor at its primitive list with
the stated positive top, the cofactors at their clearing
multipliers, and the division at a stated top the cleared
descent, $\ell^{\,k}\,P=q\,D+r$ at the top $\ell$, one scale per
eliminated key, the exactness the remainder's read; each
remainder strips to its primitive list at its coefficients' one
shared count, the walk's rows at their stated multipliers with
the strip absorbed there, and every certificate reads at the
cleared data.  The squarefree part
$S$ is the cofactor at
$c(P,P')\,S=P$, and the B\'ezout pair $uS+vS'=1$ arrives with the descent
at $(S,S')$ ending at a unit: $P$'s roots are $S$'s, each
simple there. Every root over the stage sits in the \emph{radius segment},
between $B$'s balance partner and $B$ at the pair
$B:=[\,c+\mathcal H:c\,]$, $c$ the leading coefficient's margin
(the top key's coefficient of unequal members, the degree's own
read)
and $\mathcal H$ the height, the largest coefficient magnitude, the
leading term dominating at every point of margin at or beyond $B$.

\emph{The separation.} Between two roots
over the stage, at the stage gap $G$ at $\alpha+G=\beta$, the binomial
identity per occupied key at $i\ge2$, the constant key's read
equal at both points and the key-one read the gap's own join
$\beta=\alpha+G$,
\[
\beta^{\,i}\;=\;\alpha^{\,i}+i\,\alpha^{\,h}\,G
\;+\;G^{2}\!\!\sum_{a+b+2=i}\!(a{+}1)\,\alpha^{\,a}\beta^{\,b}
\qquad(h+1=i) ,
\]
summed against the coefficients, reads
$S(\beta)=S(\alpha)+G\,S'(\alpha)+G^{2}\,T$ at the collected tail
$T:=\sum_is_i\sum_{a+b+2=i}(a{+}1)\,\alpha^{a}\beta^{b}$; at $V$ the coefficient
fold of the B\'ezout witness $v$ at the radius and the \emph{curvature fold}
$\Lambda:=\sum_i\tbinom i2\,|s_i|\,B^{\,e}$ over the occupied
keys at the joins $e+2=i$, $|s_i|$ the coefficient's magnitude, the
stage's distinct
roots satisfy
\[
\Lambda\,V\,G\ \ge\ 1\ ,
\qquad
2\,\max\{\Lambda\,V,\ 1\}\ \delta\;=\;1\ ,
\]
one pair comparison and one cofactor per polynomial
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}), $\delta$ below the separation and at
most $[\,1:2\,]$; the radius $B$ is the
\emph{leading-term bound}. The object is a distance between
roots of ground polynomials, and such a distance is a separation
bound, which is explicit.
\begin{proof}
\emph{The magnitudes.} At $\langle u\!:\!v\rangle$ and
$\langle u'\!:\!v'\rangle$ with $u=v+a$ and $u'=v'+b$ the product
$\langle uu'+vv'\!:\!uv'+vu'\rangle$ reads $uu'+vv'=uv'+vu'+ab$, its
magnitude $ab$, the magnitudes' product, and at $u'+b=v'$ the
product's members swap, the magnitude $ab$ again; the sum's members differ
by $a+b$ at like sides and by the gap of $a$ and $b$ at unlike
sides, at or below $a+b$, the further cases at the members'
trichotomies.
\emph{The descent.} Each remainder joins the two
above it through its division, so the last is a factor of
every earlier one, the two seeds among them; and a common factor $g$ of the two seeds is a factor of every
remainder down the descent, $P=SQ+R$ at the cofactors $g\,P_1=P$
and $g\,S_1=S$ reading $R=g\,(P_1+\check T)$ at $T=S_1Q$, the
check the memberwise swap over the balance pairs, the last
remainder among them. An irreducible factor $q$ of $S$ has
some multiplicity $m\ge1$ in $P=q^{m}R$, the remainders of $q'$
(the derivative's degree drop) and of $R$ (the exact
multiplicity) at $q$ occupied and their B\'ezout witnesses
composing to an occupied remainder of $m\,q'R+q\,R'$ at the count
$m$ a natural, $q\,R'$'s summand the sum's unit there; at $m=1$
the derivative is that read outright, $P'=m\,q'R+q\,R'$, and at
the join $m'+1=m$ it is $P'=q^{\,m'}(m\,q'R+q\,R')$ at
multiplicity exactly $m'$: the greatest common divisor's $q$-part sits one power
below $P$'s, the unit at $m=1$, so the cofactor $S$ reads $q$ at
one, and at $S=qT$ the remainders of $T$ and of
$S'=q'T+qT'$ at $q$ are occupied: $P$'s roots are $S$'s, each
simple there.
\emph{The radius.} At a
point of margin $y=1+g$ at or beyond $B$, with $k$ the top key,
the geometric telescope $g\sum_{i<k}y^{\,i}+1=y^{\,k}$ reads the
tail's cap $\mathcal H\sum_{i<k}y^{\,i}$ below $c\,y^{\,k}$ at the
radius' read $c\,g\ge\mathcal H$, so the leading term dominates
and the evaluation reads unequal members on the leading term's own
side, the tail joined at a magnitude below the term's.
\emph{The separation.} At a root $\alpha$ the unit witness
$v(\alpha)\,S'(\alpha)=1$ reads at the magnitudes: $V$ the
coefficient
fold of $v$ at the radius, so the margin of $S'(\alpha)$
cross-multiplies to $\mathrm{margin}\cdot V\ge1$. The two
roots' equal-membered reads leave $G\,(S'(\alpha)+G\,T)$ of equal
members, so at $G$'s unit witness $S'(\alpha)$ and $G\,T$ are
balance partners, and the margin of $S'(\alpha)$ sits at or below
$G\,\Lambda$ at the curvature fold, the
splitting count $\sum_{a+b+2=i}(a{+}1)=\tbinom i2$ and both roots
capped by the radius: so $\Lambda\,V\,G\ge1$.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[The box read at several coordinates]\label{lem:boxread}
At a polynomial $P$ over the pairs in the coordinates
$y_1,\dots,y_k$ (Definition~\ref{def:poly}, one variable joined at
a time) and a \emph{box}, per coordinate a segment $[\,a_i,b_i\,]$
of pairs at $a_i\le b_i$, the \emph{box read} is the comparison
$P(y)\ge0$ at every point $y$ of the box, $y_i$ between $a_i$ and
$b_i$ at every $i$. At a \emph{cut list} per coordinate, finitely
many pairs from $a_i$ to $b_i$ in order, the \emph{pieces} are the
products of consecutive cut segments, each with its \emph{base
corner}, the lower ends, and its \emph{widths} $w_i$, the segments'
gaps; at $B_i$ the larger of the magnitudes of $a_i$ and $b_i$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s magnitude carrier) the
\emph{derivative fold} $M_i$ is the coefficient fold of the
derivative $\partial_iP$ in $y_i$ (Definition~\ref{def:poly}) over
its monomials at the bounds $B_1,\dots,B_k$, one read per
coordinate. Then the box read holds where every piece's base
corner clears the priced widths,
\[
P(\text{base})\ \ge\ \sum_{i\le k}w_i\,M_i\qquad\text{at every piece},
\]
finitely many cross-multiplied comparisons, and holds strictly
above the sum's unit on the box where each comparison does. The \emph{Taylor fold} of a polynomial $P$ in one coordinate at a
piece $[\,a,\,a+w\,]$ is
$\tau_P:=\sum_{j\ge1}|P^{(j)}(a)|\,w^{j}\,[\,1:j!\,]$, the magnitudes
of the finite Taylor read's keys at the foot
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s magnitude carrier), and $P$'s every
value on the piece sits between $P(a)$ less $\tau_P$ and $P(a)$
joined to $\tau_P$; at a polynomial in several coordinates the fold
joins coordinate by coordinate along the telescope of the proof,
each step's fold at the earlier coordinates' pieces. The
\emph{interval read} of a formula on a piece composes its atoms'
\emph{segment reads}, each a segment of pairs holding the atom's
every value on the piece, through the displayed operations: a sum's
segment is the ends' sums, a product's the least and the largest of
the four cross products, a natural power's the ends' powers at a
segment on the upper side, and a quotient's the least and the
largest of the four cross quotients at a divisor segment off the
sum's unit on one side; the atoms are a coordinate at its own
segment, a series with positive coefficients at an argument segment
on the upper side between its ends' values, and a polynomial in a
coordinate at its Taylor fold; the box read holds on a piece whose
interval read sits on its upper side or at equal members. The \emph{halving cover} of a box at a stated
\emph{region} of the box, a stated \emph{depth}, a natural, a stated
\emph{clip}, a read of a piece returning a piece inside it holding
the region's points of the piece, or the vacant read at a piece off
the region, and a stated per-piece comparison, is the recursion: a
piece reads its clip, the vacant read holding outright; a clipped
piece at which the comparison holds is a \emph{leaf}; a clipped
piece at which the comparison refuses at an occupied depth is cut at
the midpoint of the coordinate whose width against the coordinate's
range in the box is largest, the earliest at a tie, into two pieces
read at the depth's predecessor; and at the vacant depth the refusal
is the cover's own. The cover holds where every piece is vacant or a
leaf, one decidable read, and then the box read holds at every point
of the region at the comparison each leaf clears, the priced read or
the interval read. The \emph{leading-key read} at a polynomial $P$ in
the box's coordinates joined to a further coordinate $\varepsilon$ on
the segment from the sum's unit to a pair $\varepsilon_0$: at $j$ the
least key of $\varepsilon$ occupied in $P$, $P=\varepsilon^{j}(P_j+
\varepsilon\,R)$ at $P_j$ the key's coefficient, a polynomial in the
box's coordinates, and $R$ the further keys' fold, and the read
$P\ge0$ holds at every point of the box and every $\varepsilon$ at or
below the least of $\varepsilon_0$ and $[\,m:F\,]$ where $P_j$ less a
positive pair $m$ holds the box read (at one coordinate the segment
count vacant with one endpoint value positive,
Lemma~\ref{lem:hermitesign}) and $F$ is the coefficient fold of $R$
at the box's bounds and $\varepsilon_0$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s
magnitude carrier); and the \emph{grid read} at a positive pair $m$:
at the cut lists cutting every coordinate at pieces of widths at or
below $[\,m:\sum_iM_i\,]$, the priced comparison holds at every piece
whose base corner's value sits at or beyond $m$, so the box read
holds where $P$ sits at or beyond $m$ at the finitely many base
corners. On a
range unbounded in one coordinate the read joins the box read to the
leading-term bound: at $P$ read in $y_1$ with the further
coordinates in their segments, at a top key $n$ whose coefficient
$c_n$, a polynomial in the further coordinates, keeps its upper
side on their box at a margin $c$ at or beyond a stated pair, and at
$\mathcal H$ the largest coefficient fold of the further keys over
their box, $P$ keeps its upper side at every $y_1$ at or beyond the
radius $[\,c+\mathcal H:c\,]$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s
leading-term bound), so the read on $[\,a_1,\infty)$ is the box
read on $[\,a_1,\,[\,c+\mathcal H:c\,]\,]$ joined to the radius's
comparison.
\begin{proof}
At a point $y$ of a piece with base corner $a$, the difference
$P(y)-P(a)$ telescopes through the coordinates, the $i$-th step
moving $y_i$ alone at the earlier coordinates at $y$ and the later
at $a$; each step is a one-variable difference, the binomial
identity per occupied key of $y_i$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}),
$y_i^{\,n}-a_i^{\,n}=(y_i-a_i)\sum_{j+l+1=n}y_i^{\,j}a_i^{\,l}$, the
fold's magnitude at or below $n\,B_i^{\,n-1}$ at both points of
magnitude at or below $B_i$, so the step's magnitude sits at or
below $(y_i-a_i)$ against the coefficient fold of $\partial_iP$ at
the bounds, at or below $w_i\,M_i$ (the further coordinates' powers
at their bounds), and the difference's magnitude at or below the
widths' fold. So $P(y)$ sits at or beyond $P(a)$ less the fold, at
or beyond the sum's unit at the piece's comparison, and strictly
above it where the comparison is strict. The Taylor fold: $P(a+h)=\sum_{j}P^{(j)}(a)\,h^{j}\,[\,1:j!\,]$ is one
identity of the polynomial at every $h$ (Definition~\ref{def:poly}'s
derivative, the binomial identity per key), and at $h$ at or below
$w$ the keys from one on sit within their magnitudes' fold at
$w$. The interval read: an atom's every value on the piece sits in
its segment read (a series with positive coefficients rises with its
argument key by key; a polynomial at its Taylor fold), and the displayed
operations at two segments read their members' segments, the sum
at the ends' sums, the product and the quotient at their extremes
over the two segments, attained at the ends since each is monotone
in each member at the other fixed, the power so; so the formula's
value at every point of the piece sits in its interval read. The
halving cover: by induction on the depth, every point of the
region inside a piece sits inside a leaf's clip, the cut's two
pieces holding the piece's points between them and the clip
holding the region's, so the comparison at that leaf reads the
point. The leading-key read: at every point of the box and every
$\varepsilon$ at or below $\varepsilon_0$ the fold $R$'s magnitude
sits at or below $F$, so $P$ sits at or beyond
$\varepsilon^{j}\,(m-\varepsilon\,F)$, at or beyond the sum's unit at
$\varepsilon\,F\le m$. The grid read: at every piece the widths' fold
$\sum_iw_iM_i$ sits at or below $[\,m:\sum_iM_i\,]\sum_iM_i=m$, at or
below the base corner's value. The unbounded range: at
$y_1$ of magnitude at or beyond the radius the top term's magnitude
$c\,y_1^{\,n}$ clears the further keys' fold
$\mathcal H\sum_{j<n}y_1^{\,j}$ at the geometric telescope,
$\langle y_1\!:\!1\rangle\sum_{j<n}y_1^{\,j}=\langle y_1^{\,n}\!:\!1\rangle$,
the gap of $y_1$ above one at or beyond $[\,\mathcal H:c\,]$ at the
radius (Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s leading-term bound), at every
point of the further coordinates' box, the coefficient bounds read
at the box.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The stage splits every polynomial]\label{lem:stagesplit}
Every polynomial of degree at least $1$ over a located stage splits,
over a stored tower (Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}), into located linear
factors and \emph{definite} quadratic factors at pair data $(h,q)$,
the root relation $z^2+q=h\,z$, at the definiteness gap $g$ at
$h^2+g=4q$, the data tower elements, multiplicities by
iterated divisions.
\begin{proof}
\emph{Factorization closes over finite cofactor lists.} Over
$\mathbb P$ a polynomial reads at its primitive integer form, the
pair coefficients cleared at one shared second member with the
content collected, and a factor reads primitive as well, the
contents splitting off (Gauss); a primitive factor of degree $d$ is
determined by its values at $d+1$ integers of occupied value, a
point of equal-membered value reading its linear factor outright,
and each value is one of the finitely many cofactor reads of the
primitive form's value there at either side, a natural or its
balance partner: the value lists are finite, each selection
interpolates to one polynomial, and the division tests it,
the remainder of equal members exactly at a factor
(Kronecker). Over an extension $K(\varepsilon)$ the norm
$\mathrm{Res}_x\big(S_\varepsilon(x),f\big)$
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}'s resultant, in the variable $x$) maps
$f$ to the
stage below; at a shift $z\mapsto z+\lambda\varepsilon$ whose norm
is squarefree (the failing $\lambda$ are roots of one resultant,
finitely many, a scalar-pair $\lambda$ off them read directly), the
greatest common divisor of $f$ with each factor of the shifted
norm, the division descent's end, recovers $f$'s factors
over the extension (Trager), descending to $\mathbb P$. The
remainder lists at an
irreducible factor (Definition~\ref{def:poly}) are a
discrete field, every occupied element at its B\'ezout
unit witness, so iterating the adjunction reads a full formal root
list, the \emph{splitting data}: finite
algebra over the stage, in which a root of a product is a root of
one factor.

\emph{The quadratic extensions.} A located positive $c$ adjoins
one extension, the remainder lists at the relation $z^2=c$'s polynomial
(Definition~\ref{def:poly}); the \emph{adjoined root at} $z^2=c$
is the linear monomial's class, located at the bracket of $c$'s
sorted display against $1$, the two side reads the refinement's seed
(Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct}(1)) with the equality outcome
naming the root outright, so the extension is a located stage again
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}). The \emph{located
pairs} are the remainder lists at $z^2+1$
(Definition~\ref{def:poly}), $(a,b)$ written $a+ib$ at
$i$ the linear monomial's class, the \emph{key swap} the linear
key's memberwise swap, an automorphism of the carrier's reads. A
located pair at $b$ of unequal members has a square root
$u+iv$ on three such extensions:
$w$ the adjoined root at $z^2=a^2+b^2$, then over $K(w)$
$u$ the adjoined root at $z^2=[\,1:2\,]\,(w+a)$ and
$v$ the adjoined root at $z^2=[\,1:2\,]\,g$ at the gap
$g$ at $a+g=w$, the order's witness ($w^2$ exceeds $a^2$ at $b$'s
occupied square, so $w$ exceeds $a$ and its balance partner),
$v$'s side one bracket read against $b$'s; the tower
reads $u^2=v^2+a$ and $(2uv)^2=b^2$ outright, so
$(u+iv)^2=a+ib$. A quadratic over located pairs at the root
relation $z^2+q=hz$ splits over located pairs, the trichotomy of
its \emph{discriminant datum} $D$ at $D+4q=h^2$: at $D$'s second
component of unequal members the extensions read its square root
$u+iv$, the two roots the data at $2z=h+(u{+}iv)$ and
$2z+(u{+}iv)=h$; at the second component of equal members the
first component $D_1$'s trichotomy reads: on its upper side, $e$
the adjoined root at $z^2=D_1$ with the roots the data at
$2z=h+e$ and $2z+e=h$; at equality, the double root, the
datum at $2z=h$; and on its lower side, $e$ the adjoined root
at $z^2=m$ at $D_1$'s margin $m$, the roots the data at
$2z=h+e\,i$ and $2z+e\,i=h$.

\emph{The Laplace descent.} The claim: a stage polynomial $p$ of
degree $k\ge1$ has a located root or a definite quadratic
divisor, verified by the division. Induct on the degree's
$2$-adic valuation $\nu$. At odd degree the leading term dominates
beyond Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s radius, the side reads at the
radius and at its balance partner differ, and a located root's
designation follows at every width,
Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct}(1)'s refinement at the entry's side reads.
At positive $\nu$, at a
scalar pair $t$ the resolvent
\[
B_t(x)\;:=\;\prod_{l<l'}\big\langle\,x\;:\;z_l+z_{l'}+t\,z_lz_{l'}\,\big\rangle
\]
over $p$'s formal root list has symmetric coefficients, hence stage
coefficients through the elementary reads (the lexicographic descent
on symmetric monomials, one generic identity), and degree
$\binom k2$ at the valuation join $\nu'+1=\nu$: the induction hands
each $t$ a
located root or a definite divisor, either way a located pair
$\beta_t$ (the second component of equal members, or the adjoined
root at $z^2=[\,1:4\,]\,g$ at the definiteness gap $g$), a
witness-verified root of $B_t$. Take
the splitting data over the one tower with every $\beta_t$ and
$i$: there $B_t$ is the displayed product and $\beta_t$, a root of
$B_t$ in a field, is one factor's own root: $\beta_t$ meets a pair
$(l,l')$. Over $\binom k2+1$ distinct scalar pairs $t$ two meet one
pair, and there, the lesser parameter written $t'$ at the gap $w$
at $t'+w=t$,
\[
w\,q+\beta_{t'}\;=\;\beta_t\,,
\qquad
h+t\,q\;=\;\beta_t
\]
name the located pairs $q$ and $h$, each one value by the positive
gap's rescaling, the displays' own joins at the meeting pair
($\beta_t=z_l+z_{l'}+t\,z_lz_{l'}$ at both parameters), with the
relation $z^2+q=hz$'s quadratic a factor of $p$; the finitely many
parameter pairs are each tested by the division, and the
display guarantees a passing test. At a passing pair the
discriminant trichotomy
splits the quadratic, giving a root $a+ib$ of $p$ with $a,b$ tower
elements. At $b$ of equal members, a bracket read, $a$ is a
located root; at $b$ of unequal members the key swap fixes
$p$ and maps the root to its swap image, the division of $p$
at $z^2+(a^2+b^2)=2az$ reads its remainder $Rz+T$ with $Ra+T$ and
$Rb$ of equal members at the two roots, so $R$ and $T$ read equal
members at $b$'s unit witness: a definite divisor. Iterated
divisions close the split.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The located sign is a count]\label{lem:hermitesign}
Over a located stage $K$, let $S$ be squarefree of degree $N$ with
its split over a stored tower
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stagesplit}). A stage value at a root is
a balance pair, its \emph{side} the members' order read, the
\emph{upper} at the first member exceeding and the \emph{lower} at
the second (Definition~\ref{def:ground}); the pairing below is
additive over a value's site, $H_u=H_v+H_p$ at $u=v+p$, so the

\begin{theorem}[The fiber family is a bounded chord pencil]
\label{thm:trigpencil}
At the banded rows, every pencil entry within the locality band of

translation, its deck relation $T^2+1=t\,T$
(Definition~\ref{def:deck}), the

through finitely many translation powers per direction,
$T_i^{\,j}$ at the direction's own translation, the power bounded
by the grade's spatial support, each adjoint-paired read a
deck-family polynomial at the direction's chord
(Definition~\ref{def:deck}): the momentum variables are the
chords $t_1,\dots,t_d$, one per direction, the momentum point $K$
their list (Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}). The chain object is therefore one algebraic
family over the $\big(K;[\alpha\!:\!\beta]\big)$ base at the
chords,
with integral chord data; its divisor records the band, the gap, and every ``assembled'' coefficient as reads at the ends of $\mathcal C$.
Its \emph{fiber symbol} is the family's characteristic Laurent polynomial
$\mathcal S(K;k,r)$, the pair $(k\!:\!A(K))$'s site-datum determinant at the
level $k$ scalar against the gram's determinant, one value at

symmetric pair pencil (Theorem~\ref{thm:pairpencil}), so a
separation's block is the reversed separation's transpose, the

\begin{proof}
A pencil entry between two states reads within the locality band
of their supports (Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries}), so a graded
block's entries at two translates read the sum's unit beyond the
grade's spatial support, finitely many translation powers per
direction, and on a chord block the adjoint-paired reads
$T^{\,b}+(T^{*})^{\,b}$ are the deck families' values at the
located chord (Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}), integral in the chords.
Two stated lists of the fiber read congruent pencils
(Theorem~\ref{thm:pairpencil}'s transport), and at a unit
congruence the determinant of the level pair's site datum against
the gram's determinant reads one value, the congruence's
determinant's square clearing against the grams' determinants at
the product read (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}); the polytope is finite
at the localities above, and the coefficients are polynomial pairs

The pencil is symmetric (Theorem~\ref{thm:pairpencil}), so the

\begin{lemma}[The fiber index is its grading, and the pencil is

Per fiber on the odd tori (Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}) the configuration

and the \emph{separation profile}, the band components' relative
positions up to translation, read at the \emph{band neighborhood} of
a configuration, a class or a component, its vertex neighborhood
joined to the vertices of the plaquettes meeting it
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries}'s reach), two components
\emph{separated beyond the band} where every plaquette of the region
meets at most one of their band neighborhoods, and \emph{within} it
at a plaquette meeting both. The grading is
total, a class being its datum, and the regions are the datum's own
coordinate ranges: the \emph{head}, every content below a head bound

band component's content at or beyond the bound; and the \emph{slab}

\[

\qquad\text{at every closure member $\lambda_0$ and every dominant
$\lambda$ at the list's clearance,}
\]

the simple coroot pairs of $\lambda$ at or beyond the \emph{list's
coroot magnitude} $m_L$, the largest magnitude of a closure
member's content against a positive root's coroot, one member read
(the string caps, Lemma~\ref{lem:strings}), one at the $A$-series'
fundamental pair and at every minuscule list, the collar the labels

H_C=J_C^{\mathsf T}H_{AF}J_C.
\]
At first-factor content $a_i$, the far selection is
$c_j+a_i\le C$. Let $e_A,f_C$ be the factors' least roots,
with the far factor taken at cutoff $C$, and put
$S_A=H_A-e_AG_A$, $S_F=H_F-f_CG_F$. Then
\[
H_C-(e_A+f_C)G_C
=J_C^{\mathsf T}(S_A\otimes G_F+G_A\otimes S_F)J_C\succeq0.
\]
At an occupied admitted list its least root is $e_A+f_C+\Delta_C$ at a
stage gap $\Delta_C\ge0$. This gap reads the sum's unit exactly
where the image of $J_C$ intersects
$\ker S_A\otimes\ker S_F$ at an occupied vector. Its level-gap
form is
\[
H_C-(e_A+f_C+\Delta_C)G_C
=J_C^{\mathsf T}(S_A\otimes G_F+G_A\otimes S_F)J_C
-\Delta_CG_C.
\]

At a head floor $H_A=\ell G_A+T_A$ with $T_A\succeq0$,
and a full-window ground $e\le f_C$, the read at a positive
offset $h\le\ell$ is the positive fold
\[
H_C-(e+h)G_C
=J_C^{\mathsf T}(T_A\otimes G_F+G_A\otimes S_F)J_C
+(\ell-h+f_C-e)G_C\succeq0.
\]
Its count is the sum's unit; at $\ell-h+f_C-e>0$ it is
positive definite. The comparison $e\le f_C$ holds where
extension by unit labels identifies the far list's pencil
with the full window's restriction to that image. In particular,
this is the read on the invariant carrier when the far region
is the links outside the head neighborhood and its plaquettes
are the full region's plaquettes contained in those links.

At a positive-definite admitted block $P$ and coupling $B$
to the further places, the whole count reads
\[
\operatorname{rev}
\begin{pmatrix}Q&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&P\end{pmatrix}
=\operatorname{rev}(Q-BX),\qquad PX=B^{\mathsf T}
\]
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). Here $B$ is the block of the actual
cutoff pencil, with every admitted column. The correction is
$BX=X^{\mathsf T}PX$, at the block's Gram solve.
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i)} $E$ adds the contents, a plaquette
term meets at most one component's neighborhood
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries}), and a stencil
move moves one component within its own locality band with the others
spectators, so the rows are per component.
\emph{(iii)} A product of two tensors reads factorwise, the product
index's fold collecting to the factors' folds' product at the ground
identities (Definition~\ref{def:ground}), so the gram's pivot
congruence at its positive pivots, the split at order-one blocks a
positive-definite datum reads off its leading minors of unequal
members (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}'s minor sequence), and the site
datum's split compose
to the summand's own congruence, its image the split's blocks at the
pivots' positive scales, and the image's form at every vector is the
fold of the blocks' reads at the scales, on its upper side or of
equal members (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).
\emph{(iv)} The
factors' congruences' tensor maps the full tensor sum's site datum at a
level to the diagonal at the summed roots against the scales'
products ((iii)'s tensor congruence; Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), and
the count at a level is the root pairs' count below it
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}'s congruence read at the diagonal).
The contents add at a product configuration, so the cutoff's
index is precisely the displayed selection
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}). The two factor level-gap forms
are positive semidefinite. Their tensor folds and their
restriction through $J_C$ have that read by (iii) and
Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}. In the factors' split coordinates,
the folded form's kernel consists of the root pairs at both
least roots: every other pair has a positive gap at a positive
Gram weight. Thus its restriction has an occupied kernel
exactly at the stated intersection. The least-root read gives
$\Delta_C\ge0$, with equality exactly there
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}). Substitution of the head floor and
the two ordered gaps gives the displayed fold at $e+h$.

Extension by unit labels preserves the pairing and the electric
form. A plaquette contained in the far link set has its far
entry. Every further plaquette has a link outside that set,
whose two state labels are unit and whose character factor is
nonunit; the link's unit evaluation reads the sum's unit
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}; Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}).
The magnetic restriction is therefore the far pencil's, and
compression puts the full least root at or below $f_C$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). The last count and its correction
are the positive principal pivot's deflation, with
$BX=X^{\mathsf T}PX$ at the solved identity's transpose.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[The decimation: the counts live on the decimated head]
\label{thm:decimation}
Fix a fiber, its grading (Lemma~\ref{lem:grading}), a head bound
$\Lambda_h$, and a pair bracket $[\ell_1,\ell_2]$ of spectral
levels. The pencil decimates onto its head in three located
steps, each step a Schur complement
(Lemma~\ref{lem:greenprod}; Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}'s deflation),
and the decimation is the count's own presentation.

\emph{(i) The depth direction is the walk's shape.} The fiber's
sector is its fusion closure from the vacuum class, the depth chain
(Construction~\ref{con:depthchain}), and the pencil blocked at the
shells is block tridiagonal over the depth with the vacuum class
the boundary shell, the pencil at the depth order its own count at
the places' congruence (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), and the count at
every level splits over the chain's pivot recursion,
$\operatorname{rev}=\sum_\kappa\operatorname{rev}(X_\kappa)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:greenprod}(i),(ii)): the walk's shape at matrix blocks
(\S\ref{sec:channel}), the boundary pivot the vacuum's dressing. The
split is order-free, each slab ordering of the elimination reading
the one count, and an ordering is certificate data, its validity divisors
entering the emitted list as any boundary's do. The
ground jump is a divisor point of the decimated head: the level is the
distance of the first two jumps of one counting function, the walk's own
read, its boundary defect the vacuum's diagonal, the plaquette
character's evaluation at the sum's unit (Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries};
Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}).

\emph{The counted pivot.} At a level datum $Z$, a
principal pivot $P$ of unequal-membered determinant has the read
\[
Z=\begin{pmatrix}P&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&Q\end{pmatrix},
\qquad PC=B,\qquad Q=B^{\mathsf T}C+Z_P,
\qquad \operatorname{rev}Z=\operatorname{rev}P+\operatorname{rev}Z_P
\]
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). The head count equals the whole
count at the pivot's count the sum's unit. At two stated
lines $z_-,z_+$ and a prescribed count $g$, the certificate
reads the two total counts,
\[
\operatorname{rev}P_-+\operatorname{rev}Z_{P_-}
=g=\operatorname{rev}P_++\operatorname{rev}Z_{P_+}.
\]
The pivot's split and its solved witness are the data at
each line. For the detector datum $SD-hS$ at a positive pair
$h$, the prescribed
count is the sum's unit (Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}), its
blocks the whole-square restrictions of
Definition~\ref{def:pencil}.

\emph{(ii) The tower tails decimate on their dominance cells.} A class's
diagonal is intensive, the far plaquettes reading equal members on it
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries}): the content sum against the local
magnetic stencil, the stencil rows one capped list
(Lemma~\ref{lem:grading}; Lemmas~\ref{lem:fpcap},~\ref{lem:loopcap}).
A tail block's positive-pivot datum is a split with every
block on its upper side and its kernel block vacant
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). A \emph{dominance certificate}
reads the following comparisons on that block: per row, the \emph{gap}
$d_i:=a_{ii}+\check f_i$, the diagonal's entry joined to the
balance partner of the off-row entries' magnitude fold $f_i$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s magnitude carrier), at the
comparison $f_i\le a_{ii}$, the gap on its upper side or
at equal members. The form sits at or beyond the
gaps' fold of squares $\sum_id_i\,x_i^2$ at every vector, at or
beyond the sum's unit where the comparison holds; every split of the
block then reads the upper side throughout, at every gap beyond the
sum's unit the kernel block is vacant, so the determinant sits off
equal members with located brackets and the adjugate its solve
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}); the block is a nonsingular principal
pivot of the datum at its designated places, inertia adds at it with
its count the sum's unit, and the datum's count is its deflation's,
the decimated head's (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), at a chain's tail the
slab recursion's own with the count telescoping over the head slabs'
pivots (Lemma~\ref{lem:greenprod}(ii)). The fold $f_i$ runs
over every off-diagonal column of the stated block. A creation
at a disjoint plaquette contributes where its output is a member
of that block, at the coefficient read of
Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}. The support comparison is the
remainder's form read,
\[
f_*\,|\langle x,\mathsf R_\Pi x\rangle_G|
\le\nu d_L\,\langle x,\mathsf E_\Pi x\rangle_G,
\qquad
\mathsf M_\Pi=\mathsf R_\Pi+\sum_i(a_i+a_i^\dagger)
\]
(Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}). The full block's dominance
comparison reads its full fold $f_i$. At either representative,
on a cell of the entries' side reads, its validity is the
side read of that comparison at the
stated matrix entries, with its own located divisor
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}). The constant-coefficient instance is
the walk's boundary recursion, the deck quadratic's interior root
(Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}).

\emph{(iii) The slabs at the deck pivot.} Beyond the locality band the slab direction's bulk
datum repeats (Lemma~\ref{lem:grading}); its pivot is the
deck-interior solvent of the pivot identities
(Lemma~\ref{lem:spectator}(iii); Lemma~\ref{lem:deckfactor}), the
deck orbit's interior member at $m=1$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}'s read,
valid exactly off the bulk block's own band, the crossing locus of its
deck relation, and at a graph read of unequal members
(Lemma~\ref{lem:spectator}(iii)): the decimation's validity divisors there
are the tail's band and the graph read's side, located data
of the bulk block alone. At
$d\ge2$ the slab step is Lemma~\ref{lem:relfiber}'s clearance, the
relative coordinates fibered and the deck pivot the $d=1$ sharpening.
At two slab families with equal entries on the stated range,
the pivot differences obey the sandwich identity and its
geometric brackets at their transfer certificates
(Lemma~\ref{lem:spectator}(i),(ii)). A total-content cutoff
reads the product selection of Lemma~\ref{lem:relfiber}(iv).
Its positive fold gives the separated block's lower read at
the actual ground-translated line. Every coupling to the
further places enters the deflation at its actual matrix
and solved witness, and (i)'s total count is the whole count.

\emph{The decimated symbol.} On the bracket, within the validity cells of
(ii) and (iii), the count of the full fiber pencil is the decimated
head's, the dropped places the tower block's, every class at a
component's content at or beyond the head bound, joined to the far
block's, the classes at a separation beyond the band off the tower
block, a class in both ranges the tower block's, its row (ii)'s
comparison, where (iii)'s ball reads the slab direction's bulk at
contents below the bound alone; the decimated head a finite
symmetric pencil over the located stage
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}), entries pair data of the deck
coordinates and the located pivots, cell functions over $(t,\tau,r)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}; Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(iii)). The
spectrum on the bracket is where the decimated determinant reads equal
members,
Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid} per cell concrete; and the cells the
validity divisors cover are the decimation's own output, every boundary a
located root.

\emph{The divisor list, named.} The decimation's validity divisors
are the stated certificates' comparison fields: the \emph{pivot
divisors}, the pivot and congruence determinants and the side
comparisons of the nonsingular split blocks, with the
\emph{dominance divisors} at a
dominance certificate's full row folds ((ii)); the \emph{deck divisors},
the bulk blocks' crossing loci with the graph read's side,
Lemma~\ref{lem:spectator}(iii)'s
counts ((iii)); and the \emph{jump divisors}, the decimated determinant's
roots at the bracket's levels (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}). The list is
finite per stage, its cells partition the base, counts constant per
cell and persisting at a boundary beside a positive-semidefinite
cell (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}); the emitted record, the located root
list with its per-cell counts and the binding read of which comparison
binds at each boundary, is the decimation's displayed object, every entry one
stage read of the crossing divisor (Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}).
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i)} A pencil row joins two classes
at a plaquette term's entry off the sum's unit, a border row or a
stencil row of Lemma~\ref{lem:grading}, and a joined class sits at
most one depth beyond the class it joins, so the pencil blocked at
the shells is block tridiagonal over the depth. Inertia adds at
every nonsingular principal pivot (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), so
each slab ordering of the elimination reads the one count.
At a counted principal pivot, Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}'s
unit-triangular congruence reads $P\oplus Z_P$. Its two
counts add, giving the displayed total at each stated line.
The positive-pivot instance has its first count at the sum's
unit. The detector's prescribed count is the spectral read
of Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}; its compression includes the
action's image in both blocks at $SD=D^{\mathsf T}GD$.
\emph{(ii)} The peel telescopes at the symmetric datum
(Theorem~\ref{thm:pairpencil}): a vector's form peels at the
leading row, the leading square with the doubled cross fold against
the trailing block's form, and each cross term joins its magnitude's
squares at one square's multiple,
\[
2\,a\,xy+|a|\,(x^2+y^2)\;=\;|a|\,(x+y)^2\ \ \text{at $a$ its own
magnitude, and}\ \ |a|\,\langle x\!:\!y\rangle^2\ \text{at the swap,}
\]
at or beyond the sum's unit by its shape, so the leading row's
magnitudes withdraw from the trailing rows' folds into their gaps
and the descent closes on the order: the form sits at or beyond the
gaps' fold of squares. A split's lower
list at an occupied count would name a vector pricing the form strictly
below the sum's unit against the fold (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), so
every split reads the upper side; at
every gap beyond the sum's unit a kernel
column's image,
off the unit family at the congruence witness's clearing, would read
its form at equal members against the strict floor
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), so the kernel block is vacant.
\emph{The decimated symbol.} The tower block and the far separated
block are nonsingular
principal pivots of the datum at their designated places, every split
of each reading the upper side with the kernel block vacant ((ii);
at (iii) the tail block's determinant is its recursion pivots'
product, each pivot inside the ball at the deck pivot's floor with
its every split on the upper side, and the extended sector's pair
positive semidefinite below the bracket's top
(Lemma~\ref{lem:greenprod}(ii); Lemma~\ref{lem:spectator}(iii);
Lemma~\ref{lem:relfiber}(iii))), so inertia adds at them at counts
the sum's unit and the datum's count is its deflation at the dropped
places (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[The charged cells]\label{lem:chargedcell}
Fix a fiber on the odd tori (Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}). The
\emph{$d_f$-ality} of a label is its chain endpoint, the fundamental
or the unit label Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}'s descent ends at, one
value at every chain: a chain to the unit label reads the label's
degree at full columns outright (Construction~\ref{con:labels}),
$|\lambda|=m\,d_f$, and one to
$\omega_j$ at the two-sided join $|\lambda|+m'\,d_f=j+m\,d_f$ at
naturals $m$, $m'$, the fundamentals' degrees their indices. Two
labels are one \emph{class} where their degrees join to full
columns, $|\lambda|+m\,d_f=|\mu|+m'\,d_f$ at naturals $m$, $m'$,
the endpoint the class's one fundamental or the unit; the dual's
endpoint is the complement at the join $a+a'=d_f$ at nonunit
endpoints and the unit at the unit's, the dual's
degree joining the label's to full columns,
$|\lambda^*|+|\lambda|=d_f\,\lambda_1$.

\emph{(i) Charge is a cut-free class, and the pencil grades by it.} At an
occupied configuration every touched vertex reads an invariant count
of at least one at the incident product, incoming links dualized
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}), and reads the \emph{vertex
law}, the outgoing against the incoming degree folds at the unit
class,
\[
\sum_{\mathrm{out}}|a_\ell|+m\,d_f
\;=\;\sum_{\mathrm{in}}|a_\ell|+m'\,d_f
\qquad\text{at naturals }m,\ m'.
\]
The \emph{flux} through a cut is the class of its crossing links'
degree fold, one class per direction, its endpoint the class's
read, and two parallel transverse cuts' fluxes are one class; a cut transverse to direction $i$ is crossed by direction-$i$
links alone (Construction~\ref{con:lattice}'s direction reads), so
the directions' classes are independent data, and the
\emph{charge} $c$ is the occupancy family over the directions at
the flux endpoints, a direction occupied at a nonunit class by its
fundamental's index $c_i$, the \emph{charged directions} its
members; one direction at $d=1$. At a member's table the vertex
law reads at the member's \emph{class group}, the classes over the
root folds, finite data per member
(Construction~\ref{con:sertables}): the $d_f$-ality at the matrix
units, the degree at full columns; the series' classes the
contents' parity data against the root folds' spans (every even
list at $B_\ell$, the short family's doubled keys generating; the
even-sum lists at $C_\ell$, the letter-pair moves with the long
family's; the even lists at key-four sums at $D_\ell$, the pair
moves'), two classes at $B_\ell$, the spinor's odd parity against
the unit's, two at $C_\ell$, the first fundamental's odd sum
against the unit's, and four at $D_\ell$, the parity with the
sum's key-four remainder, the vector's and the two spinors' with
the unit's; and the fixed members' classes the adjugate rows'
remainder families at the fold key, the unit's alone at $G_2$,
$F_4$ and $E_8$ at key one, three at $E_6$, the key-three
remainders pairing $\omega_1$ with $\omega_5$ and $\omega_3$ with
$\omega_6$, and two at $E_7$, the key-two remainders occupied at
$\omega_2$, $\omega_5$ and $\omega_7$. At a member whose class
group is its unit alone every configuration reads the unit class,
the charged sectors are the one sector, the winding clauses read at
the unit class's one instance, and the cell list's tension family
drops, its root list the unit class's, every other read fixed: the
one-sector read is the class fold's own derivation. The fiber
pencil (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}) is block diagonal over the
charges and its counts split (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), $M$ of the
unit charge class and the vacuum line sitting there.

\emph{(ii) The winding floor, attained.} Every label reads
$\hat c_2$ at or above its endpoint's, $Q$ falling along the chain
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}), the endpoint read
$\hat c_2(\omega_j)=[\,j\,g_j\,(r+2):2d_f^{\,2}\,]$ at the
complement gap $j+g_j=d_f$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}), its first component the $j\,g_j$ count
at the $(r+2)$ weight, written $w(j):=j\,g_j$ below. The floor
merges over a
cut: at a family of
nonunit endpoints whose degree fold sits at a nonunit class $c$,
two members merge at their sum's trichotomy against $d_f$: below,
to the fundamental at the sum, at the cost identity
$w(a_1)+w(a_2)=w(a_1{+}a_2)+2\,a_1a_2$; at $d_f$, the pair drops
outright at $w(a_1)+w(a_2)=2\,a_1a_2$, the rest still at $c$; and
beyond, to the fundamental at the gap $g$ at $d_f+g=a_1+a_2$, at
$w(a_1)+w(a_2)=w(g)+2\,g_1g_2$ over the complement gaps
$a_i+g_i=d_f$, the cost at or beyond $2\,g_2$ at $a_1\le r$: every
family
descends to the one member $c$, so its content is at least
$\hat c_2(\omega_c)$, one value with its complement's at the dual

endpoints' floors tie exactly at the dual pair, the sum's
trichotomy against $d_f$ their read at $j'+a=j$: below,
$w(j')+a\,b=w(j)$ at the join $j+j'+b=d_f$; at $d_f$, the dual
pair's one value; and beyond, $w(j)+a\,b'=w(j')$ at $d_f+b'=j+j'$,
so off the dual pairs the floors' trichotomy is one symbolic read
at every residue. At a charged direction $i$ every direction-$i$
cut is crossed at a nonunit net class, so the charged diagonal
sits at or above the summed floor
\[
L\,\sum_{i\ \mathrm{charged}}\hat c_2(\omega_{c_i})\ \ge\ L\,\hat c_2(f)\ .
\]
At a member's table the winding floor per class is the class's
least read: a series member's is the descent's, a nonunit-class
chain ending on its own class's end members
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}), the spinor's read at $B_\ell$, the

$D_\ell$'s three nonunit classes; and a fixed member's is the
fundamental fold's class-respecting read, at $E_7$ a nonunit-class
end content occupying one of $\omega_2$, $\omega_5$, $\omega_7$
with its Casimir clearing the least of their displayed list, the
minuscule member's join $[\,57:2\,]$, and at $E_6$ occupying a
fundamental of its own class or two of the further nonunit class,

(Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}). The class floors add over a cut's

$2$, a spinor's with the vector's clearing the further spinor's at

The floor is attained by the \emph{winding strings}: one straight

\emph{(iii) At bounded excess the charged head is the dressed string,
and its pencil is one window-free head at a length shift.} Write the
\emph{excess} of a charge-$c$ class for the witness gap of (ii)'s
comparison, the summed
winding floor with the excess joining to the content, the grading the charged decimation reads. The
exclusions are extensive, read per cut, each cut's price
direction-free, the direction count entering at the cut families'
list alone, and every price is a read of the member's class floor
table, (ii)'s floors with their subadditivity folds; the
\emph{member price} $\varpi_0$ is the least of the two cut price
reads below, one trichotomy fold over the member's displayed
class data, the $d_f$-ality the class read at the matrix units,
each extra crossing's floor clearing the merge read, the
unit-class read at $2d_f^{\,2}$ against $2\,(r+2)$ over the
square's growth $d_f^{\,2}=(r+1)^2$ and the netted pair's at
$2\,r\,(r+2)$ against $2\,(r+2)$ at the occupied factor; the
off-cut read below prices the deviation links at their own count,
the dressing bound's read at the excess floors rather than the
cut count's. A
transverse cut with two or more nonunit classes among its
crossing multiset's members prices an excess at or above the
\emph{merge gap}, (ii)'s subadditivity fold at the crossing pair
against the net class's floor, positive at every nonunit pair of
the member's class group: twice a class floor at a unit-class
join, $D_\ell$'s spinor pair at the cross-multiplied $\ell$
against $2$ with the vector's own read at a mixed pair, and
$E_6$'s shared least against its double ((ii)'s folds), and at
the $A$-series the merge gaps at or above
$[\,r+2:d_f^{\,2}\,]$, the instance. A
cut crossed beyond its net class prices the excess at its extra
crossings' own floors: an extra crossing at the unit class and a
nonunit label reads $\hat c_2$ at or above the unit class's least
nonunit read, $\theta$'s read one at the
$A$-series, at $D_\ell$, and at $E_6$ and $E_7$, the
vector's $[\,r+2:2\,(r+1)\,]$ at $B_\ell$ and the short dominant
root's $[\,r:r+1\,]$ at $C_\ell$; and a crossing family netting
to the unit class holds two members at their classes' floors, at
or above twice the least class floor, the $A$-series' fundamental
pair $2\,\hat c_2(f)$ the instance. And an occupied link
off every charged direction's cuts reads the member's floor
outright (Lemma~\ref{lem:casfloor}), the $A$-series'
$\hat c_2(f)$.

\emph{The head classification.} At excess below $\Lambda_h$ the
cuts crossed beyond their one net crossing number at most $L_0$,
the least natural at $\varpi_0\,L_0\ge\Lambda_h$, one
cross-multiplied read at the member price with its witness the

(Definition~\ref{def:ground}), the $A$-series' at
$(r+2)\,L_0\ge\Lambda_h\,d_f^{\,2}$, and at $L>L_0$ the head's
classes are the \emph{dressed string}: the winding strings
of (ii), one straight $\omega_{c_i}$-cycle per charged direction

\begin{theorem}[Euclidean restoration is a count]\label{thm:restoration}

\emph{The symmetry passes to the fiber symbol.} $E=\sum_\ell\Delta_\ell$ and

\]

\emph{The invariant spaces, degree by degree.}

\begin{theorem}[The continuum reads]\label{thm:continuum}
Fix the member and the direction count. A \emph{continuum

and the cutoff-tail probe caps

\section{The network constituents}

\begin{theorem}[Network reduction and the two-vertex coupling law]
\label{thm:network}
(i) A three-link path labeled $R$ is one edge
labeled $R$ (the convolution identity), so the

space is $\Theta(R_1,k,R_2;\alpha,\beta)$-networks with $E$

link weights (Construction~\ref{con:twoplaq}).
(ii) Couplings between sectors differing on the shared link need
the label-index reads of Proposition~\ref{prop:repring} on the shared edge
alone: the
module--pair weights are
\[
\begin{gathered}
