\sum_k m_kd_k=r^2(r+2)^2\\
\text{(the block count over
Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}'s list, Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(ii))},
\end{gathered}
\]
with $d_k$ and $m_k$ the dimension and the multiplicity of
Proposition~\ref{prop:repring} at the channel $k$, so the sum is the
completeness of $\mathrm{adj}\otimes\mathrm{adj}$, whose dimension is
$r^2(r+2)^2$; the weights are the channel table's reads
(Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}),
\[
\begin{gathered}
w\;=\;\Big([\,1:r^2(r+2)^2\,],\ [\,c_1:r(r+2)\,],\
[\,(r+1)^2r(r+4):4r^2(r+2)^2\,],\\
[\,g\,(r+3):4r(r+2)\,]_{g+1=r},\
[\,g\,(r+3):4r(r+2)\,]_{g+1=r},\
[\,(r+1)^2(r+2)\,w':4r^2(r+2)^2\,]_{w'+2=r}\Big)
\end{gathered}
\]
over the channel list, the leading-term reads in the residue: the
first two weights' second members exceed in degree, and the four
channel weights read $[\,1:4\,]$ at the top
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s leading terms).
(iii) \emph{The weights are the data.} The slot-two self-energy assembled from
these weights and the network energies is
$\sum_kw_k\,[\,q_k:2q_k+p_k\,]$ at $\hat c_2(k)=[\,p_k:q_k\,]$, the
factor's gap the module pair's network eigenvalue against the
module count, $3+\hat c_2(k)+3$ against the adjoint loop's content
$4$ at $\hat c_2(\mathrm{adj})=1$ ((i)'s eigenvalue), the resolvent
factor a constructed
pair. The recoupling constituent's content is the finite
tetrahedral list: the within-pair middle matrix
$\langle(\mathrm{adj},k',\mathrm{adj})|\chi_L(U_1)|
(\mathrm{adj},k,\mathrm{adj})\rangle$ at the plaquette character
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), the adjoint walk's instance at
$\chi_{\mathrm{adj}}(U_1)$ (Construction~\ref{con:xfusion}), the
middle index the
channel table's occupied Casimir values, the dual pair's shared
value one joint block at the summed weight, computable per entry
by the $E_{\mathrm{link}}$ interpolant, the projection onto one
Casimir value a polynomial in $E_{\mathrm{link}}$
(Construction~\ref{con:units}'s Lagrange read) entered cleared at
the node differences' product, one value across the clearing
scale (Definition~\ref{def:ground}'s homogeneity principle), at
the channel distances' occupied gaps (Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}).
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i)} A path's two interior vertices are two-valent, each
reading the unit label's count at the incident label against its
dual, $N^{\mathbf 1}_{R\bar R}=1$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}),
so the path's three labels are one label and its fiber the edge's;
the electric member reads each link's Casimir at the link weights
$(3,1,3)$ (Construction~\ref{con:twoplaq}), the fold
$3C_2(R_1)+C_2(k)+3C_2(R_2)$. \emph{(ii)} The shared link's label
runs over the channels of $\mathrm{adj}\otimes\mathrm{adj}$ at

(Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}), the weight the channel's share of the
dimension identity $\sum_km_kd_k=d_{\mathrm{adj}}^{\,2}$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(ii)) at
$d_{\mathrm{adj}}=r\,(r+2)$; the six weights are the table's $m_R$

\emph{(iii)} The module pair's network eigenvalue against the

\section{The drift and the divisor}

\begin{theorem}[The uniform drift]\label{thm:drift}
At every label $R$ the adjoint row reads
$\sum_km_kd_k\hat c_2(k)=d_Rd_{\mathrm{adj}}(\hat c_2(R)+1)$, the
fold over the row's channels at the multiplicities against the
dimensions: \emph{the dimension-weighted fusion walk's Casimir
drift is exactly $+1$, uniformly in $R$}
($\sum_kw_k\hat c_2(k)=2$, the channel table's second closure
identity, Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}). With strictness (the unit
label is the one label of dimension one: a nonunit reduced shape
reads an occupied head row at its positive degree against the
withdrawn full column's vacant last row, the rows weakly
descending (Construction~\ref{con:places}), so a consecutive row

factor $h+1$ against the unit display's one with every further
factor at or beyond its left partner
(Corollary~\ref{cor:weyldim}'s display), so $d_\lambda\ge2$), the
closure datum is a \emph{constant} rather than a decaying one. And
the display holds at every second factor: at labels $R$ and

\[
\sum_km_kd_k\,\hat c_2(k)\;=\;d_R\,d_\lambda\,\big(\hat c_2(R)+\hat c_2(\lambda)\big)\ ,
\]
the derivation below at $\lambda$'s block, so at the magnetic list
the closure's rows fold to
\[
\sum_{\lambda_0\in\bar L}\sum_km_kd_k\,\hat c_2(k)
\;=\;d_R\,\Big(d_L\,\hat c_2(R)+\sum_{\lambda_0\in\bar L}d_{\lambda_0}\hat c_2(\lambda_0)\Big)
\]
(Construction~\ref{con:fusion}).
\begin{proof}
\emph{The member tier.} Trace the Casimir over
$W_R\otimes W_\theta$ at the trace read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}), one value at every orthogonal
spanning list. At an exhaustion the blocks' lists join to one
orthogonal spanning list, the blocks pairwise perpendicular
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(i),(ii)), and the fold splits per
block at the cleared products, each block's diagonal pairings the
scalar's multiples of the self-pairings
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockirr}(ii); Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}): the
trace reads $\sum_km_kd_k\,C_2(k)$, one summand per channel at
its count. The tensor's operators read by the Leibniz rule and
the Casimir's fold collects at the factors
(Construction~\ref{con:gentable}),
\[
C_\otimes\;=\;C_R\otimes1+1\otimes C_\theta
+2\sum_\alpha[\,\langle\alpha,\alpha\rangle:2\,]\,
\big(E_\alpha\otimes F_\alpha+F_\alpha\otimes E_\alpha\big)
+Z\ ,
\]
each root term's two orders splitting at the four arrangements
with the one-sided pairs collecting to the factors' own folds,
and $Z$ the diagonal fold's cross read, the form's additivity at
the joint contents,
$q(\mu+\nu)=q(\mu)+q(\nu)+2\,\langle\mu,\nu\rangle$ per content
pair. The trace factorizes over the tensor list, two tensors
pairing at the factors' pairings' product
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(iii)), so each term's trace is the
factor traces' product: the two one-sided terms read
$C_2(R)\,d_R\,d_\theta$ and $d_R\,C_2(\theta)\,d_\theta$; a root
term's factor trace is a fold of cross-content pairings, each of
equal members at the content sum's orthogonality
(Construction~\ref{con:gentable}), so the root terms' traces read
equal members; and $Z$'s trace is the double fold
$2\sum_{\mu,\nu}\mathrm{mult}_R(\mu)\,\mathrm{mult}_\theta(\nu)\,
\langle\mu,\nu\rangle$, the form's bilinearity collecting it to
$2\,\langle F_R,F_\theta\rangle$ at the content folds
$F_X:=\sum_\mu\mathrm{mult}_X(\mu)\,\mu$. The $\theta$-block's
contents are simple folds, the root list's members with the unit
content (Proposition~\ref{prop:row}'s content list) at each
root's fold over the simple list
(Construction~\ref{con:gentable}), so
the pairing collects at the halved products to $F_R$'s coroot
pairs, $2\,\langle F_R,\alpha_i\rangle
=F_R(\alpha_i^\vee)\,\langle\alpha_i,\alpha_i\rangle$, and each
reads equal members: the multiplicities are one value at every
reflection (Lemma~\ref{lem:strings}), a content joined to its
$s_i$-image reads the coroot pair with its balance partner, and a
fixed content's pair is its own partner. So
\[
\sum_km_kd_k\,C_2(k)\;=\;d_R\,d_\theta\,
\big(C_2(R)+C_2(\theta)\big)\ ,
\]
and the display clears at $C_2(\theta)=2\,(r+1)$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:anchor}), one value across the clearing
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}'s homogeneity principle):
$\sum_km_kd_k\hat c_2(k)=d_Rd_\theta(\hat c_2(R)+1)$. At a second
factor $\lambda$ the trace runs over $W_R\otimes W_\lambda$: the
one-sided terms read $C_2(R)\,d_Rd_\lambda$ and
$d_RC_2(\lambda)\,d_\lambda$, a root term's factor trace is a fold
of cross-content pairings at equal members at the content sum's
orthogonality, and $Z$'s trace is $2\,\langle F_R,F_\lambda\rangle$
at the content folds: $F_\lambda$ is fixed by every reflection (the
content symmetry, Lemma~\ref{lem:strings}, the fold's members
permuted at one multiplicity each), so at every simple index
$F_\lambda(\alpha_i^\vee)\,\alpha_i$ reads the sum's unit at the
reflection's join and $F_\lambda$'s simple coroot pairs read equal
members, the content itself the unit fold at the coroot reads'
injectivity (Construction~\ref{con:gentable}), and the cross fold
reads the sum's unit: the display at $\lambda$.

\emph{The label calculus at the residue.} At the matrix units the
constant family holds every consecutive coroot pair at equal
members, so the content folds read the constant family and the
derivation runs at the alternant display's recursion
(Theorem~\ref{thm:weylchar}), the display at every content list
of the block's width with a key at the count's unit reading the
moved folds' one value. Sum the display over the recursion
family's keys: the moved folds reindex at the move's own round
trip, per place pair $a<b$ and per occupied target $\kappa$ the
sources at the shifts $1\le l\le\kappa_a$, one source per
shift at the reverse move, the second letter's weight reading the
target's own $\kappa_b+l$ and the shifted first letter's
$\kappa_a+l$; the two reindexed folds share the shift fold
$\sum_{l\le\kappa_a}l$, a summand on both members fixing the
value (Definition~\ref{def:ground}), and the summed display reads
\[
q(\lambda+u)\,d_\lambda
+2\sum_\kappa\mathrm{mult}(\kappa)\sum_{a<b}\kappa_a\kappa_b
\;=\;\sum_\kappa\mathrm{mult}(\kappa)\,q(\kappa+u)
+2\sum_\kappa\mathrm{mult}(\kappa)\sum_{a<b}\kappa_a^{\,2}\ .
\]
The swap symmetry (Lemma~\ref{lem:strings}'s read at the matrix
units) reads each place fold place-free, the first moment
$M_1$, the square fold $M_2$ and the product fold $M_{11}$ one
value per place and place pair with
$d_f\,M_1=k_\lambda\,d_\lambda$
at the contents' degree read, so the summed display collects to
$q(\lambda+u)\,d_\lambda+2\,p\,M_{11}
=d_f\,M_2+2\,U_1\,M_1+q(u)\,d_\lambda+2\,p\,M_2$ at $p$ the
place pairs' count and $U_1$ the unit display's total. The fused
carrier's family splits twice, over the channels at the
exhaustion's content refinement (Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(ii))
and over the factors at the contents' addition
(Construction~\ref{con:places}), so each moment fold reads both
ways, the channels' counted fold against the factors' split at
the further factor's count,
\[
M_1(F)=d_\theta\,M_1(R)+d_R\,M_1(\theta)\ ,\qquad
M_2(F)=d_\theta\,M_2(R)+2\,M_1(R)\,M_1(\theta)+d_R\,M_2(\theta)\ ,
\]
with $M_{11}(F)$ at $M_2$'s shape, the cross read
$2\,M_1(R)\,M_1(\theta)$ shared: the collected display at the
fused carrier, read against the two factors' own collected
displays at the further factors' counts, withdraws the quadratic
folds (a summand on both members fixing the value) and leaves
\[
\sum_cN^c\,q(c+u)\,d_c+q(u)\,d_Rd_\theta
\;=\;\big(q(R+u)+q(\theta+u)\big)\,d_Rd_\theta
+2\,d_f\,M_1(R)\,M_1(\theta)\ ,
\]
whose $d_f$-multiple reads the moments at the degree folds,
$d_f\,M_1(R)=k_R\,d_R$ and $d_f\,M_1(\theta)=d_f\,d_\theta$ at
$\theta$'s degree $d_f$. The square identity
(Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}) with the row read
$\langle\lambda,2\rho\rangle+(d_f+1)\,k_\lambda
=2\sum_i\lambda_iu_i$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:weylchar}'s collection at
Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}'s fold) reads
$d_f\,q(\mu+u)=d_fQ(\mu)+k_\mu^{\,2}+d_f(d_f+1)\,k_\mu
+d_f\,q(u)$ at every shape; every channel shares the degree
$k_c=k_R+d_f$, the contents adding over the factors at $\theta$'s
degree, so the dimension identity $\sum_cN^cd_c=d_Rd_\theta$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(iii)) withdraws the shared reads and
the display closes at $Q(\theta)=2d_f$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}):
\[
\sum_cN^c\,d_c\,d_fQ(c)\;=\;d_Rd_\theta\,
\big(d_fQ(R)+2d_f^{\,2}\big)\ ,
\]
the display's $\hat c_2$-cleared read at
$[\,d_fQ:2d_f^{\,2}\,]$ (Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}); at a second
factor $\lambda$ the collected display runs at $\lambda$'s block,
every channel at the degree $k_c=k_R+k_\lambda$,
the moments' read $2\,d_f^{\,2}M_1(R)\,M_1(\lambda)=2\,k_Rk_\lambda\,d_Rd_\lambda$
withdrawing the degree squares' cross term at the dimension
identity, and the display closes at the second factor's own cleared
bracket $d_fQ(\lambda)$:
$\sum_cN^cd_c\,d_fQ(c)=d_Rd_\lambda\,(d_fQ(R)+d_fQ(\lambda))$.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The divisor identification, and the crossing divisor]
\label{thm:divisorid}
\emph{(i) The identification.} The spectrum is the root locus of
the exact fiber symbol (Theorem~\ref{thm:trigpencil}): on a window a
level is a pencil root exactly where the determinant reads equal
members, the
factorization read of Lemma~\ref{lem:split} at the gram's
determinant off the sum's unit, and the Feshbach
determinant reads equal members with it, one Schur factor of the whole
at a complement of unequal-membered determinant
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), at every coupling
outright, each root a located divisor point.

\emph{(ii) The crossing divisor.} For a symmetric stage pencil of the
chain with $G\succ0$, a window compression or a fiber pencil, the
entries polynomial in the base coordinates over the stage's field
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}'s band congruence), write $\chi(x)$ for the level
pair's site-datum determinant (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}'s $\chi$) and
take the squarefree split $\chi=c\prod_jS_j^{\,j}$ over the base's
polynomial pairs, the division descent's iterated greatest common
divisors, the equality test cross-multiplied
through the iterated division, each $S_j$ taken
primitive over the base's polynomial ring with the contents collected
into $c$, itself a base polynomial (Gauss): the split is an identity
of base polynomials and specializes at every stage point. The
\emph{crossing read} is
\[
D\;:=\;\prod_j\mathrm{Res}_x\big(S_j,S_j'\big)\ \cdot
\prod_{i<j}\mathrm{Res}_x\big(S_i,S_j\big)\ ,
\]
the resultants Definition~\ref{def:elim}'s at the variable $x$, a
base element off the sum's unit. At
a base point off $D$'s root locus the specialized split keeps the generic
structure, every root of $\chi$ at that point
a root of exactly one $S_j$, simple in it, of multiplicity $j$ in
$\chi$, and distinct roots stay distinct: \emph{root collisions sit on
$D$'s located root locus alone}, the jump divisors of the
decimation's list; a decimated head reads its counts as the fiber
pencil's on its bracket, so its jumps inherit the confinement.

\emph{(iii) The ground's read.} On a cell with pairs $l<h$,
the pencil pair at $l$ positive semidefinite and the counting
function flat at $h$
across the cell, the ground multiplicity is
$\mathrm{count}(h)$, both reads cell functions read
once (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}); by (ii) it moves across a located
boundary only where a ground collision sits on the boundary, the
boundary's own two-sided bracket counts. On the vacuum sector's
pencil at the free end's side it reads $1$ over the cell attached to
the free end, the least root in the free end's level bracket
(Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend}) at multiplicity $1$ there.
\begin{proof}
\emph{(ii)} A factor of $D$ of equal members reads an
occupied cross pair on
a squarefree or coprime pair, against its B\'ezout read $up+vq=1$
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}), so $D$ sits off the sum's unit. At a
base point off $D$'s root locus the leading $x$-coefficients multiply to $\det G$ there, on its upper
side by the split, so every one reads unequal members and the degrees
hold; each $S_j$ stays squarefree and the pairs stay coprime, the
resultants' own reads there; so every root of $\chi$ at that point is
a root of exactly one $S_j$, simple in it, of multiplicity $j$ in
$\chi$, and distinct roots stay distinct.
\emph{(iii)} A level
bracket of pairs $(l,h)$ isolating the free ground, the unit's line
against content $4\hat c_2(f)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend}), reads
the pair at $l$ positive semidefinite and $\mathrm{count}(h)=1$
at the free end, both reads
constant over the attached cell (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}), so the
least root sits in the bracket at multiplicity $1$ there.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The scheme bridge is a count]\label{thm:bridge}
\[
\big[\,d_{\mathrm{adj}}\,C_2(\mathrm{adj})\;:\;d_f\,C_2(f)\,\big]
\;=\;2\,d_f
\]
exactly, the pair of two weight-$1$ objects, one value at every form
point
(Proposition~\ref{prop:form}), and the read is a count: the $f$-flux
bridge's component at the contact end is
$b_f^{\mathrm{equiv}}=2d_f\,b_X$, one
rescaling of the coupling coordinate.
\begin{proof}
$d_{\mathrm{adj}}=r\,(r+2)$ with $\hat c_2(\mathrm{adj})=1$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:adjchar}; Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}), and the fundamental
count $d_f$ with
$\hat c_2(f)=[\,r(r+2):2d_f^{\,2}\,]$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:casimir}), so
the pair reads the cross-multiplied natural identity
$r(r+2)\cdot2d_f^{\,2}=2\,d_f\cdot d_f\cdot r\,(r+2)$; the $r=2$
evaluation is $6$.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The ruler excess]\label{def:excess}
At the residue $r$ the \emph{ruler excess} is the polynomial
\[
A(u)\;:=\;\sum_{j=1}^{r}[\,1:j\,]\,u^j
\]
(Definition~\ref{def:poly}), the one polynomial supported from
key one with $A'+u^r=1+u\,A'$, $r$ the pairing's residue.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The walk residue]\label{thm:walkresidue}
The tower pairing is forced. At the residue $r$:
for the principal adjoint tower (the $k\theta$-string, $\theta$ the highest root, $\hat c_2(k)=[\,k(k+r):r+1\,]$), the Casimir $C_2(m\theta)=m\,(m+r)$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:anchor} splits into a square part and a row-weight part,
and the pairing is the second over the whole:
\[
\varphi_m=\big[\,m\,r:m\,(m+r)\,\big]=[\,r:m+r\,],
\qquad
\varphi_m+\psi_m=1\quad\text{at}\quad\psi_m=[\,m:m+r\,]\ ,
\]
two weight-$1$ objects read as one pair, one value at every form
point
(Proposition~\ref{prop:form}), every datum forced, $\psi_m$ the
pairing's complement, the one-value read. Its generating object is
\[
\Psi(u):=\sum_{m\ge1}[\,1:m\,]\,\psi_m\,u^m
=\sum_{m\ge1}[\,1:m+r\,]\,u^m\ ,
\]
and the shifted series $F(u):=u^{r}\Psi(u)=\sum_{j\ge r+1}[\,1:j\,]\,u^j$ satisfies
the recursion
$F'=u^{r}+u\,F'$, coefficientwise one read per degree: its
divisor pair reads the least occupied degree $r$ and the pole order
$1$ at $u{=}1$, both naturals. Against the harmonic ruler
$R(u):=\sum_{m\ge1}[\,1:m\,]\,u^m$, the ruler
at the recursion $R'=1+u\,R'$, its pole order $1$ as well, the pole
excess is
one polynomial, coefficientwise exact and finitely supported:
\begin{gather*}
R(u)\;=\;F(u)+A(u)\ ,\qquad A(u)\;=\;\sum_{j=1}^{r}[\,1:j\,]\,u^j
\quad(\text{Definition~\ref{def:excess}})\ ,\\
A'+u^r=1+u\,A',\quad\text{the support from key one}\ ,
\end{gather*}
the one polynomial with the geometric derivative, closing
$F'+A'=R'$ term by term, a
divisor-characterized object. The value's second coordinate is its
read at $u=1$, the polynomial evaluation
\[
A(1)\;=\;H_r=\sum_{j=1}^{r}[\,1:j\,]\ ,
\]
one pair per residue, the ruler's excess over the walk; and the coefficientwise record at the
$\Psi$-level is the finite telescope, exact at every $M$,
\[
\sum_{m=1}^{M}[\,r:m(m+r)\,]
+\sum_{j=M+1}^{M+r}[\,1:j\,]
\;=\;H_r\ ,
\qquad
[\,1:m\,]=[\,1:m+r\,]+[\,r:m(m+r)\,]\ ,
\]
the tail itself an $r$-term expression. One object, one pole, one
read: $\varphi$ fixes $\Psi$, $\Psi$'s divisor fixes $F'$, and the
ruler's excess is the polynomial $A$, the construction settling the
coordinate outright. The exponent is an integer at $r=1$ alone; the pairing's own
pole residue $r$ agrees with it there and separates from it at $r=2$
on, so the residue-one instance leaves the two
together, and the construction rather than the instance is what selects.
\begin{proof}
The pairing: $C_2(m\theta)=m^{2}+m\,r$, the square part $m^{2}$
and the row-weight part $m\,r$, and the second over the whole is
$[\,m\,r:m\,(m+r)\,]=[\,r:m+r\,]$ at the shared factor $m$
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}'s one value at $ad=cb$); the
complement joins at $[\,r:m+r\,]+[\,m:m+r\,]=[\,m+r:m+r\,]=1$.
$\Psi$'s coefficient is $[\,1:m\,]\,[\,m:m+r\,]=[\,1:m+r\,]$; the
shift by $u^{r}$ reads $F$'s coefficient at the key $j=m+r$ as
$[\,1:j\,]$ from the key $r+1$ on, so $F'$ has the coefficient one
at every key at or beyond $r$, the recursion $F'=u^{r}+u\,F'$ key
by key, the least occupied degree of $F$ the key $r+1$, its
derivative's $r$, and the pole order one at $u=1$ the geometric
series' own. $R'$ has the coefficient one at every key, $R'=1+u\,R'$,
and $R$ against $F$ reads the keys one to $r$ alone,
$R=F+A$ at the displayed $A$, whose derivative has the coefficient
one at the keys below $r$, $A'+u^{r}=1+u\,A'$, and $F'+A'=R'$ key by
key. $A(1)$ is the fold of the coefficients, $H_r$. The summand
identity reads $(m+r)=m+r$ at the clearing $m\,(m+r)$, the three
terms' first members there; summing it over $m$ from one to $M$ reads
$H_M=\sum_{m\le M}[\,1:m+r\,]+\sum_{m\le M}[\,r:m(m+r)\,]$, and the
first sum is $H_{M+r}$ less $H_r$, the shifted keys, so the
telescope collects at $H_r$ with the tail
$\sum_{j=M+1}^{M+r}[\,1:j\,]$ the shifted sum's excess over $H_M$.
The exponent: $H_1=1$; at $r\ge2$ let $2^{k}$ be the largest power
of two at or below $r$ ($k\ge1$) and $P$ the product of the odd
naturals at or below $r$; every $j\le r$ off $2^{k}$ is $2^{a}b$ at
an odd $b$ and $a<k$ (at $a\ge k$ the natural $j$ is $2^{k}$ itself or
sits at or beyond $2^{k+1}$, past $r$),
so $2^{k}P\,[\,1:j\,]$ is the even natural $2\cdot2^{k-1-a}P_b$
at the cofactor $P_b$ at $b\,P_b=P$, while $2^{k}P\,[\,1:2^{k}\,]=P$ is
odd; the fold $2^{k}P\,H_r$ is an even natural joined to an odd
one, odd, while every natural's $2^{k}P$-multiple is even, so $H_r$ is off
the naturals at every $r\ge2$. The pole residue $r$ reads one at
$r=1$ with $H_1$; at $r\ge2$ the two separate, $H_r$ below $r$ (the
terms beyond the first at or below $[\,1:2\,]$,
$H_r\le[\,r+1:2\,]<r$).
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The contact pair]\label{def:contactpair}
At the contact end the walk is the head's compression to the tower
labels, the tower matrix (Proposition~\ref{prop:row};
Lemma~\ref{lem:contactcell}), and two divisors read it: the channel's, the boundary
resolvent $G_0$ with its $\iota$-symmetrized weight
(Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}), and the tower's, the generating object
$\Psi$ against the harmonic ruler (Theorem~\ref{thm:walkresidue}). The
\emph{contact pair} is the two divisors' reads: the first coordinate is
the channel's order count at the base $c_1$
(Definition~\ref{def:channelreads}); the second is
the ruler's excess over the walk read at one, $A(1)$
(Definition~\ref{def:excess}).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The contact pair's assembly]\label{thm:closing}
The contact pair of Definition~\ref{def:contactpair} reads
factor by factor, and there are two: the walk
exponent $H_r$ on the ruler's side, the polynomial excess $A(1)$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:walkresidue}) and coupling-free; and the channel's bit count,
read off the divisor of $G_0$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}). At the
contact end the walk is the head's compression to the tower labels
(Proposition~\ref{prop:row}; Construction~\ref{con:xfusion}), and
its two divisors are: the vacuum's boundary resolvent
$G_0$ with its $\iota$-symmetrized weight
(Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}) and the tower's generating object
$\Psi$ against the harmonic ruler
(Theorem~\ref{thm:walkresidue}); the mass weight is
the pair $[\,\langle c_1^{\,2}\!:\!1\rangle:c_1^{\,2}\,]$ against
its complement $[\,1:c_1^{\,2}\,]$, the two summing to one, its
side the upper at base two and equal members at base one, the mass
point at the crossing there, the divisor count one value throughout
(Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}). At every window and coupling of the
closed segment, each window cut's edge, where one is named, is the
compressed pair's least root, a located root of the window pencil's
symbol (Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(i); Lemma~\ref{lem:split};
Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}),
read at a word image with the two moments at equality and the first
positive, the state the word sector's own
(Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(i),(ii); Lemma~\ref{lem:statespace}).
So the pair's two coordinates read:
\[
\big(3,\ H_r\big) ,
\]
and both are divisor reads.

The pair $(3,H_r)$ is what the theory determines: two orders, both
naturals,
summing to $3$, and an exact pair, the first coordinate read at the base
$c_1$, a fusion multiplicity moving with the residue
(Construction~\ref{con:xfusion}). The two reads are of two divisors, the channel's ($G_0$, Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}) and the tower's
($\Psi$, Theorem~\ref{thm:walkresidue}), and the coordinates read
them alone.
\begin{proof}
The second coordinate is the walk's pole
excess against the harmonic ruler, the polynomial read $A(1)=H_r$
on the ruler's side, off
$F'$'s divisor pair, the least occupied degree $r$ and the pole order
$1$ at $u{=}1$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:walkresidue}). The first is the channel's order count: the
boundary entry at its renewal witness $G_0=z+c_1zG_0$ reads its
divisor as the witness's
own, the mass point at $c_1z_*=1$ a simple pole, order $1$, and the
$\iota$-symmetrized weight reading the base at order $2$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}); the two orders against the base give
$c_1^{\,1}\cdot c_1^{\,2}=c_1^{\,3}$, the order count $1+2=3$
(Definition~\ref{def:channelreads}). The mass weight's side is the
pair $\langle c_1^{\,2}\!:\!1\rangle$'s, the upper at $c_1=2$ and
equal members at $c_1=1$, where $z_*=1$ sits at the crossing
(Theorem~\ref{thm:channeldiv}); and the edge clause is
Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(i),(ii) at the window's compressed pair
with the state Lemma~\ref{lem:statespace}'s.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Truncation control]\label{thm:truncation}
Fix a region $\Lambda$. At the coupling $[\alpha\!:\!\beta]$ the truncation at Casimir cutoff
$\Lambda_C$ is a projection $\Pi$, the statement homogeneous on the ray,
and the off-block coupling is the magnetic form's cap. $M$ is
multiplication by
$\sum_p\chi_L(U_{\partial p})$ (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), each
plaquette term capped as a form, two-sided at the closure's
dimension fold (Lemma~\ref{lem:loopcap}), so the sum is capped
two-sidedly and with it the pencil's magnetic part
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}),
\[
\beta M\ \preceq\ W\;:=\;\beta\,\#p\,d_L
\qquad\text{with}\qquad
W+\beta M\ \ \text{positive semidefinite},
\]
the closure's dimension fold times the region's plaquette count at
the magnetic weight, $d_L=2d_f$ the $A$-series read at the
fundamental with its dual (Lemma~\ref{lem:fpcap}),
independent of the cutoff; $E$ being diagonal reads its off-block
part at the sum's unit ($\Pi E\,\Pi'$ at the complement projection
$\Pi'$ at $\Pi+\Pi'=1$), so the off-block coupling of $H$ is the magnetic one
alone, under the one form cap $W$. The cap's compression
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}) bounds the magnetic part inside the removed
block, whose electric diagonal sits at or above $\alpha\Lambda_C$, so that
block's floor is $f:=\langle\alpha\Lambda_C:W\rangle$,
at the join $W+f=\alpha\Lambda_C$;
writing $E_{\mathrm{low}}$ for the higher of the two window levels the window cut of
Definition~\ref{def:K} reads plus the cap $W$, an admissible cutoff
reads $E_{\mathrm{low}}<\alpha\Lambda_C$, and at its witness gap
$\varsigma$,
\[
E_{\mathrm{low}}+\varsigma\;=\;\alpha\Lambda_C,
\]
the removed block's floor sits at least $\varsigma$ above each level.
A compression lowers each count below a line (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}),
raising each low level, and the cap's two splits collect to the
polarization
$2\langle x,\,\beta M\,y\rangle+c_W\langle
x,x\rangle+\varsigma\langle y,y\rangle$ on its upper side or of equal
members at $x$ in the head and $y$ in the removed block, at the
pair weights $W$,
$\varsigma$ and the \emph{shift cap} $c_W$, the cofactor at
$\varsigma\,c_W=W^2$ (Definition~\ref{def:ground}, $\varsigma$
the admissible cutoffs' own gap), so the shifted split reads
$H+c_W\!\oplus\!\varsigma\ \succeq\ H_{11}\!\oplus\!H_{22}$
with the removed block's floor above every level, counts are monotone
under $\succeq$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), and each level's downward
shift is at most $c_W$. At a cutoff holding two roots, with
the ground simple there and at every larger cutoff, the
gap of the first two roots changes by at most $c_W$:
each root falls by a datum between the sum's unit and $c_W$.
Thus the finite cut and the regional cut's located edge, where named,
bracket each other at the priced width,
\[
E_0\,\varsigma\,\mathcal K^{\mathrm{reg}}_\Lambda\ \le\ E_0\,\varsigma\,\mathcal K_{\Lambda,\Lambda_C}
+\beta^2\,\#p^2\,d_L^{\,2} ,
\qquad
E_0\,\varsigma\,\mathcal K_{\Lambda,\Lambda_C}\ \le\ E_0\,\varsigma\,\mathcal K^{\mathrm{reg}}_\Lambda
+\beta^2\,\#p^2\,d_L^{\,2} ,
\]
degree matched on the ray as the level is, the two reads' bracket
priced by one pair comparison each way at every $\alpha$, the
closure's dimension fold ($2d_f$ at the $A$-series) and
the region's plaquette count its data: the truncation is certifiable at every window size with exact
atoms, and the window cuts approach the regional cut with a modulus rather than
along a subsequence. The gap chain reads the modulus at the $\alpha{=}1$ representative, and the
display is homogeneous on the ray (Proposition~\ref{prop:segment}), every
representative's read one rescaling of it.

\emph{The cutoff-tail certificate.} At $\alpha=1$ and
positive pairs $h,\eta$, let $C$ be a stated cutoff with
\[
\eta C>\eta W+\eta h+W^2,
\qquad
\operatorname{rev}\big(H_C:(e_C+h+\eta)G_C\big)=1,
\]
where $e_C$ is the cutoff pencil's designated least root.
The cutoff comparison includes its positive gap and the
count includes its pivot split. Then at every $C'\ge C$,
with $e_{C'}$ that cutoff's least root,
\[
\operatorname{rev}\big(H_{C'}:(e_{C'}+h)G_{C'}\big)=1,
\qquad
\mathcal K_{\Lambda,C'}([1:\beta])\ge[\,h:E_0\,].
\]
The ground is simple on this cutoff tail, and
$[\,h:E_0\,]$ belongs to the regional cut
(Definition~\ref{def:K}). The cutoff is finite certificate
data at the two displayed reads. At $\eta=h$ these are
$hC>hW+h^2+W^2$ and the count one at $e_C+2h$.
\begin{proof}
The cap's two splits are read at the vector
$Wx+\varsigma y$ and at its partner $Wx+\varsigma\,\check y$, $\check
y$ the memberwise swap of $y$: the diagonal blocks' reads withdraw
between the two reads, the coupling's pairings double, and the
cofactor at $\varsigma\,c_W=W^2$ clears the doubled weight, so the
two collect to the polarization.
The positive removed block at a level $z$ has its Schur
correction between the sum's unit and $c_WG_{11}$, the
polarization's positive split at that block's pivot
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). Thus the larger count at $z$
lies between the head counts at $z$ and $z+c_W$.
The ordered-root reads of Lemma~\ref{lem:split} give
the stated fall of each root. At simple grounds their
gap changes by at most $c_W$, the two falls' difference.
The lower bracket gives a floor on the whole cutoff
tail where positive, and the upper bracket caps that
tail, giving the regional read of Definition~\ref{def:K}.

For the cutoff-tail certificate put $s=[\,W^2:\eta\,]$
at $W>0$. Fix $C'\ge C$ and set $z=e_{C'}+h$.
Compression and the unit vector's pencil read give
$e_{C'}\le e_C\le0$ (Definition~\ref{def:pencil};
Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), hence $z\le h$.
The tail at the split between $C$ and $C'$ has form
\[
P_z\succeq(C-W-h)G_{\mathrm{tail}}\succ sG_{\mathrm{tail}}.
\]
Its coupling $B$ is the actual magnetic off-block.
The two-sided magnetic cap gives its squared-action
cap $W^2$: the magnetic split puts every root between
$-W$ and $W$, its square at or below $W^2$, and
the cross image is a projection of that action's image
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}; Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).
At the solved witness $P_zX=B^{\mathsf T}$ the
polarization with $\eta s=W^2$ therefore gives
\[
0\preceq BX=X^{\mathsf T}P_zX\preceq\eta G_C.
\]
The count at $z$ is the deflated count and satisfies
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{rev}(H_{C'}:zG_{C'})
&=\operatorname{rev}(H_C-zG_C-BX)\\
&\le\operatorname{rev}\big(H_C:(e_{C'}+h+\eta)G_C\big)\\
&\le\operatorname{rev}\big(H_C:(e_C+h+\eta)G_C\big)=1.
\end{align*}
The actual ground is strictly below $e_{C'}+h$, giving
the reverse comparison. The count and ground multiplicity
are one, so Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut} gives the cut.
A vacant removed list reads the head count directly.
At $W=0$ the magnetic part reads the sum's unit,
$B=0$, and the removed electric contents exceed $C>h$;
the count comparison holds at the diagonal tail outright.
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[The dual truncation]\label{lem:dualtrunc}
At the coupling $[\,\sigma:1\,]$ at a pair $\sigma$, the cap, the
floor and the compression of
Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation} read with one substitution, the
two terms' roles exchanged in the bound's inputs: on a fixed
region, the magnetic cap at weight one is
$W:=\#p\,d_L$, the plaquette caps' fold
(Lemma~\ref{lem:loopcap}; Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}).
The off-block coupling and the removed block's magnetic part
read that cap by compression and polarization. At an index
compression with a verified two-sided cap, the argument reads that
cap at the block's Gram (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). The removed
block's electric diagonal sits at or above $\sigma\Lambda_C$, and each
level shifts downward under the compression by at most the
shift cap $c_W$, the cofactor at $\varsigma\,c_W=W^2$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}), at the order
$\lambda+W<\sigma\Lambda_C$'s witness gap $\varsigma$,
$\lambda+W+\varsigma=\sigma\Lambda_C$. A count at level $\lambda$ is
therefore pinned on the finite head whenever the bracket
$[\lambda,\ \lambda+c_W]$ is clear of the head's divisor
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}, the level as the parameter): every count of
the dual pencil, the pair $(\sigma E\!:\!M)$'s site datum
$H([\,\sigma:1\,])$, lives on a finite head
pencil, at every cutoff with
\[
\sigma\,\Lambda_C\ >\ \lambda+W+c_\vartheta
\qquad\text{at}\qquad \vartheta\,c_\vartheta=W^2 ,
\]
one pair comparison at a clearance pair $\vartheta$, the admissible set
an output whose floor rises toward the contact end. The transfer is one-sided: the compression lowers counts and raises
levels, each level's downward shift capped at $c_W$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}; Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), so between two
head jumps the lower comparison reads at its equality, the head ground at
or above the full one, and the clearance rides the upper jump alone: the
admissible levels are those beyond the ground bracket's top whose
sum with $c_W$ sits below the second
jump's bottom, the measured gap spent on one side.

\emph{The count beyond every cutoff.} The display defines the dual
pencil's count at $\lambda$ over the unbounded content range: at a
level whose bracket $[\lambda,\ \lambda+c_W]$ is clear of
the head's divisor, it is the head count at any cutoff beyond the
display's bound, and two admissible cutoffs read one integer.

\emph{The seam identity.} The ray at end weights $[\,q^2:p^2\,]$
names one integer pencil pair, $(q^2E:p^2M)$, with its site datum
$S$ at the join $q^2E=p^2M+S$, and the two coordinates'
representatives are the datum's positive rescalings,
\[
q^2\,H\big([\,1:\tau^2\,]\big)\;=\;S\;=\;p^2\,H\big([\,\sigma:1\,]\big)
\qquad\text{at}\qquad q\,\tau=p,\quad p^2\sigma=q^2 ,
\]
so every subspace read agrees at rescaled levels: a
rescaling-fixed direct summand reads at rescaled levels, the
fibers among them (Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}), and on each,
\[
\operatorname{count}_{[1:\tau^2]}(\lambda)
\;=\;\operatorname{count}_{S}(q^2\lambda)
\;=\;\operatorname{count}_{[\sigma:1]}(\sigma\lambda)
\]
at every level, the reversal count blind to the positive factors
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), brackets, jumps and extents rescaled by the one
factor with their levels. A stored level therefore names its
representative, and a seam comparison is two reads of the one integer
pencil at matched levels, the factors the display's.
\begin{proof}
The cap at the dual representative is the fold of the region's
plaquette caps at magnetic weight one. Compression keeps each
two-sided comparison, and Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}'s
polarization gives the off-block read at that cap. Substituting
$\alpha=\sigma$ and $\beta=1$ gives the displayed cutoff and
shift comparisons at the electric floor $\sigma\Lambda_C$.
\emph{The count beyond every cutoff.} The
smaller head is the larger head's own truncation (the projections
nest), the display runs on the larger head at the one cap $W$ (a
compression of a cap is a cap, Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}) with the
removed block's floor at least $\varsigma$, and the clear bracket
pins the count both times, so two admissible cutoffs read one
integer.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The near-contact cell]\label{lem:contactcell}
The dual pencil, the pair $(\sigma E\!:\!M)$'s site datum
$P(\sigma)$, is affine in $\sigma$, and on a
fiber head (Lemma~\ref{lem:dualtrunc}) its entries are one
polynomial-pair list in $(t,\sigma)$ over the residue beyond the
locality band
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}; Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries}), the window entering
through its sampled momenta and its separation range alone, the residue a
further coordinate beyond the reach bound
(Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(iii); Lemma~\ref{lem:serstable}(iii)
at the further series). Every count of the dual chain is
therefore Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}'s cell function over
$(t,\sigma,r)$ with located divisors: the \emph{contact cell} is the
contact end's, its $\sigma$-extent $\sigma_1$ the divisor's first positive
root, an output of
Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(iii)'s reads, the residue direction the
classifications' (Lemma~\ref{lem:chaininstances};
Lemma~\ref{lem:serdivisors} at the further series), the divisors'
roots against the families' clearances; anchors at pair $\sigma$ are window
reads; and $r=1$ enters as a residue read like any other, $c_1=1$ flowing
through the channel data (Lemma~\ref{lem:channels}).

\emph{The truncation pair.} On the vacuum sector's one-plaquette
chain (the unit label's fusion closure under the magnetic list,
Construction~\ref{con:depthchain}, one label per index entry at
the electric read $4\hat c_2$) the
chain's count at a level is bracketed by two finite divisors. The
first is the plain truncation, a compression, its counts at or
below the chain's (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). The second is the
\emph{cutoff-bordered} pencil: the head with one auxiliary row
per cutoff label (a head label whose fusion by a closure member
leaves the cutoff, Proposition~\ref{prop:fusionfinite}), coupling
one and auxiliary diagonal the pair
$[\,\langle 4\sigma\Lambda\!:\!d_L+\lambda\rangle:\varkappa_B\,]$
at the cutoff $\Lambda$ on the labels' Casimir, its first member
the seed floor $F:=\langle 4\sigma\Lambda\!:\!d_L\rangle$ at the
level on the second member, the floor of the whole excluded block,
every excluded label at Casimir at or beyond $\Lambda$ by the
cutoff's own read and its loop's content at four times it
(Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}); $d_L$ is the magnetic form cap, kept
by every principal block (Lemma~\ref{lem:fpcap}); and the
\emph{border cap} $\varkappa_B$
is the product of the coupling's largest row and column sums,
$BB^{\mathsf T}\preceq\varkappa_B$ on the cutoff labels'
support, the two-sided Schur read. At every
level below $F$ the chain's count sits between the pair's two
counts at every cutoff, and a
level whose two counts agree is a located count of the chain
itself, the count beyond every cutoff
(Lemma~\ref{lem:dualtrunc}). At $r=2$ the
label lattice is two-row, a reduced shape at most $r$ rows deep
(Construction~\ref{con:labels}). At every member the depth chain's
head shells (Construction~\ref{con:depthchain}) are the chain's
leading block, the chain's counts at or beyond the head's at every
level (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}'s compression read). A shell
ordering of the
elimination is certificate data (Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(i)), its
validity divisors (the seed's dominance root and the envelope's own
positivity ceiling) entering the emitted list as any boundary's do;
the deep tower rows repeat off the collar (Lemma~\ref{lem:grading}),
the decimation's constant-stencil direction.

\emph{The contact end is interior to its cell.} At the contact end the head pencil
is the magnetic member's balance partner
(Proposition~\ref{prop:segment}), its level pair's datum the
balance partner of $M+\lambda G$, and the counts are the closure
fold's reads, $N_L$ against the level at the orthonormal characters
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fpcap}; Theorem~\ref{thm:pairpencil}): the contact
end sits inside the contact cell and its counts are the cell's, direct
reads; at a level on the closure fold's divisor, Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}'s boundary
clause extends the positive-semidefinite cells into the closed
endpoint.
\begin{proof}
\emph{The truncation pair.} Between any two cutoffs the
excluded block sits at or above $F$ ($\sigma$ times its Casimir
floor against the magnetic cap), so at every level below $F$ the
chain dominates the shifted split, the head less the border cap's
multiple of the cutoff labels' support projector at the gap's
cofactor beside the excluded block less the gap
(Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}'s shifted split at the border cap's
Schur read, $BB^{\mathsf T}\preceq\varkappa_B$ on the support),
the excluded member positive semidefinite there, and the chain's
count sits at or below the shifted head's (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia},
counts monotone); the bordered pencil's auxiliary pivots are
positive below $F$ and inertia adds at them, its deflation the
shifted head (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}): the chain's count sits
between the pair's two counts.
\emph{The contact end.} At a
level off the closure fold's divisor the cell's determinant reads unequal members at
the contact end, so the contact end sits inside the contact cell.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The contact drift]\label{lem:contactdrift}
At the dual representative, the pair $(\sigma E\!:\!M)$'s site

At the fundamental fold $\lambda=\sum_im_i\,\omega_i$ the key is the

+\sum_im_i\,\langle\omega_i,2\rho\rangle\ ,

every summand a natural product at the fundamental form reads

\begin{lemma}[The corner pencil]\label{lem:corner}
Toward the contact end the chain reads in the \emph{corner
coordinate}: the ray $[\,\eta^2:1\,]$ at the scale pair $\eta$,
its levels at the \emph{corner scale}, a level the product
$\eta\,\eta'$ at a \emph{height} $\eta'$, itself a balance pair
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}). The corner data are the dual
pencil's at the substitution $\sigma=\eta^2$,
$\lambda=\eta\,\eta'$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:dualtrunc}), and the corner
count is the reversal count of the form pair
\[
\operatorname{rev}\big(\,\eta^2E+\eta\,\eta'_-\,G\ :\
M+\eta\,\eta'_+\,G\,\big)
\qquad\text{at}\quad
\eta'=\langle\,\eta'_+\!:\!\eta'_-\,\rangle ,
\]
the height's members cross-added onto the pair's two sides
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}; Theorem~\ref{thm:certconstruct}), every entry's
weight a natural product of the scale's members and the height's. The
corner's \emph{shifted scaling}: at the magnetic form
cap $d_L$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:fpcap}) the shifted pencil
$Q(\sigma):=\sigma E+S_\theta$, at $S_\theta$ the pair
$(d_L\,G\!:\!M)$'s site datum, is a sum of two
positive-semidefinite forms (the electric diagonal's; the cap's,
Lemma~\ref{lem:fpcap}), and at scales $\sigma'<\sigma$ (two equal
scales reading one pencil outright) with the cofactor $\rho$
at $\rho\,\sigma=\sigma'$,
\[
\rho\,Q(\sigma)\ \preceq\ Q(\sigma')\ \preceq\ Q(\sigma) ,
\qquad
\rho\,\mu_j(\sigma)\ \le\ \mu_j(\sigma')\ \le\
\mu_j(\sigma) ,
\]
$\mu_j$ the shifted roots; the comparison is cutoff-free and
window-free, a form comparison compressing. The ground's electric
weight rides the contact drift at a certified positive rate
(Lemma~\ref{lem:contactdrift}), and the tail's count read is the
sector's tail certificate's (Construction~\ref{con:sectorcert}), the
block chain's at bounded shells (Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerblock}) and
the band-one walk's at the single-plaquette window
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerpivot}).
On a fiber
head the entries are Lemma~\ref{lem:contactcell}'s list at the
substitution, one polynomial-pair list in $(t,\eta,\eta')$ over the
residue beyond the locality
band, so every corner count is Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}'s cell
function over the $(t,\eta,\eta')$ base with located boundaries,
and the \emph{corner divisor} is Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}'s
crossing read at that base. The \emph{corner cell} is the contact end's,
and its data are one located output per member and
direction count (Construction~\ref{con:lattice}'s direction
reads), the \emph{extent} $\eta_1$, at a chain of bounded shells
the corner divisor's first positive root in the scale over the
cell, at its leading-term radius in the residue
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}; Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(iii)), and
at a chain whose shells grow with the depth the tail certificate's
ceiling (Construction~\ref{con:sectorcert}(iii)), and one located datum per ray of
the cell, the \emph{floor} $\kappa$ at the ray, the least of the
certificate's three positive lower margins for the regional
records' located gaps above their grounds at the ray:
the unit fiber's second root's, the further fibers' least first
root's over the band's chords, $t^{2}$ below $4$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}), and the charged sectors' first roots'
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount} at the chord;
Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}(iii),(iv)), one trichotomy fold read
ray by ray, its residue and rank direction
the cell coordinate's read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(iii); Lemma~\ref{lem:serstable}(iii)). The
ray coordinate reads the outputs back at squares: the ray
$[\,a:b\,]$ sits in the extent exactly at
$a\,d_1^{\,2}\le n_1^{\,2}\,b$ at $\eta_1=[\,n_1\!:\!d_1\,]$, and
a level reads through its height, the cofactor at
$\eta\,\eta'=\lambda$ (Definition~\ref{def:ground}), the height
against the floor one pair comparison: the level's square against
the weight product, the two end weights' own scale.

\emph{The boundary families.} The corner cell's boundaries are the
located roots of four families over the $(t,\eta,\eta')$ base, each
family one of the chain's comparisons read at the substitution and
entering the list as any boundary does (Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}, the
emitted record), the corner divisor's own root list in the scale
beside them, the extent its first positive member: the \emph{jump
family}, the pencil determinant's roots at the bracket's heights,
the decimation's own jump divisors at the substitution
(Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}); the \emph{cutoff family}, the
tail's dominance comparison at the line
(Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(ii)): at a line the labels whose
diagonal clears their off-row magnitude fold are dominant at every
cutoff, the chain's count at the line sits at or below the floored
head's, the head less the tail coupling's solve at the gaps
(Construction~\ref{con:sectorcert}(i)), one finite pencil per scale
and line, and the dominance root in the scaled square keys the
head, the plateau read $[\,2:3\,]\,(s-2\eta)$ against the line's
rate at the residue two (Construction~\ref{con:residuetwo}), so the
cutoffs enter through the floored head alone, cutoff-free at every

(Lemma~\ref{lem:fpcap}); the \emph{deck family}, the bulk blocks'
crossing loci with the graph read's side and the spectator caps'
three counts, each a cell datum of the corner base
(Lemma~\ref{lem:spectator}(iii); Lemma~\ref{lem:deckfactor}), the
$r=1$ reads among them, and the contraction cap read on the cell
at the boundary root's isolation datum: the cell is a component of
the divisor list's complement, the located root's bracket its
margin, and the cap's margin squares to the crossing read,
$\langle1\!:\!z^2\rangle^2=z^2\,\langle w^2\!:\!4\rangle$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:deckfactor}); and the \emph{tension family}, the charged
sectors' tension, the winding shift's dressed floor against the
unit class's dressing folds, and the separated sectors' clearance
at the height floor
(Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}(iii),(iv);
Lemma~\ref{lem:relfiber}(iii)), one root list per charge vector.
Every window read sits in the list's cells: the momenta are
sampled in $t$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}), the slabs read within
the spectator brackets (Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(iii)), the cutoffs
within the floored head, and the sectors at their families; so
the extent and the floor are outputs of the one list, and the
cell's $t$-section at the outputs is the whole range exactly where
the list's $t$-roots sit off it, itself a located read. The rank
direction inherits: the substitution fixes every entry's residue
dependence, so the families' divisors are the chain's own read at
corner base points, the deck base the member-key count, one value at every cleared
residue (Proposition~\ref{prop:row};
Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(ii)).

The chain's
\emph{height} at a scale is its cut's edge at the corner scale
(Definition~\ref{def:K}; Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(i)), the ray's
floor a member pair of its cut, the cut's meet at or below each
regional cut (Definition~\ref{def:K}), and each cutoff-tail
probe cap a cap on it
(Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(iv), the first moment at the gradient
and boundary reads of Theorem~\ref{thm:momentform}). Each cell reads its edges at word
images: the flat window's upper end is the cell's second root, a
point of its own divisor (Lemma~\ref{lem:split};
Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(i)), and the window cut's edge there,
where one is named, is the compressed pair's least root, read at a
word image with the two moments at equality and the first
positive, the state the word sector's own
(Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(i),(ii)), one word image per window read
on the cell at the corner scale.
The extent's positivity is
the contact end's interiority read, the $\sigma_1$ brackets
Lemma~\ref{lem:contactcell}'s own outputs.
\begin{proof}
The corner count is the seam pencil's own: the display is cleared
by the scale's square at the seam identity's integer pencil
(Lemma~\ref{lem:dualtrunc}), the reversal count blind to the
positive factor (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). At the shifted
scaling $Q(\sigma')$ is the sum $\rho\,Q(\sigma)+w\,S_\theta$ at the
gap $w$, the scales' order's witness at $\rho+w=1$, read against
its second summand positive semidefinite, and the root reads the
comparison's counts (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). The extent's
bracket at bounded shells is the corner divisor's first positive
root's, the divisor the crossing read over the cell's base
(Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}), and the contact end sits inside its
cell (Lemma~\ref{lem:contactcell}), so the extent is positive; at
growing shells the extent is the certificate's ceiling, a halving of
one, positive by its shape.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The cell floor]\label{lem:cornerfloor}
At a corner ray (Lemma~\ref{lem:corner}) the \emph{corner floor}
is positive at every tail scale, the certificate's common lower
margin at the ray. The depth chain's decimated head at the dual
representative at the ray's scale
(Construction~\ref{con:depthchain}; Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}),
finite at the ray at Lemma~\ref{lem:dualtrunc}'s cutoff and
Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(ii)'s head bound, reads its ground
$\varepsilon_0$ and its three located gaps above it
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), each at or beyond the corresponding
certificate margin: the unit
fiber's second root's, the least first root's over the further
fibers' band, the chords at $t^{2}$ below $4$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}; Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount} at the chord), and
the charged sectors' first roots'
(Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}(iii),(iv)). Per fiber the vacuum
sector's depth chain reads the count at the certificate's line at
most one at every tail scale, the sector's tail certificate at the
fiber's shells (Construction~\ref{con:sectorcert}; at a chain of
bounded shells the block chain's certificate,
Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerblock}, the band-one walk at the
single-plaquette window its scalar instance,
Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerpivot}(v),(vi); the count a cell function of
the chord, Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}), the line above the unit
fiber's lower line by the certificate's lines' gap at the scale: at the unit fiber the crossing is
the ground's, the lifted witness reading the ground at or below
the lower line (Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerpivot}(v)), so the ground is
one level at its multiplicity one (Theorem~\ref{thm:SO}) and the
unit fiber's second root sits at or beyond the line; at a further
fiber the crossing is vacant, the count at the line the sum's
unit, so the fiber's first root sits at or beyond the line; and
the charged sectors' first roots clear the ground at the winding
floor and the tension's side
(Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}(ii),(iii)): the floor, the least of the
three positive margins, is positive, and every pair $\kappa$ at $E_0\kappa$
below the floor is a member of the ray's cut
(Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}). The certificate's lines' gap is the
common lower read at the ray, the individual roots read at their
windows. The total counts are the decimation's
(Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(i)), the charged lower read the
tension's (Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}(iii)). In each region
the finite lower witness's content and the stated head's contents
give a cutoff key from which the upper count is one and the
ground simple, with every positive gap at or beyond the
certificate's lines' gap. The deeper sectors' couplings enter
their actual deflations (Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation};
Lemma~\ref{lem:relfiber}(iv)). The heights read two-sided
at the ray: the floor's clearance below, and above the window's cap
line at the tail read (Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerkey}) and the
cutoff-tail probe caps (Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(iv)), the
chain's height at the ray between them, one bracket per ray. At
the adjoint list's one-plaquette sector at the residue one the
head is the band-one walk (Proposition~\ref{prop:row}), the
single-plaquette window at the unit fiber alone, and the gap is the
band-one certificate's (Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerpivot}(v),(vi)), the
lines' gap $o\,\eta$ at every tail scale; at every further residue
the band-one walk is that sector's compression to the tower
labels, its lower line and its cap line lifting to the sector
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), and the sector's count at the line is
the tail certificate's at the sector's shells, growing with the
depth (Construction~\ref{con:sectorcert}(iii)), the residue two at
Construction~\ref{con:residuetwo}'s profile at the certificate's
data and their reads (Construction~\ref{con:residuetwocert};
Lemma~\ref{lem:residuetworeads}) and every further member and
residue at its own (Pending~\ref{pen:sectorcertfurther}).
\begin{proof}
The head at the ray is a finite symmetric pencil over the located
stage (Lemma~\ref{lem:dualtrunc}; Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(ii);
Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}), so its roots are located with the split's
congruence (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}) and each gap is one located
comparison; the further fibers' least first root over the chord
range is the divisor's read along the chord, the count constant off
its located roots (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}), and the charged
sectors' first roots are the dressed strings' head reads at the
ray (Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}(iv)). The certificate's two lines
are corner levels at the vacuum sector's depth chain, the head's
shells its blocks (Construction~\ref{con:sectorcert};
Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(i)), and the count splits over the
fibers, the chain block diagonal at the chord splitting with the
counts adding (Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}; Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}),
each fiber's count at the line the certificate's own read there, a
cell function of the chord (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}): at the
unit fiber the ground sits at or below the lower line at the
lifted witness and the count reads at most one at the line, so the
counting function is flat between them, the ground the one root
below the line at its multiplicity one (Theorem~\ref{thm:SO};
Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(iii)) and the unit fiber's second root
at or beyond the line; at a further fiber the certificate's
crossing is vacant, the count at the line the sum's unit, so the
fiber's first root sits at or beyond the line; the lines' gap is
cleared by the first two gaps at every tail scale.
Fix one region and scale. Write $l,u$ for the certificate's
lower and upper lines, with $l+h=u$ at its positive gap.
Its verified total count at $u$ is at most one on its
stated cutoff tail, and its lower witness $x$ has finite
content. Let $C_s$ be the largest of one, the stated head's
contents and the witness's occupied contents, a finite
trichotomy fold (Definition~\ref{def:ground};
Proposition~\ref{prop:leastwindow}). At every $C\ge C_s$
the witness's form is its original read, giving
\[
e_C\le l<u,\qquad
1\le\operatorname{rev}(H_C:uG_C)\le1.
\]
Thus the ground is simple on this cutoff tail. Since
$e_C+h\le u$ and $e_C<e_C+h$, count monotonicity gives
\[
\operatorname{rev}\big(H_C:(e_C+h)G_C\big)=1.
\]
This is the regional floor $[\,h:E_0\,]$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}; Definition~\ref{def:K}). The
two-component and deeper sectors' admitted product forms read the
positive fold of Lemma~\ref{lem:relfiber}(iii),(iv) at the stated
floors. Their couplings enter the certificate's deflations,
whose pivot counts join to its total count
(Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(i)); every comparison of regional
records reads Construction~\ref{con:sectorcert}(ii)'s cap and
margin counts at those actual data. The caps are Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerkey}'s
cutoff-tail lines and Lemma~\ref{lem:attained}(iv)'s cutoff-tail
probe caps, each at or beyond the chain's height
(Definition~\ref{def:K}, the cut's meet at or below each regional
cut). Its simple-ground key is $C_s$ above; joining that
key to the two trial members' contents gives the key of
Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerkey}'s cap. At the adjoint list's one-plaquette
sector at the residue one the head is the band-one walk's, its
count at the lines the certificate's ((v) the ground below the
lower line, (vi) the count at most one at the line), the gap the
lines' own; at a further residue the compression's lower line and
cap line lift (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), the count at the line the
tail certificate's at the growing shells
(Construction~\ref{con:sectorcert}(iii)).
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{construction}[The corner window's data]\label{con:cornerwindow}
At two directions or beyond the \emph{square window} of side $L$
has the vertices at the coordinates from one to $L+1$ in every
direction with the links and plaquettes among them, one window of
the directed family (Definition~\ref{def:carrier}), $\#p$ its
plaquettes' count, $\#\ell$ its links' count, and $g$ the
direction gap at $g+1=d$; every plaquette's boundary word runs from
its corner along the lower direction's link forward, its \emph{base
link}, then along the higher direction's link at the corner moved
one step in the lower direction forward, and returns along the lower
direction's link at the corner moved one step in the higher direction
and along the higher direction's link at the corner, both backward
(Construction~\ref{con:lattice}). The window's data are the reads
below, each a read of the window's finite lists.

\emph{The counts.} A plaquette's boundary holds four links; a
link sits on at most $2g$ plaquettes, two in each plane through its
direction, the plane's plaquette at the link's tail, holding the
link forward as its base link or as its corner's higher link, and
the plaquette at the tail moved back one step in the plane's other
direction, holding it backward, the second occupied exactly where
the tail's coordinate in that direction sits beyond one; a
\emph{cube} is three directions in order with a corner whose three
coordinates sit below the side, its six \emph{faces} the plaquettes
at the corner in each two of its directions and at the corner
stepped along the third, and a plaquette is a face of at most
$2\,(g-1)$ cubes, two in each direction off its plane; and the
lists' counts are box counts, the
sites whose coordinates at $k$ stated directions sit below the side
and are free at the further directions numbering $L^{k}(L+1)^{g+1-k}$,
one digit per direction: the links' count
$\#\ell=(g+1)\,L\,(L+1)^{g}$, the plaquettes' count
$\#p=[\,g\,(g+1):2\,]\,L^{2}(L+1)^{g-1}$, and, at three directions
or beyond at the gap $h$ at $h+2=g$, the cubes' count
$[\,g\,(g+1)\,(g-1):6\,]\,L^{3}(L+1)^{h}$. The window's \emph{tree} is the comb
rooted at the \emph{root}, the vertex at coordinate one in every
direction (Construction~\ref{con:lattice}'s boundary read): a
vertex's \emph{root path} ascends the directions in their order,
at most $L$ links per direction and at most $(g+1)\,L$ links in
all; the \emph{path word} $R_{v\leftarrow w}$ between two vertices
is the tree path's adjoint coefficient, the ordered product of the
links' adjoint coefficients at the traversals' dagger reads
(Lemma~\ref{lem:loopcap}'s move identity), orthogonal at the
evaluation identity, two paths composing at their join,
$R_{u\leftarrow v}\,R_{v\leftarrow w}=R_{u\leftarrow w}$, a link
traversed both ways withdrawing at the evaluation identity
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}), and the transposed word the
reversed path's, $R_{v\leftarrow w}^{\mathsf T}=R_{w\leftarrow v}$;
a plaquette's \emph{root path} is its base link's tail's, and a
link sits on the root paths of at most $\#p$ plaquettes, the
count's own read. At a plaquette $p$ and a boundary link $\ell$ the
\emph{loop region} $R_{\ell p}$ is the region between the boundary
arc off $\ell$ and the tree path from the base link's tail to
$\ell$'s tail, the plaquettes of the columns descended in the later
directions at the plaquette's corners, one column of width one per
descent at a height at most the side, so at most $g\,L$ plaquettes,
the \emph{region's count} $n_{\ell p}$; the region is occupied at
the two links off the corner alone, the tree path from the corner
to the corner moved by one step in a direction $a$ of the plane
descending the directions beyond $a$ to the first positions and
ascending; and a plaquette sits in at most $[\,2:(g+1)\,L\,]\,\#p$
regions: a plaquette of the plane $(a,k)$ at $a<k$, at the corner
$y$, sits in the region of $(p,\ell)$ exactly where $p$'s plane holds the
direction $a$, $\ell$'s tail is $p$'s corner moved by one step in
that direction, $y$ sits at the first position in every direction beyond $k$ (a
corner off the first position there sits off every region), and
$p$'s corner agrees with $y$ at every direction below $k$, sits
beyond $y_k$ at $k$ and is free beyond $k$, the $g$ planes through
$a$, at most $L$ positions at $k$ and $L+1$ at each
later direction, at the plaquette count
$\#p=[\,g\,(g+1):2\,]\,L^{2}(L+1)^{g-1}$; so the regions' counts
fold to at most $[\,2g:g+1\,]\,\#p$ over the pairs whose region
holds one plaquette, at or below $2\,\#p$.

\emph{The incidence.} The \emph{incidence} $K$ is the plaquette-link
list at the traversals' signs, one at a boundary link traversed
forward, its balance partner backward, and the sum's unit off the
boundary (Construction~\ref{con:lattice}); the plaquettes'
\emph{Gram} $\Delta:=KK^{\mathsf T}$ reads $4$ on the diagonal, the
boundary's link count, at two plaquettes sharing a link the two
traversals' signs' product, the balance partner of one at two
plaquettes of one plane (the shared link traversed at exchanged
directions), and the sum's unit at two plaquettes off a shared
link, symmetric at the product's exchange and positive
semidefinite as a Gram (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), its form the
links' folds' squares' fold,
\[
W^{\mathsf T}\Delta W\;=\;\sum_\ell\Big(\sum_{p\ni\ell}K_{p\ell}\,W_p\Big)^{2}\ .
\]
\emph{The kernel and the range.} At two directions the kernel is
the unit family: a plaquette combination pairing every link at the
sum's unit reads that unit at every coefficient, a plaquette at the
window's boundary holding a link of one plaquette, its coefficient
that link's read, the withdrawn window a window and the descent
closing at the count. At three directions or beyond the
\emph{cubes' boundaries} $N$ are the plaquette-cube list at the
faces' signs, per cube one sign at each of its six faces, the signs
those at which the six boundary words fold to the sum's unit at
every link, each link of a cube on two of its faces and the two
faces' signs at the link's two traversals joining to that unit,
one sign family per cube at the sign one at the face at the cube's
corner in the cube's two lower directions, so
$K^{\mathsf T}N$ reads the sum's unit entrywise; and a plaquette
combination pairing every link at the sum's unit is a combination
of the cubes' boundaries by the descent in the last direction: its
read at a top face, a plaquette at the last position whose cube is
one, withdraws at that cube's boundary's multiple, and a top link,
a link at the last position in an earlier direction, then sits on
one occupied plaquette, the face below it in the link's plane with
the last direction, whose coefficient the link's pairing reads at
the sum's unit, so the combination sits on the window one position
shorter, the descent closing at the plane window at the two
directions' read. The \emph{kernel list} $N_0$ is the cubes'
boundaries' collection (Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}, one member joined
per refusal along the cubes in the corners' order), vacant at two
directions, spanning the kernel with its Gram $N_0^{\mathsf T}N_0$
positive definite at the independence, its count the kernel
dimension, the descent's kernel list and the collection two
independent lists inside one span (Definition~\ref{def:elim};
Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}), and the \emph{range projector} is
\[
\Pi\;:=\;1-N_0\,\big(N_0^{\mathsf T}N_0\big)^{-1}N_0^{\mathsf T}\ ,
\]
the solve the adjugate against the determinant
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}), one value at every spanning list of the
kernel, the projector onto the range at the kernel's own span, the
identity at two directions,
symmetric at the solve's symmetry and idempotent at the solve's
identity, with $\Delta\,\Pi=\Pi\,\Delta=\Delta$ at $\Delta N_0$ the
sum's unit, $\Pi$'s diagonal a self-pairing at or below one, and
a vector's \emph{range part} $\Pi\,u$ against its \emph{kernel
part}; the \emph{shifted Gram} $\Delta+N_0N_0^{\mathsf T}$ is
positive definite, its form the Gram's joined to the kernel list's
pairings' squares, the sum's unit at a vector in the kernel
perpendicular to the kernel list, the unit vector alone, and the
\emph{range solve} at a range vector $u$ is
$\Delta^{-1}u:=(\Delta+N_0N_0^{\mathsf T})^{-1}u$, the adjugate
against the determinant: the solve's kernel part reads the sum's
unit (the kernel list's Gram against it at that unit, the Gram
definite), so $\Delta\,\Delta^{-1}u=u$ and
$\Pi\,\Delta^{-1}u=\Delta^{-1}u$.

\emph{The roots' bracket.} Every root of the Gram sits at or below
$8g$, $\Delta\preceq8g$: each link's fold's square sits at or below
its plaquette count $2g$ against the plaquettes' squares
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}'s Cauchy--Schwarz), and the fold
collects each plaquette's square at its four links. And every root
off the sum's unit sits at or beyond $[\,2:L^{2}\,]$, the
\emph{Poincar\'e read} $[\,2:L^{2}\,]\,\Pi\preceq\Delta$, at the
\emph{Hodge fold}: the Gram joined to the cubes' boundaries' Gram,
$\Delta+NN^{\mathsf T}$, reads plane type by plane type, on the
plaquettes of one plane at their corners' coordinates, the two
in-plane \emph{Dirichlet folds} joined to the \emph{Neumann folds}
in the further directions, a Dirichlet fold the consecutive
differences' squares' fold along the plane direction at the sum's
unit beyond both ends, the list $2$ on the diagonal with the
balance partner of one at consecutive keys, and a Neumann fold the
consecutive differences' squares' fold along a further direction,
$2$ on the interior diagonal, one at the two end keys and the
balance partner of one at consecutive keys; the identity reads
entry by entry: at one plaquette the diagonal $4$ joined to the
count of cubes holding it, two per further direction less one at
an end position; at two plaquettes of one plane at consecutive
positions in a plane direction the shared link's exchanged
traversals, the balance partner of one, with the cubes' Gram at the
sum's unit there, the two off every common cube, a cube's two
faces of one plane type sitting opposite; at two plaquettes of one
plane type at consecutive positions in a further direction the
incidence at the sum's unit, the two holding distinct links, and
the cube between them at its two opposite faces'
signs, the balance partner of one at the faces' words running the
one way; and at two plaquettes of distinct plane types sharing a
link, the pair in one cube alone, the cube at the shared link's
corner in the two planes, the incidence's read $K_{p\ell}K_{q\ell}$
against the cube's two faces' signs' product, the two joining to
the sum's unit at the faces' signs' read $N_{pc}K_{p\ell}+N_{qc}K_{q\ell}$
at that unit; and the sum's unit at every further pair, a pair off
a shared link and off a common cube, the Gram and the cubes' Gram
both reading the unit there: two plaquettes sharing a link are of
one plane type at consecutive positions in a plane direction or of
distinct plane types in the cube at the shared link's corner, and a
cube's two faces of one plane type sit opposite at consecutive
positions in the further direction while its faces of distinct
plane types share a link, so every pair sits in one class above. So
at a range member $W$, the cubes' boundaries
pairing it at the sum's unit, the Gram's form is the Hodge fold's,
the Neumann folds' read at or beyond the sum's unit by their shape,
and the Dirichlet folds telescope: along one plane direction a
plaquette's read is the differences' fold from the end, its square
at or below the side against the differences' squares
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}'s Cauchy--Schwarz at the count), so
the self-pairing sits at or below the side's square against either
direction's differences' fold and at or below half the side's square
against the two folds' join, $W^{\mathsf T}W\le[\,L^{2}:2\,]\,W^{\mathsf T}\Delta W$.
The identity is one mechanism at every cell degree: the $k$-cells'
Gram joined to the $(k{+}1)$-cells' boundaries' Gram reads, cell
type by cell type, $k$ Dirichlet folds in the cell's directions
joined to Neumann folds in the further directions, the four entry
classes above at a cell in place of a plaquette and its faces in
place of its links; at $k=2$ it is the display above, and at $k=3$
the cubes' Gram $N^{\mathsf T}N$ joined to the four-cells'
boundaries' Gram $N_4N_4^{\mathsf T}$, a \emph{four-cell} four
directions in order with a corner whose four coordinates sit below
the side, its eight cubes the cubes at the corner in each three of
its directions and at the corner stepped along the fourth, and
$N_4$ the cube-cell list at the signs at which each four-cell's
eight cubes' boundaries fold to the sum's unit, one sign family per
four-cell at the sign one at the cube at the four-cell's corner in
the four-cell's three lower directions, each plaquette of a
four-cell a face of two of its eight cubes with the two cubes' signs
at the plaquette's two face signs joining to that unit, so
$N\,N_4$ reads the sum's unit entrywise, and at three directions or
beyond, at the \emph{cubes' range projector}
$\Pi_3$, the projector off the four-cells' boundaries' collection
and the identity at three directions, a cube chain in the cubes' range has its self-pairing
at or below a third of the side's square against its Gram read,
$[\,3:L^{2}\,]\,\Pi_3\preceq N^{\mathsf T}N$.

\emph{The tower and the modes' kernel.} The Gram splits over its
located roots $e_K$ with a unit congruence to diagonal
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}; the roots located and separated at
Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}), the roots off the sum's unit inside
the bracket above, and the \emph{blocks} $\Pi_K$, one per distinct
occupied root, are the interpolant polynomials in $\Delta$ through

\[
w_K^{2}\;2\kappa_\Sigma\,e_K\;=\;1
\]
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stagesplit}'s quadratic extension at the located

\mathsf S\;:=\;\sum_Kw_K\,\Pi_K\ ,

a matrix over the tower, symmetric, $\mathsf S\,\Pi=\Pi\,\mathsf S=\mathsf S$,
with the \emph{kernel identity}

\mathsf S\,\Delta\,\mathsf S\;=\;[\,1:2\kappa_\Sigma\,]\,\Pi
\]
at the blocks' reads and the adjoined relation, its form at or

\emph{diagonal}, the \emph{kernel's diagonal} per plaquette,
\[
D_p\;:=\;(\Delta\mathsf S)_{pp}\;=\;\sum_K[\,1:2\kappa_\Sigma w_K\,]\,(\Pi_K)_{pp}\ ,
\]
a tower element between the sum's unit and $D_+:=2g$, each block's
diagonal a self-pairing, the blocks' diagonals folding to $\Pi$'s
at or below one, and
$[\,1:2\kappa_\Sigma w_K\,]^{2}=[\,e_K:2\kappa_\Sigma\,]\le[\,4g:\kappa_\Sigma\,]\le D_+^{2}$
at every root at or below $8g$; its \emph{corner fold}

the boundary's fold a part of the links';
and at a pair $\varepsilon$ at or below one the \emph{shifted
kernel's solve} on the range is
\[
(\mathsf S+\varepsilon)^{-1}\;:=\;\sum_K[\,1:w_K+\varepsilon\,]\,\Pi_K\ ,
\qquad

\]
its diagonal at or below $W_0:=1+8\,\kappa_\Sigma\,g$ (every root at
or below $8g$ reads $[\,1:w_K\,]^{2}=2\kappa_\Sigma e_K\le16\,\kappa_\Sigma g$,
and a pair sits at or below the successor of its square's half),
and at a range vector $u$ the \emph{dual weights} over the links
\[
c^{(u)}\;:=\;K^{\mathsf T}\,\Delta^{-1}\,(\mathsf S+\varepsilon)^{-1}u\ ,
\]
at the two identities $K\,c^{(u)}=(\mathsf S+\varepsilon)^{-1}u$
(the Gram against the range solve the range vector itself) and
$\sum_\ell c^{(u)}_\ell\,(K^{\mathsf T}u')_\ell=u'^{\mathsf T}(\mathsf S+\varepsilon)^{-1}u$
at a further range vector $u'$, and the fold
$|c^{(u)}|_2^{\,2}=u^{\mathsf T}(\mathsf S+\varepsilon)^{-1}\Delta^{-1}(\mathsf S+\varepsilon)^{-1}u\le2\kappa_\Sigma\,|u|^{2}$
($\Delta^{-1}=2\kappa_\Sigma\,\mathsf S^{2}$ on the range at the
adjoined relation, and $\mathsf S$ against $\mathsf S+\varepsilon$
at or below one block by block), so
$|c^{(u)}|_1^{\,2}\le\#\ell\,2\kappa_\Sigma\,|u|^{2}$ and the fold

unit range vector and at or below $C_1\,|u|^{2}$ at $|u|^{2}$ at or
beyond one (a value at or below the successor of its square, halved).

\emph{The profile.} The \emph{profile} $W$ sits on the plaquettes
of the first two directions' plane at every position of the further
directions, $W_p:=w_x\,w_y$ at the plane coordinates $(x,y)$ of the
plaquette's corner, $1\le x,y\le L$, and $w_b:=b\,(L+1+b^{\vee})$

the plaquette at the corner $(x,y)$ forward at its base link and
the plaquette at the corner $(x,y-1)$ backward at its lower
direction's link at the corner moved one step in the higher
direction, each occupied exactly where its corner's coordinates sit
at or below $L$ and the parabola at the sum's unit at the ends

$(x,y)$, $1\le y\le L$ and $1\le x\le L+1$, the value
$w_y\,\langle w_{x-1}\!:\!w_x\rangle$, the plaquette at the corner
$(x-1,y)$ forward at its higher direction's link at the corner moved
one step in the lower direction and the plaquette at the corner
$(x,y)$ backward at its higher direction's link at the corner; and
the sum's unit at a link of a further direction; so at the
$(L+1)^{g-1}$ positions of the further directions the Gram read and
the self-pairing are
$W^{\mathsf T}\Delta W=2\,(L+1)^{g-1}\sum_{b=1}^{L}w_b^{2}
\sum_{b=0}^{L}\langle w_{b+1}\!:\!w_b\rangle^{2}$ and
$W^{\mathsf T}W=(L+1)^{g-1}\big(\sum_{b=1}^{L}w_b^{2}\big)^{2}$; it
sits in the range at three directions or beyond, a
cube's two faces in the plane reading one value at the exchanged
signs and its further faces off the support, so the cubes'
boundaries pair it at the sum's unit. Its Gram read against its
self-pairing is the two directions' consecutive differences' folds
at two closed sums,
\[
30\sum_{b=1}^{L}w_b^{2}\;=\;L\,(L+1)(L+2)\,(L^{2}+2L+2)\ ,
\qquad
3\sum_{b=0}^{L}\big\langle w_{b+1}\!:\!w_b\big\rangle^{2}
\;=\;L\,(L+1)(L+2)\ ,
\]
so $W^{\mathsf T}\Delta W=e_W\,W^{\mathsf T}W$ at the \emph{mode

$\sigma_W:=W^{\mathsf T}(\mathsf S+\varepsilon)^{-1}W$, between

roots' floor and the diagonal's cap, with the \emph{profile's

$|\omega|^{2}\le W_0^{2}\,|W|^{2}$.

\emph{The fluxes.} The \emph{moved flux} of a plaquette is its base

\[
f_p\;:=\;R_{0\leftarrow p}\,\nabla\chi_p\ ,
\]

\]

squares} are the generator actions joined to the balance partners

\[

\]
over the links and the generator list, a fold of squares

\emph{The loops.} At a plaquette $p$ and a boundary link $\ell$ the

\emph{The off-range fold.} The moved fluxes' \emph{off-range fold}

+[\,L^{2}:3\,]\,|N^{\mathsf T}f|^{2}$, reads
$|(1-\Pi)f|^{2}\le[\,L^{2}:3\,]\sum_c|\langle\partial c,f\rangle|^{2}
\le[\,L^{2}:2\,]\sum_c|\langle\partial c,f\rangle|^{2}$
over the cubes. A face's flux reads at the joined block
(Lemma~\ref{lem:loopcap}): the character's gradient is the joined

$\langle\partial c,f\rangle_a=\tr\big(X^{R}_a\,M_c\big)$ at
$M_c:=\sum_{q\in\partial c}s_q\,E^{0}_q$, $E^{0}_q$ the face's gap

\]
The root-moved gap differs from the corner-moved one at the

$\delta_{L_q}\le g\,L\sum_{q'\in R(L_q)}\delta_{q'}$ (the joined

the difference's fold of squares sits at or below
$3\,|E'_q|^{2}\,|G_q|^{2}\,(2+|G_q|^{2})$ (the three-member fold of

below $24\,(1+2\,d_L)\,\delta_q\,\delta_{L_q}$. The two-member fold
of squares doubles, $|M_c|^{2}\le2\,|\sum_qs_qE'_q|^{2}+2\cdot6\sum_q|E^{0}_q-E'_q|^{2}$,
and over the cubes each plaquette is a face of at most $2\,(g-1)$
