\begin{lemma}[The moment folds]\label{lem:momentfold}
On a depth chain's head at the dual representative
(Construction~\ref{con:depthchain}), at the ground's block
recurrence $B_{m}^{\mathsf T}\psi_{m}+B_{m+1}\psi_{m+2}=A_{m+1}\psi_{m+1}$
(the eigen-identity's row read at the shells' blocks, the diagonal
block at the ground root cross-added, Lemma~\ref{lem:greenprod}(iii)'s
row read), its scalar spelling
$b_{m}\psi_{m}+b_{m+1}\psi_{m+2}=A_{m+1}\psi_{m+1}$ at single-label
shells, the ground enters every datum read through two
moment streams,
\[
\rho[P]\;:=\;\sum_m \psi_m^{2}\,P(m)\ ,
\qquad
c[P]\;:=\;\sum_m \psi_m\,\psi_{m+1}\,P(m)\ ,
\]
$P$ over the polynomial weights, and the streams solve the
recurrence's own folds, exact at every scale:

\emph{(i) The fold identities.} The recurrence folded against
the middle member's $\psi_{m+1}P(m{+}1)$ reads
\[
c\big[\,b\,P\,\big]+c\big[\,b\,P^{+}\,\big]
\;=\;\rho\big[\,A\,P\,\big]
\qquad(P^{+}(m):=P(m{+}1))\ ,
\]
and folded against $\psi_{m+2}P(m{+}1)$ a second identity of
the recurrence at the
shifted weights, its second-bond term reduced by one further fold
of the recurrence: every correlator beyond the two streams
re-enters them, so the family closes on $\rho$ and $c$ alone, one
identity per weight, each a display of the recurrence at a
polynomial weight.

\emph{(ii) The graded system, and its clearance.} At the corner
the weights read in the pair coordinates ($u=m\eta$,
$s=m^{2}\eta$): the bond reads the border rows' one repeated
datum (Lemma~\ref{lem:grading}), the folds' bond weights
collecting at that datum's factor, and the diagonal $A_m$ reads
$\sigma E_m$ at weight-degree two, so each fold relates the
streams' degree-$k$ reads to degree-$(k{+}2)$ at one scale
factor, the second fold's reduction withdrawing its top weight to
the reads at or below the weight's degree's successor with the
boundary square $\psi_0^{\,2}$, the down-shift's read at the
vacant head key. The identities at weights through a stated
degree, with the base reads, the unit read $\rho[1]$ at the gram,
the depth read $\rho[m]$ and the bond read $c[1]$, each a
single-region read of clause (v), and the boundary square, are
one square linear system for the truncated moment vector, the two
streams' reads through the stated degree with the boundary
square, over the located stage, its entries polynomial in the
scale and the rates at the eigenvalue's bracket (the
certificate's two lines, Lemma~\ref{lem:cornerpivot}(vi)), the
far edge's reads, the weights' reads at the head's last key
against its square, $(n{-}1)^{t}\,\psi_{n-1}^{\,2}$ at the head's
depth count $n$, entering the rows at clause (iii)'s priced tail
weight: the solve is the elimination's
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}), and the system's determinant
clearance is one located divisor read over the corner base
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}), the validity cell the certificate's
architecture.

\emph{(iii) The truncation cap.} Beyond the stated degree the
streams' tails read in the dominance region, where the ground's
components ride the transfer factors
(Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(ii)): the beyond-degree weight is
priced by the certificates' geometric caps against the transfer
factors' cap, one comparison at the stated degree, the degree held at its
statement, every compared datum a gram weight or a weighted square
at or beyond the sum's unit, the pairings' own side
(Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(ii)).

\emph{(iv) The scale comparison.} Two scales' systems share their
shape, the coefficients differing by displayed polynomial reads
of the scale and the base reads within the scale sandwich's
priced widths (Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(vii)), so on the
clearance cell the two moment vectors differ by the elimination's
cofactor reads at those differences, one width per moment, and
the widths take the scale factor: the streams' reads close across
the scales on the clearance cell.

\emph{(v) The datum assembly.} A single-region datum read is a
stream read at banded weights, the band its support's reach
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries}): a width-one datum reads the
square stream at its diagonal weights with the doubled bond stream
at its bond weights (Lemma~\ref{lem:greenprod}(iv)), and a wider
band's read re-enters the two streams by (i)'s folds; so its scale
closure is (iv)'s on the clearance cell; separated and
Euclidean data assemble from single-region reads at the crossing
certificates (Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(iv)--(vi)), the
certificates cell data (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}), so the
assembled reads close where the parts do. The block chains read
the streams at block weights through the folds of their own
recurrence, Lemma~\ref{lem:greenprod}(iii)'s row read.

\emph{(vi) The height reads at two lines.} On a window with
simple ground the height
reads at two lines, one count per line: at a \emph{floor line} under
which the window's pencil is positive semidefinite the ground sits
at or beyond the line, and at a \emph{cap line} with the window's
count at or beyond two below it the window's second root sits at or below the
line (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}'s count read), so the height sits at or
below the lines' gap against the scale; the floor is a
positive-semidefinite certificate of the window's pencil above the
line, a fold of squares at generator actions joined to coefficient
multiplications (Construction~\ref{con:coeff}), and the cap the
two-by-two block read at two stated members perpendicular in the
gram (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}'s block reads), the window's count at
or beyond two at every line beyond the floor line by the members'
diagonal reads' sum against the gram, the two-by-two compression's
count two at or below it; the certificate's data and the members' reads are polynomial
pairs in the scale and the side, their comparisons' validity
divisors located over the scale and the side
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}). At a fixed region, suppose the
floor line holds on every cutoff from a stated key, and the
two members have finite content supports in that region.
From the larger of that key and their two contents onward,
their forms and Gram are their original reads. At simple
grounds on this tail the lines' gap therefore caps the
regional height, and hence the global height
(Definition~\ref{def:K}).
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i)} The recurrence at the middle member $m+1$ multiplied by
$\psi_{m+1}P(m{+}1)$ and summed over $m$ reads $c[bP^{+}]$ at the
first bond, $c[bP]$ at the second at the index shifted, and
$\rho[AP]$ on the right, the display; multiplied by
$\psi_{m+2}P(m{+}1)$ and summed it reads the first bond at the
second-bond correlator $\sum_mb_m\psi_m\psi_{m+2}P(m{+}1)$, the
second at $\rho$ at the shifted bond weight and the right side at
$c[AP]$, and the row read once more,
$b_{m+1}\psi_m\psi_{m+2}+b_m\psi_m^{2}=A_{m+1}\psi_m\psi_{m+1}$,
returns the second-bond correlator to the two streams. A
commutator's ground read is of equal members outright, a
commutator of two symmetric operators' pairing at a ground
reading equal members, the folds the streams' two reads.
\emph{(vi)} Write $g_x,g_y>0$ for the two perpendicular
members' Gram entries and $a,d,c$ for their two diagonal
entries and cross entry in the form above the floor line.
That form's positive split gives $c^2\le ad$
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}'s squared Cauchy--Schwarz).
At $\lambda>[\,a:g_x\,]+[\,d:g_y\,]$, both entries
$a-\lambda g_x,d-\lambda g_y$ sit on their lower sides and
\[
(\lambda g_x-a)(\lambda g_y-d)-c^2
=\lambda(g_xg_y\lambda-g_ya-g_xd)+ad-c^2>0.
\]
Thus the compression has count two, and the full count
is at least two (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). With the ground
simple and at or beyond the floor line, the gap is at
most $\lambda$. The two members' least contents give
their inclusion at every larger cutoff
(Proposition~\ref{prop:leastwindow}), with their pairings
and pencil forms fixed at that inclusion
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries}). The floor read holds on
the stated tail, so the cap does as well; the regional
upper-cap read of Definition~\ref{def:K} gives the last clause.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The cone read]\label{lem:cone}
The jump family's momentum structure at the corner is isotropic at
degree two: on the decimation's validity cells the decimated determinant's
root locus is the fiber symbol's own, one Schur factor at a
complement of unequal-membered determinant
(Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(i)); the fiber
symbol's coefficients are permutation-invariant polynomials of the
chord list at every coupling of the approach
(Theorem~\ref{thm:restoration}, at Lemma~\ref{lem:corner}'s base),
their momentum reading even in each coordinate at the deck
relation's exchanged roots (Definition~\ref{def:deck};
Theorem~\ref{thm:restoration});
the degree-two invariants at that evenness are the standard
square's span
(Theorem~\ref{thm:restoration}, degree $2$ at the rings'
coincidence);
and the direction data enter at degree four, the breaking
multiplicities positive there. So the jump family's loci at the
corner read the isotropic square at degree two with one located
coefficient per root: the symbol's momentum reading is $S_0(k)$ at
the unit monomial with $S_2(k)$ against the isotropic square $Q$
at degree two, the odd degrees at the sum's unit and the direction
data at degree four; at a located root $\varepsilon$ of $S_0$,
simple at Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}'s separation, the locus at
the moved level $\varepsilon+a\,Q$ reads the symbol's degree-two
term as $S_0'(\varepsilon)\,a+S_2(\varepsilon)$ against $Q$, and
the coefficient is $\bar a$ over the clearing $c$ at the
derivative's unit witness $u\,S_0'+v\,S=c$ cleared
at the extension's monic $S$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}), $\bar a$ the
balance partner of $S_2\,u$ reduced at $S$, one stage element per
root; and the direction reads two momentum degrees down.
\begin{proof}
At a level off the designated pivot's root the cleared deflation's
determinant is the pencil's own at one Schur factor
(Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(i); Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}'s
determinant split), so the decimated determinant's root locus on
the validity cells is the symbol's. The symbol's coefficients are
one value at every relabeling of the chord list and even in each
coordinate (Theorem~\ref{thm:restoration}), so its momentum
reading holds the isotropic square alone at degree two, the sum's
unit at the odd degrees and the direction data from degree four
(Theorem~\ref{thm:restoration}'s degree reads). At the moved level
$\varepsilon+a\,Q$ the symbol reads
$S_0(\varepsilon+aQ)+S_2(\varepsilon+aQ)\,Q$ through degree two,
and the binomial identity per occupied key
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}) reads $S_0(\varepsilon+aQ)$ as
$S_0(\varepsilon)+S_0'(\varepsilon)\,aQ$ with $Q$'s square two
degrees beyond, $S_0(\varepsilon)$ of equal members at the root, so
the degree-two term is $S_0'(\varepsilon)\,a+S_2(\varepsilon)$
against $Q$, the locus its equal members. At the root simple at
the separation the unit witness $u\,S_0'+v\,S=c$ reads
$u(\varepsilon)\,S_0'(\varepsilon)=c$, $S(\varepsilon)$ of equal
members (Lemma~\ref{lem:stage}), so at $\bar a$ the balance partner
of $S_2\,u$ reduced at $S$ the read
$\bar a\,S_0'(\varepsilon)+c\,S_2(\varepsilon)$ is
$S_2(\varepsilon)\,u(\varepsilon)\,S_0'(\varepsilon)$ against
itself, equal members: the coefficient is $\bar a$ over $c$.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The free cell]\label{lem:freecell}
The pencil at the $\alpha{=}1$ representative, the pair
$(E\!:\!\tau^2M)$'s site datum $H([\,1:\tau^2\,])$, is affine in
$\tau^2$, and on a fiber head (Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}) its entries
are one polynomial-pair list in $(t,\tau)$ over the residue beyond
the locality band
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}; Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries}), the window
entering through its sampled momenta and its separation range alone,
the residue a further coordinate beyond the reach bound
(Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(iii); Lemma~\ref{lem:serstable}(iii)
at the further series): every count near the free end is
Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}'s cell function over $(t,\tau,r)$ with
located divisors, and the \emph{free cell} is the free end's, its
$\tau$-extent the divisor's first positive root, an output, the
contact cell's construction at this end (Lemma~\ref{lem:contactcell}).
At each window and coupling the ground is the least located root
$\varepsilon_0$ of its pencil (Definition~\ref{def:pencil};
Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), and the certificate's fixed data are
positive offsets $\ell<h$, common to every region and cutoff
on the stated root-coordinate segment. Its two count reads are
\[
\operatorname{rev}\big(H:(\varepsilon_0+\ell)G\big)
=\operatorname{rev}\big(H:(\varepsilon_0+h)G\big)=1\ .
\]
The level gap reads these counts at $\ell$ and $h$, and the
absolute lines read the ground at that window and coupling.
The polynomial displays include a ground coordinate $e$:
the site data at $H=(e+\ell)G+S_\ell$ and
$H=(e+h)G+S_h$ are polynomial in $e$ and the base coordinates,
and their counts enter at $e=\varepsilon_0$, the least root's
designation. The cell's boundary families are
the decimation's divisor list at the $\alpha{=}1$ representative
(Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}): the jump family, the pencil
determinant's roots at the two ground-translated lines, the
validity families of the stated pivot certificates, with the
dominance family at a dominance certificate, the deck
family with the spectator caps' three counts each
a cell datum (Lemma~\ref{lem:spectator}(iii)), and the tension
family of the charged sectors (Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}(iii),(iv));
the two total counts give ground multiplicity one, with the
ground below the lower line and every further level at or
beyond the upper line.
The free cell's \emph{certificate} is the flat window at the fixed
pair of offsets, the ground-relative level read's pair, read
outright at the free end
(Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend}) with the counts at the two lines cell
functions (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}). At every region, every
cutoff and every root-coordinate pair of the cell, its record
reads these two counts at that cutoff's ground designation.
The floor satisfies $\ell+E_0\kappa_1\le h$.
At the specialization $\gamma=E_0\kappa_1$,
$\ell=\gamma$, $h=2\gamma$, a cutoff $C$ with the positive comparison
\[
\gamma C>\gamma W+\gamma^2+W^2,
\qquad W=\tau^2\#p\,d_L,
\]
and the upper count give the cutoff-tail
certificate of Theorem~\ref{thm:truncation}; the lower count
is its head's count at $e_C+\gamma$, one by monotonicity
and the ground below that line. The floor and extent are
located outputs per member and direction count
(Construction~\ref{con:lattice}'s direction reads): the
\emph{extent} $\tau_1$, the first positive member in the root
coordinate of the families' root list, the members' root lists
joined, over the band, the chords at $t^{2}$ below $4$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}), at its leading-term radius in the residue
(Theorem~\ref{thm:windowsep}; Lemma~\ref{lem:rankstable}(iii);
Lemma~\ref{lem:serstable}(iii)), the cutoff and its ground
designation among each window record's data, with its sampled
momenta and the spectator brackets read at that record, the deck
family's cell data (Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(iii);
Lemma~\ref{lem:spectator}(iii)). A finite chained cover reads
the two total counts at every point of its stated segment:
each piece has its own pivot witnesses, and at a shared
endpoint the two pieces read the original pencil's counts
(Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}; Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}).
The validity comparisons are the fields of those witnesses
on their pieces.

\emph{The scalar dominance instance.} At positive data
$\Lambda_h,d_L,p_v,f_*$, a row-cap record at
matrices $E,M$ and stated tower places reads
\[
\Lambda_h\le c_i,\qquad
f_*m_i\le 2d_Lp_vc_i,\qquad
c_i:=E_{ii},\quad m_i:=\sum_{j\ne i}|M_{ij}|
\]
at every stated place, the full row fold at the matrix's
column list. Here $p_v$ is the per-vertex plaquette count
(Construction~\ref{con:lattice}). At a fixed upper level
$u<\Lambda_h$, its two comparison polynomials are
\[
d_0(\tau):=f_*\langle\Lambda_h:u\rangle
-2d_Lp_v\Lambda_h\tau^2,\qquad
d_1(\tau):=f_*-2d_Lp_v\tau^2.
\]
At a diagonal electric matrix, the unit Gram, a level
$z\le u$ and the displayed cap
read, the row gap has the comparison
\[
f_*(c_i-z-\tau^2M_{ii}-\tau^2m_i)
\ge d_1(\tau)(c_i-\Lambda_h)+d_0(\tau)-\tau^2f_*M_{ii}.
\]
Where the right member is positive at every stated row,
it gives a positive dominance pivot at those places.
At $M_{ii}\le0$ this holds at $d_0(\tau)>0$ and
$d_1(\tau)\ge0$. At the ground-translated
line, $u=h$ gives $e+h\le u$ at $e\le0$
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}). Each displayed polynomial
has one positive root, its constant and quadratic coefficient
at opposite sides with positive margins. This instance's
root list is occupied, and its first positive member is a
located read of that record. A certificate's count
covers verify its actual pencil and Gram on the stated range.
The cell's $t$-section at the
extent is the whole band exactly where the list's $t$-roots sit off
it, itself a located read.

\emph{The free end is interior to its cell.} At the free end the
pencil is its electric member $E$,
diagonal at the free reads: the decimated symbol's jumps are the occupied
contents and the level is the member floor label's loop read, one
diagonal computation at every window (Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend}); the
free end sits inside its cell
with its counts the cell's, direct reads; at a level on the content
list, Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}'s boundary clause extends the
positive-semidefinite cells into the closed endpoint. The free-end reading of
Definition~\ref{def:K} is those reads.

\emph{The first creation threshold.} Let $e_L$ be the least of
$4\hat c_2(\lambda)$ over $\lambda\in\bar L$, the trichotomy
fold over the magnetic closure (Definition~\ref{def:ground};
Construction~\ref{con:fusion}). At every member and direction
count, every region and every total-content cutoff
$C<E_0+e_L$, the window cut admits every positive pair $\kappa$
at the read
\[
\nu d_L\tau^2+f_*\kappa\le f_*,
\qquad f_*:=\hat c_2(f_0),\qquad E_0=4f_*.
\]
The threshold reads $2E_0$ where the magnetic closure holds a
floor label. Here $\nu$ is the per-link plaquette count of
Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}. At the window's ground
$\varepsilon_0$ the two counts are
\[
\operatorname{rev}(H:E_0\kappa G)
=\operatorname{rev}\big(H:(\varepsilon_0+E_0\kappa)G\big)=1.
\]
At the residue one and the member's stated magnetic list
$\{f\}$, the window cut also holds throughout
$C<3E_0$, at every region and direction count, at
\[
3\nu d_L\tau^2+2f_*\kappa\le2f_*.
\]
The corresponding ground-translated count is one.

At residue one, list $\{f\}$ and cutoff $C=E_0=:c$,
the whole window at a region of $N$ plaquettes has forms
\[
G=I,\qquad
H=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\tau^2\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\\
-\tau^2\mathbf1&cI_N\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For $N\ge1$ and $\tau>0$, its least root is
$-\rho_N$ at the positive located datum
\[
\rho_N(c+\rho_N)=N\tau^4.
\]
The further roots are $c$ at multiplicity $N-1$ and
$c+\rho_N$ once. Thus the cut admits one at every
root-coordinate pair. At two directions the display holds also
on the odd tori of Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}: the unit joint chord fiber has
roots $-\rho_N,c+\rho_N$, and every further occupied fiber
reads $c$ at its order. The ground-relative distances are
$c+2\rho_N$ and $c+\rho_N$, respectively.

\emph{The creator range and its complementary count.}
At every member and magnetic closure, fix a region and
total-content cutoff $C$. Let $\mathcal R_C$ be the span
of the images of the admitted maps $\mathcal C_i$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}, each at its input selection
$c+e_i\le C$. Its orthogonal complement is
\[
\mathcal N_C:=\bigcap_i\ker\mathcal C_i^\dagger,
\qquad
\mathcal N_C^+:=\mathcal N_C\cap\mathbf1^\perp.
\]
The unit line sits in $\mathcal N_C$, and the window splits
orthogonally as
\[
\mathcal W_C\perp\mathcal N_C^+,
\qquad \mathcal W_C:=\mathbb P\mathbf1\perp\mathcal R_C.
\]
The list of $\mathcal W_C$ starts at the unit, followed
by the creator images' collection, run per electric
content. The list of $\mathcal N_C^+$ is the collection
of the occupied window list's residuals off those images,
per content (Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}); the Grams are
the lists' actual pairings. Let $W,Z$ be the two lists'
columns in the output window list. Their forms are the
restrictions of Definition~\ref{def:pencil}, in particular
\[
G_N=Z^{\mathsf T}GZ,\qquad
E_N=Z^{\mathsf T}EZ,\qquad
R_N=Z^{\mathsf T}G\mathsf R_\Pi Z,\qquad
H_N=E_N-\tau^2R_N.
\]
At a located line $z$, a pair $\xi$ and a positive
datum $\omega$ of $z$'s stage at
\[
\nu d_L\tau^2+\xi=f_*,
\qquad f_*z+\omega=\xi E_0,
\]
its site datum $S_N(z):=H_N-zG_N$ has the positive fold
\[
f_*S_N(z)
=\tau^2(\nu d_LE_N-f_*R_N)
+\xi(E_N-E_0G_N)+\omega G_N\succ0.
\]
At $B:=W^{\mathsf T}HZ$, the form at the combined list is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}W&Z\end{pmatrix}^{\mathsf T}
(H-zG)\begin{pmatrix}W&Z\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
H_W-zG_W&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&S_N(z)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The count is
\[
\operatorname{rev}(H:zG)
=\operatorname{rev}\big(H_W-zG_W-BX\big),
\qquad S_N(z)X=B^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The unit row of $B$ reads the sum's unit, so the deflation
fixes the unit row of $H_W-zG_W$. At a vacant
$\mathcal N_C^+$ the count reads on $\mathcal W_C$ directly.

At an occupied magnetic closure and a pair $h<E_0$, this
complementary pivot has one common validity divisor,
\[
d_h(\tau):=
f_*\langle E_0:h\rangle-\nu d_LE_0\tau^2.
\]
It has exactly one positive located root $\tau_N$,
\[
\nu d_LE_0\tau_N^2=f_*\langle E_0:h\rangle.
\]
At every root-coordinate pair $\tau<\tau_N$, every
region and every cutoff,
the complementary count holds at $z=e+h$, where $e$
is that window's ground. The divisor and its root
depend on the member, direction count, closure dimension
fold $d_L$ and offset.

\emph{The translated line on its upper side.} Let $e^+$
be the largest $4\hat c_2(\lambda)$ over the occupied
magnetic closure, the trichotomy fold over that list.
At $\tau<\tau_N$ and
\[
d_h(\tau)^2\ge
4f_*\nu E_0h(h+e^+),
\]
every window whose ground satisfies $e+h\ge0$ reads
\[
\operatorname{rev}\big(H:(e+h)G\big)=1.
\]
This holds at every total-content cutoff and every
region, the comparison's data the member, direction
count, closure folds $d_L,e^+$, offset and root-coordinate pair.

\emph{The ground-side root.} At the complementary data,
write $\delta:=d_h(\tau)$, $c_\rho:=4f_*\nu E_0$, and let
$a_\rho,b_\rho$ be the positive gaps at
\[
a_\rho+f_*^2=c_\rho,\qquad
b_\rho+2f_*\delta=c_\rho e^+.
\]
At the positive quadratic root $q_\rho$ and its read
\[
q_\rho^2=b_\rho^2+4a_\rho\delta^2,\qquad
\rho_*:=[\,2\delta^2:b_\rho+q_\rho\,],
\]
one has $a_\rho\rho_*^2+b_\rho\rho_*=\delta^2$.
At every region and cutoff whose ground reads
$e^\vee\le\rho_*$, the count is
\[
\operatorname{rev}\big(H:(e+h)G\big)=1.
\]
At $\delta^2\ge c_\rho h(h+e^+)$ the root satisfies
$\rho_*>h$, so this count includes the lines
$e+h<0$ at $h<e^\vee\le\rho_*$.
Under this comparison, at $e^\vee>\rho_*$,
the unit pivot at the line $e+h$ exceeds the positive
stage gap $\langle\rho_*:h\rangle$.

\emph{The comparisons' common segment.} At
$c_\rho:=4f_*\nu E_0$, define the positive data
\[
a_0+f_*^2=c_\rho,\qquad
b_0:=2f_*^2E_0+c_\rho e^+,\qquad
k_0:=f_*^2E_0^2,\qquad
h_0:=[\,k_0:2(b_0+a_0E_0)\,].
\]
Then $0<h_0<[\,E_0:4\,]$. Let $q_0$ be the positive
root at $q_0^2=c_\rho h_0(h_0+e^+)$, let $w_0$ be the
positive gap at
\[
q_0+w_0=f_*\langle E_0:h_0\rangle,
\]
and let $T_0$ be the positive root at
\[
\nu d_LE_0T_0^2=w_0.
\]
At every root-coordinate pair $\tau\le T_0$, the
complementary comparison at $h=h_0$ reads
\[
d_{h_0}(\tau)\ge q_0>0,\qquad
d_{h_0}(\tau)^2\ge c_\rho h_0(h_0+e^+).
\]
The datum $h_0$ and these located roots depend on the member,
direction count and magnetic closure alone. The complementary
count and the translated-line counts above consequently hold
at these data on their stated cutoff and ground ranges.

\emph{The count on the input lists.} Let $\mathcal C$ be
the joined column list of the maps $\mathcal C_i$, with
domain the direct sum of their input windows, each in
its window list at Gram $G_i^-$, and let $\mathcal J$
be the joined list of the maps $\Pi[\mathsf M,C_i]\Pi_i^-$.
At the data of the complementary count, put
\[
\Gamma:=\mathcal C^{\mathsf T}G\mathcal C,\qquad
\Theta:=\mathcal C^{\mathsf T}G\mathcal J,\qquad
L_N:=Z^{\mathsf T}G\mathcal J,
\qquad S_N(z)Y_N=L_N,
\]
and let $\mathcal T_z$ be the direct sum of the input
actions $K_i^-+(e_i-z)I$. Let $\mathbf r$ be the column with one
at each input window's unit key and the sum's unit at
every further key. Then
\[
\operatorname{rev}(H:zG)
=\operatorname{rev}
\begin{pmatrix}
-z&-\tau^2\mathbf r^{\mathsf T}\\
-\tau^2\mathbf r&\Gamma\mathcal T_z-\tau^2\Theta-\tau^4L_N^{\mathsf T}Y_N
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The range block is symmetric at the identity
\[
\Gamma\mathcal T_z-\tau^2\Theta
=\mathcal C^{\mathsf T}(H-zG)\mathcal C
=\mathcal T_z^{\mathsf T}\Gamma-\tau^2\Theta^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The input directions in $\ker\mathcal C$ give a kernel
block of the displayed count. At $z=e+\gamma$, with $e$
the output ground and $0<\gamma<E_0$, each input action
has the positive-definite read
\[
K_i^-+(e_i-z)I
=(K_i^--eI)+(e_i-\gamma)I\succ0
\]
in its input pairing.

The Gram blocks read at two smaller input selections.
Let $\Pi_{ij}^-$ select the contents at
$c+e_i+e_j\le C$, and put
$\mathcal C_{j|i}:=C_j\Pi_{ij}^-$ with output in
$\Pi_i^-$, and $\mathcal C_{i|j}:=C_i\Pi_{ij}^-$ with
output in $\Pi_j^-$. On their input and output lists,
\[
\Gamma_{ij}
=G_i^-\big(
\mathcal C_{j|i}\mathcal C_{i|j}^\dagger
+\Pi_i^-[C_i^\dagger,C_j]\Pi_j^-
\big).
\]
At $C<e_i+e_j$ the first term reads the sum's unit.
At disjoint plaquette boundaries the commutator term
reads the sum's unit (Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}).

\emph{The parity elimination at residue one.} At the
magnetic list $\{f\}$, the configuration index of every
region and total-content cutoff has two grades, the unit in
the even grade and each
plaquette multiplication exchanging the grades. On their
lists the forms read
\[
G=G_+\oplus G_-,\qquad
H=\begin{pmatrix}E_+&-\tau^2 B\\-\tau^2 B^{\mathsf T}&E_-\end{pmatrix}.
\]
At every located line $z<E_0$, the odd block
$D_-:=E_--zG_-$ is positive definite and the count is
\[
\operatorname{rev}(H:zG)
=\operatorname{rev}\big(E_+-zG_+-\tau^4 BX\big),
\qquad D_-X=B^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The solve is blockwise on odd configurations: at content
$c_a$, its block is $(c_a-z)G_a$, the positive scalar
gap against the configuration Gram's adjugate solve
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}).
Write $D_-(z):=E_--zG_-$ and $X_z$ for that solve,
and put $F_z:=E_+-zG_+-\tau^4 BX_z$. At the ground
$e:=\varepsilon_0$ and a positive pair $\gamma$ with
$e+\gamma<E_0$, the two-line read is
\begin{gather*}
\operatorname{rev}\big(H:(e+\gamma)G\big)
=\operatorname{rev}(F_e:\gamma W_\gamma),\\
W_\gamma:=G_++\tau^4 BY_\gamma\succ0,
\qquad D_-(e+\gamma)Y_\gamma=G_-X_e.
\end{gather*}
The form $F_e$ is positive semidefinite, and its kernel
maps bijectively to the ground kernel by
$v\mapsto(v,\tau^2X_ev)$.
\begin{proof}
At a fixed window and a
level off the content list the cell's determinant reads unequal
members at the free end, the diagonal's entries off the level, so
the free end sits off the divisor and inside its cell, its counts
the cell's. The counts at the certificate's two ground-translated
lines are read at the ground's designation in the polynomial
displays with coordinate $e$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}). At the
free end the ground reads the sum's unit and the absolute lines
read the offsets (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), where
the pencil is its diagonal electric member (Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend})
and the ground alone sits below either line, so both counts read
one on the cell, the ground's multiplicity one over the cell
attached to the free end (Theorem~\ref{thm:SO};
Theorem~\ref{thm:divisorid}(iii)), and every further level sits
beyond the upper line.

For the scalar dominance record, subtracting the
displayed lower member from the row gap's $f_*$-multiple
gives the positive fold
\[
f_*(u-z)+\tau^2(2d_Lp_vc_i-f_*m_i)\ge0.
\]
The diagonal magnetic term enters both compared members
at $\tau^2f_*M_{ii}$'s balance partner. A positive
right member makes the actual row gap positive; the
dominance read of Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(ii)
then gives the positive pivot. The principal block's
off-row fold is a subfold of $m_i$, so its row gap
sits at or beyond the full row's. At $M_{ii}\le0$ the
diagonal term is on its upper side or at equal members,
and $c_i-\Lambda_h\ge0$ gives the stated instance.
The two polynomials have
positive constant margins at $u<\Lambda_h$ and
positive quadratic coefficients on the second member;
their positive roots are the quadratic extensions'
positive members (Lemma~\ref{lem:stagesplit}).
For a finite chained count cover, a point of the segment
belongs to a piece, whose split reads the original
pencil's total count by Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}'s
counted-pivot identity. At a shared endpoint either
piece reads that count. This gives the count on the
covered union (Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}).

For the cutoff read, project off the unit line to the occupied
index, with projection $\Pi_+$. Every occupied input has content
at least $E_0$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}), and each creation
$C_{p,\lambda}$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone} raises it by
$4\hat c_2(\lambda)\ge e_L$. Thus at $C<E_0+e_L$ its
occupied-to-occupied compression is the sum's unit, and its
adjoint's is as well. The occupied compression of $K_\Pi$ is
therefore that of $\mathsf E-\tau^2\mathsf R$.
The displayed comparison gives a positive gap $a$ at
$\nu d_L\tau^2+a=f_*$, with $a\ge f_*\kappa$. On the
occupied subspace the electric-relative read of
Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone} yields
\[
f_*\langle x,K_\Pi x\rangle_G
\ge a\langle x,\mathsf E x\rangle_G
\ge aE_0\langle x,x\rangle_G
\ge f_*E_0\kappa\langle x,x\rangle_G.
\]
The pair at $E_0\kappa$ is consequently positive semidefinite
on a subspace of codimension one, so its reversal count is at
most one (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}'s dual clause). The unit
vector's pencil form is the sum's unit
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), and its form after withdrawing
$E_0\kappa G$ is strictly on its lower side, so the count is
at least one. It equals one. The least root satisfies
$\varepsilon_0\le0$, and the line $\varepsilon_0+E_0\kappa$
sits at or below $E_0\kappa$ and strictly above the ground.
Its count is at most one by monotonicity and at least the ground
multiplicity by the split (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), so both that
count and the ground multiplicity are one. The spectral count
then gives the window cut (Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}).
The creation threshold is attained on two plaquettes with disjoint
boundaries: the $f_0$-loop on the first has content $E_0$ and
sits in $P_p$ for the second; creation there at a closure member
of loop content $e_L$ is an isometry on that input
(Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}), with occupied output at content
$E_0+e_L$. A box containing the two plaquettes admits this read,
and the three-square chain contains such a pair at $d=1$.

\emph{The two-creation range at residue one.}
Write $c:=E_0=[\,3:2\,]$, $f_*=[\,3:8\,]$, and
$b:=\tau^2$. The magnetic closure is $\{f\}$, with
$d_L=2$ and one creator $C_{p,f}$ per plaquette.
The next occupied content after $c$ is at least
$c'=[\,9:4\,]=[\,3:2\,]c$. An occupied support has every
vertex of degree at least two (Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}).
Five links would give at most five vertices; at five vertices
every degree would be two, an odd cycle, and at at most four
vertices a simple bipartite graph has at most four links.
Thus a support off the four-link cycles has at least six links,
at content at least $6f_*=c'$. A four-link cycle has one label
around it, the two-valent unit read
(Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}); at residue one the label of
row length $n$ reads $[\,n(n+2):8\,]$ per link
(Definition~\ref{def:c2hat}). Beyond $n=1$ this is at least
one, giving content at least four on the cycle. The six-link
boundary of two adjacent plaquettes at the fundamental label
attains $c'$. Four-link cycles in a box are its plaquettes:
their four unit coordinate steps use two directions, each once
forward and once backward; the square chain has its own
four-link cycles at its plaquettes.

For $c\le C<3c$, let $N$ be the plaquette count.
The unit, the $N$ fundamental loops, and the admitted products
of two loops at disjoint boundaries are orthonormal, the pair
norm the creation isometry's read
(Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}). Two distinct pair products have
distinct supports: a plaquette in one pair off the other pair
meets each of the other's plaquettes in at most one boundary
link, so at least two of its four links lie off that pair.
Orthogonality follows from the configuration Gram
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}).
At a positive scalar $u$, the action
\[
K_u:=u\mathsf E_\Pi-b\sum_i(a_i+a_i^\dagger)
\]
on these groups has matrix
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
0&-b\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}&0\\
-b\mathbf1&ucI&-bB\\
0&-bB^{\mathsf T}&2ucI
\end{pmatrix},
\]
where a column of $B$ is $e_i+e_j$ for an admitted pair.
Let $Q$ be the Gram fold
$\sum(e_i+e_j)(e_i+e_j)^{\mathsf T}$ over the excluded
unordered pairs, every pair excluded at $C<2c$. Counting all
unordered pairs gives
\[
BB^{\mathsf T}+Q+2I=NI+\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T},
\qquad Q\succeq0.
\]
\emph{The six-link sources.} At residue one the occupied
contents below $2c$ are $c$ and $c'$ alone. The four-link
and five-link cases are the reads above. Seven links below
$2c=3$ would all have label $f$, since one label at or beyond
$\theta$ raises the content to at least $[\,26:8\,]>3$.
The $f$-link subgraph has even degree at every vertex, the
class read at residue one (Construction~\ref{con:fusion};
Lemma~\ref{lem:chargedcell}(i)), and therefore splits into
even cycles in the bipartite box; its link count is even.
For six links, at most one label could be $\theta$, leaving
five $f$-links, which the even count excludes; a label beyond
$\theta$ already exceeds the content bound. Thus all six
labels are $f$, their even subgraph one six-cycle, since two
cycles have at least eight links. Eight links have content
at least $2c$.

For $C<3c$, the action $K_u$ consequently has the preceding
block on the unit, single loops and pair products and a block from six-cycle states
of content $c'$ to their created plaquette products of content $c'+c$.
Their map is $\mathsf B_6\chi_s:=\sum_p a_p\chi_s$, the
six-cycle $s$ at its character. Source states have
identity Gram; the product images read in their own Gram.
At $C<c'+c$ the map reads the sum's unit. At $C\ge c'+c$,
its diagonal square is
\[
(\mathsf B_6^\dagger\mathsf B_6)_{ss}=N-m_s,
\]
where $m_s$ counts plaquettes whose boundaries meet the
six-cycle's links: the other creators are isometries on
$\chi_s$ and their images have distinct supports
(Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}).

Two product images can share a support at three decompositions
of four paths, of lengths $1,3,3,3$. To read this list, a
six-cycle and its disjoint-boundary plaquette share at most
two vertices: three square vertices would require two paths
of length at least three between adjacent square vertices,
the square edges excluded, and a path of at least two between
diagonal vertices, exceeding six links. At two diagonal
vertices the square's two length-two paths and a length-two
part of the six-cycle would give three common neighbors of
two grid vertices; distinct grid vertices have at most two,
their coordinate differences giving two orders of two unit
steps at most. At two adjacent vertices the square gives
paths of lengths one and three, and the six-cycle gives two
paths of length three. These four paths have exactly three
decompositions into a square and a six-cycle. At one shared
vertex or at disjoint vertices the decomposition is unique.
A six-cycle has at most one link joining opposite vertices:
two such links give a pair of vertices with three common
neighbors. Such a link is its chord, the length-one path.

On the four paths let $U_0,U_1,U_2,U_3$ be their coefficient
products from one common end to the other. The three states
are
$\chi_f(U_0U_i^\dagger)\chi_f(U_jU_k^\dagger)$,
with $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$. Their diagonal Gram reads one.
Each off-diagonal read is $[\,1:4\,]$: contracting $U_0$
between two traces gives $[\,1:2\,]$ times the joined trace,
contracting the next path gives another $[\,1:2\,]$, and
the final character pair reads one. These are the coefficient
block orthogonality and character unit reads
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}; Proposition~\ref{prop:repring});
the three-link paths read their one-edge coefficients by
convolution (Theorem~\ref{thm:network}(i)). The self-dual
character fixes the trace under path reversal.

If $s$ has a chord, its two length-three paths close at that
chord to two plaquettes. Let $t_s$ count the further
plaquettes at the chord. Each gives two off-diagonal entries
$[\,1:4\,]$ in the row of
$\mathsf B_6^\dagger\mathsf B_6$, the other two
decompositions. Each resulting six-cycle determines the
added path and its plaquette, so these entries have distinct
keys. At a six-cycle without a chord, $t_s=0$ and the row
is diagonal. The count $t_s$ injects into the $m_s$ list:
translate each further chord plaquette along the detour of
one of the first two plaquettes. Its chord moves to the
parallel outer edge of that plaquette, a link of $s$.
The translated plaquette is in the box; a different plane
has its detour coordinate constant at either of the two
admitted positions, and the opposite plaquette in the
detour's plane translates to the first plaquette itself.
Translation is injective, so $t_s\le m_s$. On the square
chain the chord belongs to the first two plaquettes alone,
and $t_s=0$.

It follows that
\[
\mathsf B_6^\dagger\mathsf B_6\preceq NI.
\]
Below the target content the map is the sum's unit. At
$C\ge c'+c$ the comparison's form is the fold of differences' squares
at $[\,1:4\,]$ over the paired row keys, joined to the
diagonal squares at $m_s-[\,t_s:2\,]\ge0$, the row's
off-diagonal fold $[\,t_s:2\,]$. This is the diagonal
dominance split (Theorem~\ref{thm:decimation}(ii)).

The scalar $u$ is the cofactor at
\[
f_*u+\nu d_Lb=f_*.
\]
At $3\nu d_Lb+2f_*\kappa\le2f_*$ it reads
$[\,1:3\,]<u\le1$. With $\gamma:=c\kappa$, the
parameter reads are
\[
2\gamma\le(3u-1)c,\qquad \gamma\le uc.
\]
The second follows from $u\le1$. The remainder comparison
of Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone} gives $K_\Pi\succeq K_u$
in their pairing, directly at the electric form.

The actual pencil's compression to the unit and single
loops has magnetic entries one at the vacuum couplings
and the sum's unit between single loops. An entry of the
latter kind is the evaluation of three plaquette characters.
The plaquettes occurring an odd number of times form a
list of one or three members. At three members a boundary
has at least two links outside the other two boundaries,
since distinct plaquettes share at most one link. Thus
some link has odd fundamental class, and its unit
coefficient is the sum's unit
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}; Construction~\ref{con:fusion}).
The entry at one member has that class on its boundary
as well. For $N\ge1$ and $b>0$, the compression to the
unit and the sum of the single loops therefore has least
root $-a$, where $a(a+c)=Nb^2$ and $a>0$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}). The actual ground satisfies
$\varepsilon_0\le-a$ by compression
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). Put
\[
\rho:=\varepsilon_0^\vee\ge a,\qquad
z:=\varepsilon_0+\gamma=\gamma-\rho,\qquad
c_u:=uc,\qquad \sigma:=c_u-z,\qquad d_u:=c_u+\sigma.
\]
Both $\sigma$ and $d_u$ are positive. The two reads
\begin{gather*}
\rho(c+\rho)\ge Nb^2,\\
\sigma d_u=\rho(c+\rho)
+\rho\big((3u-1)c-2\gamma\big)
+(uc-\gamma)(2uc-\gamma)
\end{gather*}
give $\sigma d_u\ge Nb^2$. At the line $z$, the pair
block of $K_u$ is $d_uI$. Its deflation onto the unit
and single loops is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
-z&-b\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\\
-b\mathbf1&v_0I+hQ-h\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
h:=[\,b^2:d_u\,],\quad
v_0:=[\,\delta+2b^2:d_u\,]>0,
\]
where $Nb^2+\delta=\sigma d_u$. On the hyperplane
$x_0+[\,b:c_u\,]\sum_i x_i=0$, its form is
\[
v_0\sum_i x_i^2+h x^{\mathsf T}Qx
+[\,b^2\sigma(2c_u+\sigma):c_u^2d_u\,]
\Big(\sum_i x_i\Big)^2,
\]
a positive fold, with the pair-block directions joined
through the deflation's congruence
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).

For the six-cycle block put $v_1:=uc'-\gamma>0$ and
$v_2:=u(c'+c)-\gamma>0$. Its target at $z$ has scalar
$v_2+\rho$ in its pairing, and its deflated source reads
at or beyond
\[
\big(v_1+\rho-[\,Nb^2:v_2+\rho\,]\big)I\succ0,
\]
since $\mathsf B_6^\dagger\mathsf B_6\preceq NI$ and
\[
(v_1+\rho)(v_2+\rho)
=\rho(c+\rho)+\rho\big((4u-1)c-2\gamma\big)+v_1v_2
>Nb^2,
\]
at $2c'+c=4c$ and
$(4u-1)c-2\gamma\ge uc>0$.
The orthogonal complement to these blocks, collected per
electric content, reads $K_u$ at $u\mathsf E_\Pi$ alone:
a creation would reach $3c$ or beyond, and an adjoint
image below $2c$ would be a floor loop or a six-cycle,
already included among the sources. The complement's
pairings against their created images are the sum's
unit. Its contents exceed $c$, so their $u$-multiples
exceed $z\le\gamma\le uc$.

The positive subspace of the whole lower pencil has
codimension one, giving
\[
\operatorname{rev}\big(H:(\varepsilon_0+\gamma)G\big)
\le\operatorname{rev}\big(GK_u:zG\big)\le1.
\]
The first comparison is $K_\Pi\succeq K_u$, read as
forms (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}); the actual ground
contributes at least one below $\varepsilon_0+\gamma$.
Thus the count and the ground multiplicity are one,
and the cut follows (Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}). At $N=0$
the region is acyclic; at $C<c$ its window is the unit
line; and at $b=0$ the free diagonal read holds
(Lemma~\ref{lem:freeend}). These give the further
cases of the stated range.

At $C=c$ the support classification above leaves the
unit and the fundamental plaquette loops alone. Their Gram
is the identity, their electric entries $0,c,\dots,c$,
and their magnetic entries are the unit couplings at one,
with the loop-to-loop entries at the sum's unit by the
three-character read above. Let $u$ be the loops' sum.
The coefficient lists whose sum is the sum's unit form
a subspace of dimension $N-1$, perpendicular to the unit
and $u$, at pencil $cI$. On $(\mathbf1,u)$ the forms are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}0&-\tau^2N\\-\tau^2N&cN\end{pmatrix},
\qquad\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&N\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Adjoin the positive root $q$ at
$q^2=c^2+4N\tau^4$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:stagesplit}).
It exceeds $c$; the gap at $c+2\rho_N=q$ gives
the displayed product identity. The two roots of this
pair are $-\rho_N,c+\rho_N$, by its determinant and
Lemma~\ref{lem:split}. Its least root is strictly below
the further roots, and every positive level gap is at
or beyond $c$, giving the cut at one
(Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}). The cases $N=0$ and $\tau=0$
are the unit line and the free-end diagonal read.

On an odd torus of side at least five, a cycle of at
most four links has its coordinate steps within one
unwrapped box, since an occupied winding uses at least five links.
The four-link support classification and the magnetic
entry computation therefore hold there as well.
At two directions translations permute the plaquettes
transitively, so the fixed loop list is the line at $u$.
Every further joint chord fiber lies in its perpendicular
complement and reads $c$. The unit line with $u$ gives
the displayed two roots
(Lemma~\ref{lem:fiberdec}).

\emph{The creator range's complement.} A vector pairs
every creator image at the sum's unit exactly where every
creator adjoint reads it there, by the pairing adjoint's
identity (Definition~\ref{def:pencil}). Thus the joint
kernel is the range's orthogonal complement. The creators
raise electric content, so their images pair the unit
line at the sum's unit. Their range is preserved by the
electric action: the image $\mathcal C_i x$ has its
electric image $\mathcal C_i(\mathsf E x)+e_i\mathcal C_i x$.
The orthogonal complement is preserved as well, the
electric action self-adjoint. Collection per content
therefore gives the displayed orthogonal decomposition,
with positive Grams and full span
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}; Definition~\ref{def:elim}).

On the joint kernel, every full $C_i^\dagger$ reads the
sum's unit: its image from the output window lies in its
stated input window (Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}). The
creation pairings between two joint-kernel vectors read
that unit at the adjoint identity, and the annihilation
pairings do so outright. The plaquette split consequently
gives $H_N=E_N-\tau^2R_N$. The remainder comparison gives
$\nu d_LE_N-f_*R_N\succeq0$, and the electric floor gives
$E_N-E_0G_N\succeq0$ on the part perpendicular to the
unit (Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}; Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}).
Substituting the two witnessed joins into the site datum
gives the displayed positive fold; its last term is
positive definite at $\omega>0$ and the positive Gram.
The block is therefore a positive principal pivot, with
its solve at the adjugate against its determinant, and
inertia gives the stated count
(Definition~\ref{def:elim}; Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).

The unit's Hamiltonian image is
$K_\Pi\mathbf1=-\tau^2\sum_i\mathcal C_i\mathbf1$,
the electric and remainder reads at the sum's unit and
the annihilation read there as well. It belongs to
$\mathcal R_C$, so it pairs $\mathcal N_C^+$ at the
sum's unit. This is the unit row of $B$, and the unit
row of $BX$ reads that unit. The vacant complementary
list contributes its vacant count, with the full window
then spanned by $\mathcal W_C$.

For the ground-translated line, at $d_h(\tau)>0$ its
positive margin gives the pair
$\xi:=[\,f_*h+d_h(\tau):E_0\,]$.
The divisor identity gives $\xi+\nu d_L\tau^2=f_*$.
The ground satisfies $e\le0$
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), so the second witness is
\[
\omega=d_h(\tau)+f_*e^\vee>0,
\qquad f_*(e+h)+\omega=\xi E_0.
\]
These are the two witnesses of the complementary
count, at every window. The divisor's constant is
positive at $h<E_0$, and its quadratic term is the
balance partner of a positive datum at the occupied
closure. Its positive root is the quadratic
extension's positive member
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stagesplit}); the trichotomy of squares
puts the divisor on its upper side exactly below
that root among positive root coordinates.

\emph{The translated line on its upper side.} Put
$b:=\tau^2$ and $\rho:=e^\vee$. The active closure
members are those at $e_i\le C$, their count $m_C$,
and the admitted creators' count is $s:=Nm_C$ at
the region's plaquette count $N$. If $s$ is occupied,
let $u:=\sum_i\mathcal C_i\mathbf1$ over those creators.
Its loop summands are orthonormal: at one plaquette
this is character orthogonality, and at different
plaquettes an unshared link reads a nonunit coefficient
against the unit (Construction~\ref{con:coeff};
Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}). Thus
\[
\langle u,u\rangle=s,\qquad
\langle u,\mathsf E u\rangle\le s e^+,\qquad
\langle\mathbf1,K_\Pi u\rangle=-bs.
\]
The magnetic read $\langle u,\mathsf M u\rangle$ sits
on its upper side or at equal members. A term at three
distinct plaquettes has an unshared link: each square
shares at most one link with each other square, so at
least two of its links occur there alone. At two
distinct plaquettes one has such a link as well.
Those evaluations read the sum's unit. The terms
on one plaquette are unit coefficients of products
of characters, natural folds of fusion counts
(Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}). Consequently
$\langle u,K_\Pi u\rangle\le s e^+$.

The ground form $H-eG$ is positive semidefinite.
Its compression to $(\mathbf1,u)$ has diagonal
entries $\rho$ and $\langle u,K_\Pi u\rangle+\rho s$,
and off-diagonal entry $-bs$. Its determinant read
therefore gives
\[
b^2s^2
\le \rho\big(\langle u,K_\Pi u\rangle+\rho s\big)
\le \rho s(e^++\rho).
\]
With $z:=e+h\ge0$, one has $0\le\rho\le h$, so
\[
s b^2\le \rho(\rho+e^+)\le h(h+e^+).
\]
At a vacant $s$ this comparison holds outright.

For a vector $x$ perpendicular to the unit, put
$n:=\langle x,x\rangle$, $t:=\langle x,\mathsf E x\rangle$
and $v:=\langle x,\mathsf A x\rangle$, where
$\mathsf A$ is the admitted creators' sum for this read.
At one plaquette the projections $C_iC_i^\dagger$
over the active closure are pairwise orthogonal,
by $C_i^\dagger C_j=\delta_{ij}P_p$ there, and their
sum sits below $Q_p$. The earlier support count
therefore gives
\[
\sum_i\langle C_i^\dagger x,C_i^\dagger x\rangle
\le [\,\nu:f_*\,]\,t,\qquad
\sum_i\langle P_p x,P_p x\rangle\le s n.
\]
Here $p$ is the plaquette of $i$ in the second fold.
The adjoint image sits in $P_p$, so $v$ is the
pairing of the two lists $(C_i^\dagger x)_i$ and
$(P_p x)_i$. Their squared pairing read gives
\[
f_*v^2\le s\nu t n
\]
(Construction~\ref{con:coeff}'s squared Cauchy--Schwarz).
Every inactive creator's form on the window reads the
sum's unit, since it raises past the cutoff.
The magnetic split and remainder comparison then give
\[
f_*\langle x,(K_\Pi-zI)x\rangle
\ge \xi t-f_*z n-2f_*b\,|v|.
\]
The electric floor is $t\ge E_0n$. Write
$d_z:=\xi E_0-f_*z$, so $d_z\ge d_h(\tau)>0$
at $0\le z\le h$. The identity
\[
E_0(\xi t-f_*z n)^2-d_z^2t n
=(t-E_0n)(\xi^2E_0t-f_*^2z^2n)
\]
has its right member on its upper side or at equal
members: $t\ge E_0n$ and $\xi E_0>f_*z\ge0$.
The stated parameter comparison and the two pairing
reads give
\[
E_0(\xi t-f_*z n)^2
\ge d_h(\tau)^2t n
\ge4f_*\nu E_0s b^2t n
\ge4f_*^2E_0b^2v^2.
\]
At an occupied $x$, the quantity $\xi t-f_*z n$
is positive at $d_z n>0$. The trichotomy of squares
therefore gives $\xi t-f_*z n\ge2f_*b|v|$,
so the form at $z$ is positive semidefinite on the
unit's perpendicular complement. Its count is at
most one (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). Since $z=e+h>e$,
the actual ground contributes at least one
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}). The count is one.

\emph{The ground-side root.} The identities
$E_0=4f_*$, $\nu\ge2$, $e^+\ge E_0$ and
$0<\delta<f_*E_0$ give the two positive gaps
$a_\rho,b_\rho$. The quadratic extension's positive
member $q_\rho$ exceeds $b_\rho$ at the trichotomy
of squares (Lemma~\ref{lem:stagesplit}). Substitution
of $\rho_*$ at $q_\rho$'s relation gives
$a_\rho\rho_*^2+b_\rho\rho_*=\delta^2$.
The polynomial
\[
P(\rho):=(\delta+f_*\rho)^2-c_\rho\rho(\rho+e^+)
=\delta^2-b_\rho\rho-a_\rho\rho^2
\]
therefore reads
\[
P(\rho)=\langle\rho_*:\rho\rangle
\big(a_\rho(\rho_*+\rho)+b_\rho\big).
\]
At $\rho\ge0$ its second factor is positive, so its
side is the first factor's, with equality at the root.

Put $u:=[\,\xi E_0:f_*\,]$ and $T:=h+u$.
The join $\xi E_0=\delta+f_*h$ gives $h<u$ and
$\delta+f_*T=2\xi E_0$. Also
\[
c_\rho T(T+e^+)>c_\rho u^2
=4\xi^2E_0^2[\,\nu E_0:f_*\,]>4\xi^2E_0^2.
\]
Thus $P(T)<0$ and $\rho_*<T$. At
$0\le\rho\le\rho_*$ and $z=h-\rho$ one consequently has
$f_*^2z^2<\xi^2E_0^2$ and
$d_z=\xi E_0-f_*z=\delta+f_*\rho>0$.
For every $x$ perpendicular to the unit, the determinant
and squared-pairing reads above give
\[
s b^2\le\rho(\rho+e^+),\qquad
f_*v^2\le s\nu t n,
\]
at $\rho=e^\vee$, with $t\ge E_0n$. The displayed
square identity has its right member on its upper side
or at equal members at $f_*^2z^2<\xi^2E_0^2$.
Since $P(\rho)\ge0$, it gives
\[
E_0(\xi t-f_*z n)^2\ge d_z^2t n
\ge c_\rho\rho(\rho+e^+)t n
\ge4f_*^2E_0b^2v^2.
\]
At an occupied $x$ the quantity before squaring is
$\xi(t-E_0n)+d_z n>0$. The trichotomy of squares
gives $\xi t-f_*z n\ge2f_*b|v|$.
The magnetic split's comparison therefore puts the
form at $z$ on its upper side or at equal members
on the unit's perpendicular complement. Its count is
at most one, and the ground below $e+h$ gives at
least one (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}; Lemma~\ref{lem:split}).
At $\delta^2\ge c_\rho h(h+e^+)$ the read
\[
P(h)=(\delta+f_*h)^2-c_\rho h(h+e^+)
>\delta^2-c_\rho h(h+e^+)\ge0
\]
gives $\rho_*>h$. For $\rho>\rho_*$ the unit pivot
$-z=\rho-h$ exceeds $\rho_*-h$ at the sum's
injectivity (Definition~\ref{def:ground}).

For the common segment, $E_0=4f_*$ and $\nu\ge2$ give
$c_\rho=16\nu f_*^2>f_*^2$, so $a_0$ is a positive gap.
The displayed $b_0$ exceeds $2f_*^2E_0$, giving
$0<h_0<[\,E_0:4\,]$ at the cross-multiplied read.
The polynomial identity at the offset is
\[
f_*^2\langle E_0:h\rangle^2-c_\rho h(h+e^+)
=k_0-b_0h-a_0h^2.
\]
At $h=h_0\le E_0$, its second and third terms satisfy
\[
b_0h_0+a_0h_0^2\le(b_0+a_0E_0)h_0=[\,k_0:2\,].
\]
Thus the first display exceeds the sum's unit at $h_0$.
The positive quadratic root $q_0$ is strictly below
$f_*\langle E_0:h_0\rangle$ by the trichotomy of squares,
giving $w_0>0$. The quadratic extension at
$[\,w_0:\nu d_LE_0\,]$ gives $T_0>0$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:stagesplit}). For $\tau\le T_0$, the
divisor reads
\[
d_{h_0}(\tau)=q_0+\nu d_LE_0\langle T_0^2:\tau^2\rangle,
\]
whose second term is on its upper side or at equal members.
This gives both comparisons, with the earlier count displays
read at $h_0$ and $\tau$.

\emph{The count on the input lists.} Join the rectangular
identities of Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}, at
$\alpha=1$ and $\beta=\tau^2$, over the input lists.
They give
\[
(K_\Pi-zI)\mathcal C
=\mathcal C\mathcal T_z-\tau^2\mathcal J.
\]
Multiplication by $\mathcal C^{\mathsf T}G$ gives the
stated range form; its transpose gives the further
identity at the symmetry of $H-zG$.
Every input window is a compression of the output
window, so $K_i^--eI$ has a positive-semidefinite
read in its pairing (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).
Each $e_i\ge E_0$, the member floor's comparison,
so $e_i-\gamma$ is positive at $\gamma<E_0$ and
the stated input action is positive definite.

The map $(s,x)\mapsto s\mathbf1+\mathcal Cx$
has image $\mathcal W_C$. Its pullback reads the
deflated form's count: a negative subspace in the
domain maps injectively to its image, since a kernel
vector reads the form at the sum's unit, and every
negative subspace in $\mathcal W_C$ lifts at a right
solve, the image collection's Gram-dual solve
(Lemma~\ref{lem:lowerspan}; Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}).
Thus the two maximal negative counts agree.
The kernel of this map is the input kernel of
$\mathcal C$, the unit perpendicular to its image,
so it contributes a kernel block.

The unit row of the complementary coupling is at the
sum's unit. Its range pairing at the joined creator
list is $-\tau^2\mathbf r^{\mathsf T}$: at every admitted
creator,
\[
\mathcal C_i^\dagger\sum_j\mathcal C_j\mathbf1
=\mathbf1
\]
on its input window. At its own plaquette the
character orthogonality reads the matching label
once; at a different plaquette an unshared boundary
link puts the adjoint image at the sum's unit
(Theorem~\ref{thm:coeffone}; Construction~\ref{con:coeff}).
Pairing the input unit against its window list gives
the stated column. Pair the joined rectangular
identity against $Z$. Since
$Z^{\mathsf T}G\mathcal C=0$, it reads
\[
Z^{\mathsf T}H\mathcal C=-\tau^2L_N.
\]
The complementary deflation's correction is therefore
$\tau^4L_N^{\mathsf T}Y_N$, symmetric and positive
semidefinite at
$L_N^{\mathsf T}Y_N=Y_N^{\mathsf T}S_N(z)Y_N$.
This gives the displayed pullback matrix.

For the Gram recursion, the adjoint and creator
images fit in their stated windows, giving
\[
G_i^-\mathcal C_i^\dagger\mathcal C_j
=\Gamma_{ij},\qquad
\mathcal C_i^\dagger\mathcal C_j
=\Pi_i^-C_i^\dagger C_j\Pi_j^-.
\]
Split the last product as
$C_jC_i^\dagger+[C_i^\dagger,C_j]$.
The adjoint $C_i^\dagger$ sends a content $c$ in
$\Pi_j^-$ to a content $c'$ at $c'+e_i=c$, so
$c'+e_i+e_j\le C$. Its image is therefore in
$\Pi_{ij}^-$, and the following $C_j$ sends it
into $\Pi_i^-$. The product is precisely
$\mathcal C_{j|i}\mathcal C_{i|j}^\dagger$.
At $C<e_i+e_j$ that intermediate list is vacant.
The local commutator's disjoint-boundary read
gives the last assertion.

\emph{The parity elimination.} At $d\ge2$, let
$x_j(v)$ be the coordinate count of a vertex $v$ from
the box's lower face in direction $j$. For a link in
direction $i$ from $v$, let $\eta_\ell$ be the parity
of $\sum_{j<i}x_j(v)$. Reversing the link keeps that
parity. On a plaquette in directions $i<j$, the two
direction-$i$ parities agree and the two direction-$j$
parities differ by one, so the boundary fold reads odd.
On the square chain, assign odd parity to each square's
least boundary link belonging to that square alone,
and even parity to the further links. Its boundaries
each read one odd link. Both assignments are finite
index reads (Construction~\ref{con:lattice};
Definition~\ref{def:ground}).

At a configuration $a$, define its grade as the parity
of $\sum_\ell\eta_\ell n(a_\ell)$, where $n$ is
the label's row length at residue one, and the unit
label reads the vacant count. The vertex and fusion
class laws are the parity of this row length
(Construction~\ref{con:fusion}). Fusion by $f$ at a
plaquette changes every boundary link's class by one
and fixes the further link classes, so the two grades
of every occupied magnetic entry differ by the odd
boundary fold. Its blocks within either grade are the sum's
unit. The electric and Gram forms preserve the grades,
being diagonal on configurations, and the unit has
even grade (Definition~\ref{def:carrier};
Definition~\ref{def:pencil}). The total-content
projection preserves this split at every cutoff.

The odd configurations are occupied, each with content
at least $E_0$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}). Thus for
$z<E_0$ each block $(c_a-z)G_a$ is positive definite.
Each block's solve is the Gram's adjugate against its
determinant and the positive scalar gap. The direct sum gives the
displayed $X$. The odd-block deflation is
$E_+-zG_+-\tau^4 BX$, symmetric at
$BX=X^{\mathsf T}D_-X$. Inertia adds at this positive
pivot with its reversal count the sum's unit
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}), giving the stated count.
At an occupied plaquette count, $C\ge E_0$ and $\tau>0$, the
actual-ground compression above gives $\varepsilon_0<0$,
so every line $\varepsilon_0+E_0\kappa$ at
$\kappa\le1$ lies below $E_0$ and has this read.
The unit-only and free-end windows have their direct
diagonal reads.

For the two-line read, subtract the two solved identities
$D_-(e)X_e=B^{\mathsf T}$ and
$D_-(e+\gamma)X_{e+\gamma}=B^{\mathsf T}$. Since
$D_-(e)=D_-(e+\gamma)+\gamma G_-$, they give
\[
X_{e+\gamma}=X_e+\gamma Y_\gamma,
\qquad F_e=F_{e+\gamma}+\gamma W_\gamma.
\]
On the odd configuration $a$, the form $BY_\gamma$
has the contribution
\[
[\,1:(c_a-e)(c_a-e-\gamma)\,]\,
B_aG_a^{-1}B_a^{\mathsf T},
\]
where $B_a$ is the corresponding column block and
$G_a^{-1}$ denotes its adjugate solve. Both scalar gaps
are positive. Each contribution is positive semidefinite,
the Gram-dual square at a positive scalar, so their fold
joined to $G_+$ is positive definite
(Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia}). The parity count at $e+\gamma$
and the displayed difference give the two-line identity.
At $e$, the full level-gap form is positive semidefinite
(Definition~\ref{def:pencil}), and the odd block is
positive definite; its deflation $F_e$ has the positive
read by inertia. Its lower kernel row forces the odd
coordinate to be $\tau^2X_ev$, and its upper row is
$F_ev=0$, giving the stated kernel correspondence.
\end{proof}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The four-point floor]\label{lem:fourpoint}
Fix two plaquettes sharing one link, the theta graph
(Construction~\ref{con:fiber}), a closure member $\lambda_0$ of the
magnetic list (Construction~\ref{con:fusion}, the member's stated
list's first member), the \emph{pair probe}
$\varphi:=\sum_{c\in P}\chi_c$ over the label set
$P:=\{\lambda_0,\bar\lambda_0,2\lambda_0,2\bar\lambda_0\}$, the
Cartan squares at the Cartan strictness
(Construction~\ref{con:fusion}), involution-fixed at the duals and
free of the unit label, $q_i:=\varphi(U_{\partial p_i})$ the pair's
modules, and the ray $[\,1:\tau^2\,]$ at a window ground $\psi$
beyond the graph's locality band (Lemma~\ref{lem:stableentries}).
Write $m_a:=\mathrm{Eval}(\varphi^{\,a})$ for the probe's free
moments, $m_0=1$, $m_1$ the sum's unit at the nonunit members,
$m_2=\#P$ at the orthonormal characters
(Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}), and $T_a(k)$ for the $k$-count of
the $a$-th power, the coefficient of $\chi_k$ in $\varphi^{\,a}$, a
natural fold of fusion counts, $T_0(k)=\delta_{k\mathbf 1}$,
$T_1(k)$ one at $k\in P$, and $T_2(\lambda_0)\ge2$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:repring}). The
\emph{connected four-point read} at the pair, each field twice, is
the moments' partition fold at $\mu_{ab}:=\omega(q_1^{\,a}q_2^{\,b})$,
one term per partition of the four fields at the blocks' moment
product, the weight $j!$ at the join $j+1=b$ over the block count
$b$, the one-block term at weight one, and the side the count's
parity,
\[
\varkappa_4:=\big\langle\,
\mu_{22}+2\mu_{10}^2\mu_{02}+2\mu_{01}^2\mu_{20}
+8\mu_{10}\mu_{01}\mu_{11}
\,:\,
2\mu_{10}\mu_{12}+2\mu_{01}\mu_{21}+\mu_{20}\mu_{02}
+2\mu_{11}^2+6\mu_{10}^2\mu_{01}^2
\,\big\rangle\ .
\]
At every member the read holds a positive located floor on a cell
at the free end's side. Write $a_\lambda:=[\,1:4\hat c_2(\lambda)\,]$
for a closure member's \emph{loop weight}, the plaquette content's
cofactor (Proposition~\ref{prop:E0}); at two closure members
$\lambda,\mu$ the \emph{pair networks} $F^{\lambda\mu}_k$ are the
channel split of the adjacent product
$\chi_\lambda(U_{\partial p_1})\,\chi_\mu(U_{\partial p_2})=\sum_kF^{\lambda\mu}_k$
over the shared link's channels $k\in\lambda\otimes\bar\mu$, the
electric reads $e^{\lambda\mu}_k:=3\hat c_2(\lambda)+3\hat c_2(\mu)+\hat c_2(k)$
and the weights $w^{\lambda\mu}_k:=\langle F^{\lambda\mu}_k,F^{\lambda\mu}_k\rangle
=[\,m_kd_k:d_\lambda d_\mu\,]$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:network}(i),(ii) at the
pair's labels; Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(ii)), the weights folding
to one and their electric fold to the \emph{distant read}
$e^{\lambda\mu}_\infty:=4\hat c_2(\lambda)+4\hat c_2(\mu)$, the two
closure identities $\sum_kw^{\lambda\mu}_k=1$ and
$\sum_kw^{\lambda\mu}_k\,\hat c_2(k)=\hat c_2(\lambda)+\hat c_2(\mu)$
(the dimension identity, Lemma~\ref{lem:blockcount}(ii); the
uniform drift at the second factor, Theorem~\ref{thm:drift}); and
the \emph{pair excess}
\[
J_{\lambda\mu}\;:=\;\sum_kw^{\lambda\mu}_k\,
\big\langle\,[\,1:e^{\lambda\mu}_k\,]\!:\![\,1:e^{\lambda\mu}_\infty\,]\,\big\rangle\ ,
\qquad
e^{\lambda\mu}_\infty\,J_{\lambda\mu}\;=\;\sum_{k<l}w^{\lambda\mu}_kw^{\lambda\mu}_l\,
\big\langle e^{\lambda\mu}_k\!:\!e^{\lambda\mu}_l\big\rangle^{2}\,
[\,1:e^{\lambda\mu}_ke^{\lambda\mu}_l\,]\ ,
\]
every summand a square at pair weights, positive by its shape at
distinct channel reads. Then the read sits within the priced
tail's bracket of the jet's value
\[
\hat\varkappa_4\;=\;2\,\tau^4\sum_{\lambda,\mu\in\bar L}
(a_\lambda+a_\mu)\,T_2(\lambda)\,T_2(\mu)\,J_{\lambda\mu}\ ,
\]
whose side is its upper at every member, the margin at or beyond
the diagonal pair's read at $\lambda_0$,
\[
\hat\varkappa_4\;\ge\;\tau^{4}\,
\big[\,d_\theta:12\,d_{\lambda_0}^{\,4}\,\hat c_2(\lambda_0)^{3}\,(6\,\hat c_2(\lambda_0)+1)\,\big]\ ,
\]
the diagonal pair's excess read at its unit channel against its
adjoint channel, the adjoint occupied once at least in
$\lambda_0\otimes\bar\lambda_0$ (the generators' copy,

\section{The reconstruction}

\begin{theorem}[The spectral bracket reconstruction]\label{thm:reconstruct}
The Euclidean bracket families have the following spectral reads
over the located stage. The data are the bracketed ground reads
(Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}), the restoration counts with the
cone read (Theorem~\ref{thm:restoration}; Lemma~\ref{lem:cone}),
and the pairing's definitional positivity
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}), per member and direction count
at every window of the corner cell.

\emph{(i) The spectral data are located divisor data.} Per fiber
the energy roots with their weights are the split's own
(Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), the Euclidean families read as the
weight folds over them (Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(v)), and
on the clearance cell the moment folds' solve returns the
truncated moment vector from the streams' reads
(Lemma~\ref{lem:momentfold}), the located divisor read its
clearance: the divisor data read the Euclidean families as
their weight folds, one solved witness per family, the lower's
and the upper's (Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(v)).

\emph{(ii) The root loci through degree two.} Per probe pair the
family is the weight fold over the located roots at the fiber's
chord, at the probe's spectral weights from (i). The roots'
momentum reading is the cone's: at every located root the locus at
the moved level reads the isotropic square at degree two with the
root's located coefficient, the odd degrees at the sum's unit and
the direction data at degree four (Lemma~\ref{lem:cone}). The
families are window-free within
the spectator brackets (Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(iii)), the
growth caps their $m$-point folds' reads
(Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(v)).

\emph{(iii) The state reads close the families.} The pairing's
positivity is the families' own Gram read at every finite probe
list, every split of the
Gram on the upper side throughout (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia});
the window's energy gap is its cut
(Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}), the word sector is the state's space,
cyclic (Lemma~\ref{lem:statespace}), and every read holds at
every window ground at once: each output is a located bracket
read of the inputs, one solve and one count per datum.
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i)} The split's congruence diagonalizes the gram and the
level gap at the located roots (Lemma~\ref{lem:split}), a root's
weight the coordinate's square against the gram's diagonal
entry, and the Euclidean members are the two solved witnesses'
$N$-fold reads, diagonal at the gaps, the lower's
$[\,g_\gamma:N\,]$ and the upper's $[\,N:N+u\gamma\,]$ per root
(Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(v)), so a family is the weight fold
of those reads over the roots; the moment folds' square system
solves at the elimination's adjugate against its determinant on
the clearance cell (Lemma~\ref{lem:momentfold}(ii)), the
determinant's clearance the located divisor read
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cellcount}). \emph{(ii)} Per probe pair (i)'s fold
runs at the fiber's chord, and each root's locus at the moved level
reads $S_0'(\varepsilon)\,a+S_2(\varepsilon)$ against the
isotropic square with the direction data two degrees down
(Lemma~\ref{lem:cone}), the root's degree-two identity. The
families are window-free because
two windows' grounds differ by the transport display's off-line
part, capped at the drift over the tied depths
(Theorem~\ref{thm:groundreads}(iii)), and the $m$-point folds'
magnitudes fold the head caps against the separations' certificate

\emph{(iii)} A family's Gram at a probe list, its reads at the probe
pairs, prices its form at coefficient data as the family's read at
the probes' combination, the pairing bilinear
(Definition~\ref{def:ground}), and that read is (i)'s weight fold
at the combination's coordinate squares, every weight the gram's

Gram reads the upper side throughout (Lemma~\ref{lem:inertia});
the window's energy gap is its cut because a window's spectral read
is its cut at every ground (Lemma~\ref{lem:speccut}), and the word
sector is the state's space at
$\omega(\bar A\,B)=\langle A\psi,\,B\psi\rangle$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:statespace}).
\end{proof}
\end{theorem}

x'=[\,1:q\,]\,(A\,x+b),\qquad
A^{\mathsf T}JA=q^2J,\qquad
\det A=q^{d+1},\qquad A_{00}\ge q,
\]
at a natural $q$, a square list $A$ and a matched list $b$ over
the balance pairs of counts; $J$ is diagonal, one at the time key
and its balance partner at each spatial key. The map transports
the words with their supports and probe indices. The transports
read identity, composition, product and involution at the words'
located reads. The map at
\[
q'=q^{d+1},\qquad A'=q\,\operatorname{adj}(A),\qquad
b'=\big(\operatorname{adj}(A)b\big)^{\vee}
\]
reads the two composites at the identity, the superscript the
componentwise balance partner, and the two transports compose
to the identity as well.

\emph{The pairing comparisons.} At every finite word list, every
displayed affine map and every positive pair $\epsilon$, construct
scale keys, region keys at each admitted scale, cutoff keys at
each such region, and bracket-refinement keys, with their
comparison witnesses. At every admitted datum beyond its keys,
the two orientations of each component of the transported-pairing
difference sit at or below $\epsilon$, with the identification's
widths included.
Writing $P,Q$ for words and $gP,gQ$ for their transports, the
pairing's component comparisons at every positive pair width read
\[
\langle v_{gP},v_{gQ}\rangle=\langle v_P,v_Q\rangle,
\]
with the unit word fixed. These are the full correlation reads at
the actual probes' weights.

\emph{The continuity moduli.} At every displayed affine map,
every word and positive pair $\epsilon$, construct a positive
pair width about that map in the coefficient reads
$[\,1:q\,]A$ and $[\,1:q\,]b$. The bracket controls the
self-pairing of the difference of the transported vectors at or
below $\epsilon^2$. Every affine datum at located coordinates
obeying the displayed identities is read by a bracket family of
displayed maps at every positive pair width. The word reads
extend along those bracket families, with
the composition, pairing and support identities throughout.
The spacetime translations' time reads agree with the words'
Hamiltonian time evolution. The interpretation on the completed
state space is the invariance item of Remark~\ref{rem:dictionary}.
\end{pending}

\section{The quasi-local algebra}

\begin{definition}[The quasi-local algebra]\label{def:qla}
$\mathfrak A$ is the carrier of the infinite lattice with its filtration
by least windows: every element has one
(Proposition~\ref{prop:leastwindow}), so $\mathfrak A$ is the union of
the regions' local algebras. A winding operator exists only on the finite
torus: its index support wraps a cycle of the torus, while every
configuration of the infinite lattice's index has finite support
(Definition~\ref{def:carrier}), so winding operators lie outside every local algebra and outside
$\mathfrak A$ with them.
\end{definition}
